## Fuzz / crash / security / perf todo index

Canonical shared file: `/Users/lorinc/Library/Application Support/JetBrains/CLion2026.2/scratches/PR_KNOWLEDGEBASE.txt`. The old `scratch_684.txt` and `scratch_699.txt` names are retired.

## PR workflow gate

Use this as the single read/write knowledgebase for Bitcoin Core and secp256k1 PR triage, review state, priority changes, and prepared fixes.
Before selecting, checking out, reviewing, or amending a fork PR branch:

1. Search this file for the PR number, branch name, source commit, affected symbol, and related PR family.
2. Apply every matching warning, split recommendation, coverage gap, supersession note, and upstream-overlap note to the work.
3. Verify the entry against the current branch and current upstream before changing code. External audit reports are triage leads until replayed locally.
4. Update this file after fetches, rebases, review findings, pushes, closures, supersessions, or changed priorities.
5. Never create or revive the retired project-specific scratch lists.

## 2026-08-07 severely suboptimal algorithms sweep and first prepared fix

The fetched audit report is commit `fa0eca5770f3e9ad5bd08a37c83ce28c436144cd`, `security-review/bitcoin-core-2026-08-05/11-suboptimal-algorithms.md`. It records a ten-area sweep of master `c4fbd3c72114e3466329ec6f4b0f0a4b7ebce3b1`. The report says its top findings were re-verified at that target. Treat the remaining entries as audit leads until they are replayed against current upstream.

* [x] **Top 1, `gettxoutproof` x `AccessByTxid`, reproduced and prepared:** current `upstream/master` `1be0b46297c6b61fefb870db6b3b18c273bcaf97` still performs a full UTXO fallback scan for every caller-supplied txid under `cs_main`. Local branch `l0rinc/rpc-bound-gettxoutproof-utxo-lookups` is prepared at `c7073a40020066568860402f113b593bf2bbbb98` as seven signed commits: `76d2b625ab` moves the authoritative lookup limit into `coins.h`, `59772d8514` tests that limit, `15ffe38e82` purely extracts the UTXO scan, `51455e508e` consults a synced txindex first, `2376d500ae` preserves lookup order while releasing `cs_main` every 1,000 probes, `624cbe648f` checks for RPC interruption between batches, and `c7073a4002` shares one request-wide budget round-robin, documents the multi-txid tradeoff in RPC help, and adds a release-note placeholder.
  **PR-ready evidence:** The focused unit test verifies the probe count through output 2 and that a miss stops at the named lookup limit. A clean Debug comparison measured a 20-txid request at 6.76 seconds on master and 1.13 seconds on the production-equivalent branch tree, a concurrent `getblockcount` at 5.57 seconds and 0.14 seconds, and the same request with a synced txindex at 5.70 seconds and 0.05 seconds. The final RPC implementation is identical to that measured tree; the additional production change relocates the existing lookup limit into its header, and the test split adds only unit coverage. The exact tip builds, the focused unit and functional tests pass, the release-note lint and `git diff --check` pass, and all seven signatures verify. No competing PR or issue was found. PR #35531 is complementary because it reduces txindex costs, while this branch consults that index before the bounded UTXO fallback. The prepared PR text and exact benchmark command are in `scratch_777.txt`. Tracking is configured as `origin/l0rinc/rpc-bound-gettxoutproof-utxo-lookups` and is intentionally `[gone]`; nothing was pushed.
* [ ] **Top 2, Miniscript `thresh` eager quadratic dynamic programs:** the ops, stack-size, and witness-size calculations grow and rescan a `sats` vector for every sub regardless of `k`, and they run during node construction before type checks. The report estimates a roughly 330 kB descriptor can drive about 4e10 iterations through descriptor RPCs, wallet loading, or signing under `cs_wallet`; `Node::ToString` also copies quadratically on deep chains. Reproduce on current master with a focused descriptor benchmark before choosing whether to truncate each dynamic program at `k + 1`.
* [ ] **Top 3, wallet inactive-coinbase descendant abandonment:** the `AddToWallet` traversal in `wallet.cpp` has no visited set, so a diamond descendant DAG revisits txs exponentially and writes each visit separately. The sibling `RecursiveUpdateTxState` already tracks completed txs. Reproduce current-master reachability with a small reorg/rescan wallet fixture, then evaluate a visited set together with one wallet database transaction.
* [ ] **High-priority queue from the same report:** `ParseOutputs` repeatedly searches a UniValue object under `cs_wallet`; PSBT signing rebuilds the unsigned tx two or three times per input under `cs_wallet`; `MarkDestinationsDirty` scans all wallet txs even when the destination set is empty; `getdescriptoractivity` performs per-mempool-input chainstate seeks while holding `cs_main` and `mempool.cs`; the HTTP receive path reparses chunked bodies and the send path erases from the buffer front; `PruneOneBlockFile` scans the full block index for every file under `cs_main`; `pushKV` work in `decodepsbt` grows with the number of unknown fields supplied, while `getprioritisedtransactions` grows with persisted prioritisation history; verbose `getrawmempool` walks entry graphs under `mempool.cs`; and each inv-backlog drain re-sorts the full uncapped backlog under `mempool.cs`. The original #35889 `gettxspendingprevout` erase loop is still live on current master while the upstream fix remains unmerged. Prefer the smallest individually benchmarked fixes, and keep global-lock work as the common review theme rather than combining unrelated subsystems in one PR.

## 2026-07-23 current-master surface and upstream PR refresh

Live GitHub states and heads for the PR batch below were refreshed on 2026-07-23.

### Supersessions and parser audit

* [x] **F1 coin-cursor overrun resolved upstream; unsafe WIP remains:** merged [#35572](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35572) restored DB-only cursor decoding on master. Current `CCoinsViewDB::Cursor()` and `CCoinsViewDBCursor::Next()` propagate `CoinEntry::key`, so advancing from coin records to a different record type invalidates the coin cursor instead of leaving `keyTmp.first == DB_COIN`. This is the same remediation previously validated for F1; current master is no longer affected.
  `origin/l0rinc/custom-coinentry-serialization` at `b1afdcec0c` still assigns `DB_COIN` unconditionally in both initial cursor setup and `Next()`. If that WIP is revived, carry the key-type propagation fix and regression proof with it; do not present F1 as live on master.
* [x] **Current-master package recheck:** `UpdatePSBTOutput()` still constructs `MutableTransactionSignatureCreator` with `input_idx = 0` without a zero-input guard on `afa5e46bbc`. The existing Kernel C API, HTTP request reparse, and latent V2-send entries remain unresolved by this upstream movement. Keep F1 and the merged silent-payments label-flush fix in the resolved column rather than folding them into a live-finding count.
* [x] **Parser and serialization passes, no finding:** Bech32 validates printable ASCII and case before indexing `CHARSET_REV`, then validates separator/checksum positions before slicing. UniValue parses iteratively with `MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 512`, bounded token/escape reads, control-character rejection, and UTF-8/surrogate filtering. `httprpc` authenticates before JSON body parsing, applies method whitelists to singleton and batch requests, isolates batch-element errors, and retains the global HTTP work-queue cap.
  `SpanReader`/`SpanWriter` check sizes before copying or taking subspans and explicitly avoid empty-span `memcpy`. Wallet SQLite statements use fixed SQL with bound blobs, and null blobs become empty spans that fail through the bounded deserializer. `ParseFixedPoint`, `ParseMoney`, and `AmountFromValue` bound intermediate arithmetic and enforce `MoneyRange()`. No new issue was found in these passes.
* [x] **BIP32 path canonicalization nit only:** `ParseHDKeypath()` accepts raw components in `[2^31, UINT32_MAX]`; the high bit then makes them format as hardened components even without an apostrophe in the original text. The current unit test explicitly accepts `4294967295`, and the current tree has no production caller of this helper. Treat this as a latent API/canonicalization choice, not an `importdescriptors` crash or production finding.

### Reviewed upstream PR batch

* [x] **[#35744](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35744), coins DB resize/cursor lifetime / external dynamic proof:** open remotely at `d3484251b3`; local review stack `b446775e8e`, `ea101a2d8a`, then `1154f96c5f` on current master. A deterministic external harness held a live cursor, called `ResizeCache()`, then destroyed the cursor against master. It exited 134 at LevelDB `version_set.cc:753` with `VersionSet::~VersionSet(): Assertion 'dummy_versions_.next_ == &dummy_versions_' failed`, demonstrating that the lifetime violation is structural and does not require a race. A fixed variant built from `d3484251b3` kept `resize_done == 0` while the cursor remained alive and changed it to 1 after cursor destruction, confirming that resize waits for live cursors.
  `b446775e8e` adds one `coins_db_cursor_resize` characterization test. It retains the old `CDBWrapper` and redirects replacement to a separate temporary path, so the old code can complete resize with a real cursor alive rather than aborting in LevelDB. Its TODO-marked assertions record that the cursor leaves `m_db_mutex` available to an exclusive probe on another thread and that resize returns `std::future_status::ready` while the cursor is alive. It then destroys the cursor and waits for resize before checking the status. `ea101a2d8a` replaces the exclusive `Mutex` with a `std::shared_mutex` and changes only those assertions to exclusive-lock unavailability and `std::future_status::timeout`, removing both TODOs. Compaction still takes the mutex exclusively in this commit. `1154f96c5f` documents the `m_compaction` access invariant and moves the compaction wait before the exclusive resize lock, so cursors remain available during compaction until replacement begins. Each cursor must stay on its creating thread, and that thread must not create another cursor for the same DB or acquire `cs_main` while it is alive. Current callers satisfy these constraints. A 2026-07-25 review confirmed the lifetime and lock ordering; its timing nit is real because the probe verifies cursor ownership but not that ResizeCache reached the exclusive lock, and a destructor-only cs_main assertion would not catch a blocked reacquisition. The characterization focused test passes with the old outcomes; the final focused test passes in three runs, and all 14 `coins_tests` cases pass. Temporarily releasing the cursor lock makes both flipped assertions fail. Earlier unchanged production code also passed `feature_assumeutxo.py`, `rpc_dumptxoutset.py`, and `rpc_scantxoutset.py`.
  2026-07-28 ref check: the pre-push stack SHAs recorded here earlier (`14a03453e5`, `13a304a5b4`, `e53a7ccce3`, `5bf0a9a2ba`, `09c8638c60`, and the claimed tip `14a03453e5`) no longer exist in this checkout after the signed rebase. The recoverable shared-lock stack is `origin/l0rinc/coins-cursor-resize-lifetime` at `38b8476960`, with eight re-signed commits: `49d961776e refactor: extract common lock acquisition`, `4d25c38ad5 sync: add shared mutex lock checking`, `852a9f0901 sync: support non-LIFO lock release`, `264766d580 script: check signature cache shared locking`, `e638704c6f test: check cuckoo cache shared locking`, `1678b11ff2 test: characterize coins DB cursor lifetime`, `05c0e6cb6f coins: block DB resize during cursor iteration`, and `38b8476960 coins: allow DB cursors during compaction`. The local branch `l0rinc/coins-cursor-resize-lifetime` is a stale single-commit branch at `5a92e480d3`, ahead 1 and behind 147 relative to its tracking ref; use the `origin/` ref as the source of the broader shared-lock work and do not force-push the local single-commit branch over it.
* [x] **[#35654](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35654), malformed first coin key:** redesigned locally as nine single-responsibility commits: `b8c94f812c` characterizes and documents the cursor interface; `d2acc5e64d`, `96b5eac968`, and `066663cfe3` separately name cached key state, extract decoding, and make the outpoint optional; `d09a2de4e8` alone changes malformed-key semantics; `3f1cb89980`, `7067cd1fbd`, and `4640da40e1` separately centralize reset, explain prefix-first decoding, and simplify `GetKey()`; `3cd39097f4` adds logging and its assertion. * [x] **[#35714](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714) and [#35688](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35688), fail-stop and formal-UB fixes:** #35714 is open at `e1a337ee96` and returns after a block/undo flush failure before writing block-index or coins metadata or advancing `m_last_flushed_block`. It is compatible with merged [#35621](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35621): #35621 ignores the `FlushStateToDisk()` return at the `AcceptBlock()` caller boundary so a storage failure is not reported as a block-validation failure, while the internal fatal notification still requests shutdown. #35714 changes the callee's block/undo-file failure boundary so later state writes do not proceed after durable block data fails to flush. This closes success-after-failed-write paths that could leave an unpersisted master key, mismatched passphrases across memory/disk, or partially encrypted descriptor records.
* [x] **[#35754](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35754) and [#35620](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35620), CI inputs and LevelDB cache budget:** #35754 was reduced locally to the accepted SDK archive verification and uv lint dependency lock at `d452df531d`, dropping the Git-source, lint-binary, test-package, container-image, and GitHub Action pins. With up to two write buffers, the total configured DB-cache budget remains conserved.
* [x] **[#35680](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35680), competing private-broadcast accumulation fix:** open at `85d109a3ef` and directly overlaps detached `a918be2797`. It replaces retained per-attempt records with cumulative per-transaction sent/confirmed counters plus per-node state only for live connections; disconnect removes the node entry while retry priority remains in the cumulative counters. It also deliberately changes `getprivatebroadcastinfo` to expose totals and only currently connected peers. The detached fix instead preserves confirmed peer history and only aggregates disconnected unconfirmed attempts. Both fix the dynamically proven accumulation; do not promote `a918be2797` as a novel fix without an explicit alternative-design decision.

* [x] **Medium / authenticated RPC abort / fork PR [#237](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/237) open draft:** `l0rinc/psbt-zero-input-output-update` is pushed at `0fa3581395`. A valid intermediate BIP370 zero-input PSBT processed by `descriptorprocesspsbt` with a matching private descriptor reaches `SignatureHash()` with input index zero and aborts. In NDEBUG builds it reads `vin[0]` out of bounds. The availability scope is an application that submits user PSBTs to authenticated RPC with a signing descriptor. This is not a P2P or consensus path, and no particular public service is established as affected. `walletprocesspsbt` hides output secrets, so it does not reproduce the ECDSA path, while `wsh(and_v(v:pk(key),older(144)))` reaches the checker path. The ECDSA characterization uses a valid input because the zero-input invocation aborts; its fix expands the output-metadata matrix to zero and one inputs. The checker predecessor is an out-of-bounds read, reliably diagnosed only under a sanitizer, so its characterization starts with one input before the checker fix expands the same matrix. ECDSA and Schnorr signing, plus MuSig2 operations, fail at their sighash boundaries, and the checker rejects, while scripts and key origins continue to be collected. `psbt_tests`, `script_tests`, and `rpc_psbt.py` passed locally. The rewritten `script_sign` source compiled under ASan/UBSan/libFuzzer, but the local Xcode toolchain lacks `libclang_rt.fuzzer_osx.a` so the fuzz binary could not link or run. Moving the ECDSA direct creator out of its valid-input fuzz branch changes later input consumption, so the corpus needs refresh. Current upstream still lacks the guards. Do not extract a competing fix.

* [x] **Low / authenticated RPC integrity / fork PR [#238](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/238):** `l0rinc/mempool-saturate-info-fee-delta` at `e6f1949707` is source-verified. Two valid `prioritisetransaction` calls can leave `m_modified_fee == INT64_MIN`; `CTxMemPool::GetInfo()` then subtracts the positive base fee and invokes signed-overflow UB. Trap builds abort and ordinary builds can report a huge incorrect `nFeeDelta`. The `SaturatingSubtract()` checks are overflow-safe and the regression covers both boundaries plus unsigned values.
* [x] **Medium-low / unauthenticated HTTP parsing CPU DoS / upstream PR [#35735](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35735):** the new server recreates an `HTTPRequest` and reruns `LoadControlData()`, `LoadHeaders()`, and `LoadBody()` from the beginning of the receive buffer after every incomplete read. A drip-fed chunked body re-scans chunk lines and rebuilds the body each time. An isolated in-place benchmark measured 1/2/4/8 MiB bodies at 0.59/2.9/12.3/51.8 s, about 4x per doubling; the 32 MiB cap projects to roughly 13-16 CPU minutes per connection. Authentication happens after parsing and `-rpcservertimeout` resets on each received byte. Default localhost binding limits exposure. Preserve parse state and the chunk-scan offset per client rather than retrying the whole buffer.
  The exact receive-side fix is now owned by open upstream #35735 at `0ced8c35ae`, so do not duplicate it. `origin/detached608` made parser state atomic for retrying one request object, while `l0rinc/http-no-copy-large-replies` fixes the separate send-side front-erase quadratic (`3491187726`).
* [x] **Review complete / `l0rinc/verifydb-parallel-disconnect-prevouts` at `34f07419e7`:** no race or stale-flush defect found. The prefetch queue is built reverse-transaction/reverse-input, matching `DisconnectBlock()`; each real input is consumed through `HaveCoin()`, so the final flush can proceed. Intra-block spends correctly fetch empty coins. The legacy same-tx metadata lookup can consume a different output first, but its metadata is shared and the actual lookup then hits the overlay. A failed disconnect resets the queue, and a completed queue means all workers' coin reads have been awaited before flushing.

The planned upstream review is an ACK with five optional reviewer-friendliness comments; merging #35351 as-is is explicitly acceptable.
* [x] **Targeted `txgraph` mutation/removal audit, not a full state-machine review:** no ordered-container mutation or dangling-locator defect was found in the checked fee, quality, removal, and split paths on `upstream/master` `26b730cdbf`.
  `SetTransactionFee()` writes through stable position-indexed storage, marks acceptable generic clusters `NEEDS_RELINEARIZE`, and rejects main-graph mutation while chunk-index observers exist. `SetClusterQuality()` extracts the owning pointer before reinserting it under the new quality; singleton fee updates are plain member writes.
  `RemoveTransaction()` queues removals, and `ApplyRemovals()` sorts the complete batch by still-valid cluster sequence before processing. `GenericClusterImpl::ApplyRemovals()` clears locators and mappings before changing cluster quality; `DepGraph::RemoveTransactions()` preserves positions as holes and removes only unused trailing entries, so surviving mapping indexes remain valid through split/relinearization. Sequence uniqueness and upper bounds are asserted by the invariant checker. A full audit of the relinearization state machine remains a separate multi-turn candidate.

### Boundaries and current local work

* [ ] **Txindex hardening nit, not an active bug:** `BlockTxPosition` and `BlockSeqKey` encode `block_seq` in three bytes. Offset width is enforced with a static assertion, but `block_seq` only has a comment-level `2^24` bound. At `2^24` connected blocks, complemented encoding wraps and can overwrite `BlockSeqKey{0}`. This is about 318 years at the current block rate. If the txindex work reaches review, add `assert(block_seq < (1 << 24))` in `WriteTxs()` as an explicit invariant; do not present it as current user risk.
* [x] **Supersession correction / dbwrapper scratch streams:** upstream [#35156](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35156) merged the dbwrapper scratch-`DataStream` work. Do not treat `detached511` as a fresh dbwrapper optimization; only its separately scoped wallet-side follow-up remains to assess.
* [x] **Added locally to fork PR [#174](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/174):** `l0rinc/asmap-optimizations` at `0b6a083726` rebases the five ASMap optimization commits onto `upstream/master` `afa5e46bbc` and adds `net: reserve address group output` as the sixth, independent commit. It reserves the maximum `GetGroup()` result before appending and complements the PR's ASMap lookup fast paths without changing address-group bytes. The remote `detached534` ref still needs an approved force-push; do not revive the standalone `l0rinc/netgroup-reserve-groups` branch. Paste-ready PR text is in `scratch_711.txt`.

Do not extract a correctness fix from these reviews.
* [x] **Index correctness branches reviewed clean:** `origin/l0rinc/index-restart-chainstate-race` at `7730fe7f33` closes the real restart-time `m_chainstate` use-after-free by using the stable chain manager block manager and synchronizing remaining pointer access. `origin/l0rinc/index-crash-recovery-followups` at `086281064f` rewinds a persisted stale child instead of treating a null next block as synced. `origin/l0rinc/index-pre-genesis-sync` at `b1131f18f1` handles the constructible null-tip/null-best state before genesis and guards flushed locators. The pre-genesis and restart branches touch `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain()` with different null semantics; reconcile that function explicitly if both are stacked or submitted.
* [ ] **Valid concept, stale branch / `origin/l0rinc/assumevalid-reindex` at `84d2706c57`:** skipping script checks during `-reindex` or `-reindex-chainstate` reuses prior validation trust while retaining PoW, Merkle, amount, and UTXO checks; no memory-safety or consensus-acceptance defect was found against the branch's own base. Current master replaced its `bool fScriptChecks` hunk with the `script_check_reason` ladder, where a non-null reason enables checks and `nullptr` skips them. A rebase must integrate the reindex policy into that ladder and re-verify the new control flow. Preserve the explicit `-assumevalid=0` policy: it means always verify and must override the reindex optimization. Do not revive this branch with a purely mechanical rebase.
* [x] **Review complete / pruned historical block fetch proxy:** `origin/l0rinc/txindex-block-fetch-proxy` at `019b499da6` is clean. Local fetches are limited to previously processed active-chain blocks. A response must hash to the requested block, passes `IsBlockMutated()` with witness checks when SegWit is active, and then passes `ProcessNewBlock()`/`CheckBlock()` before it is stored. The selected peer must be outbound, not block-relay-only, advertise `NODE_NETWORK` and `NODE_WITNESS`, and have the requested header; a malicious peer can withhold or time out but cannot substitute fabricated history for wallet rescans, txindex reads, or transaction proofs.
  The P2P resource surface is bounded by four concurrent local block requests and a 30-second predicate wait. Duplicate guards cover both local requests and ordinary in-flight downloads; peer disconnect, shutdown interruption, `notfound`, send failure, and timeout remove the request and wake waiters.
  Persisted fetched blocks carry `BLOCK_LOCAL_ONLY`. P2P block and compact-block serving, inventory continuation, REST block/transaction reads, and ordinary txindex reads reject that marker; only explicit local callers opt in. Historical storage also suppresses `NewPoWValidBlock`, and because the block is already in the active chain it cannot create a new wallet tip event.
  Retention is bounded: pruning pins each current block file for both normal and AssumeUTXO cursors, then clears `BLOCK_LOCAL_ONLY` when that file is eventually pruned. The documented privacy cost remains that the selected peer learns the requested historical block hash.
  Packaging guidance is unchanged: this remote branch also contains the large txindex key/format stack. Split that format overhaul from the fetch-proxy feature before upstream submission even though the reviewed proxy trust chain is sound.
* [x] **Review sweep complete at the refs above:** every named l0rinc Core and secp256k1 branch in this wave now has a verdict. The only new txindex note is the existing `2^24` sequence guard nit; `assumevalid-reindex` remains a safe concept on a stale base with an explicit policy correction required. No additional proven-finding package item was added.

## 2026-07-23 fork PR audit refresh

Source: external LLM scan of all 124 fork PRs, including five deeper passes over roughly 55 active PRs. The findings below have not all been independently replayed in this checkout. Treat them as mandatory review context, then verify the current PR tip, current upstream code, and related PR state before acting.

### Higher-priority findings and risks

* [ ] **PR #237, zero-input PSBT:** authenticated `descriptorprocesspsbt` abort. A legal BIP370 zero-input PSBT reaches `UpdatePSBTOutput()`, which otherwise attempts to sign input index zero. The demonstrated availability risk is an application processing a user PSBT with a signing descriptor, not P2P or consensus. `walletprocesspsbt` hides output secrets, so it is not the ECDSA reproducer. Upstream commit `7e19ce200b` fixes a different bug. The branch includes focused functional `descriptorprocesspsbt` coverage.
* [ ] **PR #225, dirty undo-file flush:** fixes still-open [Core #25539](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/25539). A crash after `WriteBlockIndexDB()` can persist `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` before the corresponding undo file is synced. Restart then fails `VerifyDB` and requires reindexing. This is a small, well-tested crash-recovery fix.
* [ ] **PR #236, empty-headers sync-slot release:** remote unauthenticated IBD liveness issue. On an inbound-only node, one peer can send an empty headers response and retain the sync slot indefinitely because the timeout path requires at least one preferred download peer. Keep this focused fix high priority.
* [ ] **PR #190, `pruneassumevalid`:** split out the hasher change before considering the feature. Replacing `SaltedTxidHasher` and `SaltedWtxidHasher` for attacker-influenced mempool keys with SipHash-1-3-jumbo weakens DoS resistance and conflicts with the earlier coins-cache performance result.
* [ ] **PR #178, AssumeUTXO hash verification during IBD:** every from-genesis chainstate is `Assumeutxo::VALIDATED`, so the current proposal performs a multi-minute full UTXO hash and forced flush under `cs_main` at height 840000 for an advisory check. Gate it behind a debug option or do not merge it in this form.
* [x] **PR #218, pruned block-index bookkeeping:** the older audit warning is superseded. The open draft now points to `l0rinc/validation-pruned-unlinked-blocks` at `a06f160417`, with `d0b438e8ee` owning the redownloaded-candidate ordering fix and the second commit owning the pruned-unlinked liveness fix. See the current verified entry above; do not treat detached `33e185fd64` as unpromoted work.
* [ ] **PRs #223, #224, and #232, index consistency:** treat these as one related silent-wrong-data family while keeping their commits separate. The reported failures include disconnected chainstate being reported as synced across restart, `gettxspendingprevout` returning a spend from an inactive block after a crash during reorg, and an `m_chainstate` lifetime race after snapshot completion.
* [x] **PR #245, concurrent headers REDOWNLOAD cap / local stack split:** the published tracking ref is `4fcd95dfd3`, while the local eight-commit stack is at `285e825565`, based on `upstream/master` `1be0b46297`. It admits every low-memory PRESYNC state and gates only entry into REDOWNLOAD, where each peer can grow a 15,218-entry compressed-header buffer. The same public sufficient-work chain can be replayed to every peer during IBD, so reaching this phase does not require attacker-mined proof of work.
  Current local stack: `f585cf3da8 refactor: extract low-work headers test helper`, `fcaa4f3550 optimization: build low-work test headers locally`, `0da5e60a56 test: measure concurrent redownload buffers`, `141c89f268 test: characterize IBD headers redownloads`, `dcc0fa53db test: cover post-IBD headers redownloads`, `489bdec294 refactor: extract helper to clear sync state`, `a6f8b8bbb3 net: limit inbound headers redownloads`, and `285e825565 net: limit non-full-outbound redownloads`. The stack progresses from fixture reuse and runtime measurement to old-behavior coverage, unchanged post-IBD scope, shared cleanup, inbound admission, and the final non-full-outbound policy. The IBD characterization adds continuation parameters with their first callers and covers continuation and slot reuse before both fixes. The inbound-only commit changes the intermediate assertion values but preserves TODOs that explain the unresolved behavior. The final policy commit removes those TODOs when block-relay-only peers are also limited. Replacement admission uses aggregate counts before and after the attempt, avoiding `getpeerinfo()` ordering. The refusal `LogDebug` call remains on one line without a trailing `\n`, and exempt full-relay redownloads still count toward the threshold. Preserve `backup/limit-headers-redownload-before-message-proofread-20260807`, `backup/limit-headers-redownload-before-peer-order-fix-20260807`, `backup/limit-headers-redownload-before-final-simplify-20260807`, and the earlier PR245 backups. No remote write was made by Codex. Current evidence supports public low-to-moderate P2P DoS hardening and a concise security-list notification, without an embargo or urgent takedown. Use `scratch_753.txt` for the current PR prose.
* [ ] **PRs #204 and #109, HTTP response handling:** stack #204 first. #204 covers HEAD replies carrying a body, keep-alive stream desynchronization, and ignored handler-set `Connection: close`. #109 addresses repeated front erasure during partial sends, which can move roughly 160 GB for a 100 MiB batch reply.

## 2026-07-23 merged-commit review

`df44afdc9`, `eae193e75`, `d23641564`, `af0da2fce` plus `d53852be3`, `6244212a5`, and `e0463b4e8` were checked against `upstream/master` at `290cb2f17e`. The report named seven commits but contains six distinct issues.

### Triage and duplicate check

* [x] **Medium / authenticated RPC availability / fork PR [#247](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/247) open draft:** [#34749](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34749)'s `d23641564` erases resolved items from `prevouts_to_process` while holding `mempool.cs` in `gettxspendingprevout`. A large `mempool_only=true` request makes each erase move the remaining vector tail, giving quadratic work under the mempool lock. [Core #33904](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33904) adds a REST interface and does not change this loop. The local replacement contains `2834cded3e`, `aaacd68b10`, `29fcd36384`, and `401430f05a`: they characterize mixed-result order, replace request pointers with input indexes, store and assemble response slots in request order, then remove the quadratic erase pattern. The older `origin/l0rinc/performance-inefficient-vector-operation` only reserves fuzzer vectors and is unrelated.
* [x] **Medium / local Tor endpoint availability / fork PR [#253](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/253) open draft:** `eae193e75` retries immediately after a successful Tor-control connection drops. `ThreadControl()` only sleeps after `Connect()` fails, while `disconnected_cb()` disconnects and returns to the loop. A local process that accepts then closes the configured `-torcontrol` socket can consume a core. `l0rinc/torcontrol-backoff-after-disconnect` and its matching origin ref now point to `bc0ebcc9b8`. Open Core #34486 touches retry state for `networkactive` but leaves this established-session reconnect path immediate.
* [x] **Medium / configuration correctness / fork PR [#256](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/256) open draft:** `6244212a5` used `GetBoolArg("-asmap", false)` to distinguish embedded data from an external file. A relative filename beginning with a nonzero digit parses as true and silently selects embedded data. [#33770](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33770) requires an explicit filename for bare `-asmap`, but leaves this path unchanged. `l0rinc/asmap-file-argument` now contains the two-commit characterization and fix stack at `4063d8d582`; `origin/l0rinc/asmap-file-argument` exists at the same head.
* [x] **Low / Kernel C API robustness / fork branch:** `df44afdc9` returns a null C handle for an out-of-range ancestor in release builds after asserting in Debug, while the C++ wrapper constructs a non-null `BlockTreeEntry` wrapper. `origin/l0rinc/kernel-ancestor-null` already contains `6552e3bc05` `kernel: return null for out-of-range ancestors`, with C API and wrapper tests. It is not in Core and no Core fix PR was found. Keep it with the Kernel API follow-ups rather than reimplementing it.
* [ ] **Low / latent crypto ownership:** `af0da2fce` and `d53852be3` gave the AES-256 classes owning raw context and IV pointers while retaining implicit copy operations. There are no current copies, so this is a future misuse hardening issue rather than a reachable crash. Delete copy construction and assignment in a focused crypto commit when working in this area.
* [ ] **Low / RPC and REST error handling:** `e0463b4e8` calls `CHECK_NONFATAL(witness_stack.size() == 1)` when serializing `coinbase_tx`. Stored blocks that failed witness-malleation checks can still have `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA`, so `getblock` and REST can report an internal error for an invalid block they are otherwise able to return. No matching Core PR or fork branch was found.

### Confirmed current-master follow-ups

* [ ] **Medium / local wallet cache consistency:** `f89418c71c` `descriptor: keep cache conflict merges atomic` remains needed. `DescriptorCache::MergeAndDiff()` inserts parent xpubs before it checks later derived or last-hardened conflicts. An exception can leave the in-memory cache ahead of the database until restart. The trigger needs a conflicting descriptor cache. No network, unauthenticated RPC, wallet-key loss, or persisted database corruption was shown. The old full patch needs a test rebase, but the production loop remains unchanged on `7b6f9ba7ba`.
* [ ] **Medium / local snapshot integrity:** `03206fa7de` `validation: reject duplicate snapshot coin records` is a distinct AssumeUTXO candidate. A duplicate serialized coin record increments snapshot metadata while cache insertion ignores the duplicate outpoint, so a malformed `loadtxoutset` file can retain the same UTXO hash with a false coin count. This is a local snapshot-import boundary, not a P2P or consensus bypass. Reproduce on current master before proposing because the original test and functional contexts need rebasing.
* [ ] **Medium / authenticated RPC policy robustness:** `6c6c1135b7` `validation: saturate modified fee aggregates` extends the fee-overflow family. Two conflicts with extreme local `prioritisetransaction` deltas can overflow `m_conflicting_fees` before RBF policy checks. The commit records a functional two-conflict reproducer. It needs an independent current-master replay and should remain separate from the existing RBF PRs unless their scope is consciously widened.
* [ ] **Medium / local MiniMiner arithmetic:** `00c94a8e87` `node: saturate MiniMiner modified fee arithmetic` reports signed overflow in aggregate, subtraction, and negation paths after extreme local prioritisation. It is related to the broader fee-saturation work but is not a reason to add unrelated changes to #217 or #238. Reproduce after the RBF aggregate candidate because its original fuzz replay was blocked by a separate cluster assertion.
* [ ] **Low / private RPC correctness:** `cc29103982` `fuzz: harden PSBT finalization and merge oracles` found that generic raw `finalizepsbt` can report complete and extract a transaction with a nonempty invalid `final_scriptSig`. `walletprocesspsbt` rechecks through `CWallet::FillPSBT`, so this is not a fund-loss, consensus, memory-safety, or cryptographic failure. The production patch applies cleanly to current master. No focused fork PR is known locally.
* [ ] **Low to medium / local IPC interface integrity:** `0053886bf8` `ipc: reject malformed UniValue JSON messages` applies cleanly. The current IPC fuzzer returns before malformed JSON reaches `CustomReadField(TypeList<UniValue>)`, where `UniValue::read()` currently clears the destination and its false result is ignored. A raw IPC client can therefore deliver null UniValue instead of receiving an error. This is not P2P reachable. The zero-input transaction guard in the same fuzzer is only an untested serialization domain. An empty transaction still serializes to nonempty `Data`, so no bug is proved there.
* [ ] **Low / local wallet API availability:** `dfe7f9348f` `wallet: handle unconfirmed coins without coin control` applies cleanly. `AvailableCoins()` documents a nullable `CCoinControl`, but the unconfirmed TRUC filter dereferences it when a wallet owns an in-mempool transaction. The local deterministic test crashed at `wallet/spend.cpp:398`. Current RPC callers construct a coin-control object, while benchmarks and wallet tests call the nullable API. Keep it as a compact wallet follow-up.
* [ ] **Low / local configuration:** `af47c65fd3` `node: avoid cache allocation percentage overflow` applies cleanly. On 64-bit builds, `-dbcache=8796093022208` makes `total_cache * 10 / 100` wrap before the one-GiB txindex cap. It is local configuration only and does not affect consensus or persisted chain data.
* [ ] **Low / parser output contract:** `c548c0dd3f` `base58: clear decoded output on failure` still has the old production behavior. Failed `DecodeBase58()` leaves caller-owned bytes intact. Current callers were not shown to use stale bytes as successful output. The production hunk needs a small rebase because nearby Base58 tests changed.
* [ ] **Low / API output contract:** `ac4fd62fdb` `versionbits: clear null statistics signals` leaves a caller-provided signalling vector unchanged when `GetStateStatisticsFor(nullptr, &signals)` returns zero statistics. No current production caller was found that consumes this stale vector.
* [ ] **Low / API output contract:** `07c3e13a5e` `fix: reset partial merkle match indices` applies cleanly. `ExtractMatches()` clears matching txids but not caller-provided indices. Current proof RPC callers allocate fresh vectors, so this is not a peer or consensus issue.
* [ ] **Low / direct mining API and IPC correctness:** `bd59cacde5` `mining: clear submitSolution failure outputs` is newly relevant after current-master [#34672](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34672). `submitSolution()` returns false for null coinbase without clearing caller-provided `reason` and `debug`, unlike the shared submission path. This is a stale-output bug for direct API or IPC users.
* [x] **Superseded source SHA / peer accounting:** `7adaea68ff` is an older form of the current detached-only `00fead6cdf` last-transaction-time fix. Use the verified ready-to-package entry above.
* [ ] **Low / block-processing bookkeeping:** `c6813954b0` corrects `fNewBlock` bookkeeping when block storage fails. The flag is currently set before persistence succeeds and can refresh peer/request state after a failed disk write. This is local disk-failure behavior, not a P2P disk-write primitive.
* [ ] **Low / BanMan map integrity:** `8d25b2f000` orders valid and invalid `CSubNet` values distinctly. Without it, invalid `Unban()` can compare equal to the valid IPv6 wildcard key and erase that ban. Normal Core callers do not supply invalid subnets.
* [x] **Superseded source SHA / feature-gated resource retention:** `464fa94c0f` is an older form of detached `a918be2797` private-broadcast cleanup. Use upstream #35680 as the primary owner and keep the detached form only as an alternative design reference.

### Current fuzzer restrictions that need follow-up work

These entries identify a currently excluded valid or adversarial domain. Only entries above with a clean-master reproducer are bugs. The rest need an oracle first.

* [ ] `src/ipc/test/fuzz/ipc.cpp`: malformed UniValue JSON is skipped before raw decoding. Remove the typed-proxy restriction with the raw request oracle from `0053886bf8` and fix the decoder first.
* [ ] `src/test/fuzz/fee_rate.cpp`: `GetFee()` is skipped when `bytes * satoshis_per_k` overflows. The related confirmed arithmetic issue is `CFeeRate::operator*` in `64ea102ca4`, not a proven current `GetFee()` bug. Extend only with checked or saturating expected values.
* [ ] `src/test/fuzz/poolresource.cpp`: allocation sizes are forced to be a multiple of the requested alignment. `7820b6e5f7` removes that invalid restriction. This is valid-domain coverage, not a production failure.
* [ ] `wallet/test/fuzz/coinselection.cpp`: the brute-force target caps pools at 16 groups and misses the 100,000-attempt boundary. `dd07d8bda3` adds an independent BnB target. Current master already has the deterministic exhaustion test, so this is coverage only.
* [ ] `src/test/fuzz/txgraph.cpp`: alternate fees were capped near `+/-2^47`. `0d2b4aaacf` widens them to full `int64_t`. The first three resulting failures were non-representable arithmetic oracles, not production defects. Keep the wider domain with checked predicates. The later full-range mutation `2de843c875` also exposed the separately confirmed equal-feerate-prefix production overflow prepared above; do not retain the blanket claim that all full-range TxGraph results are oracle-only.
* [ ] Transport fuzzers generate message types no longer than `CMessageHeader::MESSAGE_TYPE_SIZE`. #235 adds deterministic rejection coverage for the direct transport boundary. Add a dedicated fuzzer branch only after modelling rejected messages correctly.
* [ ] Mempool and package fuzzers still constrain priority deltas to `[-50 * COIN, +50 * COIN]` in several paths. This can hide authenticated-RPC overflow families. Audit remaining aggregate and MiniMiner consumers after the already-pushed fee fixes, then widen with representability-aware oracles.
* [ ] Snapshot fuzzers need explicit zero-height, zero-coin, duplicate-record, and malformed metadata cases. The duplicate-record candidate above is the strongest known gap.
* [ ] Script, Miniscript, policy-estimator, transaction, and process-message fuzzers retain size, SigVersion, command, and protocol-constant bounds for cost control. Keep a separate inventory below and only relax a bound with an independent expected-state model.

## 2026-07-21 latest fork refresh and block-tree recovery

Current `origin/master` and `upstream/master` are `32eb521002`. Fork PRs [#237](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/237), [#238](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/238), [#239](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/239), [#241](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/241), [#242](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/242), and [#243](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/243) remain open, so do not extract their PSBT, fee-delta, BDB, coinstats, block-tree, or Kernel import-path fixes again.

* [x] **Low / Kernel C API availability / fork PR [#243](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/243):** `l0rinc/kernel-null-path-lengths` at `d9c2a9724b` makes the documented nullable `block_file_paths_lens` argument of `btck_chainstate_manager_import_blocks()` mean NUL-terminated paths. The function previously dereferenced a null length array and crashed a contract-abiding C or FFI caller.
  The raw C API regression creates an empty block file and imports it with `paths={path}`, `lens=nullptr`, and `len=1`. Removing the fallback makes the focused Debug test exit `139`. The fixed focused test and all 20 `test_kernel` cases pass in a Debug `BUILD_KERNEL_LIB=ON` build. No `bitcoind`, P2P, RPC, consensus, or wallet trigger exists, and no matching open Core or fork PR was found.

* [ ] **Medium / Windows filesystem recoverability / prepared locally:** `l0rinc/windows-file-error-handling` contains `73e660495f fs: avoid truncating Windows files after failed seek` and `70744a83a3 fs: restore exclusive file creation on Windows`. `AllocateFileRange()` currently calls `SetEndOfFile()` after a failed `SetFilePointerEx()`, which can truncate a `blk` or `rev` file at its stale file position. The second commit restores exclusive `wbx` creation on the current MSVCRT-based Windows build, removing the temporary fallback that can overwrite an existing `xor.dat` or writable-directory probe file. Both fixes originate in Knots and have no Knots PR or Core PR overlap. The full `streams_tests` suite passes locally. This checkout has no MinGW compiler, so Windows CI must compile and exercise the changed path.

* [x] **Medium / local block-tree corruption availability / fork PR [#242](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/242):** `l0rinc/blocktree-corruption-recovery` at `8b5d1b1856` contains two focused commits from `origin/detached609`. A negative `DB_LAST_BLOCK` value indexed an empty block-file vector, and valid headers with corrupted on-disk heights later aborted in `GetAncestor()`. Both conditions now return `false` from block-index loading so startup offers reindexing instead of crashing.
  The fixes are reachable only after local block-tree database corruption. Public headers suffice for the height fixture, but no P2P or unauthenticated RPC path writes the index. The production guards apply cleanly to current master and have no upstream PR overlap.
  In a disposable Debug+ASan build with the guards removed, `blockmanager_negative_last_block_file_rejected` segfaulted in `CBlockFileInfo::ToString()` and `blockmanager_permuted_disk_heights_rejected` aborted in `GetAncestor()`. Restoring the guards passed both tests. The fixed Debug build also passed the full `blockmanager_tests` suite.

## 2026-07-21 audit/resurrection and fork PR refresh

Source: `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/resurrection` at `09b3c99caf` (`doc: record audit state through 2026-07-21`). Its tree is clean apart from environment-only `node_modules`, `package*.json`, and `txindex-size.log`. Those files are not audit content.

The branch contains 30 commits: 12 fixes from this audit campaign, comprising 7 production fixes, 3 fuzz-harness fixes, a Kernel series, and its documentation, on top of the earlier audit work and 569-commit fuzz/oracle stack. Every production fix has a failing-before and passing-after proof in Debug+ASan and Release and applies to master through a temporary-index check. At the audit snapshot none had an upstream PR. The wallet write-failure series, the null-mempool Kernel fix, and CI input verification are now published as #35752, #35753, and #35754.

The audit branch remains the only complete copy of this work. The fork's `detached603` and `detached609` branches retain partial snapshots, while individual fixes are now published upstream. Publish or otherwise back up the audited series before relying on a single local branch.

### Audit risk map

- [x] **Funds at risk, wallet, published as [#35752](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35752):** `b8fcf9ed17` and `3be812ef57` prevent encryption from reporting success after a failed database write leaves the wallet permanently locked. `501bd2e263` prevents a passphrase change from leaving memory and disk with different passphrases.
- [ ] **Local wallet key-material hygiene:** `b16c831eae` warns when a rewrite leaves plaintext in database slack space.
- [ ] **Availability:** `71cf0ba593` bounds cyclic empty overflow chains in hostile legacy `wallet.dat` files, which otherwise hang `migratewallet` and `bitcoin-wallet`. `53506a51e9` prevents a zero-input PSBT from reaching `SignatureHash` through `descriptorprocesspsbt`.
- [x] **Availability, fork PR [#242](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/242):** `e83b385117` and `6c6d91ce99` reject corrupt block-tree indexes that otherwise crash during startup. The invalid indexes can be constructed from public headers.
- [x] **Kernel availability, published as [#35753](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35753):** `0a2deeea1d` prevents a null-mempool crash for Kernel users.
- [ ] **FFI robustness:** `a2b3434296`, `fdac04de17`, and `02a04893fa` replace assertion-only validation at the C ABI.
- [ ] **Fuzz-harness integrity:** `d07297d903` and `4c106d58c9` close the blind spots that allowed real defects to survive.

### Fork PR priority

1. [x] **Published as [bitcoin/bitcoin#35752](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35752), wallet encryption write failures.** The closed fork [#234](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/234) supplied its four-commit characterization-first series for `b8fcf9ed17`, `501bd2e263`, and `3be812ef57`. Follow the upstream review instead of reviving the fork PR. Keep `b16c831eae` separate because warning about post-encryption rewrite failure is a lower-priority privacy and recovery improvement.
2. [ ] **Review [#237](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/237) after CI, zero-input PSBT output updates.** Its creator-boundary guards preserve output keypath updates while preventing the zero-input `SignatureHash` out-of-bounds path. It is the refined version of the audit's `53506a51e9` fix.
3. [ ] **Review [#239](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/239) after CI, cyclic legacy BDB overflow chains.** The fix is narrow, proven, and fills the empty-cycle gap left after [#34959](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34959). It should remain separate from broader legacy-wallet recovery changes.
4. [ ] **Review [#238](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/238) after CI, saturating mempool information fee delta.** This is a small, independent authenticated-RPC signed-overflow fix. Keep it distinct from the broader policy questions in [#217](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/217) and [#228](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/228).

8. [ ] **Watch [#236](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/236), empty headers sync-slot release.** It is already drafted and awaiting CI. Do not mix it with the audit series.

### Existing crash-recovery PRs

Keep these as separate review lanes after the immediate wallet, PSBT, BDB, and block-tree work:

1. [ ] **Amend [#225](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/225), flush every dirty undo file.** A reorg can append undo data to an older `rev` file after the block cursor has advanced. Flush all dirty undo files before recording `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`.
2. [ ] **Amend [#224](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/224), txospender reorg recovery.** An interrupted reorg can make the index return a stale spend from an inactive block. The fix keeps records append-only and filters lookup results by active-chain membership.
3. [ ] **Amend [#227](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/227), blockfilter crash recovery.** A crash during a reorg can leave block-filter and CoinStats entries ahead of a durable index locator. The fix recovers matching hash entries instead of rejecting the index or reading the wrong record type.
4. [ ] **Amend [#218](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/218), pruned-block bookkeeping.** It fixes two stale block-index containers after redownload or a parent arriving after its pruned child.
5. [ ] **Amend [#223](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/223), index restart rewind.** It corrects an index locator that remains at a disconnected tip and is incorrectly marked synced after restart.

Current fork PRs [#236](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/236), [#237](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/237), [#238](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/238), and [#239](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/239) have queued CI, not completed CI. ## 2026-07-20 PSBT and latest-branch refresh

Current bases after the latest pull: `origin/master` = `18c05d93016b28a9afd4c716dfe00b6e0accb30b`; `upstream/master` = `006f8f7d49a39bc1e3a302269c8ad244f05a209b` (merge of #35090).

Fork PRs were refreshed through #237. Upstream title/body searches found no zero-input `UpdatePSBTOutput` overlap; #33014 also touches `descriptorprocesspsbt`, but only fixes completeness checks for invalid input signatures.

* [x] **Medium / local malformed-wallet availability / prepared locally:** source `71cf0ba593 wallet: bound overflow page chains in the legacy BDB parser` from `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/resurrection`; focused branch `l0rinc/wallet-bound-bdb-overflow-chains` at `29cc2eed07 wallet: bound BDB overflow page chains`.
  The read-only parser follows overflow records until their data reaches the stated size. An empty overflow page can point back to itself without growing the data, so an attacker-supplied legacy wallet makes `migratewallet` or `bitcoin-wallet` hang indefinitely.
  Current master has the same loop. #34959 bounds data-growing chains, while #35150 was closed in its favor without covering empty cycles.
  The focused fix rejects a chain after it visits more nonzero pages than the database holds and adds the rejection to the existing BDB fuzzer error policy. Removing the guard makes the focused test time out after 20 seconds with exit 124. This needs a user to inspect a malformed local wallet file. No P2P, consensus, or wallet-funds impact is known.

* [x] **Medium / authenticated RPC crash / fork PR #237:** historical source `53506a51e98dc7f668f796b0479a8b2c9b0869a8` from `origin/detached609` and `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/resurrection`.
  Superseded implementation detail: the current focused branch is `l0rinc/psbt-zero-input-output-update` at `e95a5ac0b8`, which adds input-index soft failures and a rejecting checker instead of the older `DUMMY_SIGNATURE_CREATOR` approach. See the 2026-07-23 proof refresh above for the current dynamic reproducer, `descriptorprocesspsbt` reachability, and patch behavior.

* [x] **Medium / authenticated RPC signed-overflow / prepared locally:** source `2f416d9e96f91c11cddb0d6b12d0a063eef02254 mempool: saturate TxMempoolInfo fee delta` from `umbrel/fuzz-contract-cluster-oracles-20260709`; focused branch `l0rinc/mempool-saturate-info-fee-delta` at `e6f1949707 mempool: saturate transaction info fee delta`.
  `prioritisetransaction` can saturate an in-mempool transaction's modified fee at `INT64_MIN`. `CTxMemPool::GetInfo()` then subtracts the positive base fee to derive `nFeeDelta`, which is signed-overflow UB in the persistence and relay paths that construct transaction info.
  The state requires authenticated RPC access. A peer cannot create it, but can later request relay work that reads the affected information.
  The focused patch adds `SaturatingSubtract()`, uses it for `nFeeDelta`, and extends the existing overflow matrix. In the local Debug `-ftrapv` build, restoring the raw subtraction makes `MempoolInfoSaturatesFeeDelta` exit 133, while the fixed full `mempool_tests` and `util_tests` suites pass. No open upstream or fork PR matches this readout path. It is separate from the broader, blocked priority-fee design in fork PR #228.

* [ ] **Low-medium / local wallet key-material hygiene / follow-up:** `b16c831eae09494a33bd5ff09a23f82b1b97f452 wallet: warn when the post-encryption database rewrite fails` from `origin/detached603`.
  `EncryptWallet()` ignores a failed post-encryption database rewrite. Encryption still succeeds, but a local SQLite rewrite failure such as ENOSPC can leave recoverable plaintext key bytes in unused wallet pages without warning the user.
  This needs a local database failure and is not third-party triggerable. Keep it behind the PSBT crash and simplify its existing 40-line test setup before extraction.

* [x] **Fork PR #236 / upstream PR #35839 / P2P IBD availability:** public upstream head `ea55ab8c1c0e0b007202a76e2660218810dc43ca`; local `l0rinc/p2p-empty-headers-sync` is rewritten at `6d10e8e193`. The seven-commit stack folds the block-announcement retry into the main empty-headers fix so every production commit remains usable; `p2p_segwit.py` and `p2p_initial_headers_sync.py` pass at that exact commit. The outbound old-chain characterization/fix pair remains separate on top, and the final tip also passes `p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py`.

* [x] **Latest i9 tail is oracle-only:** `848eb7` through `8ec4b3` add fuzz contracts or mutation proofs and explicitly report no clean-master production defect.
* [x] **Latest Umbrel tail review:** `2f416d9e96` is the sole new clean-master production candidate and is recorded above. The remaining tail is contract or oracle coverage.

## 2026-07-20 headers-sync refresh

Current bases: `origin/master` and `upstream/master` = `18c05d93016b28a9afd4c716dfe00b6e0accb30b`.
Refs checked after the latest pull include `origin`, `upstream`, `umbrel` at `727f51942ab4`, and `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles-current` at `b91114946f4a`.
Fork PRs were refreshed through #235. No open upstream PR matches the empty-HEADERS initial-sync handoff. Fork PR #186 is a separate headers-presync clock-boundary fix.

* [x] **Medium / P2P IBD availability / fork PR #236 / upstream PR #35839:** source `6da365ba9a0c99fcf94664bf89fdf5d059e120bd p2p: avoid initial headers sync stalls`, retained in the batched `origin/detached552` history and independently revalidated by `87638fd93d129591d8e3441c98a4abfdcc3c55ec` from `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles-current`. Focused branch `l0rinc/p2p-empty-headers-sync` is locally at `6d10e8e193`; upstream PR #35839 remains at `ea55ab8c1c0e0b007202a76e2660218810dc43ca` until the user updates it.
  During IBD, the sole peer selected for initial headers sync can reply to `getheaders` with a valid empty `headers` message. Master clears the peer's low-work headers state but leaves `fSyncStarted`, `nSyncStarted`, and the long headers timeout set. No replacement peer is selected, and with only inbound peers the timeout path cannot release the slot.
  The input is peer-controlled and protocol-valid. The effect is an IBD availability stall, with no consensus, block-index, memory-safety, or wallet impact. The focused patch releases the sync slot, clears its timeout, and preserves the request timestamp so the same peer is not selected immediately again.
  The local seven-commit stack is rebased on `upstream/master` at `67efced1fc83a0b7215cc1513e7c4754fee0f12f`: `fc25b1be02 test: characterize empty headers sync stall`, `9c76ffe82f test: isolate block announcement setup`, `297c0f7ca7 refactor: name stale header check`, `7de4fba5b8 refactor: extract initial headers cleanup`, `79aca0b97f p2p: select another peer after empty headers`, `92a98ffb30 test: characterize outbound old-chain disconnect`, and `6d10e8e193 p2p: continue pending old-chain disconnect`. The main fix now includes the released-peer retry state, avoiding the broken intermediate tree reported in upstream review. Each production fix changes only established TODO expectations in the test file. The manual reproducer uses the checked-out `bitcoind`, with Python only as the two inbound peers. Final validation passed `p2p_segwit.py` and `p2p_initial_headers_sync.py` at the exact main behavior commit, then passed `p2p_initial_headers_sync.py` and `p2p_headers_sync_with_minchainwork.py` at the final tip.
  The larger i9 commit adds an oracle and an additional three-node functional test. Keep those as fuzz evidence unless review shows they are needed for the focused PR.

* [x] **Medium / feature-gated local broadcast resource retention / upstream owner found:** `2032a4f520839c3d8db5dc91a45bb9911b6902f5 net: prune failed private broadcast send records`, revalidated as `a918be2797a90cc79f65458326f9866211935535` from current i9.
  With `-privatebroadcast`, each failed private-broadcast connection can retain an unconfirmed peer record for a locally submitted transaction. Repeated failures grow the queued metadata, priority scans, and `getprivatebroadcastinfo` response work until the transaction is removed. The 114-line detached fix has deterministic unit proof, but upstream #35680 now owns the mechanism with a different RPC-state design. Do not package the detached form as novel work.

* [x] **Oracle-only refresh:** `b91114946f fuzz: assert failed UTXO snapshot activation rollback` adds no production change and found no clean-master defect. `36f57f67df`, `2312ec3081`, and `727f51942a` add compact-block collision coverage only; they do not supersede the existing compact-block tracker entries.

* [x] **Low / transport API memory safety / fork PR #235:** `l0rinc/net-reject-oversized-message-types` at `0df817b0263a5f67453711d72508b4139657b94d`.

### Newly selected queue

* [x] **Low / transport API memory safety / fork PR #235:** source `948ac5982abaf57c6369a24a4dc50da144efaf75 net: reject oversized transport message types` from `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles-current`; focused two-commit branch `l0rinc/net-reject-oversized-message-types` at `0df817b0263a5f67453711d72508b4139657b94d`.
  Both V1 and V2 transports accept a caller-supplied `CSerializedNetMsg::m_type` longer than the fixed 12-byte wire field. V1 aborts when `CMessageHeader` checks the type length, while V2 copies the complete string into a vector sized for 12 bytes, producing an ASan-confirmed heap-buffer-overflow.
  Current Core outbound types are fixed `NetMsgType` values and `sendmsgtopeer` rejects names longer than 12 bytes, so no peer, RPC, or consensus trigger was found. Treat this as production component-contract hardening, not a remotely exploitable overflow.
  The focused stack first records accepted 12-byte names, then adds guards to both transports and `CConnman`, and finally checks rejected non-empty messages in V1 and V2 unit tests. `net_tests` passes. This is open draft fork PR #235, so detached source `948ac5982a` is promoted work rather than a stranded fix.

* [ ] **Low / remotely reachable peer accounting / small-medium:** `00fead6cdf0db9556644601cfa570f7cfa930936 net: refresh peer transaction activity after every accepted path` from the same i9 branch.
  Master updates `m_last_tx_time` only for direct TX acceptance even though `ProcessValidTx()` also handles accepted orphans and package results. A peer can submit a child before its parent and leave `getpeerinfo.last_transaction` stale when the child is later accepted; under inbound pressure this can also remove the peer's newest-transaction eviction protection.
  The production change is small and its deterministic orphan test is larger. The earlier instruction to keep it behind the transport guard is superseded by the live re-verification and duplicate check above; it is now ready to package.

* [ ] **Low / BanMan API map integrity / small:** `a6e9b80aaf374bb6e1c30e81a085ec97599f80b3 fuzz: model banman transitions and fix invalid subnet ordering`.
  Invalid `CSubNet{}` and valid `::/0` compare equivalent under `operator<` even though `operator==` distinguishes them. Passing an invalid subnet to `BanMan::Unban()` can therefore erase a valid IPv6 wildcard ban.
  RPC and GUI callers validate or reuse valid subnets, and invalid persisted entries are dropped, so no peer or normal operator trigger was found. Extract the one-line comparator fix and focused ordering test from the broad fuzz commit if selected.

* [ ] **Low / direct compact-block API hardening / small:** `39b4e9a1b3a10f4a0a6ef892061a7d7ec15667fd cmpctblock: reject direct short-ID index overflow` from the new Umbrel tail.
  A direct `PartiallyDownloadedBlock::InitData()` caller can provide 65,537 short IDs plus coinbase and wrap a narrowed position to zero. P2P deserialization already rejects transaction counts above `uint16_t::max`, so this is not remotely reachable through compact blocks.
  The source commit combines the production guard and unit test with a larger fuzz mutation and its own harness repair; simplify before extraction.

* [x] **Contract coverage only:** `e5ab21eff977f13dcc023652c7c5822280141f69 mempool: cover relay sequence boundary contract` adds an `Assume`, unit assertions, and fuzz assertions for existing strict-less-than behavior. It demonstrates a mutation gap, not a clean-master production defect.
* [x] **Compact-block fuzz-source tail:** `dbbca9d552`, `9534fa1530`, `6fc934d19e`, and `eb16c3b593` extend collision coverage around the compact-block accounting work already represented by fork PR #229 and upstream PR #35727. They are oracle material, not separate fixes.
* [x] **Chainstate lifecycle fuzzer follows handled fix:** `fb6810ac8c fuzz: add chainstate_lifecycle target covering add/delete with null mempool` exercises the issue already split as fork PR #233.

## 2026-07-19 wallet durability and kernel API refresh

Current bases: `origin/master` and `upstream/master` = `18c05d93016b28a9afd4c716dfe00b6e0accb30b`.

* [x] **Medium / local wallet durability / published as [bitcoin/bitcoin#35752](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35752):** `l0rinc/wallet-encryption-write-failures` at `b388cb6b7a`.
  Commits: `94bd6442a0 test: characterize wallet encryption write failures`; `d2263cbe76 wallet: abort encryption after master key write failure`; `0897a8c29b wallet: reject failed passphrase changes`; `b388cb6b7a wallet: abort failed descriptor key encryption`.
  A record-local SQLite write failure during fresh encryption could commit encrypted descriptor keys without the master key, reported as success and permanently locking the wallet after reload.
  A failed descriptor crypted-key write could similarly commit mixed plaintext and crypted records, making the wallet refuse to load.
  The first fix also clears the newly added in-memory master key, so a failed write does not make a still-unencrypted wallet appear encrypted and prevent retrying.
  The characterization commit passes on master and models all three current outcomes; each following commit flips only its relevant assertion.
  `wallet_tests` (17 cases) and `wallet_crypto_tests` (3 cases) pass in the local Debug+TSan build.
  This needs a rare local SQLite I/O failure and has no P2P, consensus, or attacker-controlled trigger.

* [x] **Low-medium / Kernel API availability / published as [bitcoin/bitcoin#35753](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35753):** `l0rinc/delete-chainstate-null-mempool` at `a99b27f192`.
  `ChainstateManager::DeleteChainstate()` dereferences `prev_chainstate->m_mempool` even though Kernel users can construct a manager without one.
  Deleting an AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstate on the reindex/wipe path then crashes deterministically.
  Normal `bitcoind` always supplies a mempool, so this is limited to kernel API consumers.
  Reverting the guard makes `validation_chainstatemanager_tests/chainstatemanager_delete_chainstate_no_mempool` dereference null in `CTxMemPool::size()`; the full 12-case chainstate-manager suite passes with the fix.

### Deep-audit severity corrections

This addendum rechecked the cited source commits against `upstream/master` at `18c05d93016b`. It distinguishes release-build UB from Debug/fuzz-only `Assume()` failures. Reported Debug P2P runs were not rerun in this refresh.

* [ ] **Medium / authenticated-RPC UB / existing split work:** the modified-fee RBF family is more than Debug-only hardening. `236da1b3d5 rbf: avoid overflow in replacement fee delta` and `a5a8001c32 validation: saturate modified fee aggregates` fix signed `CAmount` arithmetic that is undefined in release builds as well as fatal under sanitizers. The trigger requires local `prioritisetransaction` state, so it is neither P2P nor consensus reachable. These are the substantive core of the previously published fork PR #217, not new independent work.
  `228c637014 rbf: reject overflowing fee diagrams` is related but remains a policy decision: it rejects replacements with unrepresentable diagrams. Keep the current broad PR #228 blocked until its miner-facing `prioritisetransaction` trade-off and the remaining arithmetic consumers have been redesigned together.

* [x] **Rejected after reachability review / no signed-overflow path:** `dfdf5424d43 consensus: avoid output total signed overflow`. Both `CheckTransaction()` and `CTransaction::GetValueOut()` continue only while the running total is at most `MAX_MONEY`. With individually valid outputs, the next addition is therefore at most `2 * MAX_MONEY`, far below `INT64_MAX`; the proposed all-`MAX_MONEY` transaction is rejected after its second output. Its test passes without the production change and does not characterize overflow.

* [ ] **Low / script/RPC classification / tiny source candidate:** `9a5b7a9b95 script: accept OP_CHECKSIGADD in HasValidOps` remains live: `MAX_OPCODE` is still `OP_NOP10`, while `OP_CHECKSIGADD` is `0xba`. The interpreter's pre-Taproot opcode rules are unchanged; the candidate corrects a generic validity classification that can affect raw-script reporting. Confirm the exact `decodescript`/burn-check surface before prioritizing it above the current index race.

* [x] **Superseded by fork PR #233 and published as [bitcoin/bitcoin#35753](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35753):** `0f4545e7b4 validation: handle null mempool when deleting chainstate` was split as `a99b27f192` on `l0rinc/delete-chainstate-null-mempool`; see the latest refresh above.

* [x] **Fork PR #231 closed, now published as [bitcoin/bitcoin#35754](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35754):** `ci: verify downloaded CI dependencies`, final head `8e8572e3ddd3`. It verifies downloaded lint binaries and cross SDK archives, pins Git sources used to build tools, and verifies the LLVM APT signing key. Do not extract the older audit-stack commits separately.

* [x] **Debug/fuzz-only assertion hardening:** `G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME` is enabled by `core_interface_debug` and fuzz builds, while release `Assume()` preserves the value and does not call `assertion_fail`. Re-rate the P2P/HTTP/compact-block `Assume()` additions as developer-test hardening unless they also fix independent release behavior. In particular, the reported HTTP keep-alive assertion issue is low pending an exact source commit and a release-visible consequence.

* [ ] **Headers-sync stalls / source not locally identified:** retain the previous medium-at-most rating. The reported timeout/grace issue may have escape hatches through other outbound peers, but its proposed fix was not present in the refreshed refs, so no new queue item is justified yet.

### Historical high-priority queue

* [x] **Medium / authenticated-local availability / index restart race, fixed locally:** source `10a959ad62dc98916db3505618c6fd792b39a1cc index: synchronize chainstate publication during restart` from `umbrel/fuzz-contract-cluster-oracles-20260709`; local characterization `f8084546d9 test: cover index restart reads`; fixes `4fc06e3193 index: publish chainstate during restart`, `d773b62d36 index: handle missing best index on restart`, and `7730fe7f33 index: use stable block manager for readers`.
  Snapshot completion restarts indexes with `Stop()`, `Init()`, and `StartBackgroundSync()` while RPC and REST remain available. The fix publishes `m_chainstate` under `cs_main`, protects direct block-file lookups in `TxIndex` and `TxoSpenderIndex`, and makes `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain()` return `false` while a non-empty chain has no best index.
  A focused TxIndex stress test reproduces the pre-fix assertion and reader races after 1000 restart cycles. The fixed build passed 20 repeated TSan runs plus the base, txindex, and txospenderindex suites. This is now fork PR #232; #24230 is a broader future refactor, while #211 and #223/#224/#227 cover adjacent index startup or recovery behavior.

* [x] **Already represented by fork PR #211 / index startup ordering:** `c55106fcf5 index: ignore flushed locator before first block`.
  `ChainStateFlushed()` can dereference a null `m_best_block_index` if a validated flush notification arrives before the first `BlockConnected` notification during startup. This is distinct from the restart publication race above, but is already covered by `origin/l0rinc/index-pre-genesis-sync` and must not be extracted again.

* [ ] **Low-medium / wallet API null dereference / small:** `6d6b447c03e0bdf7785c324100b7c2624a7e8657 wallet: handle unconfirmed coins without coin control`.
  `AvailableCoins()` publicly defaults `coinControl` to null, but its unconfirmed-coin TRUC branch dereferences it. The source branch's focused unit mutation reaches that branch and reports SIGSEGV; the one-line guard applies cleanly.
  All current non-test callers pass a `CCoinControl`, so this is component-contract correctness and future hardening rather than a demonstrated RPC crash. No exact open upstream PR was found.

* [ ] **Low / local startup configuration arithmetic / small:** `d8289de708c63b4c5b56b18e9944c6e5c6b96fcd node: avoid cache allocation percentage overflow`.
  Current master still multiplies huge 64-bit `-dbcache` values before dividing percentages, so an operator-only boundary can wrap an index budget to zero. The rewritten commit supersedes the older `17023c07` tracker SHA, applies cleanly, and has unit/fuzz mutation proof. No open overlap was found.

* [ ] **Low / local wallet corruption handling / tiny:** `4544a54031b16fb8f1483655e4f6baaae983a595 wallet: narrow descriptor cache index probe catch` (patch-equivalent to `origin/detached584` head `2618715533`).
  Descriptor parent-cache records intentionally trigger `std::ios_base::failure` when the optional child index is absent. Narrowing `catch (...)` to that exception prevents unrelated failures from being misclassified as parent records.
  This is defensive local-wallet error handling; the tiny fixed-width decode has no demonstrated alternative exception on valid input. No exact open overlap was found.

* [ ] **Low / partial-node mining API result shape / small:** `518fc5955bd2b37567344987b02d67b8f65a5bc7 interfaces: preserve mining lookup result arity`.
  A `NodeContext` without a mempool returns no result slots instead of one nullable result per requested txid/wtxid. Fully initialized nodes have a mempool, so this affects partial initialization, teardown, and integration users rather than normal RPC/P2P behavior. The rewritten commit supersedes `c80a3a95`, applies cleanly, and has a focused unit mutation proof. No open overlap was found.

* [ ] **Medium / authenticated RPC fee arithmetic / blocked draft:** fork PR #228 now has title `mempool: bound cumulative priority deltas` and head `03183a4571bdc77e77b2f3c02bc72fb33d5f099a1`.

### Historical high-priority queue

* [ ] **Medium-high / authenticated RPC availability / coins DB lifetime / branch-state corrected:** a persistent UTXO cursor can outlive `CCoinsViewDB::ResizeCache()`.
  `CCoinsViewDB::Cursor()` returns an iterator owned by the current LevelDB instance, while `ResizeCache()` destroys and recreates that instance.
  `gettxoutsetinfo`, `scantxoutset`, and `dumptxoutset` can keep a cursor after releasing `cs_main`; concurrent AssumeUTXO cache rebalancing can then replace `m_db`.
  Destroying LevelDB with the iterator alive reaches the `VersionSet` destructor assertion and aborts the process.
  This was already identified in the [#35465 review thread](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35465#discussion_r3428902672): [Andrew traced the released-`cs_main` RPC and AssumeUTXO path](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35465#discussion_r3429208630), and [Sipa agreed it should be fixed separately](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35465#discussion_r3429827568).
  The mutex merged in #35465 prevents background compaction and `ResizeCache()` from running at the same time; it does not extend the lifetime of RPC cursors or their underlying DB.
  No unauthenticated peer can start these RPC/snapshot operations, and no consensus corruption has been demonstrated.
  Current local branch `l0rinc/coins-cursor-resize-lifetime` is a stale single-commit branch at `5a92e480d3`, ahead 1 and behind 147 relative to `origin/l0rinc/coins-cursor-resize-lifetime`; the broader re-signed `origin/` stack is at `38b8476960` and should be checked out deliberately if this branch is revisited.
  Earlier local stack `b446775e8e`, `ea101a2d8a`, then `1154f96c5f` first characterized the live-cursor resize itself. The test retains the old DB wrapper and redirects replacement to a separate temporary path, allowing old `ResizeCache()` to return `ready` with its cursor still alive while a probe on another thread finds the DB mutex available exclusively; TODOs mark both assertions. The fix gives each cursor a shared DB lock while resize and compaction still take it exclusively, then flips the assertions to `timeout` and exclusive-lock unavailability. The final commit moves compaction outside the mutex and makes `ResizeCache()` wait for it before replacing the DB. The ordinary old production path still reproduces the LevelDB abort when it destroys the cursor's backing DB.

* [ ] **Medium / authenticated RPC fee arithmetic / blocked draft:** fork PR #228, `l0rinc/mempool-saturate-ancestry-fees` at `af4eeb3e8abb`.
  Commits: `361f30ef test: characterize saturated priority fees`; `64e2e311 mempool: derive modified fees from priority deltas`; `d7e75851 util: add saturating arithmetic helpers`; `2897d99e clusterlin: handle saturated fee aggregates`; `af4eeb3e txgraph: collapse saturated disconnected chunks`.
  Review found that saturated modified fees still reach multiple raw arithmetic consumers, while the draft's saturated equal-feerate-prefix approach can violate exact-ratio invariants.
  Redesign at the `prioritisetransaction` boundary before extracting any part; do not count the draft as a completed fix.

  This is distinct from merged #35616, which changed cache-size storage to 64-bit but did not remove the remaining multiplication overflow.
