## Imported 515-commit fuzz audit

Source range: `e1290ce7f74b50f99932e7b83e414dec2732a8b9..4f71d85906` (515 commits). This is source material, not a publication-status snapshot; the live queue below decides which exact fixes remain open.

### Most severe confirmed fix families

1. **Validation/block-index consistency:** `a1d3cd809b validation: keep failed blocks out of candidates`; `f023f524d9 validation: readd redownloaded block candidates`; `fa32e3f3df validation: keep pruned unlinked blocks linkable`; `f12f0b41a0 validation: keep preciousblock ordering monotonic`.
   Fuzzed reorg, prune, redownload, failed-branch, and `preciousblock` sequences exposed stale candidate membership or comparator-key mutations. The failure modes were assertions and inconsistent candidate ordering.
2. **Mempool/RBF modified-fee arithmetic:** `ad6e136142 rbf: avoid overflow in replacement fee delta`; `a4388ed457 validation: saturate modified fee aggregates`; `e0b7ce3143 rbf: reject overflowing fee diagrams`; `93f48f7703 mempool: handle saturated fee diagram checks`.
   Extreme authenticated `prioritisetransaction` deltas could make later RPC- or peer-submitted replacement checks overflow or leave policy comparisons outside their representable domain.
3. **Cluster mempool/MiniMiner saturation:** `74923616f3 node: clamp MiniMiner total bump fee`; `437c416435 miniminer: make consumed Linearize fail closed`; `fa7ec48c8c node: saturate MiniMiner modified fee arithmetic`; `4e25623196 txgraph: collapse saturated disconnected chunks`; `4f71d85906 node: guard MiniMiner saturated total checks`.
   These are a broad source stack, not an atomic fix. Saturating arithmetic is neither reversible nor associative, so downstream invariants and exact-ratio comparisons require independent review before extraction.
4. **Compact-block reconstruction:** `a997919a71 cmpctblock: ignore empty extra transaction slots`; `35ef347248 fuzz: check compact block init failure contracts`; `d4a9efbb74 cmpctblock: clear partial block after short fill`; `0cab4d974f cmpctblock: reset partial block counters after fill`; `5d11970700 cmpctblock: preserve FillBlock output on failure`; `a6b866ba43 cmpctblock: reject null prefilled tx refs`; `bf314aee51 cmpctblock: track extra tx source counts`.
   The strongest lead is the empty extra-transaction slot collision; the rest mostly harden malformed in-memory state and failure cleanup. **[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-04: that lead is dead. Null `extra_txn` slots came from the old `vExtraTxnForCompact.resize()`, which our own merged upstream #35670 replaced with `reserve` + `emplace_back` plus a `max_extra_txs == 0` early return, so the condition is unreachable on current master. See the fourth-pass entry at the end of this file.]**
5. **Malformed local or persisted input:** `d90ac41138 validation: reject duplicate snapshot coin records`; `198f81dfda fees: reject corrupt estimator vectors`; `3d01e02d9c dbwrapper: guard exhausted iterator reads`.
   These are local-data integrity bugs rather than unauthenticated P2P issues. The duplicate snapshot record case could preserve the unique UTXO hash while invalidating metadata counts.
6. **Atomicity and stale outputs:** `21b967ba7d key: invalidate pubkey on failed compact recovery`; `7ba1cac2c9 http: parse request fields atomically`; `aa52853d9b http: commit chunked request bodies atomically`, plus related base58, script, key, and `core_io` output-cleanup commits.
   These are lower-severity API-contract fixes where failed calls could expose stale successful output or partially parsed state.

No true thread data race was confirmed in this audit. Several state-machine failures looked race-like under prune/redownload ordering, callback replay, partial parser commits, compact-block reuse, or comparator-key mutation.

* [x] **Prepared locally / medium / authenticated-RPC priority-fee arithmetic / small stack:**
  `e119fce0d161d71604546700411a260976b83699 test: characterize saturated priority fees`;

  the functional test disconnects the authenticated RPC caller before the
  guard. P2P traffic cannot set fee deltas. Source leads: the reverse path is

  `umbrel/fuzz-contract-cluster-oracles-20260709`; the priority-state invariant
  is the narrow extraction of `e929e9812e562241d0fd973410650bf9fec19423`.
  The older three-commit attempt remains only at

### Highest-priority current queue

* [x] **Prepared / medium / authenticated log injection / regression-test / small:** `19c7dc6233 rpc: sanitize RPC method names in whitelist-rejection logs` and `4c3829c9aa wallet: reject control characters in wallet names at creation` -> [#35833](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35833) / `l0rinc/sanitize-log-inputs` at `e23645333f`, three commits on `upstream/master` `7dea464d6b51`.
  The current stack is `9d5fb22f1d test: characterize rejected RPC method logs`, `1d9b37cb1c logging: escape embedded newlines by default`, and `e23645333f wallet: reject control characters in new names`. The first commit records the singleton and batch whitelist-rejection rendering. The second moves the protection into the logging framework, so authorization and logging both keep the original method string. The wallet half stays separate because control characters remain undesirable in new filesystem paths and UI names even after log escaping.
  Proof boundaries, all replayed locally this pass. RPC: the flipped expectation fails against the parent binary with `Unexpected message "getblock\nFORGED LOG LINE" found in log`, and the framework fix renders the embedded newline as `\x0a` on both request paths. Wallet: on a pre-fix binary, `createwallet` with an embedded newline succeeded and left 12 `debug.log` lines beginning at column zero with the injected text; the new invalid-name checks fail without the production hunks. The final tree builds fully, passes `logging_tests` and `util_tests`, and passes `rpc_whitelist.py`, `wallet_createwallet.py` (including `--usecli`), `wallet_backup.py`, and `feature_notifications.py`.
  Ownership search on 2026-07-28 found no equivalent open or closed owner. Open [#35768](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35768) is adjacent and conflicts mechanically in `CreateWallet()` and `wallet_createwallet.py`, but only rejects whitespace-only new names; its review also converged on preserving existing names. Merged [#34269](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34269) introduced the create/restore empty-name guards and migration-only `allow_unnamed` exception that this branch extends, while merged [#34544](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34544) is precedent for validating wallet names as paths. Merged [#17095](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/17095) introduced `LogEscapeMessage`; review comment [#35833](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35833#issuecomment-5113804332) prompted moving the newline protection into that framework.
  The framework strips one trailing newline as the entry terminator and escapes every other newline as `\x0a`. A source audit found two intentional embedded-newline formats, `PrintExceptionContinue()` and `CWallet::CommitTransaction()`. Both opt in explicitly, and each dynamic field is escaped before the opt-in so legacy wallet names and exception strings cannot use it to forge lines. Wallets whose names already contain control characters remain loadable, while migration rollback logs a warning if it restores one.
  A 2026-07-28 `/simplify` pass re-scoped one guard and tightened the tests, leaving the commit prose as written. `RestoreWallet()` now screens the name only when `allow_unnamed` is false: `MigrateLegacyToDescriptor()` calls it on its rollback path with `allow_unnamed=true` and the wallet's own pre-existing name, so the unconditional check contradicted this branch's stated "existing names stay loadable" scope and could have aborted a rollback, masking the real migration error and leaving the backup unrestored. `wallet_migration.py` skips in this build (no legacy/BDB support compiled), so that path was not exercised directly; the change only removes a check from it, so it cannot newly break it.
  Also from that pass: `rpccall()` builds a dict and `json.dumps()` once instead of concatenating JSON by hand, so the test passes a real newline instead of a pre-escaped one; `wallet_createwallet.py` gained a `\x7f` case, since every existing assertion used `\n` and nothing pinned the predicate's breadth; the characterization commit owns the neutral test docstring; and the predicate reads `c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f` rather than mixing radixes. Considered and skipped: folding the four parallel name-rejection blocks into one `WalletNameError()` helper (rewrites two pre-existing blocks, so it belongs in its own refactor), bounding an RPC method name against a ~32 MiB request (the unbounded formatting on that path predates this branch), and adding a `FAILED_INVALID_NAME` status (the reused `FAILED_NEW_UNNAMED` maps to the right RPC error but now misdescribes the case).
  PR #35833's first 32-bit ARM job failed in `feature_notifications.py` because that test built a Linux wallet name from bytes `0x01..0x7f`, which the new policy intentionally rejects. The wallet commit now keeps the notification test on the valid printable range `0x20..0x7e`; the exact focused test passes locally.

Latest done: `4fb76c8c9d index: handle synced index before genesis activation` and `1305a6a127 index: ignore flushed locator before first block` are now prepared on `l0rinc/index-pre-genesis-sync` as `41f3f60aa6 index: handle synced index before genesis` and `5191836f53 index: skip pre-genesis flushed locators`.

Why it was the next best priority/effort tradeoff:

- It is a startup crash class in current master: `BaseIndex::Init()` documents that an index can latch synced in an empty datadir before genesis is connected, but synced-index callbacks still dereferenced null active-tip / index-best-block pointers.
- The fix is small: handle the null active tip in `BlockUntilSyncedToCurrentChain()` and skip flushed locator commits until a `BlockConnected` callback gives the index a known best block.
- The reproducer is compact: the txindex unit test loads and verifies chainstate without activating genesis, initializes txindex in that documented state, sends a genesis flush notification, then activates genesis and checks the normal notification path still advances the index.
- This is related to, but not the same as, PR #35652. PR #35652 fixes a `-reindex` shutdown condition-variable wakeup in init; this branch fixes `BaseIndex` null assumptions in the pre-genesis synced-index state.

Next likely candidates are the crash-recovery index follow-ups if you want highest severity, or the txdownload / streams / flatfile items if you want the next small PR.


--------

Most Relevant Bugs

1. MiniMiner negative bump-fee calculation
Found by the mini_miner fuzzer with a package where individual descendants looked underfunded but the shared ancestor package was already above target feerate. CalculateTotalBumpFees() could produce a
negative total bump fee and trip the production Assume(total_bump_fee >= 0).
Fixed in d1f9ae2dca by clamping the shared package shortfall to zero, keeping the production assertion, and adding a deterministic miniminer_total_bumpfee_clamps_overfunded_package test.

2. RBF replacement fee delta overflow - NEXT
Found through the tx_pool fuzzer under sanitizer replay. PaysForRBF subtracted saturated/large modified fee totals directly, so replacement_fees - original_fees could overflow CAmount.
Fixed in 48cae3b5f6 by using checked addition for the required relay-fee threshold and only subtracting on a bounded rejection path, with production preconditions plus deterministic RBF coverage.

3. Duplicate UTXO snapshot records accepted incorrectly
Found by UTXO snapshot fuzz/oracle work. A malformed snapshot could contain duplicate serialized coins: metadata counted duplicates, while insertion collapsed them by outpoint, allowing inconsistent
snapshot accounting.
Fixed in 7c8863c525 by rejecting snapshots when computed coin count differs from metadata, with stats assertions, a deterministic duplicate snapshot test, and structured fuzz coverage.

4. ~~Compact block duplicate/null transaction ref issue already tackled~~; remaining compact-block cleanup should be checked separately
Two real compact-block issues came out:

- c3322cec51: empty vExtraTxnForCompact slots could be treated as available transactions if short-id matching hit a zero wtxid case. Fixed by ignoring empty extra slots and asserting populated slots match
their witness hash.

- 8e5bc2ee22: FillBlock() with too few BLOCKTXN entries returned invalid but left partial reconstruction state around. Fixed by clearing partial state through a single cleanup path.

5. ~~HTTP/libevent-removal response contract bugs - already tackled~~
This exercise found several concrete HTTP reply-state bugs in the newer libevent-free code:

- 0809692082: response Connection: close was serialized but did not force m_keep_alive = false.
- d16ce22674: HEAD replies could synthesize body-related headers.
- 904ab0a70a: preset Content-Length could be duplicated with computed Content-Length.
- 4ababbff94: HTTP/1.0 keep-alive generation could duplicate Connection.
- 1fbcdb0cb8: later Connection: close headers could be ignored if an earlier value was keep-alive.

All were fixed with production assertions plus focused fuzzer/unit coverage.

6. Stream boundary bugs
The stream fuzz/oracle work found real boundary mistakes:

- 75ff07a32c: BufferedFile::FindByte() could scan past SetLimit.
- bba4a550d1: BufferedFile::SetPos() could move beyond the active read limit using already-buffered bytes.
- 56c64dd50e: AutoFile::tell() could report stale cached position after close/release.
These now have production checks and deterministic tests.

7. Coins cache spent-entry mutation bug
Found around coins-cache mutation oracles. SpendCoin() on an already cached spent entry could return true and mutate state, despite the intended missing/unspent no-op semantics.
Fixed in c3ee1cc3bb by returning false before mutation for spent cached entries, with coinscache_sim and deterministic test coverage.

8. Corrupt persisted-data handling
Two persistence bugs were fixed:

- 653a5157ff: fee estimator files could accept corrupt current-format vectors, including non-finite or non-monotonic bucket/sample data. Fixed by validating finite/non-negative samples and strictly increasing
buckets.

- 423dc32c13: malformed DB obfuscation metadata could be treated like an absent key. Fixed by throwing dbwrapper_error when the reserved key exists but cannot deserialize.

9. Golomb-Rice P == 64 edge
Found through serialization/fuzz boundary coverage. The P == 64 case risked shift-by-64 undefined behavior.
Fixed in 44e7900c42 by rejecting P > 64 and explicitly handling P == 64.

10. TxGraph staged memory accounting edge
The txgraph fuzzer exposed an API/oracle mismatch around GetMainMemoryUsage() before/after AbortStaging() when a ref was destroyed during staging and oversizedness state was stale.
This was handled in 2896da56c9 by documenting the exception and tightening the fuzzer to assert post-abort stability instead of the invalid stronger assumption.

Contract Hardening

A lot of the rest is intentional oracle work rather than discovered live bugs: validation/block-index reorg invariants, cluster mempool and txgraph diagram contracts, coins cache parent/overlay purity, mempool
import/persist metadata contracts, txdownloadman consistency, message signing output contracts, and HTTP reply normalization.

The latest commit, f52fa19a6d, added message-signing contracts: successful signatures must decode to compact signature size and verify against the original address/message; invalid keys must fail without
mutating the output string. I mutation-tested that by temporarily clearing the output on failure, and the deterministic test caught it.





Branch: codex/reindex-crash-all-indexes, HEAD 82f8ed8506, ahead of origin/master by 9 commits.

So far I found and fixed four new crash/reorg persistence races beyond the PR 34897-style “index committed ahead of flushed chainstate” issue.

1. txospenderindex could return spends from an inactive block
Commit: 11d686bb3e index: ignore inactive txospender records

A crash after TxoSpenderIndex::CustomAppend() wrote spender records, but before the index best-block locator was durably committed, could leave records from a block that chainstate later rolled back from.
After restart, all indexes appeared synced, but gettxspendingprevout(..., return_spending_tx=true) returned a spender from inactive block 102 while active chainstate was back at 101.

Fix: keep txospender records append-only, but make lookup ignore spender records whose spending block is unknown or not active.

2. blockfilterindex could fail startup after reorg crash
Commit: d04d560961 index: recover blockfilter headers after reorg crash

During a reorg crash, the height-keyed blockfilter entry could be overwritten by the replacement block while the durable index locator still pointed to the old block at that same height. Restart then failed
in BlockFilterIndex::CustomInit() with a header mismatch / corrupted-index style error.

Fix: make blockfilter header lookup use the reorg-aware fallback by block hash when the height-keyed entry does not match the expected block.

3. Validation could record the wrong flushed block during disconnect
Commit: 661ea17648 validation: track coins tip after disconnect flush

During DisconnectTip(), DisconnectBlock() moves the coins tip to the parent before m_chain.Tip() is updated. If FlushStateToDisk() happens in that window, the durable coins DB is at the parent, but the old
code recorded the disconnected child as the last flushed block.

Fix: after flushing coins, derive m_last_flushed_block from CoinsTip().GetBestBlock() instead of from m_chain.Tip().

4. Indexes could remain pointed at a stale disconnected child
Commit: 82f8ed8506 index: rewind stale children after disconnect crash

A pure disconnect crash can leave durable chainstate at the parent while an index best-block locator still points at the old child. On restart, there is no replacement child to process, so BaseIndex::Sync()
saw no next block and incorrectly marked the index synced while still above active chain tip.

Fix: when NextSyncBlock() returns null, detect the stale-descendant case and rewind the index directly back to the active tip before marking it synced.

The PR 34897-related fix is also present in adapted form:

- e0df33bf99 validation: track last flushed block
- 3c6bce0e96 index: Don't commit ahead of the flushed chainstate
- 257bbf2aa0 test: add test to ensure indexes dont commit too early

That one addresses the broader class where indexes commit past the durable chainstate boundary, but the four items above are the new races found here through deterministic crash/reorg/disconnect reproduction.

Verification so far:

- Deterministic crash failpoints were added in 5c7f4abf9c.
- Reorg crash matrix passed for blockfilter, coinstats, and txospender index rewind crash points.
- Disconnect crash verifier passed with all four indexes enabled.
- Unit/functional tests passed for the affected areas.
- The ongoing scratch mainnet reindex crash loop has reached 48 deliberate kill -9 crashes so far without revealing another new failure beyond the fixed ones above.



Race Findings

1. Confirmed: HTTP keep-alive send/receive race after libevent removal
- Commits: 956e0211d9, e9cec7de7b
- Bug: the send path assumed !m_connection_busy after a full keep-alive response had been sent. In reality, the receive side can already process
the next keep-alive request and set m_connection_busy=true before the send-side postcondition observes it.

- Found by: new HTTP send-buffer/optimistic-send assertions, then reproduced with an ordinary functional RPC keep-alive workload.
- Fixed by: keeping strict single-thread fuzzer/unit checks, but narrowing production assertions to facts stable across threads: buffer/send-
ready/disconnect state, not m_connection_busy.

- Potential attack: an RPC/REST client with HTTP access can rapidly reuse or pipeline keep-alive requests to hit the interleaving and crash
fuzz/debug or ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME builds. More importantly, it prevents future production logic from relying on a stale “not busy”
assumption.

2. HTTP connection-state inconsistencies, race-adjacent
- Commits: 2f715ca87d, 8c7a443dcb, ee35156b53, 1b9e405736, 58120b5522
- Bug class: response headers and connection lifecycle could disagree, especially around preset Connection / Content-Length headers and
Connection: close.

- Fixed by: normalizing generated headers, replacing stale preset headers, honoring any preset close directive, and asserting serialized
response state matches keep-alive/disconnect state.

- Potential attack: an HTTP client could trigger response-state confusion, stale content length, duplicate headers, unintended keep-alive, or
connection retention. This is RPC/REST DoS/desync class, not consensus-critical.

3. Socket readiness map contracts after libevent removal
- Commits: a4fd258bcf, 0cf78dcdf0
- Finding: fuzzing exposed that mocked sockets could collapse distinct clients into the same readiness-map key. Production assertions now check
uniqueness and event-mask preservation.

- Fixed by: making fuzz socket descriptors distinct and adding production Assume() checks around readiness insertion.
- Potential attack if regressed: wrong client readiness, lost wakeups, I/O starvation, or misrouted HTTP/P2P socket state. No real production
exploit was found here because OS descriptors should already be unique.

4. Validation flush locator consistency across async subscribers
- Commit: 52a804c649
- Finding: mutation testing showed existing tests would not catch ChainStateFlushed emitting a locator for the wrong tip during flush/reorg
combinations.

- Fixed by: production checks that flush locators are non-null, non-empty, and start at the flushed tip; fuzzing now mixes reorgs and forced
flushes.

- Potential attack if the bug existed: adversarial reorg/flush timing could cause indexes or wallets to persist state for the wrong chain tip.
No unmutated production race reproduced.

5. DB compaction / concurrent read consistency
- Commits: 3007227a45, 261a70ea88
- Finding: added oracles that waited compaction preserves observable DB snapshots and concurrent read tests verify final iterator state.
- Potential attack if regressed: local DB compaction/read races could hide or corrupt coins/index-visible state. No confirmed production race
found.

6. Threadpool and CheckQueue completion contracts
- Commits: 53752b1125, 9b6315fe9a, 539346e58f
- Finding: mutation tests caught dropped ranged tasks and skipped RAII completion paths.
- Potential attack if regressed: validation or async worker tasks could be silently dropped or not drained, causing hangs or inconsistent
completion accounting. No live production race found.

Bottom line: the main confirmed race fixed so far is the HTTP keep-alive send/receive state race. The rest are race-adjacent hardening and mutation-
proven oracles around async boundaries. I have not found a confirmed consensus, P2P validation, cluster mempool, or coins-cache race exploit so far.
Current worktree only has the unfinished crypto_common test/fuzzer edits; the temporary production endian mutation was restored.


Findings By Severity

1. Indexes could commit ahead of durable chainstate
 Commits: e0df33bf99, 3c6bce0e96, tests in 257bbf2aa0, e86a1f31c7

 Root issue: index state could be persisted for blocks whose corresponding chainstate was not durably flushed yet. After an unclean shutdown, the
 chainstate could roll back while index DBs still claimed a later best block.

 Impact: silent index inconsistency after crash, not just startup failure. txindex, coinstatsindex, blockfilter index, or txospender index could
 answer from a chainstate future that the node itself had not recovered to.

 Potential attack: an attacker who can trigger or wait for a crash during IBD/reindex/reorg, or combine this with any unrelated crash/host
 instability, may cause index-backed services to return stale or wrong answers after restart. The practical impact is strongest for infrastructure
 that exposes index RPCs to wallets, explorers, fraud monitors, or light-client services.

2. Validation reported the wrong durable chainstate tip after disconnect flush
 Commit: fc3736cac5 validation: track coins tip after disconnect flush

 Root issue: after disconnecting blocks, validation could signal/index against the wrong “last flushed” block. This made index commit gating
 believe a state was durable when the coins DB had actually been flushed to an earlier parent.

 Impact: crash during reorg/disconnect could let indexes persist locators inconsistent with the recovered UTXO set.

 Potential attack: during a reorg, an adversary capable of causing competing-chain activity plus a crash window could leave index consumers with
 stale state after restart. This is mainly a crash-recovery consistency issue, but it matters for services relying on indexed spentness or
 historical transaction/filter data.

3. Stale child indexes after disconnect crash
 Commit: 5520b78aac index: rewind stale children after disconnect crash

 Root issue: after a pure disconnect/crash path, an index could remain positioned on stale descendants when the active chain no longer had a next
 block to advance through.

 Impact: index liveness/correctness risk after reorg-style recovery: the index could fail to naturally converge to the active chain tip.

 Potential attack: a reorg plus crash could strand an index on stale branch state, causing services to serve stale answers or require operator
 intervention.

4. Txospender stale-record race on crash/reorg
 Commit: d123ac0a11 index: ignore inactive txospender records

 Root issue: txospender records were append-style disk-position records. A crash after writing spender records but before durable best-block
 update, or a reorg, could leave records for inactive-chain spends.

 Fix: keep records append-only but make lookup verify that the spending transaction’s block is still active.

 Impact: prevents gettxspendingprevout from reporting a spend from an inactive block.

 Potential attack: a malicious spender could create a spend that lands in a block later reorged out, then a crash could make an index-backed
 service believe the output remains spent. That can break wallet/accounting logic or monitoring systems.

5. Blockfilter header recovery after reorg crash
 Commit: 431a1e4acc index: recover blockfilter headers after reorg crash

 Root issue: during reorg rewind, blockfilter data copied out of the height index could become hard to recover by the expected lookup path after a
 crash.

 Fix: header lookup now falls back through the hash-key path.

 Impact: avoids missing/inconsistent blockfilter data after reorg/crash recovery.

 Potential attack: a node serving compact block filters could fail or provide incomplete filter/header responses after a reorg plus crash,
 degrading light-client reliability.

Repro/Verification Added

- Deterministic crash failpoints: 40bcd4d201
- Functional crash recovery test: feature_index_crash_recovery.py
- Covered txospender append crash, blockfilter reorg rewind crash, and disconnect flush crash.
- Manual disposable std::terminate monkeypatches exercised UTXO DB partial/final writes, validation flush boundaries, BaseIndex commits/rewinds, and
all index append paths. No additional unrecoverable UTXO/index corruption was found from that pass.

Current long-run status: 84 kills so far; latest milestone kill at 576140 recovered cleanly and the node is replaying again, currently past 449207
with no new failure artifacts.

# Secp256k1 audit log

## secp256k1 fuzz / audit / perf branch triage index

### 2026-07-24 selected MuSig zero-nonce rejection

Refs and ownership were refreshed after the latest fetch.
`upstream/master` and `origin/master` are `d2d04864ef9b056151603a3ced7980958b058028`.
No open upstream or focused fork PR owns the zero-scalar result from `secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen_internal`.
The broad source is `86f40389fb` on `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles`, but it was reimplemented as a two-commit focused branch.

* [x] **Pushed / Low rare nonce-generation correctness / fork PR #26:** `l0rinc/musig-reject-zero-nonces` at `88424b7a0d`, based on `upstream/master`, tracks matching `origin/l0rinc/musig-reject-zero-nonces`.
  `secp256k1_nonce_function_musig` maps two possible 256-bit inputs to zero after scalar reduction, so either derived nonce scalar is zero with probability about `2^-255`.
  A zero scalar produces an infinity public nonce.
  Existing VERIFY builds abort at the documented zero-scalar invariant, while no-VERIFY builds return success and save invalid nonce state.
  This is a negligible-probability production correctness failure, not a remotely triggerable or practically exploitable vulnerability.
  The first commit `1d7d39ae5c` adds an order-13 exhaustive characterization where counter `2` deterministically derives a zero second scalar.
  The second commit rejects the result before group multiplication, returns `0` through both public nonce-generation APIs, and documents the rare failure result.
  Mutation proof: removing only the guard aborts the order-13 VERIFY build at `session_impl.h:413` and makes the no-VERIFY build fail its new public-API assertion because it returns `1`.
  Final verification: focused MuSig plus full VERIFY/no-VERIFY suites and order-13 exhaustive tests passed on default 5x52 and forced 10x26 builds.

### 2026-07-26 refreshed recoverable ECDSA signature loader guard

Refs and ownership were refreshed after the latest fetch.
`upstream/master` and `origin/master` are `d2d04864ef9b056151603a3ced7980958b058028`.
No focused fork PR through #29 or open upstream PR owns this recovery-module loader boundary.
The current broad source is `c0623f5a1d` on `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles`, rewritten from `6c8a008b0d`.
That source also clears public API outputs on failure, so it was narrowed to avoid the declined #1850 output-clearing policy.
Fork PR #1 touches the same recovery APIs only for output clearing and does not validate the loader.
The only open upstream PRs touching these recovery test files are unrelated CHECK/configuration refactors #1481 and #1833.

* [>] **Next fork PR candidate / Low opaque-object API hardening:** local `l0rinc/reject-invalid-recoverable-signatures` at `68375d5426` is based on `upstream/master` and tracks matching `origin/l0rinc/reject-invalid-recoverable-signatures`, which remains at the previous tip `0eb964fc81`.
  Compact parsing already rejects scalar components at or above the group order and recovery IDs outside `0` through `3`.
  A caller can still corrupt or directly construct the raw 65-byte opaque recoverable-signature object after that boundary.
  The focused patch validates both scalar components and the recovery ID in the shared loader, then makes serialization, conversion, and recovery propagate failure without clearing their outputs.
  This requires caller-side opaque-object misuse and is not reachable from malformed compact input.
  Existing parser tests characterize the wire boundary, while the new failing-before regression mutates `r`, `s`, and the recovery ID independently and covers all three loader consumers.
  Reverting only the production hunk makes default and forced-10x26 VERIFY builds abort at `scalar_impl.h:43`; both no-VERIFY builds fail because serialization returns `1` without invoking the illegal callback.
  Final verification: focused recovery, full VERIFY/no-VERIFY suites, and order-13 exhaustive tests passed on default 5x52 and forced-10x26 builds with the recovery module explicitly enabled.
  The local `68375d5426` rewrite only simplifies the commit message; its tree is identical to pushed tip `0eb964fc81`.

### 2026-07-23 refreshed priority and selected MuSig partial-signature guard

Fetched every configured remote after the Silent Payments merge.
`upstream/master` and `origin/master` are `d2d04864ef9b056151603a3ced7980958b058028`.
No open upstream or focused fork PR owns the overflowing opaque MuSig partial-signature loader boundary.
The source commit `63516cd3b0` remains on `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles` only.
No unowned Medium-or-higher candidate remains after the refresh.

* [x] **Review complete / low opaque-object API hardening / fork PR [#24](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/24):** `l0rinc/musig-reject-overflowing-partial-sigs` at `d43948235c` is correct and has no wire-reachable vulnerability.
  `secp256k1_musig_partial_sig_parse` already rejects a scalar at or above the group order, so an attacker cannot send this state as a MuSig partial signature. It requires caller-side corruption, unsafe persistence, or manual construction of the opaque object.
  Before the patch, the shared loader used an uncatchable `VERIFY_CHECK` and serialization copied the scalar without validation. The patch uses `ARG_CHECK` so consumers with non-aborting illegal callbacks receive `0`, validates serialization too, and corrects the header return contract. `scalar_get_b32` round-trips identically to the old copy for every valid object.
  Parse failure already zeroes the opaque output, so ignoring the parser return cannot preserve an overflowing object. Tests overwrite the scalar with `max64` and cover both aggregation and serialization through `CHECK_ILLEGAL`, matching the new `ARG_CHECK` path. This does not duplicate the F3 10x26 normalization work or the EllSwift, xonly, and context-hash reviews.
  Cross-session equivalence: detached `3c88abee` covers overflow rejection in partial-signature use, and `a61d5a2d` routes serialization through the validating loader. Together they cover the focused PR's behavior and additionally leave the fixed serialization output zeroed on failure. No local porting action is needed.

### 2026-07-24 pushed opaque ECDSA signature scalar guard

Refs and ownership were refreshed before selection.
`upstream/master` and `origin/master` are `d2d04864ef9b056151603a3ced7980958b058028`.
Fork PR #25 now owns this loader boundary as a focused draft.
No open upstream PR owns it.
The broader source implementation was already pushed as `4a23eadcdd` on `origin/detached23`, `origin/detached24`, `origin/detached25`, and `origin/detached29`, but none is a focused PR for this boundary.
Per the separated-PR triage rule, it remains eligible for a narrow extraction.

* [x] **Pushed / Low opaque-object API hardening / fork PR [#25](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/25):** `l0rinc/reject-overflowing-ecdsa-signatures` at `97dab67109` based on `upstream/master`.
  `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_compact` and DER parsing already reject scalar components at or above the group order, but a caller can corrupt or manually construct the raw 64-byte opaque `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature` object after that boundary.
  Its native scalar fast path then violates the scalar invariant in VERIFY builds or reduces the component modulo the order in no-VERIFY builds.
  The focused patch changes the shared loader to return `0` after `ARG_CHECK`ing each component and makes DER/compact serialization, normalization, and verification propagate that failure.
  It intentionally does not clear caller outputs on failure, avoiding the declined #1850 clear-on-failure policy.
  The deterministic regression overwrites `r` and `s` independently with `0xff` and covers all four loader callers.
  Failing-before proof: default and forced-10x26 VERIFY builds abort at `scalar_impl.h:43`; their no-VERIFY counterparts accept the object and fail the new illegal-callback assertion.
  Final verification: focused ECDSA, full VERIFY/no-VERIFY, and order-13 exhaustive suites passed on both default and forced-10x26 builds.

* [ ] **Deferred / Low opaque keypair consistency:** `9e7060530c` correctly observes that a mutated keypair can contain individually valid but mismatched secret and public halves.

### 2026-07-23 upstream secp256k1 merge and overlap closure

* [x] **Silent Payments resolved upstream with merge proof:** [#1765](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1765) merged head `cea6d11410` as `d2d04864` and was imported into Bitcoin Core by `edf4b807f0`. An external merged-master ASan/UBSan run reported `-t=silentpayments -t=extrakeys` passing. That build was not replayed in this checkout.
  `84a02fa9` is a behavior-preserving extraction of the label-batch checker. Its flat `i = 0..2*n_batch-1` loop preserves the old pair order, `j_start + i / 2` maps each candidate to the same output as the old nested loop, and `*label_tweak` remains null on no match. Every caller has a nonempty pending batch, and the two-candidates-per-output writes remain within the 16-entry arrays.
  `1ae90bde` fixes a real first-match ordering bug. A direct x-only match at output `j` previously broke before checking pending label candidates for earlier outputs, so it could return the later unlabeled output and discard earlier label metadata. Flushing the pending range from `j - label_batch_idx` is underflow-safe and restores complete precedence. `test_recipient_scan_label_precedes_direct_match` puts the labeled `k = 0` output at index 0 and its direct counterpart at index 1; pre-fix code returns index 1, while merged code requires the labeled output and metadata.
  The previously reproduced labeled match remained spendable. A separate adversarial recipient-scan pass found correct stack bounds, direct-match infinity exclusion, work bounded by `RECIPIENT_GROUP_LIMIT`, and secret cleanup on every failure exit. Close the watch item.

* [x] **RFC6979 maximum-attempt hang fixed upstream:** [#1890](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1890) production commit `b1bc6f3e` merged as `9e4ec507`. Its generate-then-break loop exits before the unsigned index can wrap and preserves the documented valid result for every counter, including `UINT_MAX`. The public nonce callback made the old infinite loop directly API-reachable, although ordinary signing retries could not approach that count.
  Detached source `fd296e30` instead rejects `UINT_MAX` and therefore conflicts with the merged API behavior. It remains only on detached/resurrection refs. Drop it whenever replaying or rebasing those stacks. Do not carry both forms.
* [x] **Fork PR #22 overlaps merged upstream #1894:** [#1894](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1894) commit `89a54b5a` establishes the even-Y x-only invariant under `VERIFY`. `l0rinc/reject-odd-y-xonly-pubkeys` still adds production `ARG_CHECK` rejection and tests for tampered opaque objects, so describe it as upgrading #1894's VERIFY-only invariant rather than discovering a new fix. Neither path has a wire-reachable vector.

### 2026-07-22 refreshed priority and prepared EllSwift zero-u fix

Fetched `upstream`, `origin`, and `i9` after the Silent Payments merge.
`upstream/master` and `origin/master` are `d2d04864ef9b056151603a3ced7980958b058028`.
Fork PR #23 now owns the EllSwift zero-u inverse condition as a focused PR: https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/23.
The zero-u source commit `e54f3e5da0` remains only on `i9/codex/fuzz-oracles`.
Upstream PR #1863 has since merged; open upstream PR #1806 concerns different EllSwift callback behavior.
Upstream PR #1795 owns the generic WNAF issue and #1785 owns the `gej_rescale` alias issue, leaving no unowned Medium-or-higher candidate.

* [x] **Low / rare EllSwift correctness hardening:** fork PR #23 owns `l0rinc/ellswift-normalize-zero-u` at `dda3614`.
  `secp256k1_ellswift_xswiftec_inv_var` cannot accept `u = 0`, but `secp256k1_ellswift_create` derives `u` from SHA256 and reduces it modulo the field.
  Zero occurs with probability about `2^-255`.
  Current VERIFY builds abort on this condition, while no-VERIFY builds can return an encoding that decodes to a different public key.
  The two-commit branch first characterizes that no-VERIFY behavior, then maps zero to one before the inverse.
  The helper is already variable-time after the create path declassifies its hash state.
  The original serialized `u32` remains hash-derived, and the existing search retries if the replacement has no inverse for the selected branch.
  Removing only the new fallback makes the no-VERIFY EllSwift test abort at `tests_impl.h:313` with exit `134`.
  Full VERIFY/no-VERIFY C test suites passed on default 5x52 and forced 10x26 builds.
  It tracks matching `origin/l0rinc/ellswift-normalize-zero-u` at the pushed PR head.

* [x] **Test-only / owned:** `l0rinc/tests-ber-lengths` is open draft fork PR #21 at remote head `15c667cb`, while the current local rebase/simplification is `c78266aed9` on `upstream/master` `7fecac74ae`: https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/21.
  It fixes only the BER test generator, adds strict-reject/lax-accept known-answer coverage, and now asserts that undamaged randomized BER generator output lax-parses before any damage is applied. Production parsing is unchanged.

* [x] **Low / opaque-object API correctness:** fork PR #22 owns `l0rinc/reject-odd-y-xonly-pubkeys` at `b0b9b3b79c`: https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/22.
  An x-only public key represents the even-Y point for its serialized x coordinate.
  Copying the valid odd-Y full public key for scalar 2 into the opaque x-only type passes the shared loader on current master.
  It serializes to the canonical x coordinate, but `secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_tweak_add` applies its tweak to the opposite point.
  This requires a corrupt or type-confused opaque object and is not reachable through x-only parsing or normal conversion.
  The two-commit local branch first characterizes the current behavior, then rejects odd Y coordinates in `secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_load`.
  Removing only that guard makes the focused final regression fail.
  Full VERIFY/no-VERIFY CTest suites passed on default 5x52 (227 tests) and forced 10x26 (219 tests).
  It tracks matching `origin/l0rinc/reject-odd-y-xonly-pubkeys` at the pushed PR head. Merged upstream #1894 now pins the same invariant only under `VERIFY`; the remaining value of this branch is production `ARG_CHECK` enforcement, not a new invariant discovery.

* [ ] **Deferred / lower priority:** `e4b2a16e49` converts the copy-only private-key DER parser to offsets.
  A malformed BER length can form an out-of-object pointer before rejection, but the current code does not dereference it.
  Related upstream PR #1895 adds malformed-input coverage only: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1895.
  Its truncation cases retain a 300-byte backing array, so they do not exercise the claimed-length object boundary.
  Keep this as C-definedness hardening unless a concrete sanitizer or observable failure is found.

* [ ] **Deferred / lower priority:** the local `l0rinc/reject-noncanonical-opaque-pubkeys` branch detects `p + 1` field storage in public keys and MuSig key-aggregation caches.
  It is also opaque-object-only and adds normalization work to every generic public-key load, so it is not the next PR.

### 2026-07-20 magnitude-32 reachability correction and next candidate

  The uint32 carry overflow is real for verify-valid magnitude-32 limb values, including the false-zero counterexample, so all five normalization and zero-predicate paths need the uint64 carry.

### 2026-07-20 off-curve opaque public-key loader hardening pushed

* [x] **Low / dependent loader-invariant hardening:** `secp256k1_pubkey_load` accepted nonzero opaque coordinates without checking that they form a curve point.
  A corrupted opaque `secp256k1_pubkey` could then reach serialization and group operations even though `secp256k1_ec_pubkey_parse` rejects the same point.
  Pushed as fork PR #18: https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/18.
  The branch `l0rinc/reject-offcurve-loaded-pubkeys` is at `a665811228` on the local rebase of fork PR #11's checked-load commit (`71fb2a37c9`).
  The ordered stack first characterizes the current behavior (`0deac2a1d3`): loading, uncompressed serialization, and combination accept opaque `(1, 1)`, while parsing that uncompressed serialization rejects it.
  The follow-up (`a665811228`) checks curve validity and the exhaustive-build subgroup invariant in `secp256k1_pubkey_load`, then flips those three expectations to rejection.
  Removing the two new guards makes the focused EC test abort at `tests.c:6488` with exit `134`.
  Full VERIFY/no-VERIFY suites and exhaustive tests passed on default 5x52 and forced 10x26 builds.
  No open upstream or fork PR owns this focused loader check.

### 2026-07-20 post-push recheck and ECDSA candidate (superseded above)

At this point no upstream or fork PR owned the ECDSA context-routing change; it was subsequently pushed as fork PR #19.
The runtime SHA256 compression API was introduced to cover internal SHA256 operations, but explicit RFC6979/default nonce aliases still call their static-context wrapper.
Their outputs remain correct because installed compression functions are verified SHA256-equivalent, so this is **Low / API correctness and future backend performance**, not a cryptographic or security defect.
Bitcoin Core currently passes `secp256k1_nonce_function_rfc6979` explicitly when signing, but it does not currently install the compression override.

Selected and rebased it locally as `l0rinc/ecdsa-nonce-context-hash` at `144e38eb18` (`ecdsa: use context SHA256 for RFC6979 aliases`).
The one-commit patch recognizes the two built-in aliases in the shared normal/recoverable ECDSA signing helper, routes them through the supplied context, and documents the equivalent behavior for both sign APIs.
Arbitrary nonce callbacks retain direct dispatch.
The existing ECDSA context-SHA test now keeps its installed probe, proves both explicit aliases use it, and compares their signatures with the `noncefp == NULL` path.
Temporarily restoring the old `noncefp == NULL` dispatch makes the focused ECDSA test abort at `tests.c:7668` with exit `134`.
Full VERIFY/no-VERIFY C suites passed on default 5x52 and forced 10x26 builds, and recovery-enabled focused VERIFY/no-VERIFY tests plus the full VERIFY suite passed.
The matching origin branch is intentionally `[gone]` until a push.

Keep the analogous ECDH change (latest broad source `62516511a0`, previously `955dabab92`) separate.
It is the same Low callback-routing class but has no additional current Bitcoin Core call-site motivation.
After it, the test-only BER generator fix remains a lower-priority unowned candidate.

Triaged below. **Bottom line unchanged: still NO high-severity, remotely-triggerable vulnerability.** The new work adds three genuine but latent/low-severity memory-safety/availability bugs (all sanitizer- or timeout-provable, none remotely reachable) plus a batch of opaque-object-validation hardening and one more perf commit.

**NEW real bugs on `upstream/master` (all verified present):**

* [x] **Low-Medium / availability (hang) / exported symbol:** `e862628678 nonce: reject RFC6979 maximum attempt`.
  `nonce_function_rfc6979_impl` loops `for (i = 0; i <= counter; i++)` (`upstream/master:src/secp256k1.c:524`). With `counter == UINT_MAX` the `unsigned int` counter wraps after the last iteration and the loop never terminates — an **infinite hang**. Reachable via the **exported** `secp256k1_nonce_function_rfc6979` (`include/secp256k1.h:680`) with `counter=UINT_MAX`, which is a *valid* `unsigned int` (no ARG_CHECK violation), or by any custom signing loop that forwards an untrusted attempt counter. Ordinary `secp256k1_ecdsa_sign` starts the counter at 0 and can never reach 2^32 retries, so the default path is safe — this is a direct-callback DoS, not a crypto compromise. Upstream PR #1890 merged as `9e4ec507` and terminates the loop while preserving the valid maximum-counter result; no further action remains.
* [x] **Low / internal memory-safety (stack OOB read) / sanitizer-provable:** `422bab2721 scalar: guard rounded multiply shifts above product width`.
  `secp256k1_scalar_mul_shift_var` documents `shift >= 256` but indexes the fixed 512-bit product `l[8]`/`l[16]` at `(shift-1)>>6` for the rounding bit; `shift >= 513` reads one past the array (ASan: `scalar_4x64_impl.h` index 8 / `scalar_8x32_impl.h` index 16). Confirmed on `upstream/master` (`uint64_t l[8]`, unguarded rounding-bit read). **Latent:** the only in-tree caller passes the constant `384` (`scalar_impl.h:166-167`) and no public API reaches a caller-controlled shift. Split and pushed as focused fork PR #13.
* [x] **Low / parser UB (pointer-overflow) / contract-violation-gated:** `52cb1af7ad ecdsa: parse DER lengths with offsets`.
  `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_der` forms `sigend = sig + size` (`upstream/master:src/ecdsa_impl.h:142`) before validating; a caller passing `size=SIZE_MAX` triggers pointer-overflow UB (`-fsanitize=pointer-overflow`: `ecdsa_impl.h:142`) even when byte 0 already rejects the encoding. Requires the caller to violate the documented "input points to `inputlen` bytes" contract, so not remote/wire-reachable. Split and pushed as fork PR #14 from `l0rinc/ecdsa-der-size-offsets` at `b5e61084c6`; no upstream owner found.

**NEW hardening batches (all misuse/corruption-gated — NOT remote):**

* [ ] **Low-Medium / opaque-object loader-invariant hardening (~15 commits):** ~~`334bae0de4` (ec off-curve)~~, `2b7a931a0e`/`64250f7c5b`/`f812b84240` (noncanonical field storage in pubkey/musig-nonce/xonly), ~~`786bd4b38d` (ECDSA opaque scalar overflow; pushed as fork PR #25)~~/~~`6c8a008b0d` (current rewrite `c0623f5a1d`; recovery opaque scalar/ID validation prepared locally as `68375d5426`)~~, `9e7060530c` (keypair sec/pub consistency), `2b2c15ddac`/`1a5f517de8`/`cefe4c8661`/`9484be8fb9`/`ee7f44cde0`/`5b7ae25aa7`/`0863a8bbfb`/`3c1d67b2d4` (musig session/keyagg/nonce/partial-sig validation).
  Self-rated Medium, but every one states the trigger requires **local opaque-object corruption or direct API misuse — never `_parse` of wire input**. On the doc's reachability rubric this is the same **Low** class as the pushed `l0rinc/reject-invalid-loaded-pubkeys` (fork PR #18) work: it strengthens loader invariants. More defensible than the declined clear-on-failure pattern; potentially upstreamable as loader-consistency, but not urgent. The `334bae0de4` off-curve slice is now pushed as `l0rinc/reject-offcurve-loaded-pubkeys` at `a665811228` after characterization commit `0deac2a1d3`; the remaining entries stay open.
* [ ] **Low / clear-on-failure (declined #1850 pattern):** `36a009fe2f` (contrib DER export), `5bd9ae8946` (ecmult partial result), `bb15eb0698` (ecdh explicit-callback output). All self-rated Low; callers must honor the WARN_UNUSED_RESULT return. Same class already triaged as low/declined.
* [ ] **Low / arithmetic width/alias hardening (split from `104f53eae5`, now individually materialized with fuzz proofs):** `a42b2bc8b7 ecmult: make generic WNAF arithmetic width-safe` (latent w>=31), `61259f9c02 group: make gej rescale scale alias-safe` (no aliasing caller on master), plus `422bab2721` above. Severity unchanged from the `104f53eae5` cluster entry — latent, no reachable caller.
* [ ] **Performance (behavior-preserving), not a bug:** `42d7954789 field: serialize elements by word` is the **10x26** analog of the reviewed/pushed 5x52 serializer — four `write_be32` word packs replacing per-byte stores (`91e4f0283c` is byte-identical to local `l0rinc/field-5x52-serialize-word`). Same optimization class; verify byte-exactly and bench separately before any split.

Net: the original priority was **RFC6979 loop termination > scalar OOB > DER UB**.
The RFC6979 loop-termination and scalar fixes are tracked by upstream PR #1890 and focused fork PR #13; the DER UB is now fork PR #14.
None is a drop-everything CVE.

### 2026-07-10 upstream ownership correction

A complete pass over all open upstream PRs/issues and the merged SHA256 work changes the recommendation above. Keep `l0rinc/sha256-finalize-direct` only as a local experiment; **do not push it**.

* Merged upstream PR #1777 already made SHA256 compression runtime-pluggable: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1777. The API accepts a C function pointer (not a full hash replacement) and is explicitly intended for SHA-NI/ARMv8 implementations. Open issue #702 still tracks a possible compile-time override: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/702.
* The callback does **not** bypass this branch's code: secp256k1 deliberately retains message buffering, padding, and finalization and delegates only 64-byte compression blocks. The focused patch would remain compatible, but its measured absolute saving is only about 1-3 ns per benchmarked operation. That is too small to prioritize when downstreams such as Bitcoin Core can replace the dominant compression work.
* PR #1777 links an illustrative Bitcoin Core commit wiring `SHA256AutoDetect()` / its selected transform into secp256k1: https://github.com/furszy/bitcoin-core/commit/f68bef06d95a589859f98fc898dd80ab2e35eb39. No associated `bitcoin/bitcoin` PR was found, and the example predates the final API rename from `transform_callback` to `sha256_compression`, so it is evidence of intended integration rather than merge-ready current code.
* Open upstream PR #1801 touches SHA256 finalization only to add explicit narrowing casts: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1801. It does not implement direct final-block construction, but it would conflict textually and further lowers the value of proposing a marginal cleanup now.
* Open upstream PR #1785 already owns the exact `gej_rescale` alias bug from new fuzz commit `61259f9c02`: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1785. Its discussion already asks for an alias regression test or, preferably, an explicit no-alias contract. The pushed patch is correct; the missing-test concern is already on record, so no duplicate comment is needed. The fuzz branch's y/z-only regression also omits the x-alias case that #1785 identifies as the silent-corruption path.
* Open upstream PR #1795 owns both generic WNAF cleanup and the `w=31` signed-overflow finding from `a42b2bc8b7`: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1795. It deliberately narrows the internal helper to `w <= 30`; current production windows are <=24. Preserving the unused w=31 domain with wider temporaries is not a separate priority.
* Open upstream PR #1789 replaces the `ecmult_multi` cost model: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1789. Do not split PR #4 commits 54-71, which retune individual Pippenger thresholds against the old planner.
* Merged upstream PR #1825 already supersedes PR #4's tagged-hash initialization cleanup (`09c548123d`) with `secp256k1_sha256_initialize_midstate`: https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1825. Merged #1859 owns the 5x52 force-inline work, and merged `307b49f1b9` owns the EllSwift overflow fix.
* Other active performance work touching the same broad areas includes #1197 (constant-time modinv), #1703 (draft Intel SIMD, including SHA256/field/scalar), #1883 (variable-time generator multiplication), and #1028 (constant-time normalization). These are not exact duplicates of every PR #4 commit, but they make the broad stack a poor source for another unsynchronized optimization series.

No obvious correctness error was found in the pushed upstream versions that warrants a new public comment. The two tempting comments (alias regression coverage in #1785 and the w=31 boundary in #1795) are already addressed by existing review discussion or by the pushed implementation's deliberate contract choice.

None uses the four-word `write_be64` form. No new characterization test was added because this is behavior-preserving and existing `field_convert`, `field_be32_overflow`, and utility big-endian tests already exercise the byte mapping; secp256k1 has no functional-test layer.

Isolated verification on an Apple M4 Max, using separate Release builds of `upstream/master` and the one-commit candidate:
* full `bin/tests` passed with AppleClang 21 (16.183s) and GCC 14.4 (17.922s); both exhaustive suites reported `no problems found`;
* a temporary, uncommitted `get_b32` + `set_b32_mod` roundtrip benchmark used four changing field values so the compiler could not eliminate serialization; 10 interleaved `SECP256K1_BENCH_ITERS=100000` runs had medians AppleClang `0.006895 -> 0.005880 us` (-14.7%) and GCC `0.006970 -> 0.004005 us` (-42.5%);
* end-to-end `ecdsa_sign`, `ec_keygen`, and `schnorrsig_sign` rows remained within noise, so the inherited broad-stack API claims were removed;
* `secp256k1_fe_impl_get_b32` shrank from 372 to 268 bytes under AppleClang and from 384 to 80 bytes under GCC; GCC emits four `rev`/64-bit-store pairs. A five-local limb snapshot experiment made generated code larger under both compilers and was discarded.

The final commit message uses only this isolated evidence. The branch tracks the matching absent `origin/l0rinc/field-5x52-serialize-word`; nothing was pushed.

The complete production call-site audit confirms these were the only public API paths that ignored `secp256k1_pubkey_load` failure. Every other API caller consumes the status; the one remaining unchecked internal MuSig aggregation callback documents that the same keys were already loaded and uses `VERIFY_CHECK(ret)`. Code links at the reviewed base: checked public-key serialization at https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/ebf594320dc838b9de1abb54d5ba98cef84f4297/src/secp256k1.c#L300, the old ECDH omission at https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/ebf594320dc838b9de1abb54d5ba98cef84f4297/src/modules/ecdh/main_impl.h#L48, the old combine omission at https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/ebf594320dc838b9de1abb54d5ba98cef84f4297/src/secp256k1.c#L804, and the deliberate MuSig invariant at https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/blob/ebf594320dc838b9de1abb54d5ba98cef84f4297/src/modules/musig/keyagg_impl.h#L144.

Severity remains **low / defense-in-depth**, not a vulnerability claim. Failed public-key parse, negate, and tweak calls can leave the opaque object invalidated to all zeroes. Reachability therefore requires a caller to ignore one of those failures and install a non-aborting illegal callback; on old master, reusing that object in ECDH or combine triggers the callback but can still return success after continuing with invalid group state. Normal callers and the default aborting callback do not reach that continuation.

After external review, the final subject is `ecdh, ec: check pubkey_load return`. The body records the complete call-site result, the realistic invalidated-object misuse chain, and the internal MuSig invariant. The fork-only `(cherry picked from ...)` trailer was dropped because this focused patch retains only part of the broad source commit; provenance remains in this triage note and the PR-description source links above.

Verification for `d1dca5c1c3` (secp256k1 has no Python functional-test layer; these are focused C API tests):
* `cmake --build build --target tests -j 8`
* `build/bin/tests -t=ecdh --iterations=1 --seed=00000000000000000000000000000001` passed.
* `build/bin/tests -t=ec --iterations=1 --seed=00000000000000000000000000000002` passed.
* mutation proof: temporarily restored only the two unchecked production calls while retaining the final tests; ECDH failed with exit 134 at `src/modules/ecdh/tests_impl.h:52`, and combine failed with exit 134 at `src/tests.c:6475`, both because the old API returned success after the illegal callback.
* restored the committed guards, rebuilt, and reran both focused filters successfully with the same seeds.
* `build/bin/tests --iterations=1 --seed=00000000000000000000000000000003` passed in 14.644 seconds; three iteration-gated tests reported their normal skip messages (`run_sha256_known_output_tests`, `test_ecmult_constants_sha`, and `test_ecmult_constants_2bit`).
* final diff is one commit, four files, 17 insertions / 2 removals; `git diff --check upstream/master..HEAD` passed.

================================================================================
### EXECUTIVE TRIAGE — is there a high-severity vuln to apply urgently?
================================================================================

**No.** There is **no externally-triggerable, high-severity vulnerability** anywhere in these branches that needs an urgent patch to master. No valid-domain public API input here enables signature forgery, key recovery, or a supported 64-bit crash. The reproducible NULL crashes require direct contract-violating API/callback misuse; the most plausible one, EllSwift prefix hashing without its required data, is already owned by upstream #1806.

**The formerly highest-ranked correctness finding** was the 10x26 magnitude-32
normalize overflow (broad fork PR **#10** `boundary-condition-bugs`, now focused fork PR **#16**). It is:
  - **real** (silently wrong field residue or false zero result), verified by hand + bit-exact replica + 3 adversarial lenses;
  - **10x26-only** (the 5x52 path has ~12 bits of headroom and is unaffected);
  - **latent** — audited production paths use smaller magnitudes, and supported public APIs do not expose field elements directly;
  - valid only in the internal representation contract, but not currently reachable through a public API or audited production path; the focused test constructs it with test-only bounds helpers.

→ **Current disposition:** fork PR #16 owns the cleaned branch `l0rinc/field-10x26-normalize-overflow`.
  The production-reachability audit rates it **Low / latent internal hardening**, not Medium: it remains a
  worthwhile defensive field fix, but not urgent triage work or a drop-everything CVE.

→ **Candidate promoted:** `l0rinc/tests-ber-lengths` is open draft fork PR #21 at remote head `15c667cb`, with current local amended tip `c78266aed9`.
  It remains a test-only BER generator correction, not an urgent vulnerability patch. The focused patch
  fixes multi-byte length encoding and pins the strict-reject/lax-accept parser relation.

Everything else is either (a) already merged upstream, (b) only in broad/batched fork PRs or overlapped by active upstream PRs and still needs split-by-item judgment, (c) low-value
defense-in-depth / secret-hygiene that mostly mirrors the upstream-**declined** clear-on-failure pattern
(#1850), (d) performance-only — several of which are active **constant-time hazards** that must NOT be
upstreamed — or (e) fuzz-harness test infrastructure. Details below.


================================================================================
### SEVERITY TABLE
================================================================================

--- LOW: latent internal 10x26 correctness hardening ---------------------------

* [x] **`65d38b0c4e` field_10x26: fix magnitude-32 normalize overflow** — broad fork PR **#10**, split and pushed as focused fork PR **#16** from `l0rinc/field-10x26-normalize-overflow`
  (`origin/boundary-condition-bugs`); current rewritten fuzz-branch equivalent `cf5631fa16` (old fuzz hash `5aa20c645a`).
  In the 10x26 backend, `secp256k1_fe_impl_normalize` / `_normalize_weak` / `_normalize_var` and
  `normalizes_to_zero{,_var}` carry the first reduction pass through `uint32_t` temporaries. For an in-contract magnitude-32 element
  (field.h documents magnitude ∈ [0,32]; `fe_add` allows magnitude sums ≤ 32; VERIFY's `fe_verify`
  accepts it) the worst case `t0 = 0xFFFFFFC0 + 63·0x3D1 = 0x10000F02F` overflows `UINT32_MAX`, dropping
  carry bits and silently producing a wrong residue < p that passes every `VERIFY_CHECK`. Fix: uint64
  carry accumulator; branchless, constant-time-preserving, bit-identical for magnitude ≤ 31.
  - Independently reproduced: correct `64·(2²⁵⁶−1) mod p` = `0x400000F400`; master's uint32 chain
    returns the value short by `2³² + 2⁵⁸ (mod p)`. Magnitude 31 is provably safe (`t0 ≤ 0xF800E88F`).
  - The zero predicates have the same overflow: the verify-valid magnitude-32 input
    `{0xFFFF0F91, 0xFFFFF040, 0, ..., 0x0FC00000}` has a nonzero residue, but the old chain reports zero.
    The focused patch uses the 64-bit carry in all five paths and tests that counterexample plus a magnitude-32 zero.
  - Magnitude 32 is only a conservative static upper bound. No current API or production call path was
    found that drives actual limbs into the overflow band, and instrumented full tests did not reach it.
    The focused test constructs the boundary through test-only bounds helpers. This makes the issue Low and
    latent despite the real internal arithmetic error.
  - Distinct from merged #1877 (that only fixed the `fe_equal` VERIFY bound). New oracle `139f6ab9c1`
    independently preserves the same 10x26 failure boundary and was verified failing on `upstream/master`
    in the forced-10x26 mutation replay. Focused fork PR #16 now owns the cleaned patch.

--- LOW: genuine secret-lifetime hygiene gaps (broad fork PR source; some upstream overlap) ---
Real gaps in upstream's own memclear policy, but pure defense-in-depth: unreachable without a *separate*
in-process stack-disclosure primitive; upstream merges this class as routine hardening (#1849), not as
security fixes. Verifiers downgraded the analysts' "medium" to "low" on every one.

* [x] `5aa2934dec` / `c592412b24` **ecmult: clear const multiplication temporaries** — fork PR **#8**
  (`origin/detached20`; `c592412b24` also on all `rpi5-16-3-secp/*` branches). `secp256k1_ecmult_const`
  and `_xonly` leave secret-window-selected table points (`t`, `neg_y`) and the ellswift shared-secret
  Jacobian point (`rj`, `i`) live on the stack after every `secp256k1_ecdh` / `ellswift_xdh`. Note:
  the patch is **incomplete** — `s`, `v1`, `v2` (which fully determine the secret scalar) stay uncleared
  even after it, so the ~5 window bits it wipes buy little.
* [x] `0e3bd1247e` / `9e84216a65` **ecmult: clear split scalar temporaries** — fork PR **#1**
  (`origin/detached`). Clears seckey-equivalent `s`/`v1`/`v2` and `c1`/`c2`. Caveat: its
  `ecmult_endo_split tmp` hunk sits on the var-time verification-only path and contradicts upstream
  policy (e7d384488e "don't clear secrets in pippenger"); upstream would likely ask to drop it.
* [x] `b97aa6a0b3` **ellswift: clear encoding RNG state** — fork PR **#1**. The `ellswift_create`
  local SHA256 buffer retains the raw 32-byte private key in `buf[0..31]` on the BIP324 path when
  `auxrnd32 == NULL` (traced through `sha256_write`). The `sha256_clear(&hash)` in `create` is the one
  solid upstream candidate; the encode-path clears protect only public/output-derived data.
* [x] `1de0d0e9c2` **hash: clear finalized secret hash state** — fork PR **#1**. RFC6979/HMAC locals
  keep DRBG intermediates. Verifier: the HMAC *key* K never persists (rkey/temp/rng already cleared),
  so even a full disclosure can't recover the nonce → **low**; also reverses a deliberate upstream
  design (finalize kept a no-op on purpose) so it would likely be re-shaped or declined. New internal
  fuzz target `a97a9eda10` proves the proposed zero-after-finalize contract, but does not add a read primitive
  or change this severity; the normal RFC6979 caller already calls the explicit clear after finalize.
* [x] `50229825c0` **musig: clear partial-sign secrets on errors** — fork PR **#1**. Master's
  `musig_partial_sign` leaves secret nonce scalars `k` (and `sk` on the mismatch path) uncleared when
  the post-`secnonce_load` ARG_CHECKs fail — but every such path is out-of-contract misuse gated behind
  a non-aborting illegal callback. Real inconsistency, low severity.

--- LOW: API-hardening / misuse guards (broad fork PR source) ------------------
All target conditions that still exist on master are reachable only through contract-violating misuse
and a non-aborting illegal callback. Most are the "clear outputs on failure" pattern upstream **declined
in closed PR #1850**. The invalid-`pubkey_load` fix is distinct: its clean split checks an existing return
value and omits all output-clearing policy.

* [x] The musig clear-on-failure family: `06a5867c58`, `3ae8e2d851`, `a6eaa9a44f`, `bec8771373`,
  `3a87693b4f`, `4236ba0ce7`, `409f00dd93`, `14191ade2f` (fork PRs #1/#2, dup on `musig-cleanup-failures`,
  `origin/detached2`, `origin/detached3`). Non-secret outputs (pubnonces, aggnonces, sessions, partial/
  final sigs, keyagg cache).
* [x] `30bbc68e84` **musig: clear failed nonce gen pubnonces** — this **IS** the closed/declined
  upstream #1850 re-spun with the late-`memczero` style real-or-random specifically objected to.
  Severity **none** (contrary to recorded upstream consensus). Dup on `musig-clear-invalid-seckey-pubnonce`,
  `l0rinc/musig-nonce-gen-pr1849-followup`.
* [x] `81473773c2`, `212a00bee6`, `7d411c656c`, `b1b44198ec`, `8d2d89bbb0`, `ddea472f5d`, `f3a3a3766c`,

  - `2ffca2dc86` (current fork source `f1e3eba202`) **ec: reject invalid loaded pubkeys** — master's `ecdh`/`ec_pubkey_combine` ignore
    `pubkey_load`'s return and can return success (1) after the illegal callback fires on an invalid

  - `5e70ebf32f` SHA256 length guard: 2⁶¹-byte boundary is physically unreachable → defense-in-depth only.

* [x] **Published as fork draft PR [#27](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/27):**

  `clean/opt-ellswift-decode`.

the corresponding ECDH results were within run noise.

do not support claiming a measurable improvement without a relevant Linux/GCC

### 2026-07-26 selected group x-coordinate copy simplification
================================================================================

Refs and ownership were refreshed after the silentpayments merge at
`upstream/master` `d2d04864ef`. No open upstream or focused fork PR owns
`secp256k1_gej_add_ge_var` / `secp256k1_gej_add_zinv_var` x-coordinate copy

* [x] **Published as fork PR [#28](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/28):**
  `l0rinc/group-avoid-x-copy`, based on `upstream/master` `d2d04864ef`, tracks
  matching `origin/l0rinc/group-avoid-x-copy` at `833eaaa22c`.
  The branch has two intentionally separate commits:
  `52061c6b1a` adds exhaustive in-place characterization for both helpers;
  `833eaaa22c` removes their redundant local `a->x` copies.
  The direct reads are safe because each helper reads `a->x` before it writes
  `r->x`, including when `r == a`.

The characterization runs every pair in the order-13 exhaustive group, with
the output aliasing the Jacobian input. Full VERIFY and no-VERIFY test suites,
plus `exhaustive_tests 1`, passed with AppleClang 22 and GCC 14 on both default
5x52 and forced-10x26 builds. Interleaved `bench_internal add` measurements
were noisy and showed no stable runtime change, so frame this as a readability

### 2026-07-29 selected xor-mask 5x52 cmov simplification
================================================================================

Refs were refreshed after upstream #1900.
Fork PR #4 was fetched as `origin/pr/4` and still matches `origin/detached5`
at `b9a169beab`.
The broad PR remains source material only because it carries constant-time
hazards.
The local Jacobian-doubling extraction was later refreshed as
`l0rinc/group-avoid-double-var-infinity-copy` at signed `c0bbc93f0d` and folded
into `l0rinc/group-jacobian-copy-cleanups` as commit 5.
Do not treat it as a separate next PR candidate.

* [x] **Pushed to personal fork:** `l0rinc/field-xormask-cmov` at signed
  `2c85991afd14b20dab81d309bb11aa6ce03fe10b`, based on `upstream/master`
  `0a9e788901` and matching `origin/l0rinc/field-xormask-cmov`.
  Earlier local pre-push tip `7ff7e8d8b78b77a413229a8bc351c72018fd8287`
  is historical only.
  Source: cleaned `rpi5-8gb-500gb-secp/opt-xormask-cmov` commits
  `3b3fc45a99260e1163df968491e174126a7ab0d4` and
  `6a9fc991081fc14ed13151baa1407260ecb73ea7`, squashed into one focused
  branch commit.

The patch changes both 5x52 field cmovs from the two-mask blend
`(r & mask0) | (a & mask1)` to the equivalent xor-mask select
`r ^= mask & (r ^ a)`.
It deliberately keeps deriving the mask from the existing volatile `vflag`.
That volatile load is the current constant-time defense against Clang turning
secret table selection into a branch after inlining.

Validation: `git diff --check upstream/master..HEAD` clean; default and
forced-10x26 builds of `tests` and `noverify_tests` completed; `tests 16` and
`noverify_tests 16` passed on both backends.
The signed commit was verified with `git verify-commit HEAD`.
Local `ctime_tests` could not be built because this machine has neither
Valgrind nor MSan support; the cleaned source branch records passing x86_64
Valgrind `ctime_tests`, but this still needs independent constant-time/codegen
review before upstreaming.
A small AppleClang 21 Release `bench_ecmult` run with
`SECP256K1_BENCH_ITERS=100` was too noisy for a PR performance claim; use the
source branch's AArch64 measurements only as directional context unless a
proper repeated benchmark pass is run.

### CONSTANT-TIME HAZARD — performance branches, do NOT upstream/deploy as-is
================================================================================

The optimization stacks are performance-only (spot-checked `c8cdf159ed` wnaf_small rewrite and
`3a5e9f3a23` strauss no==1 fastpath: exact behavior preservation, no hidden fixes; the only
correctness-adjacent commit, ellswift-xdh overflow, is test-only on these branches with its production
fix already upstream). **But several weaken deliberate constant-time defenses on the secret-dependent
`ecmult_gen` / `ecmult_const` table-selection path (every sign / keygen):**

* [ ] `8997837d85` (older equivalent `543364964b`) **field: drop volatile in `fe_storage_cmov`** — HIGHEST CT hazard: removing the
  volatile mask lets the compiler prove `mask ∈ {0,-1}` and legally lower the select to a
  secret-dependent branch. Present in `origin/detached4`, `detached5` / `l0rinc/ci-fix-pr4`, and all
  `rpi5-16-2-secp/backup/*`. Must never be upstreamed.
* [ ] `cfd389b2b2` / `7e138f1fa1` (older equivalent `eac1d2fead`) NEON `fe_storage_cmov` / `fe_cmov` variants — CT hazard (the author's own
  `104f53eae5` audit reverted the NEON path citing exactly this). Present across the same stacks.
* [ ] `c08f30fd28` / `f96162916e` (older equivalents `80203e2923` / `ced8587c17`) **xor-mask fe/storage cmov** (`l0rinc/optimization-pruned`,
  `tmp/optimization-inline-unsplit`, `origin/detached7..13`) — moderate (keeps the volatile read) but
  still changes load-bearing CT lowering; needs valgrind/ctgrind evidence before any upstreaming.

Branches carrying the drop-volatile / NEON commits (`detached4`, `detached5`, `l0rinc/ci-fix-pr4`,
`rpi5-16-2-secp` backups) are unsafe as a whole for CT-sensitive (signing) use. `detached5` = fork PR #4.

## 2026-07-26 recovery opaque-signature PR refresh

* [x] **Published as fork PR [#30](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/30):** draft
  `l0rinc/reject-invalid-recoverable-signatures` is at `68375d5426` on
  `upstream/master` `d2d04864ef`. It has one commit,
  `recovery: reject invalid opaque signatures`, and its matching origin branch
  points at the same SHA.
* Compact parsing already rejects scalar components at or above the group order
  and recovery IDs outside `0..3`. The PR covers the separate path where an
  application mutates or constructs an opaque recoverable signature after
  parsing or signing. The shared loader now invokes the illegal callback and
  returns `0` before serialization, conversion, or recovery use invalid state.
  Malformed compact input is unaffected, and failure-output behavior remains
  unchanged.
* Current overlap search found no matching open fork PR and no open upstream PR
  with recoverable-signature or opaque-signature validation in its title/body.
  This is low-severity caller-misuse hardening, not a network or parser bug.
* Exact validation: `tests --iterations=1` and `noverify_tests --iterations=1`
  passed with seed `5eed6837` on default 5x52 and forced-10x26 builds.
  `exhaustive_tests 1 5eed6837` passed on both order-13 builds. With only the
  three loader `ARG_CHECK`s removed, the default VERIFY recovery test aborts at
  `scalar_impl.h:43` and the no-VERIFY recovery test fails its expected
  serialization rejection at `tests_impl.h:99`. Restoring the checks and
  rebuilding makes both focused recovery runs pass.

## 2026-07-25 PR #35531 historical txindex suggestion stack

* [x] **Current author head refreshed:** upstream [#35531](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35531) is open at `40c4684bda`, and `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/pr-tmp-35531` points at that exact head.
