### Correction that demotes two previously-ranked P2P items

The 2026-08-01 entry ranked `ba05bf48fe` (BIP37 filter vectors) second, on the premise that "a five-byte declaration reserves up to 4 MB before the size check". The new `9a1531ee8b` ("net: bound getblocktxn request indexes", on `i9/codex/goal7-getblocktxn-20260801`) makes the identical argument for `BlockTransactionsRequest::indexes` via `LimitedVectorFormatter<MAX_INDEXES, DifferenceFormatter>`. Both premises are **materially overstated**, and this was missed the first time: **[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-02: demoted - `VectorFormatter`/vector unserialize already batch allocations at `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE`=5,000,000 by design, so this is defense in depth, not a DoS. See the 2026-08-02 entry.]**

* `VectorFormatter::Unser` (`src/serialize.h:685-693`) already allocates in batches with the explicit comment *"For DoS prevention, do not blindly allocate as much as the stream claims to contain. Instead, allocate in 5MiB batches, so that an attacker actually needs to provide X MiB of data to make us allocate X+5 MiB."*
* The default `std::vector` unserializer (`src/serialize.h:920-930`) does the same for byte vectors: *"Limit size per read so bogus size value won't cause out of memory"*, blocks of `1 + 4999999/sizeof(T)`.
* `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE = 5000000` (`src/serialize.h:38`).

So neither path allows unbounded allocation from a short message. The worst case is a **single transient over-allocation bounded at ~5 MB**, which is the accepted cost of the existing streaming design, after which the read fails and the peer errors out. The bloom case reaches 4 MB only because `MAX_BLOOM_FILTER_SIZE`-sized declarations happen to sit under the 5 MB batch; it is not an amplification the serializer failed to anticipate. Both commits are legitimate **defense-in-depth tightenings that move a limit earlier**, not DoS fixes — and a reviewer will say exactly that. `ba05bf48fe` drops out of the top ranks; `9a1531ee8b` never enters. Neither is worth a PR ahead of items with an actual healthy-node consequence. **[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-02: demoted - `VectorFormatter`/vector unserialize already batch allocations at `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE`=5,000,000 by design, so this is defense in depth, not a DoS. See the 2026-08-02 entry.]**

Method note: "unbounded allocation from a short declaration" claims in this campaign must be checked against `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE` batching before being ranked. That check was skipped on 2026-08-01.

### txgraph branch — the fuzz-invariant blocker was found and fixed

The 2026-08-01 form of `475ab49da6` broke a documented invariant that an existing fuzz target asserts. `src/txgraph.h:208-213` promises usage "just counting the main graph"; `src/test/fuzz/txgraph.cpp:1049-1053` asserts `if (main_sim.GetTransactionCount() == 0) assert(usage == 0);`. Because `memusage::DynamicUsage` is capacity-based, a main graph churned to empty still reported non-zero — no staging required. The current tip adds `if (m_main_clusterset.m_txcount == 0) return 0;` before the sum, which restores the asserted invariant.

* [ ] **Residual gap, not yet resolved:** `m_entries` is "the set of all transactions (in all levels combined)" (`src/txgraph.cpp:627`), so with a non-empty main graph and an open staging session the reported number still includes staging-only entries, contradicting "as if `AbortStaging()` would be called". The fuzz harness does not catch this (it only asserts the zero case), and the sole production caller cannot reach it — `validation.cpp:1730-1732` states it is "not permitted to invoke `LimitMempoolSize()` while a changeset is outstanding". It remains the first question sipa is likely to ask, since he wrote both the function and the contract in merged #33157. Raise it in the PR description rather than waiting for review to find it. ## 2026-08-02 TxGraph memory-accounting review findings and PR #262 exposure

Consolidates the review findings on `l0rinc/txgraph-retained-entry-usage` that were not previously written down, and records which pushed work is exposed.

### Exposure check across pushed work — exactly one PR affected

* [ ] **Fork PR l0rinc/bitcoin#262 (`txgraph: account for retained Entry capacity`, head `475ab49da607`) needs a description change, not a code change.** Its body currently states the problem, the fix, and the test, but says nothing about the staging contract. Add the caveat there rather than letting review surface it — see below for the exact issue.
* [x] **Fork PR #254 (`l0rinc/txgraph-equal-feerate-prefix-overflow`) is adjacent but not in conflict.** It edits the same two files (`src/txgraph.cpp`, `src/test/txgraph_tests.cpp`), and `gh pr diff 254` matches `m_entries` twice — but both are incidental context reads at `GenericClusterImpl::Updated`/`SanityCheck` (~lines 1125-1140, ~2875), nowhere near `GetMainMemoryUsage()` (~3553). No semantic overlap. The only cost is that whichever merges second may need a trivial rebase, since both append a test case at the end of `txgraph_tests.cpp`.
* [x] **No upstream PR is exposed.** Checked the file lists of every open l0rinc upstream PR that could plausibly reach this code (#35744, #35714, #34132, #33324): none touches `src/txgraph.cpp`.
* [x] **PR #262's other siblings (#238, #228) are mempool fee-saturation work**, not memory accounting; no interaction.

### The staging contract issue, in full

`src/txgraph.h:208-213` documents `GetMainMemoryUsage()` as counting "just the main graph", and that "if a staging graph is present, return a number corresponding to memory usage after `AbortStaging()` would be called". `m_entries` is declared as "the set of all transactions (in all levels combined)" (`src/txgraph.cpp:627`), and `AddTransaction` appends to it unconditionally regardless of level. Only the per-level `m_txcount` — which the old formula used — was level-scoped.

Consequences, separated by whether they are actually reachable:

* [x] **The fuzz-breaking case is already fixed.** `src/test/fuzz/txgraph.cpp:1049-1053` asserts `if (main_sim.GetTransactionCount() == 0) assert(usage == 0);`. Because `memusage::DynamicUsage` is capacity-based (`MallocUsage(capacity() * sizeof(T))`, `src/memusage.h:88-92`), a main graph churned to empty reported non-zero — **no staging required**, so this was a plain, easily-fuzzed break. The current tip's `if (m_main_clusterset.m_txcount == 0) return 0;` restores the invariant.
* [ ] **The staging over-count remains.** With a non-empty main graph and an open staging session, the reported number still includes staging-only entries, contradicting the "as if `AbortStaging()`" wording. The fuzz harness does not catch it (it only asserts the zero case). Production cannot reach it: `src/validation.cpp:1730-1732` states outright that "it's not permitted to invoke `LimitMempoolSize()` while a changeset is outstanding", and the sole production caller is `CTxMemPool::DynamicMemoryUsage()` (`src/txmempool.cpp:831`). So this is a contract/documentation defect, not a live `-maxmempool` hole — but sipa wrote both the function and the contract in merged #33157 and will ask. Decide up front whether to narrow the doc wording or special-case staging; do not let review discover it.

### Review findings worth keeping

* [x] **`memusage::DynamicUsage` is the convention in this file; the replaced line was the outlier.** `GenericClusterImpl::TotalMemoryUsage()` uses it for `m_mapping`/`m_linearization` (`src/txgraph.cpp:918`), and the very next term in `GetMainMemoryUsage()` already used it for `m_main_chunkindex`. The old `sizeof(Entry) * m_txcount` was the only hand-rolled size calculation. Worth stating in the PR description — it reframes the change as removing an inconsistency rather than introducing a new estimate.
* [x] **`shrink_to_fit()` in `Compact()` was considered and rejected, for a concrete reason.** Safety is not the obstacle: `Ref::m_index` (`src/txgraph.h:228-229`) stores a `GraphIndex` (`uint32_t`), not a pointer, and every `Entry&` in the file is a transient local, so reallocation would invalidate nothing. Cost is the obstacle: `Compact()` is the last statement of `ApplyRemovals()` (`:1745`), which is the first statement of `SplitAll()` (`:1845`), which runs from `StartStaging`, `CommitStaging` and `GetMainMemoryUsage()` itself — forcing a reallocate-and-move there turns an amortized `pop_back()` into an O(n) copy on the hot mempool-mutation path. Reporting honestly is the cheap half; reclaiming is a separate performance/policy trade-off. Note also that the per-cluster vectors are shrunk only inside `GenericClusterImpl::Compact()` (`:1374-1375`), which runs from `Split()` — i.e. only when the cluster is being rebuilt anyway. "Report capacity honestly, release it only as a side effect of work already being done" is the established pattern here.
* [ ] **The fix is a special case: three or four sibling containers have the same unaccounted retained capacity.** `m_unlinked` (`:631`, `.clear()` at `:1826`), `ClusterSet::m_to_remove` (`:437`, `.clear()` at `:1743`), and `ClusterSet::m_deps_to_add` (`:440`, `.clear()` at `:2150`) are never counted, but are bounded by burst size rather than by historical peak, so they do not matter much. **`ClusterSet::m_clusters[quality]` (`:435`) is the one worth a follow-up**: `ExtractCluster()` (`:1612-1636`) uses the same swap-with-back-then-`pop_back()` idiom, while `m_cluster_usage` only charges `sizeof(std::unique_ptr<Cluster>)` per *live* cluster (`:915-924`). Same bug class, same "grows with historical peak" character, roughly 8 bytes per slot instead of ~65-96 per `Entry`. Deliberately left out of #262 to keep it one mechanism per PR.
* [x] **A trap in the test that was removed before pushing.** An earlier form of the regression built the churn with `std::vector<TxGraph::Ref> refs(CHURN_COUNT)` plus two range-for loops and a trailing `refs.clear()`. That `clear()` looked like dead code but was load-bearing: leaving the 1024 stale `Ref`s alive through the final measurement made usage roughly double (163992 vs 82072 measured), so the `BOOST_CHECK_GT` still passed — but it was then measuring "more raw entries" rather than "compaction retains capacity", which is what the test claims. The pushed form uses a loop-scoped `Ref` so the trap cannot be reintroduced by someone tidying the line away.
* [x] **Cost is not a concern on either side.** `memusage::DynamicUsage` on a vector is O(1) arithmetic on `capacity()`, not an iteration, so the swap is free next to the `SplitAll()`/`ApplyDependencies()` calls that precede it — and `GetMainMemoryUsage()` genuinely sits on a per-accepted-transaction path via `TrimToSize()`'s `while (… DynamicMemoryUsage() > sizelimit)` guard (`src/txmempool.cpp:918`), so that mattered enough to check. The test's 1024-transaction churn measures at the same wall-clock as the trivial baseline (~0.25s, versus ~1.16s for the neighbouring 64000-transaction `txgraph_trim_huge`), because every churned transaction is a dependency-free singleton.

### Selected and prepared — `l0rinc/rpc-deduplicate-scan-objects`

Rebased cleanly from the old `67efced1fc` base onto `556988790a`; new signed tips `f27016533e` (`test: cover duplicate descriptor scans`) and `cf5841ea11` (`rpc: deduplicate descriptor scan objects`). Production change is +12 lines in `src/rpc/blockchain.cpp`: one `IsDuplicateScanObject()` helper that serializes each scan object once into a `std::set<std::string>`, applied identically in `scantxoutset` (`:2421`), `scanblocks` (`:2656`) and `getdescriptoractivity` (`:2815`).

Ownership: `gh search prs --repo bitcoin/bitcoin` for `scantxoutset duplicate`, `scan objects deduplicate` and `scanblocks descriptor duplicate` all return nothing in any state.

**Amplification reproduced locally on current master, not taken from the audit branch.** First attempt used an `addr()` descriptor and showed *no* amplification at all — 1 vs 100 duplicates both ~0.19s — because a single-script descriptor expands trivially and the needle set dedupes downstream. The effect needs a **ranged** descriptor, where each duplicate object re-derives the whole range. Regtest, 200 blocks, `{"desc": <ranged wallet descriptor>, "range": 3000}` repeated N times:

| duplicate scan objects | request size | upstream/master | branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | <1 KiB | 0.455s | 0.159s |
| 10 | 1 KiB | 3.686s | 0.159s |
| 50 | 8 KiB | 17.920s | 0.160s |

Linear in the duplicate count without the fix, flat with it — roughly 112x at 50 duplicates from an 8 KiB request. Note for the PR description: the honest framing is that cost scales with *number of ranged scan objects*, and byte-identical duplicates are the subset that provably cannot change the result, because all three RPCs insert derived scripts into a `std::set`/`ElementSet` downstream. Distinct descriptors and semantically-equivalent-but-textually-different objects are untouched.

Validation: `rpc_scantxoutset.py`, `rpc_scanblocks.py` and `rpc_getdescriptoractivity.py` all pass on the rebased branch (6s accumulated). Both commits carry good local GPG signatures. Nothing pushed.

Scope: authenticated-RPC CPU amplification, not an unauthenticated P2P vector — a caller who can reach `scantxoutset` can already ask for expensive scans. What the fix removes is the free multiplier on top of that, where request size stays flat while work grows linearly.

## 2026-08-02 scan-object dedup review findings

Review pass over `l0rinc/rpc-deduplicate-scan-objects` after the rebase. Three changes applied, and several findings that belong in the PR description rather than the code.

### Applied

* [x] **`std::set<std::string>` -> `std::unordered_set<std::string>`**, matching the in-tree precedent for this exact trick: `PushUniqueSchema` at `src/rpc/server.cpp:254-258` serializes a `UniValue` with `.write()` into a `std::unordered_set<std::string>` and tests `.insert(...).second`. Same directory, same idiom. The set is never iterated in order, and `scanblocks`' own downstream `GCSFilter::ElementSet` is unordered too (`src/blockfilter.h:32-33`). Note this is a **convention** fix, not a performance one — measured insert cost is indistinguishable between the two containers at n=6 (150.1 vs 151.9 ns) and only diverges past n≈50 (1.63x at 50, 2.88x at 20000). Do not claim a speedup from it.
* [x] **Dropped the incidental `#include <set>`.** The file uses `std::set<CScript>` and compiled without an explicit include before this branch, so adding one was an unrelated IWYU fix widening the diff. `#include <unordered_set>` is now the only include the change needs.
* [x] **Removed `"range": 1000` from the `addr()` scan object** in `test/functional/rpc_getdescriptoractivity.py`. `AddressDescriptor` is built with empty pubkey args (`src/script/descriptor.cpp:1129-1151`) so `IsRange()` is always false, and `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` resets the range to `{0, 0}` when `!IsRange()` (`src/rpc/util.cpp:1360-1363`). The field was parsed and discarded; the dict-form coverage it was there for is unaffected. Also renamed `duplicate_scan_object` to `scan_object` in `rpc_scantxoutset.py` so all three tests spell the fixture the same way.

Re-validated after the changes: `rpc_scantxoutset.py`, `rpc_scanblocks.py`, `rpc_getdescriptoractivity.py` all pass, and the amplification stays fixed (1/10/50 duplicate ranged objects: 0.165s / 0.163s / 0.161s).

### Much better evidence than the wall-clock numbers

The earlier regtest timings (17.9s vs 0.16s at 50 duplicates) measure the whole RPC. The mechanism is sharper than that: `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` calls `desc->Expand(i, provider, scripts, provider)` (`src/rpc/util.cpp:1368`) with the cache parameter left `nullptr`, so `BIP32PubkeyProvider::GetPubKey` (`src/script/descriptor.cpp:446-500`) performs a real `Derive()` — HMAC-SHA512 plus a secp256k1 pubkey derivation — **once per index in the range, per scan object, every time**. Measured against the build's own libs with the test suite's tprv: a full `Expand` over `range=[0,1000]` costs **65.8 ms** (65.8 us/index). So one skipped duplicate saves ~65.8 ms at the default range and, at the maximum permitted range of 1,000,000 indices (`src/rpc/util.cpp:1331-1333`), roughly **65.8 seconds**. The duplicate check itself costs **under 1 us per object** (`UniValue::write()` dominates it at ~936 ns) and is flat regardless of range. That asymmetry — flat cost, linearly-scaling saving — is the argument to lead with.

### Must be stated in the PR description

* [ ] **This fixes accidental exact repetition, not adversarial amplification.** The key is `scanobject.write()`, and `UniValue::writeObject` (`src/univalue/lib/univalue_write.cpp:93`) emits keys in insertion order with no sorting, so the guard is textual. Trivially dodged by alternating spellings: key order (`{"desc":X,"range":Y}` vs `{"range":Y,"desc":X}`), bare string vs object (`"addr(X)"` vs `{"desc":"addr(X)"}`, both defaulting to range `[0,1000]`), or equivalent range encodings (`{"range":3000}` vs `{"range":[0,3000]}`). Byte-identical is the right proportionate choice — true semantic normalization would re-implement much of `Parse`/`ParseDescriptorRange` just to build a comparison key — but the PR must say so plainly, so nobody later cites it as having closed a DoS vector it did not.
* [ ] **Known follow-up: the same shape is unfixed in two other RPCs.** `utxoupdatepsbt` (`src/rpc/rawtransaction.cpp:1841-1845`) and `descriptorprocesspsbt` (`:2119-2122`) run the identical `for (obj in array) EvalDescriptorStringOrObject(...)` loop with no dedup, same cost model. Deliberately out of scope here — the commit message scopes itself to the three scan RPCs and the measurement was taken there — but flag it explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.
* [ ] **The general class is unbounded aggregate cost, and remains open.** `ParseDescriptorRange` caps a *single* object at 1,000,000 indices (`src/rpc/util.cpp:1321-1335`), but nothing caps the number of scan objects or the sum of their ranges. N *distinct* near-maximal descriptors are still unbounded in aggregate after this PR. A total-cost cap is the structurally deeper fix and a separate design question (what budget — script count, total range, wall clock? configurable? does it break legitimate multi-descriptor wallet scans?). Follow-up issue, not scope creep here.
* [x] **Honest limitation of the tests.** All three assert `result(with duplicates) == result(without)`, which is the right functional contract and correctly avoids flaky timing assertions — but because inserting the same derived scripts twice into a set was always idempotent, they pass whether or not the guard is wired in. They are a regression net for the change, not proof the optimization fires. The timing reproduction is the evidence; the tests are the safety rail.

### Considered and rejected

* [x] **Folding the dedup into `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject`, or extracting a shared "expand scan objects" loop.** The three RPCs' downstream accumulation genuinely differs: `scantxoutset` needs the per-object `provider` after expansion for `InferDescriptor` and builds both `std::set<CScript>` and a `std::map<CScript, std::string>`; `scanblocks` accumulates raw byte vectors into `GCSFilter::ElementSet`; `getdescriptoractivity` uses a plain `std::set<CScript>`. A shared helper would need a callback or output parameter just to route the provider back out. The codebase's own precedent supports the current split: `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` was extracted (`fb90ec3c33`) to share the *parsing*, while the outer loop and accumulation stayed per-RPC. Extracting the predicate once and calling it three times is the right unit.
* [x] **Moving `IsDuplicateScanObject` to `src/rpc/util.{h,cpp}`.** Conceptually it is a sibling of `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` rather than of `FindScriptPubKey`, which it currently sits beside. But it has exactly one user file today; move it if and when the `rawtransaction.cpp` sites above are fixed.

## 2026-08-02 secp256k1 remote integration sweep - i9 goal-branch wave

Complements the `## 2026-07-31 secp256k1 post-pull branch sweep` entry above, which already records this cycle's prepared/pushed branches. ### The 4 new production commits

1. [ ] **`1bf257e222` "group: avoid redundant y-coordinate copies" - the only actionable one, and it is ready.**
   Exact sibling of the x-coordinate commit already shipped in `l0rinc/group-jacobian-copy-cleanups`: it drops the `s1 = a->y` temporary in both `secp256k1_gej_add_ge_var` and `secp256k1_gej_add_zinv_var`, using `a->y` directly. **Alias safety verified by hand against the post-commit source**, since that is the load-bearing property: in `gej_add_ge_var`, `secp256k1_fe_mul(&h3, &h3, &a->y)` sits after the `r->x` writes (which cannot clobber `a->y`) and before the `r->y` write, so `r == a` is safe - the same argument that justified the x-copy commit. Natural next commit on top of the pushed group bundle; needs only the usual build/exhaustive validation.
2. [x] **`aeb60eb85a` "ecdh, ec: reject invalid loaded public keys" - independent re-derivation of the already-pushed `l0rinc/reject-invalid-loaded-pubkeys` (`b4ed6c015d`), and it settles the style question.**
   It uses the **identical early-return shape** (`if (!secp256k1_pubkey_load(...)) { return 0; }`) at both call sites, *not* the branchless `return !!ret & !overflow & pubkey_valid;` tail that the Bitcoin Core-side re-derivation `e19f8ab3af` used. Two independent secp-side derivations converged on early return; only the Core-side one differed. Cite this if a reviewer challenges the shape. No new work needed.
3. [ ] **`3286ecb3d2` "tests: use monotonic timing for benchmarks" - good standalone candidate.**
   The shared benchmark/test timer used `gettimeofday` and UTC wall time, so a host clock step inside a timed region could produce a negative or otherwise invalid duration. The commit switches to `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on POSIX, `QueryPerformanceCounter` on Windows, and a C-standard `clock()` fallback, keeping setup/teardown outside the timed region and preserving the per-operation reporting contract. Touches `src/tests_common.h`, `src/bench.c`, `src/bench_ecmult.c`, `src/bench_internal.c`, `src/tests.c`, `src/unit_test.c`. **Important scoping note: this fixes clock-step robustness only.** It does *not* address load-induced measurement noise, which is what invalidated the standalone re-measurements of `l0rinc/sha256-finalize-direct` and `l0rinc/gej-eq-x-var-zero` (9 interleaved Release runs each gave 0.00% and -0.40% against claimed -1.2% and -3.7%). Do not present this commit as fixing that.
4. [x] **`322f87c932` "musig: clear public nonce on invalid seckey" - do not propose.**
   Clear-on-failure family, which upstream declined in #1850. Same content as the retired local `l0rinc/musig-clear-invalid-seckey-pubnonce`.

### The 7 new test/bench/CI commits (recorded, none urgent)

`14af7ccbfa` cmake: require memory checker for ctime tests; `9ddceb2fe1` cmake: make RelWithDebInfo builds reproducible; `2070efb2d3` doc: define Silent Payments sender outputs on failure (`include/secp256k1_silentpayments.h`); `19c141ceae` doc: clarify EllSwift XDH callback data contract (`include/secp256k1_ellswift.h`); `6e4b9e4c72` tests: verify custom SHA-256 compression output; `ee615a099e` fuzz: cover MuSig scalar reduction boundaries (plus corpus entry); `e8e23f6b44` journal: snapshot write cleanup audit - note this one adds a stray top-level `goal38-fault/` directory that would need removing before any reuse.

The two `doc:` commits are the same "document the contract the code already has" shape that `l0rinc/reject-invalid-loaded-pubkeys` adopted for its header/changelog updates, and are cheap standalone candidates.

The one item that changes the queue is `1bf257e222` (group y-coordinate copies), which slots directly on top of the pushed `l0rinc/group-jacobian-copy-cleanups` as a fourth cleanup. `3286ecb3d2` is the next-best independent candidate. ## 2026-08-02 month-scale integration of remote branches and commits (2026-07-02 .. 2026-08-02)

Retrospective pass over everything the remotes gained in the past month, rather than another incremental fetch wave. Purpose was to find what the incremental passes missed.

### Inventory

**1,051 new remote branches and 24 updated**, by remote: `rpi5-16gb-1000gb` 468, `umbrel` 358, `origin` 110 (+16 updated), `i9` 64, `i7` 26, `rpi5-8gb-500gb` 21, `rpi5-16-3` 3 (+1), `knots` 1, `rpi5-16-2` 0 (+1), `rpi5-8` 0 (+1), `upstream` 0 (+4). Reachable from those refs and not in `upstream/master`/`origin/master`: **15,959 non-merge commits**.

### The classification trap, recorded so it is not repeated

Applying the usual "touches `src/` outside `test`/`bench`" filter to the month gives **9,899 production commits** — wildly out of line with the ~17% seen in single fetch waves. The excess is not campaign output: it is Bitcoin Knots history, `audit/resurrection` (607 commits of revived closed-unmerged PRs), and long-lived experiment branches whose base is not an ancestor of the current master. Deduplicating by `(subject, production file set)` still leaves 2,025 distinct changes, which is not a triage list.

**The discriminator that works is the campaign's own signature: a commit that touches `agent-journal/*` and production `src/` in the same commit.** That yields **116 commits, 111 distinct by subject** for the whole month — a real triage list, and consistent with the per-wave ratios. Use this filter for any future retrospective; the path-prefix filter alone is meaningless at month scale.

### Coverage gap

Of the 111 distinct campaign findings, **44 are already cited in this file by SHA and 67 are not**. The 67 are listed below by subsystem. Three of them turn out to duplicate work that is already owned, which is the most important result of this pass:

* [x] **`95e078cd0b` "coins: reject undecodable first cursor key" (`src/txdb.cpp`) is our own open upstream PR #35654** ("txdb: reject undecodable first coin cursor key", same file plus `src/test/coins_tests.cpp`). The campaign re-derived a fix we already have in review. Do not prepare.
* [x] **`69cc7a3c35` "http: reject disallowed RPC clients before parsing" is already merged as #35592** — it is literally the tip of the current baseline `556988790a`. Second instance of the campaign re-deriving merged work (after `538ea11f23`/#35787 and `1d05b4ac4f`/#35753).
* [x] **`1e0091464c` "net: reject oversized locators before deserialization" is our pushed `l0rinc/reject-oversized-locators`** (fork PR #260).

### The two worth acting on

1. [ ] **`a84b27f5c2` "mempool: account for unbroadcast transaction memory" — direct companion to our live PR #262.** `CTxMemPool::DynamicMemoryUsage()` (`src/txmempool.cpp:984-988`) omits `memusage::DynamicUsage(m_unbroadcast_txids)`; the fix adds exactly that one term to the same expression #262 edits via `GetMainMemoryUsage()`. Same bug class, same function, same `-maxmempool`/`getmempoolinfo.usage` consequence, and the branch reports a focused regression failing `0 != 80` without it. **This means #262 does not fix all of the under-accounting in that expression** — worth deciding whether to fold it in or file it as the stated follow-up, and worth mentioning in #262 so reviewers are not surprised by a second accounting PR touching one line over.
2. [ ] **`d02675177e` "rest: bound getutxos binary outpoint deserialization"** — third instance of the `LIMITED_VECTOR` pattern after BIP37 (`ba05bf48fe`) and getblocktxn (`9a1531ee8b`), and the **same allocation-bound caveat applies**: the commit's own evidence says the old path "reserved 4,999,968 bytes", i.e. exactly one `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE` batch, which is the documented deliberate bound, not an unbounded allocation. But this one carries a second, independent improvement the other two do not: it fixes the **error contract**, returning `max outpoints exceeded (max: 15)` instead of a generic `Parse error` for an oversized count. Rank it on that, not on DoS.

### The one worth acting on: `fbbe4d41bf`, and it is a live follow-up to merged #1863

`secp256k1_ellswift_create` builds its RNG state as `H(seckey32 || "\x00"*32 [|| auxrnd32] || cnt++)` and then feeds that state to `secp256k1_ellswift_elligatorswift_var`, which is variable-time by design. Upstream #1863 (already merged, recorded here as F-ec2 fixed) narrowed the declassification from `&hash` to `&hash.s` so the seckey copy left in the hash buffer stays classified. **It did not change the ordering.** Current `upstream/master` `src/modules/ellswift/main_impl.h:454-459` still reads:

```
secp256k1_sha256_write(..., &hash, seckey32, 32);
secp256k1_sha256_write(..., &hash, zero32, sizeof(zero32));
secp256k1_declassify(ctx, &hash.s, sizeof(hash.s));      <-- declassify
if (auxrnd32) secp256k1_sha256_write(..., &hash, auxrnd32, 32);   <-- then fold in aux
```

so the state is declared public *before* the auxiliary randomness is mixed in. The campaign commit moves the declassify below the aux write and updates the comment to "private key and aux randomness are hashed now".

**Why this has gone unnoticed, verified directly:** `src/ctime_tests.c:271-280` at `upstream/master` calls `secp256k1_ellswift_create(ctx, ellswift, key, NULL)` and then `(ctx, ellswift, key, ellswift)`. Only `key` is ever `CHECKMEM_UNDEFINE`d; the buffer passed as `auxrnd32` is defined/public. **The secret-aux path is therefore never exercised by the constant-time tests at all**, which is exactly why the ordering survives. The campaign commit also edits `ctime_tests.c`, which is what exposes it.

Honest framing for any PR: this is constant-time *annotation and coverage*, not a demonstrated timing leak. Moving the declassify makes it cover the aux contribution, which matches the design intent (the hash output is consumed as public randomness by a `_var` routine). Left as-is, marking `auxrnd32` secret makes the ctime tests fail. Pitch it as "#1863 follow-up: the same function still declassifies before the last secret input, and the ctime tests never cover that input", and note that the campaign's diff is written against the pre-#1863 source (`declassify(ctx, &hash, sizeof(hash))`), so it needs rebasing onto the current `&hash.s` form rather than cherry-picking.

The MuSig nonce-invalidation family is the clear-on-failure pattern upstream **declined in #1850**; do not re-propose without new argument. The two CI-pinning commits and the MuSig2 vector-generation determinism fix are cheap and independent.

### Retired candidate: `l0rinc/scratch-free-warning`

Earlier entries list this as a remaining cheap candidate ("fixes a real gcc-17 snapshot `-Werror` break"). **It is dead.** It was upstream PR #1880, **closed 2026-06-25**, superseded by **#1881 "tests: Fix GCC 17 snapshot warning" by real-or-random, merged the same day**. theStack had also proposed a pragma-based alternative on the thread. Remove it from the candidate list; the underlying CI break is fixed upstream by someone else's patch.

Current upstream PR ledger for `l0rinc` on `bitcoin-core/secp256k1`: **open** #1898 (`silentpayments-ctime-label-scan`), #1897 (`check-test-operation-results`). **Merged** #1890, #1889, #1877, #1859. **Closed** #1880 (superseded by #1881), #1850 (clear-on-failure declined), #1740. Current fork drafts include #11, #13, #15, #21, #36, and #37 at the exact pushed heads recorded below.

## 2026-08-02 review findings not previously recorded - cookie and package-weight branches

Both branches are described elsewhere in this file by their *outcome*, but the review reasoning behind those shapes was only ever reported in session and never written down. Recording it here because both are now published (`l0rinc/rpc-cookie-write-failure` as fork PR #261, `l0rinc/package-weight-accumulator` on `origin`), so the rejected alternatives and the measurements are what review responses will need.

### `l0rinc/rpc-cookie-write-failure`

* [x] **Reproducer went through three forms; the reasoning for each transition matters.** (1) A Linux `/dev/full` symlink on `.cookie.tmp` — `/dev/full` does not exist on macOS, so the case was a silent no-op on the development machine and on macOS CI. (2) A portable `RLIMIT_FSIZE`=0 window with `SIGXFSZ` ignored — runs everywhere but Windows, needs no device or symlink, and the full 799-case `test_bitcoin` passed with the process-global window in place (the case was moved to `BOOST_FIXTURE_TEST_CASE(..., BasicTestingSetup)` so no node threads were alive during it). (3) The current injected-writer seam — portable including Windows, no global state.
* [x] **Measured: a cookie-sized payload never reaches disk before `close()`.** Probe on a 76-byte write: after `file << ...` both `fail()` and `bad()` are 0; only `close()` sets `fail()`. A 100 KB payload does trip at the insertion. Because `badbit` persists into `close()`, **a single post-close check subsumes a post-write check**, which halved the production diff from 8 added lines to 4 before the design changed again.
* [x] **`WriteBinaryFile()` fixes the defect by construction** — `src/util/readwritefile.cpp:36-49` checks the `fwrite` byte count *and* the `fclose` return. Precedent for exactly this use: `src/i2p.cpp:369` and `src/torcontrol.cpp:536` both write credential files through it under the same "umask is 0077" rationale. The hand-rolled `ofstream` was a third idiom for one job.
* [x] **The 3-state `AuthCookieWriteResult{OpenError, WriteError, Ok}` was a bool in a trenchcoat.** `OpenError` is unreachable in production (`WriteBinaryFile` collapses open/write/close into one bool) and the sole consumer tested `!= Ok`. Collapsing to `bool` let `WriteAuthCookieFile` be deleted outright — `WriteBinaryFile` already has the exact `AuthCookieWriteFn` signature — and turned the overload pair into a defaulted parameter, matching `DumpMempool(..., fsbridge::FopenFn mockable_fopen_function = fsbridge::fopen, ...)` at `src/node/mempool_persist.h:16-18`. The defaulted form only became possible once the writer was bool-typed, since the previous default was `static` in the .cpp.
* [x] **Load-bearing detail in the test, easy to "simplify" away.** `WriteIncompleteCookie` writes an **empty temp file** and *then* returns failure. Drop the write and a regression that ignores the writer's failure still passes, because `RenameOver` fails on a missing source and returns `Error` anyway. Verified in both directions; the empty file is what lets the rename succeed and clobber the cookie, which is what the assertion catches.
* [x] **Considered and rejected:** an RAII guard for the rlimit/signal restore (two statements, no throwing call, single-use guard class costs more than the fragility it removes); a shared "atomic durable write" helper unifying the `ofstream` sites (`common/settings.cpp`) with the `AutoFile` sites (`addrdb.cpp`, `node/mempool_persist.cpp`) — four call sites, different payload types, over-engineering for this PR; temp-file cleanup on the error path — `.cookie.tmp` is left behind exactly as the adjacent pre-existing `RenameOver` failure branch already does, though note `addrdb.cpp`'s `SerializeFileDB` does `remove(pathTmp)` on every failure branch, so the function is less careful than that convention.

### `l0rinc/package-weight-accumulator`

* [x] **Full-tree `std::accumulate` sweep: `src/policy/packages.cpp:87` was the only site with the mismatch.** Roughly 15 other call sites already pass a typed init with a matching lambda — including `CalculateOutputValue` at `src/primitives/transaction.h:273`, which uses `CAmount{0}` for this exact pitfall, and `validation.cpp:1504/1506`, `script/descriptor.cpp:1336`, `wallet/coinselection.cpp:956/961/966`, `node/psbt.cpp:108`, `node/mini_miner.cpp:423/425`. The one other bare-literal init, `wallet/coinselection.cpp:991`, is **not** the same bug: its lambda declares `int sum` and the underlying `COutput::input_bytes` / `SelectionResult::m_weight` are themselves `int`, so init, lambda, and storage all agree at 32 bits. **No codebase-wide sweep is warranted, and `int64_t{0}` is the house idiom rather than a new invention** — both worth saying in the PR, since a reviewer's first instinct is to ask whether this is one instance of many.
* [x] **C++20 (`CMakeLists.txt:84`), so maflcko's `std::ranges::fold_left` suggestion on #35473 is not available** in this tree. The typed seed is the minimal current-language fix.
* [x] **Pre-fix the accumulator wraps *negative*, so the guard is bypassed rather than miscounted.** For the test's construction (25 x ~92,000,256 weight) the int32 sum wraps to about -1,994,960,896 after the 24th addition, and `total_weight > MAX_PACKAGE_WEIGHT` is then false. "Silently skips the `package-too-large` check" is the accurate framing; "miscounts the total" is not.
* [x] **A functional test is impossible, not merely inconvenient.** `src/httpserver.h:80` sets `MAX_BODY_SIZE{32_MiB}`, enforced unconditionally with no override. One ~21.5 MB transaction hex-encodes to ~46 MB of ASCII — over the whole request budget by itself, before the ~25 copies the overflow needs. So the unit test on `IsWellFormedPackage` is the only level that can reach this at all. Worth stating explicitly given #35473 was closed over its regression test.
* [x] **`BulkTransaction()` is the established helper for the fixture.** `src/test/util/transaction_utils.h:32` bulks a transaction to a target weight by padding one output script, self-asserting `weight >= target_weight` and `<= target_weight + 3`; already used at `orphanage_tests.cpp:345`, `miner_tests.cpp:290`, `util/txmempool.cpp:243`, `bench/txorphanage.cpp:44`. Using it let the magic `23'000'000` become `std::numeric_limits<int>::max() / int{MAX_PACKAGE_COUNT} + 1` — derived, self-adjusting if `MAX_PACKAGE_COUNT` changes, and guaranteed sufficient by the helper's own assert. That in turn made the `BOOST_REQUIRE_GT` precondition a tautology, so it was removed. `create_placeholder_tx()` in the same test file cannot produce this shape: it scales only by input/output *count*, so ~23 MB would need ~120,000 inputs and outputs.
* [x] **`MakeTransactionRef(huge_tx)` was a hidden 23 MB deep copy.** The template deduces `Tx = CMutableTransaction&` from an lvalue, binding `CTransaction(const CMutableTransaction&)` rather than the move overload, and `prevector`'s copy path is a per-byte placement-new loop, not `memcpy`. `std::move` removed it; `huge_tx` is dead after that line. Net effect with the derived (smaller) script: **1.52s versus 1.92s**, i.e. the reuse-plus-move version is faster despite `BulkTransaction` constructing `CTransaction` three times internally.

## 2026-08-02 live fork PR priority and post-push CI reconciliation

This section supersedes earlier secp256k1 priority statements. Live refs at the time of the audit: `upstream/master` = `origin/master` = `f8c75f89a50f90e5dc773691192a4d8cb2fa8876`. The fork has 30 open PRs, including 22 focused drafts and 8 historical batch or audit PRs.

### Priority among focused fork PRs

1. [ ] **Fork PR [#36](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/36), `contrib: parse lax DER privkey lengths by offset` - malformed-input UB in contrib code.** A four-byte input can claim a 65,535-byte internal BER length while accurately reporting its real four-byte buffer size. The old parser forms `privkey + len` before checking the claim, so the UB does not require lying about `privkeylen`. The offset rewrite removes the class and matches the sibling lax signature parser. Coordinate the deterministic malformed-DER test with upstream [#1895](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1895), which adds overlapping import tests but does not fix this pointer arithmetic.
2. [ ] **Fork PR [#11](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/11), `ecdh, ec: check pubkey_load return` - core API silent-success hardening.** ECDH and pubkey combination are the last production call sites that ignore a failed opaque-pubkey load. With a non-aborting illegal callback and an invalid public-key object, they continue through group arithmetic and can return success. This is misuse-gated, but it affects core library APIs and the fix is small, complete, and CI-green.
3. [ ] **Fork PR [#23](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/23), `ellswift: normalize zero inverse inputs` - valid but astronomically rare correctness path.** A hash-derived `u = 0` occurs with probability about `2^-255`. VERIFY builds abort and production builds can emit an encoding for a different point. The focused fault-injection test and both backends are green.
4. [ ] **Fork PR [#16](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/16), `field_10x26: avoid normalize overflow` - real latent arithmetic bug.** All five first-pass 10x26 normalize and zero-predicate carry chains need the 64-bit accumulator at magnitude 32. No current public or in-tree path reaching magnitude 32 has been demonstrated, so this remains below the public-API items. Origin is still the pre-rebase `b938a5d092`; local `4b7a7d5e03` is the equivalent patch rebased onto a newer master. Decide which history to keep before upstream submission.
5. [ ] **Fork PR [#13](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/13), `scalar: guard shifts above product width` - latent internal stack OOB.** `shift = 513` indexes past both scalar backends, but the sole in-tree caller uses the literal 384. The mathematically forced result above the 512-bit product width is zero. Sanitizer evidence and both backend tests are strong, but upstream may prefer a contract assertion.
6. [ ] **Fork PR [#15](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/15), `ec, extrakeys: preserve overlapping tweak inputs` - low-priority In/Out alias consistency.** The APIs identify the modified objects as In/Out, but they do not explicitly promise that the separate `tweak32` pointer may overlap their storage. The old highest-priority classification was therefore too strong. The focused fix remains internally consistent: secret-key tweak add/multiply, public-key tweak multiply, and MuSig cache tweaks already consume `tweak32` before writing the In/Out object. The retraction in `fdcee19fdc` concerns separate Out/In arguments and does not require broadening this PR to x-only tweak output, pubkey combination, or Silent Payments output aliases. The simplified regressions compare the complete opaque objects and still fail against the original clear-before-read ordering. The local and fork branches now match at `3bbd8985dd`, with commits `07f5d7e573` and `3bbd8985dd` on `upstream/master` `f8c75f89a5`.

The next group is valid hardening with no demonstrated normal-call path: [#18](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/18) off-curve opaque pubkeys, [#22](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/22) odd-Y opaque x-only keys, [#25](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/25) overflowed opaque ECDSA signatures, [#30](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/30) invalid opaque recoverable signatures, [#24](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/24) overflowed opaque MuSig partial signatures, and [#34](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/34) malformed Silent Payments opaque state. PR #18 contains PR #11's checked-load fix and adds a curve check to every pubkey load, so hold it until #11 and the hot-path cost/design question are resolved. PR #34 still has two review questions documented locally: whether `combined` must be exactly zero, and whether canonical storage validation belongs in core instead of reaching into `fe_impl_*` from the module.

Lower correctness and API consistency items are [#31](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/31), which preserves a Silent Payments label index only beyond realistic transaction output counts, and [#32](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/32), which aligns the context-destroy declaration with its existing NULL-safe implementation.

### Blocked focused PRs

* [ ] **Fork PR [#26](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/26), `musig: reject zero nonce scalars` - real constant-time CI regression.** The 59 failed checks are not stale infrastructure. Valgrind reports secret-dependent branches in `secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen_internal`. The new expression uses short-circuit `||` while testing the two secret nonce scalars, then declassifies only the result after the branch has already occurred. Replace the short-circuit operation with a constant-time combination such as bitwise `|`, replay `ctime_tests`, and rerun exhaustive order 13 before considering the branch ready. Once fixed, this belongs near PR #23: it makes an effectively impossible exhaustive-group event fail cleanly, not a practical vulnerability.
* [ ] **Fork PR [#38](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/38), `ellswift: declassify after auxiliary randomness` - current approach is incorrect.** Current 32-bit Linux and macOS Valgrind jobs fail in `secp256k1_ellswift_xswiftec_inv_var` after the secret auxiliary buffer is introduced. Moving the `hash.s` declassification below the auxiliary write does not declassify the auxiliary bytes still buffered for the final SHA256 compression, so the PRNG result remains secret-marked when variable-time EllSwift code consumes it. Redesign the annotation boundary around the generated PRNG output after all secret input has been hashed. Do not publish the current two-commit stack upstream.
* [ ] **Fork PR [#33](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/33), `tests: cover field boundary values` - C89 build failure.** The three new calls precede declarations in `run_field_misc`, tripping `-Wdeclaration-after-statement`. Move the calls below the declarations. The tests are mutation-kill coverage and do not reproduce the magnitude-32 bugs.

### Test, optimization, and cleanup priority

* [ ] **Test correctness:** [#21](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/21) fixes the BER generator's byte-versus-bit shift and restores intended lax-parser coverage. It is a real test defect, but production behavior is unchanged.
* [ ] **Optimizations:** [#35](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/35) xor-mask 5x52 cmovs, then [#27](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/27) EllSwift denominator-square reuse. Revalidate performance claims on the submission base.
* [ ] **Group cleanup:** [#37](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/37) is the consolidated Jacobian cleanup stack. PRs [#28](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/28) and [#29](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/29) are subsets and should be closed in favor of #37. Optional follow-up `1bf257e222 group: avoid redundant y-coordinate copies` must be extracted without its `agent-journal` file and exhaustive-tested. It is not required before publishing #37.

### Retire or close

* [x] **Fork PR [#14](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/14), DER offsets:** real-or-random's review correctly identifies the `SIZE_MAX` test as a caller-contract violation because the supplied object is not actually that large. Prepare it as hygiene with an honest "latent" framing, not as a bug fix.

### Selected and prepared — `l0rinc/mempool-unbroadcast-memory`

Based on `556988790a`. Two signed commits, nothing pushed:

1. `0350c12cb5` `test: characterize unbroadcast memory accounting` — records reported usage before and after `AddUnbroadcastTx()`, asserting the delta is 0, then that `RemoveUnbroadcastTx()` returns to the baseline. Passes on unmodified master.
2. `a3747a3372` `mempool: account for unbroadcast transaction memory` — adds `memusage::DynamicUsage(m_unbroadcast_txids)` to `CTxMemPool::DynamicMemoryUsage()` (`src/txmempool.cpp:831`) and flips the expectation.

Validation: `mempool_tests` passes 6 cases, full `test_bitcoin` passes; reverting only the production term fails the focused case with **`0 != 80`**.

Why this one: it is the **completion of the accounting story our live PR #262 started**. #262 fixes the `GetMainMemoryUsage()` term of that same expression; this fixes the sibling term one call over, and the two are independent (the pushed #262 branch does not touch line 831). Ownership re-verified: no upstream PR in any state for unbroadcast memory usage.

**Honest magnitude, to state in the PR rather than let review discover:** `m_unbroadcast_txids` is a `std::set<Txid>` (`src/txmempool.h:284`) holding only locally-submitted transactions that have not yet been seen relayed, and entries are removed once broadcast. At ~80 bytes per node it is bounded by local submission volume, not by remote activity or mempool history — so unlike #262's retained-capacity growth this is a small, self-limiting gap. It is a correctness-of-accounting fix, not a resource-exhaustion fix, and should be pitched that way.

### The "critical findings" claim does not survive contact with the reports

* [x] **`umbrel/codex-security/secp256k1-A6XIUV` (`f2d1e8b243`) reports three findings, all self-rated `low`.** Its own `report.md` scan summary reads `Severity mix | low: 3`, `Confidence mix | high: 3`, and the word "critical" appears **zero times** in the report. Worth keeping as a defence-in-depth note for the secp256k1 tree, not as a live vulnerability.

* [x] **The substantive security work in this wave is the Bitcoin Core rescan on `rpi5-8gb-500gb/security-review-2026-08-01`** (`agent-journal/rescan-2026-08-03.md`, four parts). It verifies 45 commits of drift clean, clears the REST surface, the attacker-count→allocation class, FeeFrac arithmetic, package-relay pairing, `spend.cpp` fee adjustment, and all `m_mempool` dereferences after #35753. It independently reaches the same verdict this file already recorded for `coinselection.cpp:991` (int width, ~8M UTXOs to overflow, latent hygiene only).

### The one item that was urgent — reproduced, fixed, prepared

* [x] **Descriptor range counter overflow terminates the node from a single authenticated RPC call. Confirmed live on `1ed14c6122` by direct reproduction.** `ParseDescriptorRange` (`src/rpc/util.cpp:1321-1335`) accepts an end of `INT32_MAX` — it rejects only `(high >> 31) != 0` and spans ≥ 1,000,000 — but `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` (`:1365`) counted through that range with `for (int i = range.first; i <= range.second; ++i)` while `range` is a `std::pair<int64_t, int64_t>`. Incrementing past the last iteration is signed overflow.

  Reproduction (regtest, this repo's Debug build, which carries `-ftrapv` per `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_DEBUG=-O0 -ftrapv -g3`): `scantxoutset start [{"desc": <ranged>, "range": [2147483647, 2147483647]}]` **killed the node** — the CLI returned `Error while attempting to communicate with server (EOF)` and the process was gone. After the fix the same call returns `"success": true` and the node stays up. Both states were verified against a live node, not inferred.

  Scope and trigger: `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` is shared by `scantxoutset`, `scanblocks`, `getdescriptoractivity`, `utxoupdatepsbt` and `descriptorprocesspsbt`. A ranged descriptor must provide an explicit range ending at exactly `INT32_MAX`. String inputs and objects without `range` stop at the default endpoint of 1000, while every lower explicit endpoint exits before the counter overflows. All five callers require authenticated RPC access. Under `-ftrapv` (Debug and any CI job using it) the result is immediate process death. Without it the increment is undefined behaviour and the wrapped counter would re-enter the loop from `INT_MIN`, which was **not** measured here and should not be claimed as a hang without evidence.

  Direct precedent: merged [#26275](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/26275), commit `bf2bf73bcb`, changed the separate `deriveaddresses` loop counter from `int` to `int64_t` in 2022 after reproducing the same crash at derivation index `2147483647`. `deriveaddresses` is therefore already immune. No current PR owns the shared-helper fix.

  Disclosure: prepare this as a public PR. The trigger requires authenticated RPC access and an explicit range ending at exactly `INT32_MAX`. #26275 handled the same endpoint overflow publicly, with maintainer discussion framing the release behavior as compiler-dependent undefined behavior. Reassess before publication only if an unauthenticated path or a reliable production-build crash is demonstrated.

  Ownership: `gh search prs --repo bitcoin/bitcoin` for `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject overflow` and `descriptor range int overflow` return nothing in any state. Merged #26275 owns only the separate `deriveaddresses` loop.

  Published on the fork as **`l0rinc/descriptor-range-counter-overflow`** on `1ed14c6122`, with signed commits `143a13fb2b` `test: characterize descriptor range endpoint` and `264555af3c` `rpc: avoid descriptor range counter overflow`. No upstream or fork PR owns it.

  Note the interaction with our own pushed `l0rinc/rpc-deduplicate-scan-objects`: it edits the same three RPC call sites' loops. The two are independent but will touch adjacent lines.

### 2026-08-03 addendum — provenance identifiers and the controls that isolated the crash

Recorded so the preceding section can be re-audited without re-fetching.

**Scan provenance.** The codex-security artifacts live on `umbrel/codex-security/secp256k1-A6XIUV`, added by a single commit `f2d1e8b243` ("Add Codex Security secp256k1 findings", 11 files, 2607 insertions) under `codex-security-findings/secp256k1/codex-security-secp256k1-A6XIUV/`. Canonical files are `findings.json`, `coverage.json`, `scan-manifest.json`, with `report.md` a deterministic projection of them. Scan id `4832cdcb-3112-43f0-9373-f62e1cc74d68`; target `target_sha256_14d9ed724692e982f67454f0268d054160720e522563938cbb2cd1b07616ff16`; snapshot digest `codex-security-snapshot/v1:sha256:d876b97cf2462258138efb6375a0f8afabb519b44f6bb94a7d830b75cf229f85`. Inventory was a deterministic 188-file repository sweep with no unreadable files; four candidates entered validation and three survived. The suppressed fourth is `candidate-edaf7b362f1481f2` (`src/secp256k1.c:242-245` wrapper, `src/scratch_impl.h:13-15` sink, `:73-96` implementation), disposition `suppressed`, method "targeted ASan/UBSan harness against the original checked-out implementation plus complete static caller and export tracing".

The Bitcoin Core rescan is `agent-journal/rescan-2026-08-03.md` on `rpi5-8gb-500gb/security-review-2026-08-01`, tip `814e428599`, four `docs(audit): rescan part N` commits over a single 105-line journal file. Its stated base is `origin/master 556988790a` against a prior reviewed base of `a2aab6df97`.

**The differential controls that isolate the descriptor-range crash.** The reproduction is only meaningful alongside the negative controls run in the same session against the same binary and node:

* `deriveaddresses <ranged desc> [0,2]` → returned three addresses normally.
* `deriveaddresses <ranged desc> [2147483647,2147483647]` → **returned one address normally, node stayed alive.** This is the control that rules out "descriptors break at the boundary" generally, and pins the defect to `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject` specifically: `src/rpc/output_script.cpp:228` already counts with `for (int64_t i = range_begin; i <= range_end; ++i)`.
* `scantxoutset start [{"desc": <ranged>, "range": [2147483647,2147483647]}]` → node **DEAD**, CLI reported `Error while attempting to communicate with server 127.0.0.1:18499 (EOF)`.
* Same `scantxoutset` call after the one-line widening → `"success": true`, node **ALIVE**.

The descriptor used throughout was a checksummed `wpkh(tpubD6NzVbkrYhZ4WaWSyoBvQwbpLkojyoTZPRsgXELWz3Popb3qkjcJyJUGLnL4qHHoQvao8ESaAstxYSnhyswJ76uZPStJRJCTKvosUCJZL5B/0/*)` obtained via `getdescriptorinfo`; `deriveaddresses` rejects unchecksummed descriptors with `Missing checksum`, which is why the first attempt produced no signal.

**Why the range passes validation at all.** `ParseDescriptorRange` (`src/rpc/util.cpp:1321-1335`) rejects only `low < 0`, `(high >> 31) != 0`, and `high >= low + 1000000`. A degenerate range `[INT32_MAX, INT32_MAX]` has span 0 and a high of exactly `0x7FFFFFFF`, so it clears all three gates — the span cap that bounds ordinary abuse is precisely what makes the boundary case legal.

**Committed regression.** `test/functional/rpc_scantxoutset.py` gains one line in the existing "Test range validation." block asserting the largest accepted range end scans successfully, adjacent to the `Range is too large` case that establishes the span cap. Chosen over a unit test because the crash is only reachable through the RPC layer that calls `EvalDescriptorStringOrObject`.

#### New report rows that survive source review

* [x] **`verify-commits` returns success for an operational ancestry error.** `contrib/verify-commits/verify-commits.py` treats every nonzero `git merge-base --is-ancestor` result as a normal non-ancestor. `python3 contrib/verify-commits/verify-commits.py this-object-does-not-exist` prints Git's invalid-object error, reports that the object predates the trusted root, and exits 0. This is a confirmed release-verifier failure mode, with no PR in either repository. It is contrib tooling rather than node runtime and remains outside the requested queue.
* [x] **The legacy BIP70 merchant parser has unchecked offsets and length.** `GetPaymentRequestMerchant()` in `src/qt/transactiondesc.cpp:71-94` indexes after the second common-name marker without proving the type and length bytes exist, then passes the unbounded one-byte length to `QString::fromUtf8`. The parser was introduced by merged #16852 to display merchant names from historical BIP70 records after BIP70 removal. No open issue or PR owns the bounds fix. Reachability requires a malformed legacy payment request already stored in a wallet and opening its GUI transaction details, so this is a local malformed-wallet read rather than a network or consensus vulnerability.
* [x] **HTTP pipelining can retain an uncapped per-client queue.** The report adds concrete evidence to the existing `fe66393328` entry: an allowed RPC client can continue feeding pipelined requests while the first request is busy, and invalid authentication deliberately holds a worker for about 250 ms. Open upstream PR [#35735](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35735) owns the receive-side state and backpressure change, so this is not an unowned finding.
* [x] **The chunked HTTP quadratic parser is already owned.** Open upstream PR #35735 changes request parsing state and covers this source area. The new report strengthens the pre-authentication CPU evidence but does not create an unowned finding.
* [x] **The remaining new rows are dependency or local-filesystem issues.** The AJV and MCP rows have no Bitcoin consumer, Octokit authentication uses headers rather than secret-bearing URLs, and watch-only export symlink substitution requires an authenticated caller to choose a directory writable by a lower-trust local user. They do not enter the runtime queue.

The repeated first-round rows do not change priority. PSBT field-boundary work, Berkeley DB migration cycles, private descriptor console history, PSBT file TOCTOU, CSV formula injection, external-signer intent preservation, release passphrases, predictable temporary files, and the signet faucet all retain their existing ownership or contextual classifications. None supplies the claimed critical finding.

## 2026-08-03 secp integration: seven goal branches, a docs-only rescan, and a subtraction trap

Continues from `## 2026-08-02 incremental secp fetch and EllSwift preparation`, whose cutoff was `i9/codex/goal16-api-misuse-resistance` at `98a0f684a9`. Baseline unchanged: `upstream/master` = `f8c75f89a5`.

### Method note: the subtraction trap, recorded so it is not repeated

The obvious approach — take the new tips and `git rev-list` them against the previously-known tips — reports **1,879 new commits**, of which 118 look production-touching. That number is meaningless. The `codex/goal*` branches are cut from stale bases (the `e153e2681f` family and older), so subtracting only the *known tips* re-exposes the entire historical corpus: the whole silentpayments module import, every May-era optimization branch, even PR #815's Karatsuba rework. Classifying that yields a list of "findings" that are all years-old owned or upstream work.

**The correct discriminator for the secp campaign is per-branch: `git rev-list --count 98a0f684a9..$branch`.** Each new goal branch is then revealed as **exactly +2 commits (one journal, one source)**. This is the secp analogue of the Core-side "path-prefix filter is meaningless at month scale" trap recorded above. Use per-branch subtraction against the prior cutoff, never global tip subtraction, for these branches.

### `rpi5-8gb-500gb-secp/rescan-2026-08-03` — 1,355 commits, **zero production**

A fresh audit rescan on top of the saturated `resurrection-hunt` tip. Verified: not one commit touches `src/` production or `include/`. The four new commits are `8f9cb9eaa0` (drift docs-only, #1821 coverage gap closed, open-PR sweep clean), `a9fdb60448`, `52052f3675`, and `5f9c71ff9b`. It raises **two new Silent Payments watch items, F-sp1 and F-sp2**, and three fresh 🟡 candidates from a clean re-read of the module: scan-failure secret residue, prevouts-summary integrity, and a documentation contract gap. None is substantiated with a reproducer in the branch; treat as leads, not findings. The `plug API self-defending` and `schnorr verify BIP340-conformant` conclusions are clean bills.

### The seven new i9 goal branches (+2 commits each)

**Re-derivations of already-owned fork PRs — do not prepare:**

* [x] `goal83-ecmult-current-20260803` → `415cc9cd13 musig: fail nonce generation for zero scalar`. Re-derives `l0rinc/musig-reject-zero-nonces` (`88424b7a0d` + characterization `1d7d39ae5c`). Its framing is worth borrowing even though the branch is not: it states the case as a **release-build gap** — the existing `VERIFY_CHECK(!secp256k1_scalar_is_zero(&k[i]))` pair means a zero derived nonce passes through in release builds and yields an unusable secret nonce, where BIP327 requires NonceGen to fail. Its fix uses `ret &= !is_zero` plus `scalar_cmov` to a dummy one so the constant-time path still runs, then invalidates the secnonce. If the owned PR is ever re-argued, use that release-vs-VERIFY framing.
* [x] `goal84-partial-sig-20260802` → `32773c29b9 musig: reject overflowing partial signatures`. Re-derives `l0rinc/musig-reject-overflowing-partial-sigs` (`d43948235c` + `a1b58eeae5`).
* [x] `goal58-session-state-20260802` → `c73011cb87 musig: validate semantic session state`. Same opaque-state validation family already covered by the owned musig branches.

**New, but carries a design objection — do not prepare as written:**

* [ ] `goal58-keypair-consistency-20260803` → **`2c246cc783 extrakeys: reject inconsistent keypair state`**. Genuinely novel: `secp256k1_keypair_load` never checks that the stored public key actually corresponds to the stored secret key, so a caller who mutates one half of the opaque object gets a keypair whose halves disagree. The fix recomputes the pubkey with `secp256k1_ecmult_gen_ge` and compares via `secp256k1_ge_eq_var`.
  **Two objections, both structural.** First, cost: `keypair_load` is on the hot path of `secp256k1_schnorrsig_sign*` (`src/modules/schnorrsig/main_impl.h:139`), `musig_partial_sign` (`session_impl.h:659`), silentpayments (`main_impl.h:251`), and `keypair_xonly_tweak_add` (`extrakeys/main_impl.h:272`) — adding a full generator multiplication to every one of those roughly doubles the cost of signing. Second, contract: it makes `keypair_load` require a built `ecmult_gen_ctx` and call the illegal callback when absent, so functions that previously worked with a verify-only context would start failing. Either would sink it upstream on its own. If this is ever pursued, it belongs behind `VERIFY` or as an explicit opt-in validator, not in the load path.

**Build/CI only, cheap and independent:**

* [ ] `goal100-cmake-targets-20260803` → `762f0653b8 cmake: omit verify tests from multi-config coverage`.
* [ ] `goal37-install-discovery-20260803` → `2607a6ff36 cmake: disable optional binaries in subprojects`.
* [ ] `goal39-musig-generated-20260802` → `4ce8c06277 build: distribute MuSig test vector sources` (adds the MuSig vector JSONs to the distribution).

### Baseline advance: `f8c75f89a5` → **`3873647bfb`**

Two commits, both from **upstream PR #1904 "sha256: cross-check caller supplied compression function"** (`c84ea46561` + merge). This is directly relevant to our own area of work, so it is worth recording rather than dismissing as routine drift.

It adds `secp256k1_sha256_smoke_test`, run once at startup against any caller-supplied compression function registered through `secp256k1_context_set_sha256_compression`. The existing selftest hashed a single 63-byte string, which catches a function that is wrong everywhere but not one that is wrong on multi-block input, on unaligned starts, or from a non-IV state. The new test hashes 14 message lengths (0, 1, 28, 55, 56, then 64 through 576 in block multiples) at shifted starting offsets, accumulates the digests, and compares against a fixed expected value; a mismatch invokes the illegal callback, which aborts by default. Cost is ~1.5 ms at startup. The header note is explicit that this is **not** a substitute for testing the supplied function properly.

Consequence for our queue: the `secp256k1_context_set_sha256_compression` surface now has real upstream validation, which raises the bar for anything we propose that touches SHA256 routing. The already-archived `l0rinc/ecdh-context-hash` and `l0rinc/ecdsa-nonce-context-hash` (subsumed by #1900, with their remaining `_default`-alias clause shown to be dead code) stay archived — #1904 does not revive them.

**All eight live branches still rebase cleanly onto `3873647bfb`**, verified by `git merge-tree`: `preserve-overlapping-tweak-inputs` (`3bbd8985dd`), `reject-invalid-loaded-pubkeys` (`b4ed6c015d`), `ellswift-auxrnd-declassification` (`d975d7ae03`), `tests-ber-lengths` (`c78266aed9`), `group-jacobian-copy-cleanups` (`2af9559f7d`), `scalar-mul-shift-width` (`aef223a621`), `contrib-lax-der-privatekey-bounds` (`c2d7e06668`), `context-destroy-null` (`8dfc01e3b0`). Zero conflicts, including for the two that touch `include/secp256k1.h`, which #1904 also edits. The retired `l0rinc/sha256-finalize-direct` likewise shows no conflict against the new `src/hash_impl.h`, so #1904 does not change its (already negative) re-measurement verdict.

### The finding: fork PR #11's CHANGELOG entry now lands in the wrong section, silently

`l0rinc/reject-invalid-loaded-pubkeys` (`b4ed6c015d`) adds a `#### Fixed` bullet under what was `## [Unreleased]`. **`git merge-tree` reports no conflict and a cherry-pick onto `8a700a355e` applies cleanly** — but that is misleading. Verified by actually performing the cherry-pick in a scratch worktree and reading the result:

* `## [Unreleased]` is at line 8 and is **empty**.
* `## [0.8.0] - 2026-08-03` spans lines 10-37.
* The branch's bullet lands at **line 27, inside the 0.8.0 section**, and creates a **second `#### Fixed` heading** (line 26) alongside the release's own at line 19.

So the branch would claim an unreleased fix as part of an already-shipped release and emit a malformed duplicate-heading section. Git sees no conflict because the surrounding context lines still match. **Action: move the bullet under the new empty `## [Unreleased]` before this PR is opened or refreshed.** Any other prepared branch that touches `CHANGELOG.md` needs the same check — textual cleanliness is not sufficient evidence here.

All ten live branches otherwise rebase onto `8a700a355e` without conflict, verified by `git merge-tree`: `preserve-overlapping-tweak-inputs`, `reject-invalid-loaded-pubkeys`, `ellswift-auxrnd-declassification`, `tests-ber-lengths`, `group-jacobian-copy-cleanups`, `scalar-mul-shift-width`, `contrib-lax-der-privatekey-bounds`, `context-destroy-null`, `field-boundary-tests`, `silentpayments-validate-opaque-state`.

Second consequence of the release: anything we open from here targets the 0.8.0 development cycle, so new user-visible fixes belong under the fresh `[Unreleased]`, and the "negligible probability" framings used in several branches should be re-read against the released ABI statement rather than the pre-release text.

### Prepared: `l0rinc/mempool-unbroadcast-memory`

The highest clean unowned candidate is a bounded memory-reporting correction, not a security vulnerability. `m_unbroadcast_txids` stores at most one txid per mempool transaction submitted locally and awaiting its first successful broadcast, but `DynamicMemoryUsage()` omits its set nodes. This makes `getmempoolinfo` and `-maxmempool` undercount retained memory by about one set node per entry.

The branch is based directly on `1ed14c6122` and contains two signed commits:

1. `6fc1a01b30` `test: characterize unbroadcast memory accounting` records the zero usage delta before the fix and restores the baseline after removal.
2. `65a3bea2ed` `mempool: include unbroadcast txid memory` adds the set to `DynamicMemoryUsage()` and changes only the expected delta.

The characterization commit passes independently. The focused case, all six `mempool_tests`, and all 799 unit tests pass at the tip. Removing only the production term makes the focused test fail with `0 != 80`, and both signatures verify. This replaces the stale prepared SHAs `0350c12cb5` and `a3747a3372`. Nothing was pushed.

2026-08-06 update: rebased to `b388674acf` and rewritten as `8d5c4a9290` plus `db21e03c9d`. The test now checks the public behavior: adding an unbroadcast txid increases reported usage, and removing it restores the baseline. It no longer repeats the production set type or allocator estimate. The focused case and all six `mempool_tests` pass independently on both commits, and both signatures verify. Nothing was pushed.

2026-08-06 intent audit: `DynamicMemoryUsage()` was introduced by #6410 to account for mempool-owned dynamic memory, and later persistent auxiliary containers were added to the estimate. #18038 introduced `m_unbroadcast_txids` without touching the estimate. Its review warned that stale unbroadcast entries would be a memory leak and network spam, leading to the #18895 consistency check. #19879 simplified the representation to a smaller `std::set`, and #22261 fixed entries being retained indefinitely. None discusses deliberately excluding the set from memory accounting. By contrast, #33157 explicitly documents temporary TxGraph caches and staging state that are excluded. This supports treating the omission as accidental and keeping the current one-line fix and behavioral test unchanged.

Current live status: local and `origin/l0rinc/mempool-unbroadcast-memory` both point to `db21e03c9d` over `8d5c4a9290`.

## 2026-08-04 (concurrent pass) block-index candidate ordering: reproduced but already owned

Written alongside `## 2026-08-04 full ref audit and mempool preparation` by a second session on the same fetch. The reproduced `setBlockIndexCandidates` ordering defect is real, but the initial ownership conclusion was wrong: open draft fork PR **#218** already carries the same production fix and equal-work prune/redownload regression as its first commit. The unbroadcast memory-accounting fix therefore remains the highest clean unowned candidate from this wave.

### Wave triage — independently reproduced, same verdict

Graph subtraction of the 84 new `umbrel` cycle refs (333 through **416**, one later than the sibling section's 415) against every other ref yields **194 unique commits**: 100 journal-only, 87 findings-ledger-only, 4 test-only, 3 production. The three production commits are the same ones the sibling section names, and none is in scope. Two other refs moved and add nothing: `rpi5-8gb-500gb/security-review-2026-08-01` (+1 docs commit) and a new `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/backup/...` ref carrying **zero** unique commits by subtraction.

**Watch the classifier trap here:** `agent/all-findings` is a *file*, not a directory. A path-prefix rule that only strips `agent-journal/` counts those 87 ledger commits as production and reports "90 production commits" for a wave whose real production content is three.

The campaign's own `agent-journal/URGENT.md` at cycle 416 (`3d6e0c96df`, 785 lines) independently confirms the verdict: six non-verified entries, all scoped by their own text as having no remote, consensus, or wallet impact (`Sock::SendComplete` empty spans, `logging` RPC partial application before `-8`, `CKey::Set` pointer subtraction before the length check, null-plus-zero arithmetic in `MurmurHash3`/`ToIntegral`/`DataStream`, a fuzz-corpus gap, a doc gap). Four say the source is root-owned so no fix was attempted.

### The finding: `ReceivedBlockTransactions()` mutates a live `std::set` ordering key

`setBlockIndexCandidates` is a `std::set` ordered by `CBlockIndexWorkComparator`, which tie-breaks equal-work entries on `nSequenceId` (`src/node/blockstorage.cpp:181-182`). `ChainstateManager::ReceivedBlockTransactions()` assigns `pindex->nSequenceId = nBlockSequenceId++` (`src/validation.cpp:3825`) and only then calls `TryAddBlockIndexCandidate()`. Nothing erases the block from the candidate sets first, and **a block can already be in one**: `PruneOneBlockFile()` clears `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA` without touching `setBlockIndexCandidates` (it is blockstorage code with no chainstate access), and data-less candidates are an explicitly legal state — see the pruned-node comment in `FindMostWorkChain()` (`:3154-3157`), the assumeutxo base added by `PopulateBlockIndexCandidates()` (`:4911-4924`), and `InvalidateBlock()` (`:3642-3645`). Reprocessing such a block mutates a live key.

**Reproduced, not inferred.** Cherry-picking only the branch's *tests* onto unmodified `1ed14c6122` and building Debug:

* `received_block_transactions_readds_pruned_candidate` fails with `check candidates_sorted() has failed` — the set is genuinely left unsorted.
* `received_block_transactions_links_pruned_unlinked_child` fails three checks and then **aborts on master's own assertion**, `validation.cpp:5287` `(pindexFirstNeverProcessed == nullptr || pindex == snap_base) == pindex->HaveNumChainTxs()`. This is master's invariant, not a modified one.

Restoring the production hunks makes both pass, and `validation_chainstatemanager_tests` (13 cases), `blockmanager_tests`, `validation_block_tests`, and functional `feature_pruning.py` are all green.

**Ownership correction.** This is the third site of a UB class upstream has twice accepted fixes for: issue #34503, fixed by merged **#34521**, and merged **#35070**. The symbol and behavior search missed fork PR **#218** even though its first commit `d0b438e8ee validation: re-add redownloaded candidates` erases the block from every chainstate candidate set before changing `nSequenceId` and uses the same equal-work sibling regression. The live PR is open and draft at `a06f160417`, so this finding is already published in `l0rinc/bitcoin` and must not be prepared again.

**Honest severity.** `-checkblockindex` is regtest-only by default (`fDefaultConsistencyChecks = true` only at `kernel/chainparams.cpp:616`), so on mainnet there is no assert — the set is silently left with a broken ordering invariant. The empirical precedent from the sibling instance #34503 is erase-by-key failing and an element ending up present twice; plausible consequences are a candidate that can never be erased or a wrong tie-break among equal-work candidates. **None of that is demonstrated end-to-end, and both original finding authors wrote "I did not find a consensus bypass" — do not claim one.** The trigger is also narrower than the original commit message implies: under plain auto-pruning, "in the candidate set" (work >= that chainstate's tip) and "prunable" (height <= tip-288) are mutually exclusive within one chainstate, so reaching it needs `invalidateblock`, assumeutxo, or restart states plus a requested redownload (`AcceptBlock` skips unrequested blocks with `nTx != 0`).

### Retired duplicate: `l0rinc/block-index-candidate-ordering`

The local duplicate was split into `3b2aa1529c test: characterize block candidate reprocessing` and `ef0858b526 validation: preserve candidate set ordering` on `1ed14c6122`. The characterization passes on unmodified production and records the unsorted set with a TODO. The fix changes four production lines and flips only that expectation. Focused and adjacent validation tests pass, `feature_pruning.py` passes, and removing only the production erase makes the focused regression exit 139 while traversing the corrupted set.

The erase loop sits inside the queue walk, matching PR #218. If that PR is revised, re-evaluate whether only `pindexNew` can already be a candidate before hoisting it outside the loop.

### Split off, do NOT propose: `l0rinc/block-index-pruned-unlinked-followup` @ `8a095edc53`

This is the second commit of fork PR **#218** (`validation: keep pruned unlinked blocks linkable`, our rewrite of campaign `8e40da2f31`), parked on top of the above. Its bug is real and reproduces on master (the `:5287` abort above), **but it is owned and its fix direction conflicts with upstream:**

* [x] Open upstream issue **#31512** "validation: CheckBlockIndex can fail in combination with pruning" (mzumsande) describes this exact scenario step-for-step with a functional repro. Upstream triage there: "mostly a theoretical issue", "can't be triggered remotely", and `CheckBlockIndex` is off on mainnet. ryanofsky/mzumsande lean toward **relaxing the CheckBlockIndex expectation**.
* [x] Our commit does the opposite — it retains data-less entries in `m_blocks_unlinked`, which **reverses the invariant upstream just deliberately strengthened**: the `Assume(block->nStatus & BLOCK_HAVE_DATA)` in `AddUnlinkedBlock()` (`blockstorage.cpp:262`) and the "Can't be in m_blocks_unlinked if we don't HAVE_DATA" assert. It also removes the `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA` guard in `LoadBlockIndex()` (`blockstorage.cpp:501-503`) that **closed issue #35050**, itself the fix stringintech proposed and mzumsande agreed to during #35070's review.
* Correct contribution is a comment or test on #31512, not a competing PR. **This is the same trap as the `mempool-trim` / #19880 blocker: opposite semantics with the intent unsettled upstream.**
