### Severity re-reads that survive independent verification

* [x] **`4f867fc8a3` ForceRelay duplicate backlog — DO NOT SUBMIT, stronger than "unowned".** In merged **#34628** (ajtowns, global tx rate limiting, `b33a7fcd7b`, 2026-07-25) instagibbs raised this verbatim on 2026-06-08 ("`forcerelay` peers can maybe OOM crash you by sending you the same tx over and over"); ajtowns converted the backlog to `std::set<Wtxid>` on 2026-06-26 to auto-dedupe; it was **changed back to `std::vector` before merge**, with instagibbs quantifying the exposure ("~5s inbound and ~2s output maximum … Seems more than ok!") and sipa ACKing the vector design ("The mempool itself functions as a bound"). Window is bounded by `count_floor = -rate x 5s` = -70 refilling at 14/s, and it needs `-whitelist=forcerelay@…`. **This is owned by an explicit merge-time decision.**
* [x] **`ee9ad3c5f9` direct-fetch 16/17 — the proposed fix is a regression.** `net_processing.cpp:3081` can let `vToFetch` reach 17, but `:3103` is a hard pre-check that breaks at 16 in flight, so **the per-peer cap is never violated**; the 17th block goes out on the next `SendMessages` tick. The commit's own test asserts `"getdata" not in last_message`, i.e. it forces the case into the large-reorg branch and fetches **0 blocks immediately instead of 16**. Conflicting open refactors: #35561, #34565.
* [ ] **`68b745e208` known-tx relay budget — least-bad of the three, still LOW.** Tokens are taken at `:2380-2381` while the per-peer known-filter is applied only at `:6384`. Reachable without a permission grant and genuinely un-litigated (instagibbs raised only the no-peers case, fixed by the `any_inbound_connected` clearing at `:2470-2477`). But buckets are segregated at `:2467`, so even an attacker holding every inbound slot only burns budget for announcements to its own peers while the 8 outbound full-relay peers propagate normally; recovery <=5s. The repro used `-txsendrate=1` (clamped minimum; **default 14**). The submitted fix is worse than the bug — `distribute()` would do ~490 x 125 bloom lookups with a per-peer lock each on the message-handling thread per accepted transaction, bypassing the 100ms gate, and it skips `RefundRelayTokens` when `peers.empty()`.
* [ ] **`d02675177e` getutxos — the DoS half is dead; only the error contract is real.** `sizeof(COutPoint)` is 36 and `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE` is 5000000 (`serialize.h:38`), so the reserve is `min(size, 5000000/36)` = 138,888 elements = **4,999,968 bytes, exactly one deliberate batch** whose own comment documents the 5 MiB slack as the intended anti-DoS design. It is `reserve`, not `resize`, so the pages are never faulted, and the fully-provided worst case is capped by `MAX_BODY_SIZE{32_MiB}` at ~1.05x amplification. REST is off by default (`DEFAULT_REST_ENABLE{false}`, `init.cpp:175`) and loopback-only unless both `-rpcbind` and `-rpcallowip` are set. The real half: a short body yields a generic `"Parse error"` instead of the limit message. But the commit matches on `e.what()` text (`starts_with("Vector length limit exceeded")`), which has no precedent in the tree, and it **silently drops the `tried: %d` field for the binary path** while the URI path keeps it — uncaught, because `interface_rest.py:217-222` only exercises the URI form. If pursued: bound the count with an explicit `ReadCompactSize`, keep `(max: %d, tried: %d)`, and frame it as an error-contract fix.
  * Separate pre-existing wart found while verifying: `oss << strRequestMutable` serializes a `std::string`, prepending a CompactSize length, so `oss >> fCheckMemPool` consumes the **length byte** rather than the body's first byte. `fCheckMemPool` is effectively "body non-empty" (always true), and `interface_rest.py:161-166`'s two-outpoint fixture actually parses as count=1 with a misaligned outpoint, passing only because it asserts on height/hash. The binary POST body format is undocumented (`doc/REST-interface.md:111-140` covers only the URI form). Worth its own look.

## 2026-08-04 (fourth pass) the 1385-commit wave that was 95% a rebase, and the one in-scope finding in it

Runs after the user's push+fetch, continuing the three sibling 2026-08-04 Core entries. **Baseline advanced: `upstream/master` `1ed14c6122` -> `17c5e33e9c`** (26 commits, 7 merges). Two of them matter to this ledger: **#35832 "p2p: avoid block disk reads on unnecessary requests" is now merged** — it was cited in the BIP35 entry as covering the adjacent disabled-bloom path — and #35863 fixes a `GetP2SHSigOpCount` test assertion. `l0rinc/mempool-unbroadcast-memory`, `l0rinc/block-index-candidate-ordering`, and `l0rinc/rpc-gettxspendingprevout-linear` all still rebase onto the new tip without conflict (`git merge-tree`).

### The delta, and the trap in it

70 refs moved since the previous entry: **umbrel cycles 417-479** (63 new branches, all 2026-08-04), a brand-new `rpi5-8gb-500gb/threat-model-scan-2026-08-04`, advances on `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/agent/all-findings` and `audit/transplant-index-fuzz`, `origin/l0rinc/rpc-gettxspendingprevout-linear`, `rpi5-8/perf/pruneassumevalid-ibd`, and `upstream/master`.

Reflog-old-value + graph subtraction yields **1385 new non-merge commits**: 666 journal-only, 180 test/review/CI/doc, **539 production-touching**. Every one of the 539 is dated 2026-08-04 and none is reachable from `upstream/master`.

**That 539 is almost entirely an illusion, and this is the most important thing in this entry.** Computing `git patch-id --stable` for all 539 and intersecting against patch-ids of same-subject commits already reachable from the non-updated refs:

* **512 of 539 are patch-identical to commits already in this repository.** Same patch, new SHAs — the wave is a rebase/re-push of the already-imported fuzz-audit corpus onto a fresh base.
* **27 patches are genuinely new.**

Spot-verified pairs, recorded so this is reproducible: `a1d3cd809b` and `2d9ad0b86a` (`validation: keep failed blocks out of candidates`) both hash to `5aec0b12d9cf`; `f023f524d9` and `f1dec7aa10` (`validation: readd redownloaded block candidates`) both to `66c6954a2a1a`; `f12f0b41a0` and `7bae372f06` (`validation: keep preciousblock ordering monotonic`) both to `4afd964803a2`. These are the same commits this ledger already recorded under "Imported 515-commit fuzz audit".

**Method consequence — the campaign-signature filter no longer suffices.** The recorded rule ("a commit touching `agent-journal/*` AND production `src/` together" cut a month to 116 commits / 111 subjects) now returns **3125 commits / 1733 distinct subjects** over 2026-07-04..2026-08-04. The campaign has scaled roughly fifteen-fold (cycle numbers went 215 on 2026-07-31 to 479 on 2026-08-04 — four days). Subject-uniqueness alone still leaves 1.8x duplication, and patch-id showed 95% duplication inside this wave. Note the dedup is deliberately **conservative**: the comparison pool was restricted to same-subject commits on non-updated refs since 2026-07-01, so a rebased commit that also changed its subject counts as "new". The real duplication rate is therefore at least 95%, not at most. **Add `git patch-id --stable` dedup against the existing ref set as a mandatory step before counting or ranking anything at this scale**; a subject- or SHA-based count now overstates real work by more than an order of magnitude. Pre-filter the comparison pool by subject first — patch-id'ing the full 27k-commit month pool is impractical, but the same-subject subset is ~535 commits and takes seconds.

### The 27 genuinely-new patches, triaged individually — none warrants prioritization

Each was read as a diff together with its `agent-journal/` hunk, ownership-checked by `gh search prs` (symbol **and** behaviour phrasings), by `git branch --contains`, and by diffing its production hunk against our 3391 local branch tips. Result: **8 already ours, 1 owned upstream, 16 assertion/oracle-only, 2 genuinely new and unowned.**

* **Already ours (8).** `159a7810c9` / `70a6d16370` / `a9b93af737` are the three `gettxspendingprevout` commits, equal to `3340fcb471` / `52ce8bb0bb` / `b9d291db41` on `l0rinc/rpc-gettxspendingprevout-linear` (fork PR #247). `46c0c5e583` is the pruned-unlinked change, a strict subset of `a06f160417` (fork PR #218 / issue #31512). `4fc133bdef` is the index restart race, owned by `l0rinc/index-restart-chainstate-race` (fork PR #232). `680c1fe26a` is covered by `l0rinc/mempool-saturate-ancestry-fees` + `l0rinc/mempool-bound-priority-deltas`. `6825157169`'s production hunks are our open upstream **#35833** log-injection work. `272e04923d` (HEAD body headers) is covered by local `l0rinc/http-response-framing-fixes` `100cc96c91`.
* **Owned upstream (1).** `2fd806663d` "cmpctblock: ignore empty extra transaction slots" — the KB previously flagged this as "the strongest lead" of the compact-block family. **It is now dead code.** The null `extra_txn` slots came from the old `vExtraTxnForCompact.resize()`; our own merged upstream **#35670** replaced that with `reserve` + `emplace_back` plus a `max_extra_txs == 0` early return. Retire that "strongest lead" note.
* **Assertion/oracle-only (16).** Worth stating plainly because it governs how to read this whole corpus: `Assume` is `inline_assertion_check<false>` (`src/util/check.h:116,128`) — it aborts only under `G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME` (fuzz/debug) and **compiles to nothing in release**. Sixteen of the 27 add only `Assume`/`assert`, or add a typed exception whose sole catch site already catches the base class. `ab438a4e00`'s asserts live inside `CTxMemPool::check()`, which runs only under `-checkmempool`. `37fb4d27f2`'s new `Assume(!locator.IsNull())` actually **contradicts** the defensive `IsNull()` branch two lines below it.
* **Genuinely new and unowned (2), both negligible.** `09985b3aa7` (IPC rejects malformed UniValue JSON instead of passing a cleared value through) needs an `ENABLE_IPC` build plus non-default `-ipcbind`, and `src/init.cpp:759` says that socket already grants **unauthenticated RPC access** — so the change grants an attacker nothing. `db6dcf05cd` ("http: parse request fields atomically") has **nil consequence on the baseline**: `MaybeDispatchRequestsFromClient` constructs a fresh `HTTPRequest` inside every loop iteration (`src/httpserver.cpp:995`), so the partial-state case it describes cannot arise — and it points against open upstream **#35735**, which deliberately makes `HTTPRequest` stateful and resumable. Landing it would conflict, not help.

**Three of the campaign's re-derivations are strictly worse than what we already have**, which is worth recording as a pattern rather than a coincidence: on HEAD framing it changes `needs_body` but declines to suppress the body bytes, leaving a body with no `Content-Length`, while ours suppresses both; on the index restart race it wraps `OpenBlockFile` in `WITH_LOCK(cs_main)` while ours routes readers through the never-reassigned `chainman->m_blockman`; and `56e12b558b` adds an `Assume` to the very `GetInfo()` whose real signed-overflow bug (`GetModifiedFee() - GetFee()`) our `l0rinc/mempool-saturate-info-fee-delta` (`e6f1949707`) actually fixes — the oracle sits next to the defect without touching it.

Two are self-inflicted: `9b69098128` fixes an `exception_ptr` race the campaign itself introduced in `09985b3aa7`, and `5e0a9d153d` reverts a bogus `Assume(wtxid == tx->GetWitnessHash())` that `2fd806663d` added and upstream's own tests disprove.

**Method correction:** `gh search prs --state all` is **invalid** — the flag accepts only `open|closed`, and omitting `--state` searches both. Any past sweep that used `--state all` and reported "returns nothing in any state" was running a malformed query; re-verify those ownership claims.

### The one in-scope finding: kernel C API destroys embedder callbacks under its own lock

Surfaced only in the journals — **the campaign never landed a patch for it**, because their source tree is root-owned, so a production-diff-only triage misses it entirely. It appears as the single `🔴 High` entry in `agent-journal/URGENT.md` at cycle 479, sourced from `agent-journal/cycle458-abi-kernel-callback.md` and independently replayed in cycle 468 ("confirmed and persisting").

**Verified directly against `upstream/master`, not taken on the journal's word.** In `src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp`:

* `btck_context_options_set_notifications()` (`:897-902`) takes `LOCK(m_mutex)` and then assigns `m_notifications = std::make_shared<KernelNotifications>(...)`. The assignment destroys the previously held `shared_ptr` **while the lock is held**.
* `~KernelNotifications()` (`:295-302`) calls `m_cbs.user_data_destroy(m_cbs.user_data)` — arbitrary embedder C code — from inside that critical section.
* `m_mutex` is a plain `Mutex` (`:390`), not recursive.
* `btck_context_options_set_validation_interface()` (`:904-908`) and `~KernelValidationInterface()` (`:342-349`) have the identical shape.

So an embedder whose `user_data_destroy` re-enters the same setter self-deadlocks in a release build and trips the double-lock assertion in a debug one. The campaign's raw-C probe exits 134 with `Assertion failed: detected double lock for 'btck_ContextOptions::get(options).m_mutex' in kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp:901`, against a non-reentrant control that exits 0 with `destroy_count=1`.

**Honest severity.** Not remote, not consensus, not fund-loss: it is the kernel C API ↔ embedder boundary, and it needs an embedder that re-enters a setter from a destroy callback. The journal's own scope line is "Confirmed local kernel C-API availability defect; repair blocked by root-owned source", and the `🔴 High` label is the campaign's own calibration — the underlying cycle journal calls it a local availability defect. Treat it as API-misuse-resistance and lock-discipline, not a vulnerability. Its evidence is also a **retained** library from `/mnt/my_storage/bitcoin`, not a fresh build of this checkout, and there is no fail-before/pass-after because they could not edit the source. Our tree is writable, so both are cheap to produce.

**Ownership: unowned.** `gh search prs --repo bitcoin/bitcoin` for "bitcoinkernel callback", "kernel context options notifications", "btck_context_options" returns nothing; "user_data_destroy" returns only merged **#30595** (the PR that introduced the C header API). Control query "kernel" returns #35641/#30342/#33847, so search was working.

**Before preparing this, settle the policy question this ledger already flagged:** the fork-PR-#250 note records that our defensive handling of invalid C API arguments *contradicts upstream's assert-policy for the C API*. Argument validation and lock discipline are different things — moving a destructor out of a critical section does not change the API contract, whereas #250 changes what the API tolerates — but expect the same reviewer instinct ("the embedder must not re-enter"). Dedup: findings-index **F17** (`btck_chainstate_manager_destroy` null deref, FIXED 2026-08-02) is the same family, different site; cycle 458 checked prior fixes `2285ebb253` and `56c7ce125` and found neither moves displaced callback destruction outside a successful setter's critical section.

Fix direction from the journal, which is sound: build the new holder before locking; under the lock, move the old `shared_ptr` into a local and install the new one; let the local destruct after the lock scope; mirror for the validation interface; add raw-C reentrant regressions.

## 2026-08-04 (fifth pass) post-push fetch: two new upstream PRs, and a 1085-commit wave with 4 real patches

Continues the fourth pass. **Baseline advanced again: `upstream/master` `17c5e33e9c` -> `d3cfd02bd7`** (21 non-merge commits; head is the #35501 wallet witness-variant merge).

### Method note: 2869 "changed refs" were 14

`find .git/logs/refs -type f -newermt <cutoff>` reported **2869** files, which looks like an enormous fetch. It is not: the push rewrote/touched almost every **local** `refs/heads/*` reflog. Restricting to `refs/logs/refs/remotes` gives **14 updated remote refs**, which is the real fetch. Scope ref-delta scans to `refs/remotes/` when the intent is "what did the fetch bring"; count `refs/heads/` separately and only when the intent is "what did we do locally". A related gotcha found the same way: extracting the timestamp from a reflog file with `awk '... {break}'` reads the **oldest** entry, not the newest — use `tail -1` per file when clustering by fetch time.

### The delta: 2641 commits, 4 real patches

Graph subtraction over the 14 refs yields **2641 new non-merge commits**: 1248 journal-only, 308 test/review/other, **1085 production-touching**. Applying the now-mandatory `git patch-id --stable` dedup (see the fourth-pass method note): the 1085 collapse to **548 distinct patch-ids, of which 544 already exist elsewhere in this repository. Four are genuinely new.** `audit/transplant-index-fuzz` alone contributed 1381 commits and, once again, essentially all of it is rewritten history rather than new work.

A coverage caveat worth stating so the number is not over-read: of the 546 distinct production subjects in this wave, only **152 appear textually in this file** and 394 do not. That is not 394 missed findings — the patch-id dedup proves 544 of 548 patches already exist in the repository, and earlier passes recorded them by family, by PR number, or by their remote rollup rather than by subject line. It is a fresh confirmation of this file's own standing rule that **subject-absence is a weak coverage signal**; patch-id identity is the authoritative check, and subject matching is only useful as a cheap pre-filter for the pool.

### Own-push reconciliation — this is the substantive part of the pass

Five `origin/l0rinc/*` refs moved and **two new upstream PRs were opened**, so several earlier entries are now stale.

* [x] **New: upstream PR [#35888](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35888) "net: reject oversized outbound messages"** at `d849c8e97c`. `l0rinc/net-reject-oversized-message-types` grew from 2 commits to 4: `bcd14432f9` (characterize outbound message limits), `f52038c145` (the original type-length fix), `d84fdc0ae8` (propagate rejected outbound messages), `d849c8e97c` (**reject oversized outbound payloads**). The new work closes the send/receive asymmetry the fourth-pass discussion identified: incoming transports reject payloads over `MAX_PROTOCOL_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (`net.cpp:771`) while `V1Transport::SetMessageToSend` and `V2Transport::SetMessageToSend` capped nothing. One `IsMessageWithinLimits()` predicate now enforces both the 12-byte type and the 4 MB payload at all three sites, and `PushMessage()`'s previous `Assume` is replaced by a `LogDebug` + drop — correct, because the oversized-payload case now has a **legitimate reachable caller**: the testing-only `sendmsgtopeer` RPC could send a 4,000,001-byte payload and make the peer disconnect, so an `Assume` would abort debug/fuzz builds on valid RPC input. `sendmsgtopeer` now returns an RPC error.
  * **Relationship to open PR [#35880](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35880)** (instagibbs, "fuzz: don't connman.ReceiveMsgFrom oversized msg"): #35880 filters the oversized input inside `src/test/fuzz/p2p_private_broadcast.cpp` because `ConsumeTransaction()` can fabricate a >4 MB transaction. Its "this will never happen in p2p" claim is **true for that path** — `ConnmanTestMsg::ReceiveMsgFrom` is a loopback that encodes with the node's *own* `SetMessageToSend`/`GetBytesToSend` and feeds the bytes back to the same node, so the input is what our node would emit, and consensus bounds that (`MAX_BLOCK_SERIALIZED_SIZE` == `MAX_PROTOCOL_MESSAGE_LENGTH` == 4,000,000, and the receive check is `>` so a maximal block just fits). It should **not** be read as "oversized messages never arrive over p2p": a malicious peer can send one, and that is handled at `net.cpp:771` by rejecting and disconnecting — the fuzz assert fires only because the test helper demands `ReceiveMsgBytes` succeed, which is a harness invariant, not a production one. #35888's description says explicitly that it "addresses the fuzz failure discussed in #35880 in the production send path instead of filtering the input in the harness", and its own commit message records that the OSS-Fuzz input from #35880 passes with no harness restriction. **#35880 is still open and unmerged** — if #35888 lands first, #35880 becomes unnecessary.

### The kernel finding from the fourth pass survives the baseline advance, and its policy objection is weaker than recorded

`btck_context_options_set_notifications()` is **byte-identical on `d3cfd02bd7`** — still `LOCK(m_mutex)` followed by a `shared_ptr` assignment whose destructor runs the embedder's `user_data_destroy` inside the critical section, with `m_mutex` non-recursive. No branch exists for it.

The fourth pass warned that this might run into the same objection as fork PR #250 ("contradicts upstream's assert-policy for the C API"). **Checked, and the overlap does not exist:** #250's five commits (`80257396b6` reject invalid chain types, `d2f17ee891` ignore invalid logging settings, `6f23568be8` report invalid script verification arguments, `9a1cdef1e1` reject invalid spent output arrays, `8e6eddf3bd` return null for out-of-range accessors) touch **none** of the setter functions — `git diff` for `set_notifications`/`set_validation_interface` against that branch returns zero hits. #250 argues about what the API should *tolerate as input*, which is a genuine policy question; moving a destructor out of a critical section changes no API contract at all and is ordinary lock discipline. Rank the kernel item without the #250 caveat attached.

### Fifth-pass addendum — full read of the adoption branches and journals

## 2026-08-05 THE SEVERITY REANALYSIS — this file was re-verified end-to-end, and it changes the ranking

**Read this section before trusting any severity claim earlier in this file.** Commit `ff1935f8a4` on `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/transplant-index-fuzz` adds `reviews/2026-08-05-knowledgebase-severity-triage.md` (378 lines): a re-verification of **this entire knowledgebase** against live master, by 13 parallel verification agents checking ~100 distinct code-shape claims, with PR/issue states pulled from the GitHub API. Baselines: Core `d3cfd02bd7`, secp256k1 `687155df6b`. Every source claim was read out of the pinned ref (`git show origin/master:<path>`), not a worktree.

It is the highest-quality artifact this campaign has produced, and it **overrules several standing entries here**, including one this file promoted only a day earlier.

### Headline verdict

* **Zero 🔴.** On a default-config mainnet node there is no unauthenticated, realistically-reachable crash, consensus break, or fund-loss bug anywhere in this knowledgebase. This file's own repeated "severity ceiling is medium" conclusion survives independent re-verification.
* **24 🟠**, ~70 🟡, ~200+ 🟢.
* **Only three 🟠 items are live, unowned, and replay-ready.** Everything else at 🟠 is already owned by an open upstream or fork PR:
  1. **MuSig2 crafted-PSBT abort** — `src/script/sign.cpp:324`
  2. **RBF conflicting-fee overflow** — `src/validation.cpp:1011`
  3. **MiniMiner arithmetic** — `src/node/mini_miner.cpp`

### Sixth-pass addendum — the reanalysis's own "three unowned" list is wrong on two of three

The three headline candidates were independently re-verified against `c4fbd3c721` (the reanalysis used `d3cfd02bd7`), including a **live reproduction against a real `bitcoind`**. Result: **only one of the three is actually unowned and replay-ready.** Correct the queue above accordingly.

* [x] **Candidate 1, MuSig2 PSBT abort — CONFIRMED, and stronger than the reanalysis states.** Reproduced on a real binary with `-disablewallet`, using the two PSBTs from closed PR #35154. **Two distinct abort variants**, not one:
  * **Variant A** — a wrong *non-hardened* derivation path trips `Assert(XOnlyPubKey(extpub.pubkey) == script_pubkey)` at `src/script/sign.cpp:328`. Process dead.
  * **Variant B** — a hardened index (`m/0'`) trips `assert((nChild >> 31) == 0)` at `src/pubkey.cpp:343`. Process dead.
  Asserts are live in release: `src/util/check.h:83-85` is `#if defined(NDEBUG) #error "Cannot compile without assertions!"`. **No wallet is required** — `finalizepsbt` / `analyzepsbt` / `descriptorprocesspsbt` reach `SignPSBTInput` with `DUMMY_SIGNING_PROVIDER`, and the only gate is a 4-byte fingerprint match between two attacker-supplied PSBT fields. Authenticated RPC, not P2P. DoS only: no memory corruption, no key or fund exposure.
  * **Why #35154 closed matters for how we file this.** It was **not** closed as invalid: achow101 closed it over LLM-authorship policy while disputing the "vulnerability" framing, Sjors asked for fuzz coverage, and maflcko uploaded both inputs to OSS-Fuzz. So the correct framing is a **robustness fix** (`CHECK_NONFATAL` / `return false` on the two assert sites) with a human-owned rationale and the fuzz coverage Sjors asked for — explicitly **not** a security advisory. Filing it as a vulnerability would walk straight into the objection that already sank the previous attempt.
  * Note `audit/resurrection` converts the `pubkey.cpp` Derive asserts to `return false`, which would defuse Variant B only, and never touches `sign.cpp:328` (Variant A). It is a 443-file/40k-line aggregation branch and is not a usable basis. **No focused branch owns this.**
* [x] **Candidate 2, RBF conflicting-fee overflow — NOT unowned. The reanalysis is wrong here.** `src/validation.cpp:1011` (`m_subpackage.m_conflicting_fees += it->GetModifiedFee();`) and its `PackageRBFChecks` twin are **already patched by our own open fork PR #217** (`l0rinc/rbf-modified-fee-aggregate-overflow`, head `98cb0897a7`, `SaturatingAdd`) — verified: that head touches `m_conflicting_fees` eight times in `validation.cpp`. The adjacent `PaysForRBF` delta overflow is fork PR **#209**. Severity is also lower than implied: reaching int64 overflow needs `prioritisetransaction` (admin-only RPC) because natural mempool fees are bounded by the ~2.1e15 sat money supply, and in a release build the consequence is wrapped-sum UB / a wrong RBF policy decision, **not** a crash (`-ftrapv` is debug-only). **Action: shepherd #217/#209, do not open anything new.**
* [x] **Candidate 3, MiniMiner — the premise does not hold on master.** The reanalysis rests on a production `Assume(total_bump_fee >= 0)`; **there is no such `Assume` on `upstream/master` or on our HEAD** (verified: zero occurrences in `src/node/mini_miner.cpp`). It was introduced by `f71cd9336a`, which lives only on `detached626` / `audit/transplant-index-fuzz` and is **not an ancestor of HEAD** — as is the `d1f9ae2dca` clamp that "fixes" it. So the abort is fork-self-inflicted. What remains on real master is `CalculateTotalBumpFees` (`src/node/mini_miner.cpp:427`) returning a negative value for an overfunded shared ancestor package, consumed only by **wallet** callers (`feebumper.cpp:85`, `wallet/rpc/spend.cpp:1520`, `wallet/spend.cpp:794`) — a wallet fee-estimation nit, de-scoped by our own exclusions. **Drop it from the queue.**

**Revised queue head:** the MuSig2 abort is the *only* unowned, replay-ready 🟠 in the entire knowledgebase. Everything else at that severity is owned by an open upstream or fork PR. This also means the reanalysis's own headline — "three unowned and replay-ready" — should be read as **one**, and a future sweep should not re-derive the other two as fresh work.

### Prepared: `l0rinc/musig2-psbt-derivation-abort` @ `44f69fc298` (local rewrite of pushed `b96081dbfc`)

The queue's #1 is now prepared as two signed commits on `c4fbd3c721`, **7 production lines** in `src/script/sign.cpp` plus a 24-line functional characterization and regression. `0911752fd8` observes the four current abort outcomes, restarts the node after each RPC disconnect, and marks the old `None` results with trailing TODOs. `44f69fc298` adds the production fix and flips only those two expectations to `False`. The pushed fork ref remains at `b96081dbfc`, so the local branch reports ahead 2 / behind 1. The pushed tree is preserved at `backup/musig2-psbt-derivation-abort-one-commit-20260805`, and the earlier two-commit tip remains at `backup/musig2-psbt-derivation-abort-two-commits-20260805`.

**Both variants reproduced on current master before writing anything**, using the PSBTs from closed #35154 against a `RelWithDebInfo` build with `-disablewallet`:

* `finalizepsbt <mismatched-path PSBT>` -> node dead (`Assert(XOnlyPubKey(extpub.pubkey) == script_pubkey)`, `sign.cpp:328`).
* `analyzepsbt <hardened-path PSBT>` -> node dead (`assert((nChild >> 31) == 0)`, `pubkey.cpp:343`). **`analyzepsbt` is read-only**, so inspection alone is enough.
* Both PSBTs `decodepsbt` cleanly first, confirming the only gate is the 4-byte fingerprint match.

**The fix** (`44f69fc298`): reject hardened indices with `std::ranges::any_of(agg_info.path, …)` before deriving — public derivation has no hardened form, so such a path can never produce the script pubkey — and replace the fatal `Assert` with `if (…) continue;`. Both use `continue`, matching the adjacent empty-path and fingerprint guards, so an inapplicable aggregate is skipped rather than aborting. The loop now iterates `uint32_t` instead of narrowing each index to `int`, which is implementation-defined once the hardened bit is set. `<algorithm>` is already included on master, so unlike closed #35154 no include change is needed.

**Verification:** Full `rpc_psbt.py` passes at both `0911752fd8` and `44f69fc298` after rebuilding `bitcoind` at each commit. At the characterization commit, all four RPC/path combinations abort and are observed by the passing scaffold. At the tip, the same calls return `False` and the node stays alive. The earlier final-tree runs also passed `wallet_musig.py` and `psbt_tests`/`descriptor_tests`/`bip328_tests`/`script_tests`. `git diff --check` and Python compilation are clean, and both rewritten signatures are good.

**Framing for the PR description, and this matters more than the diff.** #35154 was closed by achow101 on LLM-authorship grounds after two objections: "Stop calling RPC crashes vulnerabilities" and a policy that LLM output is not accepted where the author cannot explain or test it. **Sjors gave the constructive direction and it should be quoted as the motivation**: "It would be nice if a PSBT co-signer service doesn't need to restart their node any time a PSBT from an untrusted source does something unexpected. Perhaps we can add fuzz coverage to enforce that `CHECK_NONFATAL` is hit, rather than Assert." maflcko separately converted both inputs to the fuzz input format and uploaded them to OSS-Fuzz. So: present this as robustness for PSBT co-signer services with a reproducer and regression, **never as a security advisory**, and do not reuse #35154's "vulnerability"/"release-blocking" language or its Trail-of-Bits/ANT-2026-05771 credit block. Sjors's fuzz suggestion is worth answering explicitly — either by adding the coverage or by saying why the functional regression is the right level.

## 2026-08-05 open upstream PR comment/conflict audit

Audited all 23 open non-draft `bitcoin/bitcoin` PRs authored by `l0rinc`. All heads are GitHub `MERGEABLE`, `git merge-tree --write-tree upstream/master <head>` succeeds against `c4fbd3c721`, and the synthetic merges preserve the exact authored added/deleted lines. `git diff --check` is clean for every PR. #35818 and #35874 have fully green current checks despite stale GraphQL rollup `FAILURE` states. #35662 is now rebased to `a5ac29bfb6`, mergeable, and still running CI; the earlier four-`DIRTY` portfolio note is stale for this PR.

Actionable findings:

* **#35654 needs redesign or retirement.** The latest top-level comment correctly points out that setting the first malformed coin cursor key invalid makes ordinary `while (cursor->Valid())` consumers treat corruption as clean end-of-data. `ComputeUTXOStats` and UTXO scan/dump paths can therefore return empty or truncated results. This should report iterator decode failure instead, aligning with the separate `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors` work, rather than silently ending iteration.
* **#35714 log assertion folded locally.** Characterization commit `772b872fc0` wraps the injected flush failure with `ASSERT_DEBUG_LOG`, asserting the expected lower-level fatal log and suppressing the unique stderr line. Keep the combined `flushed && state` Boost assertions because both conditions describe the same flush result. Do not restore the removed `LogWarning`: `FlushBlockFile()` already calls `flushError()`, which reaches `AbortNode()` and logs the specific failure. Skipping `m_next_write` after the fatal error is appropriate because shutdown has already been requested; #30611 deliberately moved the timer update after the chainstate write so the interval starts when a completed write finishes.

### The 4 novel findings — replayed locally against `upstream/master`, per this file's own "leads until replayed" rule

* [ ] 🟡 **NOVEL, CONFIRMED — `ecmult_const_xonly` leaves secret-derived state uncleared.** Verified by reading `src/ecmult_const_impl.h`: the function declares `secp256k1_fe g, i; secp256k1_ge p; secp256k1_gej rj;`, computes `rj = q * P` via `secp256k1_ecmult_const`, derives `i` (the inverse) and writes `r`, then `return 1;` with **no `gej_clear`/`fe_clear` on `rj` or `i`** — confirmed by grepping the whole tail for `memczero|_clear`, which matches nothing. The caller is ellswift XDH with the secret key. The scan states it verified this is absent from **both** open upstream PR #1885's diff and the fork's `resurrection-hunt` fix, i.e. it **survives either pending stack-clearing fix** — that cross-check is the reason this is worth carrying, and it is the one item here I did not independently re-verify (it needs the PR diff). This is the strongest novel item: same family as F-ec1, but at a site nobody is fixing.
* [ ] 🟡 **NOVEL, CONFIRMED — ECDH writes a public-computable `output` while returning 0.** Verified in `src/modules/ecdh/main_impl.h`: on `overflow` or zero scalar the code does `secp256k1_scalar_cmov(&s, &secp256k1_scalar_one, overflow)`, runs `ecmult_const` with `s = 1`, and **still calls the hash function**, writing `H(P)` into `output` before `return !!ret & !overflow;`. It clears `x`, `y`, `s`, `pt`, `res` — but never `output`. Hazard is confined to callers that ignore the return value; the value written is public-computable, so it is not a secret leak. **Its premise correction is the load-bearing part and I verified it: `git log -S memczero -- src/modules/ecdh/main_impl.h` is empty — upstream ECDH never had memczero-on-failure**, contradicting a prior journal premise. Note this is *not* covered by our #11, which fixes the ignored `pubkey_load` return, a different path in the same function.
* [x] 🟡 **NOVEL but already ours — silentpayments ctime test never reaches the matching-scan/label-batch paths.** The scan's own fix pointer is branch `sp-ctime-label-scan` (`b42856dd`), which this file already carries as `l0rinc/silentpayments-ctime-label-scan` (fork PR #1898 open upstream). No new work.
* [ ] 🟡 **NOVEL, CONFIRMED — unpinned `pip install lief` in CI.** Verified: `ci/linux-debian.Dockerfile:84` is a bare `RUN pip install lief`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has **two** unpinned installs (lines 504 and 599; the scan cites only 599). The contrast it draws is real — the same Dockerfile sha512-verifies the gcc snapshot and uses a GPG-verified apt repo. CI-impact only, but it is the cheapest standalone commit in the whole list and sits in the same "supply-chain pinning" family as the Core-side #35754 work we already did.

**Two journal-record corrections worth absorbing**, because both invalidate a premise this file or its sources relied on: (1) the ECDH memczero premise above; (2) **the musig zero-nonce-scalar checks have been VERIFY-only since the original merge `f411841a`**, so fork PR #26's *closure* premise ("redundant, a runtime check already exists upstream") was wrong — impact stays ~2^-256 with an accepted-risk comment, but if #26 is ever re-argued, the "already upstream" objection does not hold. This is the same release-build-gap framing the 08-03 entry recorded for `goal83-ecmult-current`.

**Also flagged, recorded as a lead I did not fully replay:** the scan claims `fe_half`'s m<=31 precondition is undocumented and that there is a genuine 5x52-vs-10x26 divergence at m=32, **not covered by PR #16**. I confirmed the two backends' `fe_impl_half` bodies differ in shift width (`mask = -(t0 & one) >> 6` on 10x26 vs `>> 12` on 5x52) and that `src/field.h:326-330` documents only "r must be a valid field element" with no magnitude ceiling — consistent with the claim, but the m=32 divergence itself needs the numeric replay this file already did for F-m32 before it can be ranked. Wallet scope, and not a defect fix. **This is the third consecutive wave where patch-id dedup is the only thing separating a four-digit commit count from a single-digit finding count.**

### The scan artifact

All the substance of the narrow window is two docs commits on `rpi5-8gb-500gb/threat-model-scan-2026-08-04`:

* **`3f0a44ea56`** adds `security-review/bitcoin-core-2026-08-05/` (10 area files + summary) and `security-review/secp256k1-2026-08-05/` (7 areas + summary) — a static security review of Core master `c4fbd3c721` and secp256k1 `687155df`, 10 parallel deep-dives, headline findings re-verified against source by a consolidating reviewer.
* **`847eafaa1b`** adds `security-review/dedup-context-2026-08-05.txt` — **the l0rinc PR ledger and local-branch list the scan deduped against.** This is what makes it worth more than the campaign's usual output: every finding was checked against our open/closed fork PRs first, and anything already fixed *at HEAD* was dropped.

Its stated motivation is the July 2026 **ColdCard incident** (silent RNG weakening via an existence-vs-value flag check); it hunted that bug class plus loss-of-funds, bad randomness, and remotely-triggerable defects.

### Headline verdict: 0 critical, 4 high, ~50 medium — and most live ones are already ours

**The ColdCard bug class does not exist in Core**: every OS-entropy failure path aborts via `RandFailure()` (`src/random.cpp:54-58`), there is no software-RNG fallback anywhere, all key material uses the strong RNG, and build-level feature probes are value-checked and fail closed.

The dedup is the real story: **~19 items in its fix-exists ledger are live at HEAD with the fix already in one of our PRs** — #204, #214, #221, #225/#226, #234, #235, #236, #237, #239, #245, #249, #251, #253, #256, #258, #261, #266, #267, #269, plus the assumeutxo `tm6-cleanup-orphan-sweep` branch. The mempool/policy area reports **no 🔴 or 🟠 at all**, with 8 of its 9 findings annotated `fix-exists l0rinc/bitcoin#{209,217,228,238,254,262,263,268}`.

**The four 🟠 highs, with our scope applied:**

1. 🟠 **`contrib/verify-binaries/verify.py` trusted-signature threshold is a tautology — NOVEL, unowned.** Independently confirmed: at `:370-372`, `good_trusted` and `good_untrusted` partition `good`, so `num_trusted` is identically `len(good)`; `--min-good-sigs` (default 3) gates on *count only* and `--trusted-keys` cannot affect the verdict. `EXPKEYSIG` and `REVKEYSIG` both route to `good_sigs` (`:185-193`), so expired and revoked keys count toward the threshold. The README's "10 trusted signatures" example does not do what it documents. Exploitable via a forged `SHA256SUMS` carrying >=3 attacker signatures through the documented `--import-keys` flow — needs download-host compromise or first-run MITM, hence high not critical. Unchanged since 2021; symbol and behaviour searches find no PR or issue (control query returns hits). **This is `contrib/`, which our scope excludes** — but it is the release-binary verification tool users are told to run, not ordinary dev tooling. Flagged as an explicit scope call rather than silently dropped.
2. 🟠 **First-time wallet encryption discards DB write returns — fix-exists.** See the NDEBUG correction below for what actually survives. Wallet scope; fork PR #234 closed unmerged, open upstream **#35752** is the live vehicle.
3. 🟠 **`MigrateToSQLite` false success — NOVEL, but see the correction below; it largely collapses.**
4. 🟠 **HTTP responses to HEAD requests carry bodies on keep-alive connections — fix-exists, the only in-scope high.** Fork PR #204 fixes exactly these defects with tests and has never been upstreamed. Verified in detail in the addendum below, where its severity is corrected down.

### Correction to the scan: both wallet highs rest on a false "debug-only assert" premise

Verified independently against `c36ffd870e`, and it collapses the scan's strongest *novel* finding.

The scan repeatedly says these sites are guarded by "debug-only `assert(...)`" and that "in a release build" execution continues. **That is wrong for Bitcoin Core.** `src/util/check.h:83-85` is `#if defined(NDEBUG) #error "Cannot compile without assertions!"`, `src/wallet/wallet.cpp:55` includes `util/check.h`, and `cmake/module/ProcessConfigurations.cmake:123,125` call `remove_cxx_flag_from_all_configs(/DNDEBUG)` and `(-DNDEBUG)`. So `NDEBUG` cannot be defined in any translation unit and **bare `assert()` is live in every Core build, release included.**

* **🟠-3 `MigrateToSQLite` largely collapses.** `wallet.cpp` guards the failed `TxnBegin` (`assert(began)`), the per-record `Write` failure (`assert(false)`, after aborting the txn, closing and removing the new DB), and the failed `TxnCommit` (`assert(committed)`). None is skipped in release, so a failed migration is a **loud abort** with the original deleted, the partial SQLite file removed, and the `*.legacy.bak` still on disk — recoverable, and impossible to mistake for success. Downgrade from 🟠-novel to 🟡 crash-on-local-IO-failure.
* **🟠-2's "release continues past commit failure" is also wrong** — `wallet.cpp:874-884` aborts via `assert(false)` on both the `Encrypt` and `TxnCommit` failures. What *is* real is narrower: `encrypted_batch->WriteMasterKey(nMasterKeyMaxID, master_key)` at **`wallet.cpp:864` discards its return value**, so a failed master-key write inside an otherwise-committing txn can leave encrypted keys without the master-key record. That single line is the genuine defect.

**Method note for future scans:** "debug-only assert / release continues" is a recurring and confidently-stated error in this campaign's output. Core rejects `NDEBUG` tree-wide, so `assert`, `Assert`, and `CHECK_NONFATAL` all evaluate in release; only `Assume` is a no-op there (it aborts solely under `G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME`). Check which macro a finding actually names before accepting a severity that depends on the distinction.

### The ~10 genuinely novel latent items

Not in any PR or branch: exponential BDB re-parse in `migrate.cpp`; corrupt `FLAGS` treated as absent; **leveldb iterator `status()` never checked** (we have `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors` prepared — the scan rediscovered it independently, corroborating the 2026-08-05 reanalysis's "downplayed" call); `BufferedWriter`/`SQLiteBatch` throwing destructors; **unbounded pipelined-request queue on the HTTP server**; **`CheckEphemeralSpends` co-spend delay**; FORTIFY_SOURCE cmake-cache staleness; txgraph retained-capacity accounting (= our #262); **SOCKS5 NOAUTH-first killing Tor stream isolation**; **REST worker-exception info leak**.

The mempool one is explicitly minor in the scan's own words — `CheckEphemeralSpends` rejecting co-spends of a parent whose dust another mempool tx already spends is "policy over-strictness… remotely reachable at minrelay cost (minor impact)", with the reorg analogue already fixed publicly as bitcoin/bitcoin#33616.

### Two upstream merges that matter to our queue

* [x] **#35878 "net_processing: process unique tx INVs only" merged.** Adds two short-lived `unordered_set<uint256, SaltedUint256Hasher>` per INV message and `continue`s on a repeat before `AddKnownTx`/`ToGenTxid` (+9 lines, plus `p2p_tx_download.py` coverage). **This is the receive side** — an inbound peer repeating a txid within one message — so it does **not** own our queued `68b745e208` relay-token item, which is about send-side tokens taken at announcement before the per-peer known-filter applies. But it is direct evidence that upstream accepts this exact class of per-message duplicate-work bound, which is the best framing available if `68b745e208` is ever rewritten.
* [x] **#35759 "fuzz: check http_request body matches framing" merged** (`src/test/fuzz/http_request.cpp`, +19). Adjacent to our `l0rinc/http-response-framing-fixes` (`100cc96c91`) — the merged work is a fuzz oracle on the *request* side, ours is a production fix on the *response* side. Not an owner; cite it as the coverage precedent when #204 goes upstream.

### Own-push reconciliation and branch currency

The other 14 commits of the narrow window (11 patches by the month-scale count) are all ours, on four reworked branches:

### Three independent sources converge on the iterator-error work

The strongest signal in this pass, and no single source would have carried it:

1. The **2026-08-05 severity reanalysis** listed the `CDBIterator` `status()` swallow as *downplayed* — demoted by a scope rule rather than by severity, with this file's own text ("worse than a crash") supporting the higher rating.
2. **This scan independently rediscovered it** as a novel latent item, having deduped against our whole PR ledger first — i.e. it did not find our prepared branch, so the defect reads as unowned from outside.
3. The **2026-08-05 open-PR audit** records a reviewer on **#35654** making the same argument from the opposite direction: setting the first malformed coin cursor key invalid makes ordinary `while (cursor->Valid())` consumers treat corruption as clean end-of-data, so `ComputeUTXOStats` and the UTXO scan/dump paths can return empty or truncated results. Its recommendation is to **report iterator decode failure instead**, explicitly aligning with `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors`.

So #35654 as written is the *wrong shape* and our unpushed branch is the right one. The sixth pass established the remaining blocker is gone (no conflict with the reworked #34132; rebases clean). This is now a redesign of an open upstream PR rather than a new finding.

### Method note: the ref-level pre-filter is load-bearing, and it is a separate stage from the dedup

While auditing the pipeline, `ae5220ee85` ("support: preserve ASan poisoning after pool destruction", `rpi5-16-2/audit/pool-asan-cycle308`) reached neither the "new" nor the "already-known" side of the patch-id intersection. It is **not** a gap: that ref's tip SHA was already recorded at the 08-05 entry, so the ref-level pre-filter correctly excluded the whole ref before subtraction. Recorded because the failure mode is instructive — **a commit dropped by the tip-SHA pre-filter never reaches the patch-id stage, so "not in the new set" is not evidence it was seen by the dedup.** When auditing coverage, check the pre-filter and the dedup as two separate stages.

### Independent verification of the scan's in-scope items

All re-read against `c36ffd870e`, not the scan's `c4fbd3c721`.

* [x] **🟠-4 HEAD-response-with-body is live at every claimed line, but the scan overstates the default-node surface and the severity.** Confirmed: `httpserver.cpp:526` `needs_body` has no method term; `:559-561` writes `Content-Length` with no prior `RemoveAll`; keep-alive at `:533-577` is derived only from the *request* headers so a handler-set `Connection: close` (`:181-183`) is ignored; `:593` appends the body unconditionally. `httprpc.cpp:200-202` answers `HEAD /` with a 405 **before** the auth check at `:204-227`, and `rest.cpp` is method-agnostic (`git grep GetRequestMethod src/rest.cpp` → zero hits). Introduced by `cdf71998e5` (#35182), made live by `21c7542cf8`.
  * **Correction:** the scan lists `HEAD /rest/* → 200 with body` as an unauthenticated default-node trigger. **It is not** — `src/init.cpp:175` is `DEFAULT_REST_ENABLE{false}`, gated at `:795`. The only default-node trigger is `HEAD /` → 405 plus a 41-byte body (`bitcoind` does `SoftSetBoolArg("-server", true)` at `src/bitcoind.cpp:186`; `/` is registered `exactMatch` at `httprpc.cpp:347`), reachable by any local user or by any web page the operator visits via `fetch(…, {mode:'no-cors', method:'HEAD'})`.
  * **Severity: 🟡, not conditional-🟠.** Standalone, the desynced connection is the attacker's own. Cross-client poisoning is **asserted, never demonstrated**, and needs a fronting reverse proxy that pools and reuses upstream keep-alive connections — a non-default deployment, untested against any specific proxy. It is a real RFC 9110 §9.3.2 violation and a clear libevent-removal regression, which is the honest case for fixing it.
  * **Ours and finished:** `l0rinc/http-response-framing-fixes` @ `100cc96c91` (4 commits) = fork PR #204, open since 2026-07-03, also on origin as `detached580`. **No upstream PR exists** (searched `needs_body`, `response framing`, `HEAD request`, `keep-alive`, `Content-Length`, `pipelin`; control query returns hits). All four defect sites are byte-identical to the branch's base, so the substance still applies verbatim; `git merge-tree` shows **exactly one conflict**, confined to the `m_send_buffer.insert`/`m_send_ready` region at `:591-603` (drift from the #35592 ACL move and the `m_send_ready`-under-lock fix). One mechanical hunk to re-apply.
* [x] **SOCKS5 NOAUTH-first is live but nearly vacuous as framed.** `netbase.cpp:404-411` offers `[NOAUTH, USER_PASS]` in that order whenever credentials exist, and `:445-446` accepts a NOAUTH selection silently with no log line; credentials only exist under `proxy.m_tor_stream_isolation` (`:817-822`). Requires `-proxy`/`-onion`, so **not reachable on a default node**, and no remote attacker can trigger it — only the proxy chooses. The scan's stated attacker model ("malicious or MITM'd SOCKS endpoint") **defeats its own finding**, since a hostile proxy already sees every destination. The one real case is an *honest but non-Tor* SOCKS5 forwarder chained to Tor that selects NOAUTH — genuine silent degradation, narrow. Real Tor picks USER_PASS when offered, else `-proxyrandomize` would have been dead since ~2015 (`22f816ef4d`) — evidence by absence, not proof. Unowned; nearest fork work (`1aa2744f5b`, `cb90d4176d`) is fuzz/oracle coverage only. ~3-line fix. Low priority. 🟡
* [x] **REST worker-exception leak: mechanism real, no reachable trigger found.** `httpserver.cpp:168-184` does `err_msg = e.what()` → `WriteReply(HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, err_msg)`, with an upstream `// TODO:` at `:182` conceding error formatting is unfinished. But it needs `-rest=1`, and every REST failure funnels through `RESTERR` (`rest.cpp:199-201`, `:484-496`, `:518-520`, `:802-813`, `:960-975`). No path-leaking exception demonstrated; the scan concedes "no secret material observed". Do not branch it alone. 🟡
* [x] **Unbounded pipelined-request queue — DROP, owned upstream.** Live (`httpserver.cpp:991-1036` parses every complete request into an uncapped `m_req_queue`), but open upstream **#35735** states the fix exactly ("Only parse one request at a time from the receive buffer… TCP backpressure will kick in"), with #35730 (`-rpcmaxconnections`) and #35844 complementary. **Correction: #35735's head has moved to `d354b72b56` (2026-08-06); the previously recorded `0ced8c35ae` is stale.**
* [x] **leveldb iterator `status()` — ours, done, still not on origin.** `dbwrapper.cpp:404` `Valid()` still returns `m_impl_iter->iter->Valid()` unchanged, with `verify_checksums = true` at `:225`. Branch `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors` @ `16df166000` (2 commits: memenv fault-injection characterization + routing non-OK `status()` through `HandleError`) is **local-only** — `for-each-ref --contains` finds no remote. `src/dbwrapper.{cpp,h}` are identical between its base `556988790a` and `c36ffd870e`, and it **merges clean**. Trigger is local corruption, so no urgency by our scope — but it is finished, and it is the shape #35654's reviewer asked for.

## 2026-08-06 secp upstream-submission priority decision: #15 first, and why the new findings should NOT become branches yet

Answers a direct question — of the pushed `l0rinc/secp256k1` fork drafts, which goes upstream next, versus preparing this session's novel findings as new fork branches. **Verdict: take a pushed draft upstream; do not branch the new findings yet.** Readiness measured against `upstream/master` `687155df6b`; all candidates were re-checked with `git merge-tree` (every one rebases clean) and the two defect sites were re-read out of the pinned ref.

### Why not the new findings

The two confirmed-novel items from the security scan are **leads, not branches** — no characterization, no fail-before, no test. This file's own workflow gate requires that before proposing. More decisively, **`ecmult_const_xonly`'s highest-leverage action is a review comment on open upstream #1885, not a competing PR**: #1885 is the stack-clearing PR for `ecmult_const` in the *same file*, and the scan's cross-check is that it misses this sibling site. A comment lands the fix inside an already-moving PR at a fraction of the cost, and arrives while the PR is still open. The ECDH output-on-failure item and the `lief` CI pin are both cheap but neither outranks a finished, validated draft that is merely unopened.

### Ranked, with the readiness numbers

| Fork PR | Head | Behind | Defect class | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **#15 `preserve-overlapping-tweak-inputs`** | `3bbd8985dd` | 14 | legal API call returns **success with a wrong result** | **open first** |
| #13 `scalar-mul-shift-width` | `aef223a621` | 16 | sanitizer-confirmed OOB read, both backends | second — strongest *evidence* |
| #36 `contrib-lax-der-privatekey-bounds` | `fd92bb725a` | **0** | benign pointer UB in `contrib/` | free to open alongside |

* [ ] **#15 is the pick, and its defect was re-verified live on `687155df6b`.** `secp256k1_ec_pubkey_tweak_add` (`src/secp256k1.c`) does `ret = secp256k1_pubkey_load(...); memset(pubkey, 0, sizeof(*pubkey)); ret = ret && ..._tweak_add_helper(&p, tweak32);` — the `memset` wipes the object **before** `tweak32` is read. `secp256k1_keypair_xonly_tweak_add` (`src/modules/extrakeys/main_impl.h`) has the identical shape, and that one is the **BIP341 keypair/secret path**. An aliased tweak is therefore zeroed first, a zero tweak is *documented valid*, and the call returns 1 with the object untweaked.
  Why it outranks the other two: it is the only candidate where a **legal** public-API call silently produces a wrong result — the most reviewer-legible defect class here — and upstream has already labelled the sibling aliasing hazard **#1785 (`_gej_rescale` `s` parameter) as `bug`**, so this class is one upstream treats as a defect rather than as caller error.
* [x] **This revises the 2026-08-05 entry's "next upstream candidate is #36".** That was a *readiness* pick made the day #36 was rebased and validated, not a merit ranking. Two things changed: the independent security scan **rediscovered both of #15's sites** (`ec_pubkey_tweak_add` overlapping tweak "silently no-ops pubkey (returns 1)" and the `keypair_xonly_tweak_add` twin), which is fresh third-party corroboration; and #36's own framing weakened on inspection — it is `contrib/`, benign, with adjacent open #1895 and 2020 draft #781 both circling the same files. #36 is still worth opening (zero rebase, already validated) — just not *first*.
* [ ] **The one real risk to #15, and it must be preempted in the PR text.** The security scan classifies its own findings as living in a "documented-UB domain" and lists **"out-of-contract aliasing"** among them — i.e. it implicitly treats overlap as caller error. **This file's own verification says otherwise**, and that verification is the load-bearing argument: grepping `include/*.h` for overlap/alias/distinct wording finds *no aliasing policy anywhere in the public headers*, and the per-function docs are silent. So overlap is not forbidden, and the fix is legitimate rather than papering over a caller bug. Lead the PR with that, cite #1785, and do not let the "callers must not alias" objection go unanswered — it is the single likeliest reason this gets closed.

## 2026-08-06 prepared for push: `l0rinc/field-10x26-normalize-overflow` rebased onto `687155df6b` @ `b7fc137c35`

Acts on the blocker the priority entry above flagged as the costliest open gap. **Selection rationale, since it differs from the upstream-submission ranking:** the question was what to *push*, not what to open upstream, and only two secp branches were actually diverged from `origin`. `l0rinc/silentpayments-ctime-label-scan` was checked and **needs nothing** — local `2f6a919cbf` and origin `b561d6c58c` have **byte-identical trees** (`f5ad49527a…`) on the same base, so the divergence is cosmetic SHA drift on a branch already serving open upstream #1898; pushing it would only churn a live PR. That leaves this one, which is simultaneously the simplest (one commit, two files, already written and validated) and the most urgent (it is the best-substantiated secp finding we own, and fork PR #16 has been advertising a stale base for several passes).

* **Rebase:** `4b7a7d5e03` (base `7fecac74ae`) -> **`b7fc137c35`** (base `687155df6b`, **0 behind**). `git range-diff 7fecac74ae..4b7a7d5e03 687155df6b..b7fc137c35` reports `1: … = 1: …`, i.e. **exactly patch-equivalent**. Signature is good (`%G? = G`) and `git diff --check` is clean. Pre-rebase tip preserved at `backup/field-10x26-normalize-overflow-before-rebase-20260806`.
  Note the tips differ by 118 lines on `src/tests.c` even though the patch is identical — that is **master's** change, not ours: merged #1897 added 77 lines to `tests.c` between the two bases. Use `range-diff`, not a tip diff, to judge a rebase here.
* **Fail-before re-verified on the *current* baseline**, in a throwaway worktree so the checked-out branch was never touched (avoiding this file's recorded `git checkout <ref> -- <files>` index-pollution gotcha). Reverting only `src/field_10x26_impl.h` to master and keeping the test: forced-int64 Debug+VERIFY aborts **rc=134** at `src/tests.c:3467: test condition failed: fe_identical(&tmp, &lo)`. **The defect is still live on `687155df6b`.** The assertion moved from the previously recorded line 3393 to 3467 — again #1897's +77 lines, not a change in our test.
* **Pass-after, both backends:** forced-int64 10x26 Debug+VERIFY — focused `--target=fe_normalize_max_magnitude` rc=0, full `tests` rc=0 (384 s), `noverify_tests` rc=0, `exhaustive_tests` rc=0 "no problems found". Default 5x52 Release — `tests` rc=0, `noverify_tests` rc=0, `exhaustive_tests` rc=0 "no problems found".
* **State for the push:** branch is checked out, `ahead 69 / behind 1` versus `origin/l0rinc/field-10x26-normalize-overflow`. The "behind 1" is the superseded pre-rebase commit `b938a5d092` still on the fork, so this **requires `--force-with-lease`**. Nothing was pushed.

**Framing reminder for fork PR #16** (unchanged, restated so it is next to the validated head): lead with the *contract* violation — the header documents magnitude up to 32 and at that documented bound the 10x26 reduction returns a wrong residue — and do **not** claim remote reachability, because the measured public-API `fe` magnitude ceiling is 8. This is internal-contract-only and 32-bit-only.

## 2026-08-06 upstream preparation: fork PR #269 `l0rinc/musig2-psbt-derivation-abort` @ `26bd6107b0`

The two-commit branch is rebased onto `upstream/master` `b388674acf`: `2f79dcfef1 test: characterize MuSig2 derivation aborts`, then `26bd6107b0 psbt: skip invalid MuSig2 derivation paths`. Both commits have good signatures. The published fork PR still points to the pre-rebase stack `0911752fd8` + `44f69fc298`, so publication requires replacing that remote history. The pre-review rebased tip is preserved at `backup/musig2-psbt-derivation-abort-pre-review-20260806`.

The local fix also addresses achow101's unresolved inline comment on closed #35154. That patch scanned `KeyOriginInfo::path` with `any_of` and then traversed it again for derivation. The current fix checks for a hardened index inside the derivation pass, records that the candidate path is hardened, and skips the candidate after leaving the loop. This preserves the adjacent candidate-skip behavior and avoids returning early before another valid MuSig2 aggregate can be tried. The mismatched-derived-key `Assert` remains a candidate skip, and the path index type remains `uint32_t` so the hardened bit is preserved.

No new fuzz-harness code is needed to answer Sjors's coverage suggestion. The existing `psbt` target already passes decoded PSBTs through both `AnalyzePSBT()` and `FinalizePSBT()`, and maflcko uploaded both converted inputs to the OSS-Fuzz corpus. The functional characterization adds the deterministic failure-before proof: it observes all four RPC/path abort combinations, verifies the process exits unsuccessfully, restarts the node, and stays executable on the unfixed commit.

Current-base validation: `rpc_psbt.py` passes at both commits after rebuilding `bitcoind` and `bitcoin-cli` independently. At the final tip, `psbt_tests,descriptor_tests,bip328_tests,script_tests` also pass, `git diff --check` is clean, and the touched C++ diff produces no `clang-format-diff.py` output. PR details are in `CLion2026.2/scratches/scratch_773.txt`, led by the PSBT co-signer restart motivation and stripped of #35154's vulnerability, release-blocking, and credit framing.

### The one new secp ref: a **secp256k1-jdk** audit, docs-only, no C-library defect

`rpi5-8gb-500gb-secp/rescan-2026-08-03` advanced one commit to **`7e00e5e92d`**, adding `security-review/secp256k1-jdk-2026-08-06/` (7 files). Verified: **nothing outside that directory**. Its own subject says "Java-side findings only", and that holds up.

Target is **bitcoinj/secp256k1-jdk** (the Java FFM/BouncyCastle binding), not this library. Same ColdCard-incident motivation as the 08-05 master scan, and this one **executed** a full Maven reactor (218/218 tests pass) against our `libsecp256k1.so.6.0.2` with all 23 required symbols verified. Totals **0 🔴, 4 🟠, ~25 🟡**, every one on the Java side.

**Why it is still worth recording here — it is the first outside evidence of what our own hardening PRs are actually preventing.** Two C-side citations were replayed against `687155df6b` and both are accurate:

* `secp256k1_pubkey_load` is `secp256k1_ge_from_bytes(...); ARG_CHECK(!secp256k1_fe_is_zero(&ge->x)); return 1;` (`src/secp256k1.c`), and `secp256k1_default_illegal_callback_fn` ends in `abort()` (`src/util.h`). So the audit's 🟠1 chain is real: the JDK binding **does not capture `secp256k1_keypair_create`'s return** and guards the follow-up calls with Java `assert` (inert in production), so an invalid secret produces a zeroed keypair, then `pubkey_load` fires the illegal callback and **kills the JVM with an uncatchable SIGABRT**.
* **This is independent, real-world corroboration for fork PR #11's motivation.** #11 fixes *our* side ignoring a `pubkey_load` return; this is a downstream consumer ignoring a `keypair_create` return with process-death consequences. Different site, identical class. Cite it if #11 is challenged as theoretical — "no caller ignores these returns" is now demonstrably false.

**Two scope-limiting facts to carry, so a later sweep does not over-read this:**

* [x] The audit **explicitly clears our loader issue as unreachable from Java**: "The C library's own loader issue (`secp256k1.c:258-262`, corrupted-opaque decoding off-curve) is not reachable from Java because opaque objects never round-trip through Java." That bounds the downstream blast radius of fork PR #18.
* [x] **Our nonce generation is confirmed correct by execution**, not just inspection: RFC6979 replayed byte-exact against the RFC vector, added entropy enters at the exact §3.6 position, and low-R grinding is **byte-identical to Bitcoin Core's extra-entropy scheme** (replayed rust-secp vector, counter=4).

The C→Java finding mapping in its area 05 is the useful part: our VERIFY-only guards become Java `assert` return-value guards; our off-curve loaders become a Bouncy backend constructing points with no curve check; our uncleared stack residue becomes GC-heap secret residue; **our tweak-aliasing finding (#15) maps to N/A** because Java objects are immutable. That last one is worth knowing — #15 has no downstream Java analogue, so its argument must stand on the C API alone.

None. No new secp source candidate for the fourth consecutive pass. The upstream-submission ranking from 2026-08-06 stands unchanged: **#15 first** (with the "no aliasing policy in the public headers" argument leading), then #13, with #36 free to open alongside. #11's CHANGELOG bullet still needs relocating under the post-0.8.0 `[Unreleased]`, and this audit strengthens #11's motivation when it does go out.

## 2026-08-07 upstream-preparation audit: fork PR #15 makes overlap support explicit @ `8c61878e8d`

The prior #1785 framing was too strong. Upstream labelled that silent-result aliasing hazard `bug`, but its review discussion does not establish that missing `restrict` automatically permits overlap. Maintainers explicitly asked to choose between supporting aliasing with a regression or forbidding it with `SECP256K1_RESTRICT` and a `VERIFY_CHECK`.

For these public In/Out APIs, the local stack now makes the support choice explicit. `d8e99900ce ec: preserve overlapping tweak input` documents that `pubkey` storage may overlap `tweak32`, and `8c61878e8d extrakeys: preserve overlapping tweak input` documents the same for `keypair`. The implementation comments now name that exact ordering dependency instead of claiming a broad rule for other In/Out APIs. The commit messages also state the supported contract directly. The runtime hunks and regressions remain unchanged from `dec5c69cdf`; the range-diff contains only the two header clarifications, two comment rewrites, and corresponding message updates.

Both rewritten commits have good signatures and `git diff --check` is clean. Incremental Debug builds of `tests`, `noverify_tests`, and `exhaustive_tests` passed on default 5x52 and forced-int64 10x26. `eckey_edge_case_test` and `test_keypair_add` passed on both backends. The earlier fail-before and full-suite evidence remains applicable because the executable changes are identical.

The branch is based directly on `upstream/master` `687155df6b`, tracks `origin/l0rinc/preserve-overlapping-tweak-inputs`, and is zero behind upstream. The fork PR still points to the pre-rebase tip `3bbd8985dd`, so publication remains a user-only history replacement. The pre-audit local tip is preserved at `backup/preserve-overlapping-tweak-inputs-pre-upstream-audit-20260807`.

## 2026-08-07 closed-candidate triage: #35154 revived as upstream #35933

Verified against `upstream/master` `1be0b46297` and the live GitHub PR states. This supersedes the earlier entries that call the MuSig2 abort unowned or say fork PR #269 still needs to be pushed upstream.

### Serious and now owned upstream

* **[#35154](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35154), MuSig2 crafted-PSBT abort — real, still live on master, and revived as open [#35933](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35933).** `SignMuSig2()` still loops over PSBT-supplied `agg_info.path` at `src/script/sign.cpp:321-327` and then asserts that the derived key matches at line 328. A hardened index reaches the `CPubKey::Derive` assertion, while an unhardened path that derives to another key reaches the `SignMuSig2` assertion. `finalizepsbt`, `analyzepsbt`, and `descriptorprocesspsbt` reach the code without a wallet, and even the read-only `analyzepsbt` aborts the node. #35154 closed over framing and LLM-authorship policy rather than a technical refutation. ESultanik stated that Trail of Bits engineers manually patched and validated it, Sjors motivated co-signer robustness and suggested `CHECK_NONFATAL` plus fuzz coverage, and maflcko uploaded both converted inputs as OSS-Fuzz [511038132](https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/511038132) and [511235488](https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/511235488).
* **Ownership/current publication:** fork PR [l0rinc/bitcoin#269](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/269) is closed and superseded by non-draft upstream #35933, `psbt: skip invalid MuSig2 derivation paths`, at published head `7a3e2e21d1`. Its stack is `e3d1e75a51 test: characterize MuSig2 derivation aborts` plus `7a3e2e21d1 psbt: skip invalid MuSig2 derivation paths`. The production hunk matches #35154 and incorporates achow101's review request to check each index inside the derivation loop rather than scan the path twice. The fix commit preserves the original Anthropic Security attribution and credits Evan Sultanik and Ava Chow. The functional regression covers both abort inputs through `analyzepsbt` and `finalizepsbt`. The existing OSS-Fuzz issues remain supporting corpus evidence and a possible answer to Sjors's fuzz-coverage suggestion.
* **Action:** review and advance #35933. Do not create another revival or reopen #269.

### Real, already fixed on master — do not revive

* **[#35155](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35155), nonce-less MuSig2 PSBT retry abort:** closed unmerged, but its session-collision mechanism is fixed by merged [#35269](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35269), `2669019fe8`. Master keys `MuSig2SessionID` by pubnonce, creates a fresh secret nonce for another round, and invalidates the secret nonce after use. The old `Assert(inserted)` retry abort is no longer the current lifecycle.
* **[#34530](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34530), negative bump-fee discount abort:** closed unmerged, with the fix already on master through merged [#35633](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35633), `8d9e4f8dbd`. `src/wallet/spend.cpp:798-802` now applies the discount only when `bump_fee_overestimate > 0`, with the mempool-snapshot race comment. Do not revive #34530.

### Open and real — review or bump the existing PR

* **[#35665](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35665), duplicate global xpub keys from `combinepsbt`:** open, non-draft, and independently reproduced. Merging PSBTs that carry the same xpub under different key origins can serialize duplicate `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB` keys, producing a PSBT rejected by BIP 174 and Core's own deserializer. The bug dates to the merge loop added for v23. Moderate correctness issue. Review the existing PR rather than fork it.
* **[#35440](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35440), descriptor-cache xpub length:** open, non-draft. A corrupted wallet descriptor-cache record can provide a short vector to `CExtPubKey::Decode`, producing an ASAN container-overflow. The proposed fix requires exactly `BIP32_EXTKEY_SIZE`. Real but minor because the input is local wallet-database corruption.

### Not serious revival candidates

* **[#35318](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35318):** closed fuzz-harness fanout tuning, not a production defect.
* **[#34892](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34892):** open Tor bind UX warning for misidentified incoming onion connections, not a serious correctness or security issue.

## 2026-08-07 covert-fix, process-casualty, and suspicious-PR triage

Verified against `upstream/master` `1be0b46297`, current release-branch refs, the live GitHub PR states, the relevant PR bodies and close-out comments, and the exact pre-fix source for #35670. Items whose runtime mechanisms were not replayed in this pass are explicitly kept as an inventory rather than promoted to independently confirmed findings.

### #35670 adjudication: real cleanup, but the claimed cheap null crash is not present

* **[#35670](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35670), `net: optimize compact block extra tx iteration`, is merged on master as `1a3cbf1bd2` through merge `6f1c56f03a`.** The pre-fix first insertion resized `vExtraTxnForCompact` to its full configured capacity, leaving default `{Wtxid::ZERO, nullptr}` entries. The fix reserves capacity and appends only initialized entries until the ring is full. None of `upstream/28.x`, `29.x`, `30.x`, or `31.x` contains the fix, and no release tag contains it.
* **The new claim that repeated null slots make this a cheap remote unauthenticated node crash is rejected by the source.** In the pre-fix `PartiallyDownloadedBlock::InitData()` loop, the duplicate branch is guarded by `if (txn_available[idit->second] && ...)`. If the first matching default entry stores a null `CTransactionRef`, the next matching default entry short-circuits at that guard and does not dereference either null pointer. A null `extra_txn[i].second` is dereferenced only when the same compact-block short ID already selected a non-null transaction. Producing that non-null/null collision retains the 48-bit short-ID collision requirement described in the PR. Choosing the compact-block nonce and inserting `GetShortID(Wtxid::ZERO)` into the announcement does not remove the need for the second, non-null candidate to share that short ID.
* **Correction to earlier knowledgebase wording:** the default-slot condition was real before #35670 and is dead on master because #35670 removed the slots. The earlier “no defect found” conclusion was too broad, while the new “directly injectable null crash with no grinding” conclusion is also wrong. Based on the examined path, #35670 remains a correctness and efficiency cleanup with a deliberately documented collision-risk model, not evidence for an urgent security backport. The detached534–585 range does not by itself establish supporting fuzz PoCs. The named detached tips currently point to unrelated commits, so no PoC lineage is recorded without an exact branch or commit.

### Process-lost fixes and their current owners

* **[#35500](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35500), ignored `WriteMasterKey` result during passphrase change: real and still live, but now owned by open [#35752](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35752).** Master still calls `WalletBatch(GetDatabase()).WriteMasterKey(master_key_id, master_key)` without checking its result at `src/wallet/wallet.cpp:657`, then reports success. #35500 was automatically closed three days after opening by DrahtBot's quality heuristics with no human technical review. Its stronger atomicity problem is now addressed by #35752, `wallet: make encryption state updates atomic`. Review #35752 rather than revive #35500.
* **[#35672](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35672), descriptor-cache xpub length: real and still live, but an exact duplicate of open [#35440](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35440).** Master still deserializes the record-controlled vector and passes its data to the fixed-size `CExtPubKey::Decode` at `src/wallet/walletdb.cpp:815-818` without validating `BIP32_EXTKEY_SIZE`. The close comment explicitly routed review to the pre-existing PR. Review #35440 rather than revive #35672.
* **[#35844](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35844), queued HTTP-request ownership cycle: open and demonstrated.** The PR reports that disconnected `HTTPRemoteClient` objects retain queued requests through a `shared_ptr` cycle, with allocation before authentication. Its local PoC OOM-killed a 400 MB-limited node, while the remote test plateaued and stopped accepting connections rather than reaching OOM. The reporter first contacted the security team and was told public handling was appropriate because the replacement HTTP server has not shipped. #35844 conflicts with and is partly duplicated by pinheadmz's broader [#35735](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35735). Ensure the leak fix survives whichever implementation lands before v32.
* **[#35476](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35476), cleanse the AEAD Poly1305 key block: closed unmerged and still absent.** `ComputeTag()` still leaves the 64-byte ChaCha20 block used to derive the one-time Poly1305 key on the stack after `Poly1305` copies the first 32 bytes. The one-line cleanup was closed as suspected AI output, after which the author explained the rationale and accepted that maintainers might consider it too marginal for review. Track as minor secret-lifetime hardening, not a demonstrated key-recovery vulnerability.
* **[#35517](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35517), reject trailing bytes in stored blocks: closed unmerged and still absent.** `BlockManager::ReadBlock()` still constructs a temporary `SpanReader`, deserializes one block prefix, and does not check for unconsumed bytes. The close-out asked for broader motivation and context rather than identifying a technical error. Track as storage-record canonicality and corruption-detection hardening, not a remotely supplied block acceptance flaw.
