### Queue effect and systemic lesson

No evidence from this pass supports escalating #35670 as a cheap remotely triggerable crash or demanding an emergency backport on that basis. The concrete queue is to review the existing owners #35752, #35440, #35844 or #35735, and the open bug-owner inventory above. #35476 and #35517 remain unowned minor hardening candidates whose value and threat model need clearer justification before revival.

The process signal is still worth retaining. Automated provenance heuristics and terse “AI slop” closures can discard technically valid changes, as #35500 and #35476 demonstrate. They can also correctly suppress duplicates and low-context output, as #35672 and #35517 demonstrate. The durable rule is to verify the live mechanism, search for an existing owner, preserve reviewer objections, and route work to the smallest test-backed change instead of treating either the title or the close reason as a technical verdict.

## 2026-08-08 latest-ref triage and prepared BIP37 allocation bounds

The newly fetched production finding is Umbrel cycle 589, `fab6850acd` (`p2p: bound BIP37 filter vectors before allocation`), with its audit record at `f79aa39960`. Live GitHub searches found no open Bitcoin Core PR owning the `filterload`/`filteradd` deserialization mechanism. Open #35818 is adjacent bloom-constructor arithmetic, not this parser boundary. No more serious newly fetched unowned production finding was established. The LevelDB iterator-status problem remains higher-integrity-impact but is not “next”: its complete local branch `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors` already exists, and it is corruption-triggered rather than remotely created. The cycle-588 wallet weight overflow is authenticated RPC and produced a wallet error/UBSan finding rather than a default-network remote failure.

### Correction to the earlier bloom demotion

The earlier entry was right that generic byte-vector deserialization grows in `MAX_VECTOR_ALLOCATE` batches and therefore does not honor an arbitrary multi-gigabyte declaration in one allocation. It missed the operational oracle. With `-peerbloomfilters=1`, a five-byte canonical CompactSize declaration of 4,000,000 elements makes either `filterload` or `filteradd` reserve/materialize about 4 MB before the existing 36,000/520-byte protocol checks. The first absent element then throws EOF, `ProcessMessages()` catches it, and the connection remains usable. An unauthenticated bloom peer can therefore repeat the allocation with five-byte messages. This upgrades the item from generic defense-in-depth to a real configuration-gated allocation-amplification fix, but not to a default-node crash or consensus/funds/corruption issue: BIP37 service remains disabled by default, and each attempt is bounded.

### Prepared stack

Created local branch `l0rinc/bip37-vector-limits` in isolated worktree `/private/tmp/bitcoin-bip37-vector-limits`. It is intentionally stacked on open #35936 at published head `725bf357d9`, because #35936 introduces `LimitedVectorExceededError`; duplicating that type or matching `ios_base::failure::what()` text in the bloom patch would be brittle. The one new signed commit is `b93f8e5eb8 p2p: bound BIP37 filter vectors before allocation`.

The commit deserializes `CBloomFilter::vData` through `LIMITED_VECTOR(..., MAX_BLOOM_FILTER_SIZE)` and `filteradd` data through `LIMITED_VECTOR(..., MAX_SCRIPT_ELEMENT_SIZE)`. Each handler catches only `LimitedVectorExceededError` and routes it to the pre-existing misbehavior outcome; unrelated truncation and serialization failures preserve their old exception path. `p2p_filter.py` sends count-only oversized messages and requires the established `Misbehaving` log while `send_and_ping` proves the peer-processing path remains responsive.

Validation on the exact stack:

* `bitcoind` compiled successfully with AppleClang 21, RelWithDebInfo.
* `test_bitcoin -t bloom_tests,net_tests,serialize_tests --random=589005`: 47 cases passed.
* `test_runner.py p2p_filter.py`: passed the full functional test in 4 seconds after rerunning with local socket-bind access. The first sandboxed invocation failed only at startup with `Unable to start HTTP server`.
* `python3 -m py_compile test/functional/p2p_filter.py` and `git diff --check` passed.
* Both `b93f8e5eb8` and prerequisite tip `725bf357d9` have good signatures.

Nothing was pushed. Publication should be a stacked PR based on `l0rinc/reject-oversized-locators`, or the bloom commit should be rebased onto master after #35936 lands.

### 2026-08-09 PR preparation

Checked out `l0rinc/bip37-vector-limits` in the main workspace and confirmed its tracking upstream is the intended, currently absent `origin/l0rinc/bip37-vector-limits` (`[gone]`); no remote ref was created. Live #35936 remains open and mergeable at prerequisite tip `725bf357d9`. Paste-ready PR details are in `CLion2026.2/scratches/scratch_777.txt` with title `p2p: reject oversized BIP37 vectors before allocation`, a default-off `NODE_BLOOM` scope statement, and the explicit #35936 dependency. Nothing was pushed or published.

## 2026-08-09 post-bloom fetch: default-peer address and inventory vector bounds

The fetch added two independently reproduced current-master findings after cycle 589. Live GitHub title/body/comment searches found no open PR owning either mechanism, and neither appears among the 29 open `l0rinc` PRs. Both are reachable after the ordinary P2P handshake on default nodes. Both are bounded, serialized allocation amplification findings; neither audit demonstrated an OOM, crash, consensus fault, funds/key impact, memory corruption, or retained-memory growth.

### Priority 1: `ADDR` and `ADDRV2`

Current `upstream/master` `128456b62d` generically deserializes `std::vector<CAddress>` before `ProcessAddrs()` enforces `MAX_ADDR_TO_SEND = 1000`. A five-byte canonical CompactSize declaration for 1,000,000 entries makes the generic parser reserve 4,999,960 bytes (`89,285 * sizeof(CAddress{56})`) before the first missing entry throws EOF. `ProcessMessages()` catches the exception and leaves the peer connected, so an unauthenticated peer can repeat it through legacy `ADDR` or negotiated `ADDRV2`.

Umbrel cycle 591 independently reproduced both clean-master paths and the exact allocation, then prepared standalone commit `26f00aa590cbe16b2ce9a02ba72eca9b772916f5` over `128456b62d`. The fix reads and checks the count before reserving or parsing addresses while preserving the existing oversized-message punishment. Its exact-source validation covered `p2p_invalid_messages.py` over v1/v2, `p2p_addr_relay.py`, `p2p_addrv2_relay.py`, 34 `net_tests,serialize_tests` cases with 360,953 assertions, fresh targets, Python compilation, and `git diff --check`.

This leads the queue because the accepted address maximum occupies only about 56 KB while the malformed declaration triggers about 5 MB. Preventing the late allocation removes roughly 4.94 MB beyond the valid maximum, compared with roughly 3.2 MB for inventory parsing. The intended local branch is `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits`; preserve the fetched commit's standalone master base and verify the patch locally before adopting it.

### Priority 2: `INV`, `GETDATA`, and `NOTFOUND`

The sibling inventory path generically deserializes `std::vector<CInv>` before the 50,000-entry `MAX_INV_SZ` checks. A five-byte declaration for 1,000,000 entries reserves 4,999,968 bytes (`138,888 * sizeof(CInv{36})`) before EOF, and the caught exception leaves the peer usable. Umbrel cycle 590 reproduced the allocation and prepared standalone commit `2b87fbe900a985ddbc3076b6a55ba4e43966bc4e`, preserving `INV`/`GETDATA` punishment and the silent oversized-`NOTFOUND` behavior. Complete `p2p_invalid_messages.py` runs passed over v1/v2 after the fix.

Keep inventory bounds as the next sibling after the address PR. Do not combine the two automatically: each standalone commit changes a distinct protocol family and already carries focused fail-before/pass-after evidence. Reconsider combining only if review of the address PR establishes a shared parser API that materially reduces both changes.

### Address branch prepared and locally verified

Created and checked out `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` directly from `upstream/master` `128456b62d`, with intended tracking `origin/l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` configured locally and currently `[gone]`. Final signed commit: `9df1d2172c p2p: bound address vectors before allocation`.

The final commit is patch-equivalent to fetched cycle-591 commit `26f00aa590` except for one deliberate correction: it passes the `uint64_t` CompactSize count directly to `strprintf` instead of narrowing it to `unsigned`, so declarations above 2^32 are logged accurately. Valid and truncated address parsing retains the generic vector parser's clear/reserve/emplace/unserialize order, with the 1,000-entry check moved before allocation. The production diff remains limited to the shared `ADDR`/`ADDRV2` handler; the functional regression remains in `p2p_invalid_messages.py`.

Local exact-tip validation:

* Debug AppleClang build of `bitcoind` and `test_bitcoin` passed with ccache disabled for sandbox permissions.
* `test_bitcoin -t net_tests,serialize_tests --random=591005`: 34 cases passed.
* `p2p_invalid_messages.py` passed through `test_runner.py` over v1 and over v2 using the runner's global `--v2transport` flag.
* `p2p_addr_relay.py` and `p2p_addrv2_relay.py` passed through `test_runner.py`.
* Python compilation and `git diff --check upstream/master..HEAD` passed.
* `git verify-commit 9df1d2172c` reports a good signature.

No PR prose was prepared in this pass, and nothing was pushed or published. The next serious unowned item remains the inventory-vector sibling at fetched commit `2b87fbe900`.

### Inventory branch prepared as a characterization/fix pair

Created and checked out `l0rinc/inv-vector-limits` directly from `upstream/master` `128456b62d`, with intended tracking `origin/l0rinc/inv-vector-limits` configured locally and currently `[gone]`.

The stack begins with `168e7b99de test: characterize late inventory bounds`. Its functional test sends five-byte count-only `INV`, `GETDATA`, and `NOTFOUND` messages declaring 1,000,000 entries. On unchanged production code, each message reaches entry deserialization, logs the caught EOF exception, and leaves the peer responsive. The three executable old expectations carry trailing TODOs owned by the following fix.

`c3e1c532d8 p2p: bound inventory vectors before allocation` adds the bounded parser and changes only those three test expectations. `INV` and `GETDATA` now reach their existing misbehavior/disconnect policy before allocation. Oversized `NOTFOUND` is silently ignored before allocation and the connection remains usable. The production patch matches fetched cycle-590 commit `2b87fbe900` except that it passes the `uint64_t` count directly to `strprintf`, preserving diagnostic values above 2^32 instead of narrowing them to `unsigned`.

Exact-tree validation:

* The characterization commit rebuilt `bitcoind`, and `p2p_invalid_messages.py` passed over v1 and v2 while asserting the old caught-exception behavior.
* The final commit rebuilt `bitcoind` and `test_bitcoin`; 34 `net_tests,serialize_tests` cases passed with seed `590005`.
* Final `p2p_invalid_messages.py` passed over v1 and v2.
* Python compilation and `git diff --check upstream/master..HEAD` passed.

Both local commits are currently unsigned because the configured macOS GPG pinentry cancelled twice. Nothing was pushed or published, and existing untracked files remain untouched.

## 2026-08-09 weekly fetched-ref summary and post-inventory queue

This pass classified remote refs updated from 2026-08-02 through 2026-08-09, with a full review of the new Umbrel master-based production branches. Most of the hundreds of Umbrel refs dated August 2-5 are append-only campaign or journal snapshots whose tips do not introduce an independent production patch. `umbrel/codex-security/bitcoin-20260729` is a documentation and evidence import rather than a source fix. Its 22 candidate rows are already reconciled by the August 7 whole-history section above: the confirmed `verify-commits` error-status issue, contextual watch-only export race, and stronger HTTP pre-auth work evidence remain routed there, while dependency-only MCP, AJV, and Octokit rows are not Bitcoin Core findings.

The material new Umbrel sequence is cycles 589-597. Every reproduced case reaches generic deserialization before a narrower protocol or consensus-derived limit, causes one transient allocation of roughly 4-5 MB from a very short truncated payload, then reaches a caught exception. Message processing serializes the work, and none of the audits demonstrated OOM, remote crash, consensus divergence, funds/key loss, memory corruption, or retained growth. This is a family of bounded unauthenticated allocation-amplification fixes, not nine independent catastrophic vulnerabilities.

### Publication and ownership exclusions

* Cycle 589 BIP37 is configuration-gated and already prepared at published fork ref `origin/l0rinc/bip37-vector-limits` (`b93f8e5eb8`).
* Cycle 590 inventory is already prepared at published fork ref `origin/l0rinc/inv-vector-limits` (`c3e1c532d8`) as a characterization/fix pair.
* Cycle 591 address handling is already prepared locally as `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` (`9df1d2172c`), although no matching `origin` ref exists after the latest fetch.
* Cycle 592 `GETBLOCKTXN` revalidates an existing published fork branch, `origin/i9/codex/goal7-getblocktxn-20260801` (`9a1531ee8b`), and an older stacked repair. The new master adaptation `2d381386c3` has stronger zero-capacity and full-domain coverage, but the mechanism is already public and is excluded from the unpushed preparation queue.
* Live open-PR titles on August 9 and the Umbrel title/body searches found no owner for cycles 593-597. Their exact source commits are present only under the inspected Umbrel refs.

### Remaining Umbrel findings, ranked

1. **Cycle 597, transaction scripts and witness items:** `0d48c06305 tx: bound script and witness byte vectors`. Ordinary `TX` and `BLOCK` parsing reaches `scriptSig`, `scriptPubKey`, and witness-item byte lengths before transaction checks. Truncated prefixes of roughly 46-64 bytes allocate 4 MB, 4 MB, and 5 MB. The proposed transaction-scoped bulk-byte formatter rejects base scripts above 1 MB and witness items above 4 MWU before resize while preserving canonical bytes and exact conservative limits. This leads because it covers three nested containers on the broad transaction parser and has the smallest demonstrated prefixes.
2. **Cycle 596, transaction input/output vectors:** `3b8ebc992e tx: bound input and output vectors before allocation`. Legacy and witness-marker input counts plus output counts each reserve about 5 MB before EOF. Conservative ceilings are 24,390 inputs and 111,111 outputs. The patch also makes `LimitedVectorFormatter` retain generic batched allocation, which is necessary because a valid output ceiling can exceed the five-megabyte allocation batch. This is broad but more review-sensitive because it changes shared formatter behavior.
3. **Cycle 595, full-block transaction vector:** `42d5ee63d3 block: bound transaction vector before allocation`. An 85-byte block prefix reserves 5 MB before PoW, mutation, weight, or block-validation checks. The isolated fix uses the existing conservative `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT` ceiling of 16,666 and is the smallest consensus-object patch in the remaining set.
4. **Cycle 594, `BLOCKTXN` response vector:** `ee4e35ed09 p2p: bound block transaction response count`. A 37-byte unsolicited or mismatched response reserves 5 MB before request-state and response-cardinality checks. The existing compact-block index domain supplies a 65,535-entry ceiling.
5. **Cycle 593, `CMPCTBLOCK` vectors:** `b271590377 p2p: bound compact block vectors before allocation`. Ninety-three or ninety-four bytes reserve about 5 MB through either short IDs or prefilled transactions before the existing combined 65,535-transaction check. Both individual vectors need an early bound while the combined postcondition remains.

### Explicit non-candidate

`umbrel/cycle598-master-witness-stack-allocation` currently points to unchanged `upstream/master` `128456b62d` and contains no production commit. The outer witness-stack count cannot use a small semantic cap because an unknown witness version can make a multi-million-element stack consensus-valid. Keep this as an unresolved representation/allocation design problem. Do not prepare a count-limit patch without an exact consensus-valid-domain oracle.

### Selection

Prepare Cycle 597 next as `l0rinc/transaction-byte-vector-limits`, directly on current `upstream/master`, and start with a passing characterization commit. Keep Cycle 596 separate despite the nearby `transaction.h` overlap because it changes different semantic limits plus shared `LimitedVectorFormatter` allocation behavior. Re-run current-master ownership and overlap checks if either serialization path changes upstream before publication.

### Prepared result

**[SUPERSEDED 2026-08-09 (later): this two-commit stack was restructured and published. `origin/l0rinc/transaction-byte-vector-limits` is now a four-commit stack at `1f6625541c` — `ae1fbef13d test: characterize transaction byte allocations` → `ce1135a002 move: extract UnserializeByteVectorElements` → `7a04c98a0c refactor: deduplicate byte vector deserialization` → `1f6625541c tx: bound script and witness byte vectors`. The old SHAs `9743868d26`/`060c93f4d7` are orphaned (not ancestors of `1f6625541c`). Design intent is unchanged but now factors the chunked byte read into a shared `UnserializeByteVectorElements` helper used by both the generic prevector/vector paths and the new `LimitedByteVectorFormatter`, so the limit check precedes allocation without a `static_assert`. Verified: HEAD == `origin/...` == `1f6625541c`. A local /simplify pass reviewed all four commits; the one substantive correctness catch was that `LimitedByteVectorFormatter::Unser` must not brace-init `size_t size{ReadCompactSize(s)}` (uint64_t→size_t narrowing breaks 32-bit i686/arm CI) — use copy-init, matching the sibling formatters.]**

Prepared local branch `l0rinc/transaction-byte-vector-limits` as a two-commit stack on `128456b62d`:

* `9743868d26 test: characterize transaction byte allocations` pairs each exact accepted `scriptSig`, `scriptPubKey`, and witness-item byte boundary with its first oversized length, recording that the oversized cases resize their containers before truncated input reaches end-of-data. Brace-initialized `SerializeMany` helpers keep the wire fixtures declarative and deduplicate the witness transaction prefix without constructing a large mutable transaction; exact and oversized cases deserialize into separate destination objects.

### Top 10 serious local-only problems

1. **Aggregate large-response memory, Umbrel Cycle 611/613/614 — `umbrel/cycle611-getdata-response-bound-master` at `36db522889`.** An unauthenticated peer sends a 34-byte `GETBLOCKTXN` or 37-byte `GETDATA` request for a recent valid roughly 3.12 MB witness transaction or block. The default 1 MB send-buffer setting is only checked after the reply is materialized, independently per peer. Twenty stalled peers OOM-killed unmodified `bitcoind` in a 180 MiB user scope; a zero-request control did not. Across 189 default inbound slots, about 7 KB of requests can induce roughly 590 MB of response material. This is a demonstrated availability failure for memory-constrained nodes, not consensus, funds, or memory corruption. The proposed 32 MB aggregate reservation plus 64 KB inbound socket send buffer passed the three pressure regressions, but its 214-line networking change and throughput/interoperability tradeoffs need careful design review.
2. **[RE-RANKED 2026-08-09 (later) → effectively #8 by urgency: wallet-scope, not attacker-triggered; per the standing "wallet findings are not urgent" rule it belongs below the unauthenticated remote allocation family (old #3–#8), alongside the other non-remote items. See the prioritization-review section below for the corrected order. Left in place here to preserve the second-fetch evidence.]** **Taproot script-path input-weight underestimation — `i9/codex/goal96-current-20260803`, commit `20fef707e7`.** A wallet spending a known Taproot script path estimates every input as a key-path signature, so long `multi_a` satisfactions can be funded below the requested fee rate and fail relay. This is a practical wallet reliability defect, not an attacker-triggered loss path. The local patch measures leaf satisfaction, script, control-block depth, and witness element counts; its relay-floor functional case failed before and passed after.
3. **Default-peer `ADDR`/`ADDRV2` allocation amplification — `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` at `9df1d2172c`.** An unauthenticated peer sends a five-byte count declaring one million addresses. Generic deserialization reserves 4,999,960 bytes before the existing 1,000-address check, then caught EOF leaves the peer usable to repeat it. No crash or retained growth was demonstrated. The prepared signed branch moves the established 1,000-entry bound before allocation and is locally validated, but remains absent from `origin`.
4. **Transaction input/output vector allocation — Umbrel Cycle 596, `3b8ebc992e`.** Short malformed `TX` or `BLOCK` transaction prefixes can declare huge legacy/witness input or output counts and reserve about 5 MB before transaction validity or weight checks. A peer can repeat the caught parse failure; no OOM or crash was demonstrated. The proposed conservative limits are 24,390 inputs and 111,111 outputs and preserve the generic parser's batched-allocation behavior.
5. **Full-block transaction-vector allocation — Umbrel Cycle 595, `42d5ee63d3`.** An unauthenticated 85-byte block prefix can make `CBlock::vtx` reserve about 5 MB before proof-of-work, mutation, weight, or block validation runs. The parse error is caught and no crash was shown. The isolated fix applies the consensus-conservative `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_TRANSACTION_WEIGHT` ceiling of 16,666 before allocation.
6. **Outer witness-stack allocation — Umbrel Cycle 598, `e0e8c0d1a6`.** A roughly 63-byte witness transaction prefix can declare four million stack elements and make the outer vector reserve about 5 MB before the first absent element is read. A small semantic count limit is unsafe because unknown witness versions can make very large stacks consensus-valid; the patch instead avoids count-driven preallocation while retaining the full conservative `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT` domain. This is bounded transient amplification with no demonstrated crash, and it overlaps the now-published transaction-byte formatter at the witness-stack call site.
7. **Unsolicited `BLOCKTXN` response allocation — Umbrel Cycle 594, `ee4e35ed09`.** A 37-byte unsolicited or mismatched response can declare a huge transaction vector and reserve about 5 MB before request-state and response-cardinality checks. The peer controls the input on default P2P, but only a caught transient allocation was demonstrated. The proposed early limit is the existing 65,535 compact-block transaction-index domain.
8. **`CMPCTBLOCK` vector allocation — Umbrel Cycle 593, `b271590377`.** A 93- or 94-byte compact-block prefix can reserve about 5 MB through either the short-ID or prefilled-transaction vector before the existing combined-count check. Both vectors need an individual preallocation bound while retaining the combined 65,535 postcondition. No crash, retained growth, or consensus effect was shown.
9. **LevelDB iterator errors reported as clean exhaustion — `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors` at `16df166000`.** A checksum or I/O error makes the underlying iterator invalid, while `CDBIterator::Valid()` ignores `status()`. UTXO/index statistics and scan/dump consumers can therefore return empty or truncated results as if iteration completed normally. The consequence is integrity loss under local database corruption, not a remote corruption primitive. The two-commit characterization/fix branch is complete but stale-based; it should be positioned alongside #34132/#34931 and the #35654 cursor redesign.
10. **Oversized witness variant accepted by `importprunedfunds` — `rpi5-16-2/audit/importpruned-weight-cycle307` at `2ac352ee1a`.** A txid Merkle proof does not commit to witness data, so an authenticated RPC caller can supply the proven txid with a witness variant heavier than any valid block and have the wallet store it as confirmed. This can create impossible wallet history and persistent bloat, but needs wallet RPC access and does not demonstrate remote exploitation or fund loss. The five-line fix rejects transactions above `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT` before `AddToWallet`.

### Below the top-10 cut from the second fetch

* `a20a3c3f65 wallet: allow disabled send_max with inputs` fixes an RPC option-presence check: explicit `send_max=false` should behave like omission. User-visible, but not a security or integrity threat.
* `e4a249c028 util: reject dangling Split view results` deletes the dangerous rvalue API at compile time, but all current production view-returning call sites use lvalues or borrowed spans. It is proactive lifetime hardening, not a confirmed use-after-free.
* `43cbe83e3a util: annotate TrimStringView input lifetime` is diagnostic annotation only, and `ae5220ee85 support: preserve ASan poisoning after pool destruction` is sanitizer hygiene.

Nothing was checked out, pushed, or published during this reconciliation. The current checked-out `l0rinc/transaction-byte-vector-limits` tip remains exactly aligned with `origin/l0rinc/transaction-byte-vector-limits` at `1f6625541c`, and unrelated untracked files remain untouched.

## 2026-08-10 Cycle 611 aggregate response-memory implementation

Prepared `l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` on `upstream/master`, then rebased without patch changes from `128456b62d` to current `757aa573c4`. The branch is published and exactly tracks `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` at `93532f96ff`. The fetched prototype remains recoverable at `backup/cycle611-response-memory-36db522889`, and the pre-split polished stack at `backup/bound-large-response-memory-c58ed299a4`.

Final published stack:

* `39297ddeb4 test: characterize concurrent GETDATA responses` creates nine handshaken inbound peers that request the current tip as a witness block and records that unchanged code retains all nine responses concurrently.
* `53c60ddeb1 refactor: carry response memory reservations` adds the move-only ownership path through serialized messages and both transports without changing production behavior; its V2 test immediately exercises transfer and release.
* `8f3667eda7 net: limit concurrent large response memory` reserves 4 MB before serializing each block, transaction, compact-block, or `BLOCKTXN` response, reserves 8 MB for a filtered-block response group, and caps aggregate reservations at 32 MB. Blocked `GETDATA` requests remain queued for a later retry; `GETBLOCKTXN` responses are dropped while capacity is exhausted.
* `93532f96ff net: bound inbound socket send buffers` requests a 64 kB `SO_SNDBUF` for accepted inbound sockets and drops a connection if the option cannot be applied, limiting the kernel-buffer destination for bytes released from Core's accounting after `send()` accepts them.

The refactor commit deliberately replaces the prototype's parallel reservation deque and manual `PushMessage`/`SocketSendData`/`DeleteNode` bookkeeping with a move-only RAII `ResponseMemoryReservation` owned by `CSerializedNetMsg` and then the active transport. Queue clearing, private-broadcast omission, transport completion, and node destruction therefore release reservations through normal ownership. V1 releases after its payload (or an empty payload's header); V2 carries the token with its encrypted send buffer until that buffer drains.

Exact-tip validation:

* AppleClang builds of `test_bitcoin` and `bitcoind` passed with ccache disabled for sandbox temporary-file permissions.
* All 21 `net_tests` cases passed, including the aggregate-cap/retry/destruction test, V1/V2 reservation lifetime coverage, and the accepted-socket option test.
* `p2p_getdata.py` and `p2p_compactblocks.py` passed against real sockets at the exact final tip.
* Mutation proof changed the reservation predicate to permit one response beyond the cap. The regression then failed cleanly at the intended boundary with 9 responses instead of 8 and 36 MB instead of 32 MB; restoring the predicate rebuilt and passed.
* `git diff --check upstream/master...HEAD` and the changed-line clang-format check passed.

The final four commits all contain signatures. The post-rebase range-diff maps all four old commits to the published commits as patch-identical, and the working branch is clean apart from the pre-existing untracked files. Severity remains the queue's clear #1: an unauthenticated default-node availability failure demonstrated by OOM-killing a 180 MiB node with 20 stalled peers, not a use-after-free, consensus fault, funds issue, or corruption primitive.

## 2026-08-10 latest-ref refresh: compact-filter coverage and lifetime findings

The latest fetch changed four relevant remote refs: the forced update of `umbrel/cycle611-getdata-response-bound-master` from `36db522889` to `068453735f`, its Cycle 615 journal advance at `b0c4e94b13`, `rpi5-16-2/audit/kernel-range-iterator-lifetime-cycle320` to `50fe2fae08`, and the new three-commit `rpi5-16-2/audit/cross-scanner-lifetime-cycle321` at `08fbab437f`. No other Umbrel or rpi production ref changed in that fetch.

### Cycle 615: compact-filter responses escape the new aggregate cap

`ProcessGetCFilters()` accepts one normal 37-byte `GETCFILTERS` request for as many as 1,000 filters, loads the range, and queues every `CFILTER` response without consulting `fPauseSend` inside the loop. This is not enabled on a default node: serving requires both `-blockfilterindex=basic` and `-peerblockfilters=1`. The independently reported 180 MiB kill also used a synthetic filter-heavy chain with a high memory baseline, so it is not evidence for a new severe default-node crash.

It is nevertheless the most urgent follow-up to the just-published response-memory PR. The current `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` tip `93532f96ff` reserves aggregate memory for the large `GETDATA`/`GETBLOCKTXN` response classes, but not for this multi-message loop. Its 64 kB accepted-socket send buffer can move stalled compact-filter bytes out of kernel TCP buffers and into Core's unreserved send queues. In Umbrel's externally reported 260 MiB, 150-block/3,000-output/20-peer run, the pre-adjustment candidate's RSS rose from 169,464 to 215,984 KiB while each stalled peer received only about 129 kB.

The forced Umbrel update adds only 18 lines and removes one line relative to its prior prototype: it computes the actual serialized batch size, reserves that total before queueing, and transfers the reservation to the final `CFILTER` so the whole batch stays accounted until it drains or the node is destroyed. Its reported focused unit test, `p2p_blockfilters.py`, and pressure rerun passed. These measurements and test results were read from the fetched Cycle 615 journal and were not replayed locally. The code cannot be cherry-picked as-is because it targets the prototype's older boolean/manual reservation API; the published branch uses move-only `std::optional<ResponseMemoryReservation>` ownership.

Recommendation: cover this gap on the current response-memory branch before starting another independent allocation PR. Keep a passing characterization separate from the behavioral commit, adapt the small change to the final RAII ownership path, and avoid reopening unrelated networking code. After that, the next standalone target remains `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` at `9df1d2172c`: an unauthenticated default peer can repeatedly trigger about a 5 MB allocation with a five-byte `ADDR`/`ADDRV2` count prefix, and the prepared signed branch is still absent from every `origin/*` ref. **Decision 2026-08-10:** prepare the kernel range lifetime fix first. Defer Cycle 615 until `l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` is checked out again, then add it to that response-memory PR; "another independent allocation PR" referred to the separate address-vector work, not a separate compact-filter PR.

### New lifetime branches

`50fe2fae08 kernel: keep range iterators tied to their owner` fixes a real dangling-iterator API defect. `block.Transactions().begin()` currently stores a pointer to the temporary `Range`; the temporary dies at the semicolon, so a later iterator dereference has undefined behavior. The patch instead ties the iterator directly to the long-lived `Block`. This is use-after-lifetime capable, but no production caller persists such an iterator: the wrapper is used by kernel tests and the experimental `bitcoin-chainstate` program, whose source does not use `Transactions()`. The fetched regression only compares iterators created from separate temporary ranges; the prepared branch below also dereferences one after the range dies. This is a real API correctness fix, not a default P2P/RPC security priority.

`08fbab437f` is proactive compile-time hardening, not a demonstrated use-after-free. It rejects rvalue owning byte containers passed to `MakeByteSpan`/`MakeUCharSpan`, rejects temporary embedded ASMAP containers, and repairs two fuzz-only temporary call sites. The live `WithEmbeddedAsmap` production call passes an lvalue, and no unsafe production span consumer was found.

### Seven-day Umbrel production-branch status

* Already represented on `origin/*`: Cycle 589 BIP37 bounds (`b93f8e5eb8`), Cycle 590 inventory bounds (`c3e1c532d8`), Cycle 592's equivalent `GETBLOCKTXN` index bound, Cycle 597 transaction-byte bounds (`1f6625541c`), and Cycle 611's GETDATA/GETBLOCKTXN response cap (`93532f96ff`).
* Prepared locally but still unrepresented on `origin/*`: Cycle 591 `ADDR`/`ADDRV2`, polished as `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` at `9df1d2172c`.
* Remaining unpushed remote-allocation candidates, in urgency order after the address bound: Cycle 596 transaction input/output vectors (`3b8ebc992e`), Cycle 595 full-block transaction vectors (`42d5ee63d3`), Cycle 598 outer witness stacks (`e0e8c0d1a6`), Cycle 594 unsolicited `BLOCKTXN` vectors (`ee4e35ed09`), and Cycle 593 `CMPCTBLOCK` vectors (`b271590377`). Each is default-peer reachable but only demonstrates a bounded roughly 5 MB transient allocation, not a crash.
* Cycles 599-602 remain master-pinned with no production repair. Cycle 615 is not a new standalone default-node finding; it is a completeness/regression requirement for the published Cycle 611 mitigation.

No source branch was changed, checked out, or published during this refresh. The checked-out branch still exactly tracks `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` at `93532f96ff`, and the pre-existing untracked files remain untouched.

* `19c24f3e32 test: characterize kernel range iterators` uses only public API: copied `Range` views yield unequal `begin()` iterators (TODO: should compare equal), and the saved iterator is deliberately taken from a named live `Range` (TODO: one from the temporary `block_tx.Transactions()` should remain usable), then dereferenced against `block_tx.GetTransaction(0)`.
* `75eaf9875c kernel: keep range iterators tied to their owner` is the whole fix in one atomic commit: `GetFunc` becomes a required third template parameter of `Iterator`, `operator*()` fetches through `std::invoke(GetFunc, *m_collection, ...)`, `operator->()` and `operator[]` delegate to the changed operation, and `Range`'s iterator alias plus `begin()`/`end()` bind to `m_container` instead of `this`. Both TODO lines flip to the final expectations in the same commit.

The middle `4b87d05f39` refactor was dropped because its optional defaulted-lambda `GetFunc` existed only to keep a transitional two-template-argument `Iterator` form compiling, and its test proof (`Iterator<Block, TransactionView, &Block::GetTransaction>` instantiated directly in the test) was introduced in one commit and replaced in the next. `Range` is the only in-tree `Iterator` instantiation and always supplies its getter, so no default is needed. The production change is compile-atomic without introducing another transitional API: owner-backed iteration requires the getter-aware template, the getter-based dereference, the `Range::iterator` alias, and `begin()`/`end()` together. Alternatives rechecked and rejected: current `upstream/master` has no fix of its own beyond the pre-existing deleted rvalue `MAKE_RANGE_METHOD` overload, which guards temporary containers but not iterators from temporary ranges; storing the `Range` by value inside the iterator would force a default constructor and null-container state onto `Range` for the `semiregular` iterator requirement; per-container `operator[]` is impossible since `Transaction` exposes both `Inputs()` and `Outputs()`.

Endpoint delta vs the rejected three-commit tip: the defaulted lambda and direct test-only `Iterator` instantiation are gone. `operator->()` and `operator[]` still delegate to `operator*()`, leaving one getter invocation to review. The test endpoint is unchanged.

Validation on the exact rebased commits: each rebuilt `test_kernel` and passed the focused `btck_block` case; the exact tip passed all 19 cases. Mutation check: restoring only the characterization commit's `bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h` while keeping the final test fails `check transactions.begin() == transactions_copy.begin()` at test_kernel.cpp:750 (the dangling-dereference line is the UB path and cannot fail deterministically, so the equality assertion is the deterministic guard). Per-commit `git diff --check`, changed-line `clang-format-diff.py`, test endpoint comparison, and the old-to-new `git range-diff` are clean. `git verify-commit 19c24f3e32 75eaf9875c` reports good signatures from Lőrinc. `scratch_748.txt` still accurately describes the two-commit form.

## 2026-08-11 secp sweep: MuSig nonce-output alias finding and fork PR #15 push

Continues from the 2026-08-07 post-push secp sweep. The month-scale remote-tip prefilter was rerun for committer dates since 2026-07-11. Every recurring `opt-*`, `detached*`, old goal, and pre-rebase tip is already classified by the 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-07 entries. `upstream/master` and `origin/master` remain `687155df6b`.

### Fork PR #15 is current

`origin/l0rinc/preserve-overlapping-tweak-inputs` advanced `3bbd8985dd` -> `8c61878e8d` and now matches the local branch. Fork PR [#15](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/15) serves `d8e99900ce ec: preserve overlapping tweak input` plus `8c61878e8d extrakeys: preserve overlapping tweak input`, directly on `687155df6b`. Relative to the earlier tip, the production behavior and regressions are unchanged. The public headers now explicitly permit each In/Out object to overlap `tweak32`, resolving the contract ambiguity recorded in the 2026-08-07 preparation entry. No upstream PR owns this branch.

### New source finding: `f45fabe511 musig: preserve randomness across pubnonce alias`

`i9/codex/critical-assurance-20260812` is a new stale-base branch containing the already-merged `e153e2681f` field serializer, source commit `f45fabe511`, and journal correction `cdc2b1083f`. Only `f45fabe511` is new secp source work.

The behavior is real on current master. `secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen` first verifies that `session_secrand32` is nonzero, then `secp256k1_musig_nonce_gen_internal` clears `pubnonce` before the nonce function reads the random input. If `pubnonce` overlaps `session_secrand32`, the call returns 1 after deriving the nonce from zero instead of the caller's validated randomness. An independent C89 public-API reproducer against the current build used disjoint `0x11` randomness and exact-overlap `0x11`/`0x22` randomness and printed:

```
returns=111 disjoint_equal=0/0 overlap_equal=1/1
```

The overlapping calls therefore ignore two distinct random values and produce identical secret and public nonces. With optional `seckey == NULL`, the remaining nonce inputs can all be public. Reusing that nonce state in later signing can expose the signer's key contribution. Every in-tree caller, the example, and Bitcoin Core's `src/musig.cpp` use separate storage, so no current production caller reaches the overlap.

The branch's High label is not justified without first settling the API contract. `pubnonce` is an Out argument and `session_secrand32` is a separate In/Out argument. Commit `fdcee19fdc` previously retracted pure Out/In overlap fuzz oracles because separate arguments do not promise arbitrary aliasing. Fork PR #15 differs because it now documents support for its two specific In/Out-object/tweak pairs. The MuSig header does not document this overlap, and no open fork or upstream PR owns it.

The proposed branch is not ready to extract as written:

* [ ] Decide whether this exact `pubnonce`/`session_secrand32` overlap is supported. If supported, document it explicitly in `include/secp256k1_musig.h`. If not, define the rejection contract instead of silently accepting and discarding entropy.
* [ ] Reconcile the adjacent `secnonce` case. The proposed snapshot occurs after `memset(secnonce, 0, sizeof(*secnonce))`, so `session_secrand32` overlapping `secnonce` still fails before the snapshot. Supporting one output overlap while leaving the other unsupported must be explicit.
* [ ] Rebuild from current `upstream/master`. Do not cherry-pick the unrelated `e153e2681f` serializer or either `agent-journal` file.
* [ ] Split characterization before production. The characterization can record that exact and partial overlaps return success but differ from disjoint calls, with TODO-marked expectations. The fix should change only those expectations and production code.
* [ ] Account for precedent. Journal commit `2dcb596ae4` already reproduced exact overlap and proposed fail-closed behavior through non-ancestor cleanup commit `c3b7af914e`. `f45fabe511` is a different policy choice: preserve overlap and return disjoint-equivalent outputs.

Priority: serious cryptographic consequence under a caller-selected overlapping layout, but no documented support or production caller. Treat it as a misuse-gated API-contract decision, not a remotely triggerable or High vulnerability. It does not displace the existing upstream-submission order until maintainers choose support or rejection.

## 2026-08-11 post-fetch Core local-only severe queue

This section supersedes the August 9 Core ranking. It reconciles the fetched refs through Umbrel Cycle 660 against current `upstream/master` `1bec7fa22c9f` and every fetched `origin/*` ref. "Local-only" means the substantive production fix is absent from `l0rinc/bitcoin`: exact commit containment and stable patch IDs were checked across all `origin/*` commits, not only `origin/master`.

### Publication and ref reconciliation

* `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` is published at `93532f96ff`, `origin/l0rinc/kernel-range-iterator-lifetime` at `cb083e719a`, and `origin/l0rinc/transaction-byte-vector-limits` at `1f6625541c`. Exclude their published behavior from this local-only queue. In particular, the kernel temporary-range lifetime defect is no longer unpushed.
* `l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` remains local at `9df1d2172c`; no matching `origin/l0rinc/addr-vector-limits` ref exists.
* The material new Umbrel source stack is `umbrel/cycle657-current-master-severe-stack` at `61506597f4`, based directly on current master. Its first fifteen commits contain the witness-decoder, response-extension, validation, aggregate-receive, transaction-role, and orphan-accounting repairs below. The later nine count-bound commits are older bounded-allocation siblings already classified.
* `umbrel/cycle658-prune-index-durable-lock` at `0ca3674956` adds a separate current-master crash-consistency repair. The umbrella journal advanced through Cycle 660 at `a3d100a4bcdc`; Cycles 659-660 added validation evidence, not another severe source fix.
* The August 11 RPI audit refs contain genuine wallet reentrancy, IPC/subprocess lifetime, kernel callback reentrancy, and API-lifetime findings. Their demonstrated triggers require a wallet callback, local embedder, experimental IPC/external signer, moved helper object, or unsupported lifetime use. No ordinary remote P2P path was established, so they remain below the demonstrated node OOM queue.

### Top 10 serious unpushed problems

1. **Transaction witness decoder transient OOM** - current-master stack `3cb2061e92` + `958f1d920d` + `f6d2997e1a`; standalone branch `umbrel/cycle651-master-witness-decoder-fix`. One ordinary inbound peer can send a canonically encoded 4,000,000-byte `TX`, `BLOCK`, `BLOCKTXN`, or `CMPCTBLOCK` body containing roughly four million empty witness elements. Each element costs one wire byte but a 24-byte vector object; geometric growth briefly overlaps old and new roughly 96 MB buffers before semantic rejection. All four routes OOM-killed exact master at 180 MiB while an equal-size unknown-command control survived. This is the strongest target: one peer, default configuration, no proof of work, and a demonstrated process kill.

2. **Orphan witness memory is undercharged by about 24x** - current-master commit `923d2fdfb9`; standalone `umbrel/cycle650-orphan-memory-accounting` at `70a62b2ad3`. A standard 399,805-byte missing-input transaction can own 9,593,808 bytes through 399,733 empty witness elements, but the orphanage charges weight. Eight ordinary peers delivered 3,198,440 bytes and OOM-killed exact master at 140 MiB; the matched benign control survived. The local fix charges the greater of weight and recursive dynamic usage.

3. **`relay=0` peers can create a transaction-request/orphan cross-product** - current-master commit `de7eb6dd6e`; standalone `umbrel/cycle650-txrequest-cap` at `b99c9c8149`. Master does not count a peer that advertises `relay=0` against the inbound transaction-relay role, yet still accepts that peer's transaction INV/TX traffic. With 189 ordinary peers, three standard missing-input children and 239,682 bytes created 944,811 `(peer, parent)` tracker pairs. Exact master died at 190 MiB after only 222,984 bytes; the control stayed near 77 MB. No malformed transaction, nonstandard policy, or proof of work is required, but the attacker must occupy nearly all default inbound slots.

4. **Aggregate receive memory is only bounded per peer** - current-master commit `311d9666e4`; standalone `umbrel/cycle649-recv-oom` at `2895a7f253`. Legal incomplete V1/V2 packets remain in transport buffers, and fully received checksum-valid messages can remain in the processing queue when independent send backpressure prevents polling. Fifty-four ordinary peers delivered 205,211,016 bytes of partial V1 frames and killed a 320 MiB node; a distinct 39-peer completed-message case retained 124,800,768 bytes and killed the response-repair stack at 260 MiB. This is default and unauthenticated but bandwidth-backed. The local repair is broad, about 400 lines, and needs careful networking review.

5. **`GETHEADERS` responses escape the published aggregate response cap** - current-master commit `a0cc9ee1d8`, to be folded into `l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory`. A valid 93-byte request with one locator can produce a 162,003-byte 2,000-header reply; a stalled peer retains about five replies under the per-peer send watermark. At 150 peers, only 111,600 request bytes produced 750 responses and raised RSS from about 55 MB to 182 MB. The cycle demonstrated crash-scale pressure rather than a separate constrained OOM kill. The fix caps this against the existing 32 MB response pool.

6. **`GETBLOCKS` block-`INV` responses escape the published aggregate response cap** - current-master commit `06cc8e37c1`, also for the existing response-memory PR. Each valid 93-byte request can cause an 18,003-byte 500-hash `INV`; stalled peers retain about 58 replies each. At 150 peers, 1,116,000 request bytes produced 8,700 responses and raised RSS from about 54 MB to 210 MB. The local reservation kept the same run below 100 MB. This is default, unauthenticated, and distinct from BIP35 and oversized locators.

7. **Duplicate external prevouts multiply asynchronous fetch copies** - current-master commit `f969b368d7`; standalone source commit `9fe800cd4daa`. Before double-spend rejection, the eight default prefetch workers can copy the same 10,000-byte `Coin` once per queued occurrence. A requested valid-PoW 999,518-byte invalid block with 6,000 primer inputs and 12,350 spends of one outpoint killed the node at 220 MiB; disabling prevout workers survived at about 103 MB. The attacker needs an active-chain large-script output, setup inputs, and valid proof of work, so this is miner-gated despite the demonstrated kill.

8. **Compact-block announcements can fan out a large coinbase copy** - current-master commit `baaf77371d`, for the existing response-memory PR. Any synced peer can request high-bandwidth announcements with `sendcmpct(1, 2)`. After a valid 3.6-MWU block with a 900 kB coinbase was accepted, 150 stalled peers caused automatic compact-block copies and raised RSS from about 55 MB to 199 MB; the reservation limited the fixed run to 35 announcements and about 101 MB. Exploitation requires an accepted, normally attacker-mined block and many peers; no separate constrained OOM kill was run.

9. **Valid-block input scripts are copied across validation owners** - current-master commit `3962697440`; standalone source commit `9500c0bb8612`. A 996,467-byte, 3,985,868-WU valid block can spend 24,300 outputs whose legal 10,000-byte scripts total 243 MB. The overlay, precomputed transaction data, script-check closures, and undo lifetime overlap redundant copies. The block killed exact master in a 720 MiB scope; the repaired run accepted it with no OOM. This is consensus-sensitive and expensive to exploit: the attacker must mine many setup blocks with unusual outputs, mature them, and mine the trigger block.

10. **Compact-filter responses remain outside the published response accounting** - current-master stack `6bb816046c` plus `5ee747470d`, to be adapted to the existing response-memory PR. With non-default `-peerblockfilters` and `-blockfilterindex`, repeated valid `GETCFILTERS` batches and `GETCFHEADERS` replies can retain memory across stalled peers. The clearest header run used 150 peers and 3,000 requests, constructed 2,550 64,068-byte replies, and raised RSS from about 58 MB to 217.5 MB; the fixed run stayed below 100 MB. The published branch still sends `CFILTER` batches without holding one reservation for the whole batch. This is remotely reachable only for operators who enable compact-filter serving. The separate Cycle 642 pre-reservation materialization concern remains unproven and should not be bundled silently.

### Required response-PR correction

The published response branch also needs the Cycle 645 liveness correction represented by current-master commit `f7f3f8dfc1`. Under full aggregate response pressure, its current retry state can retain a denied block request ahead of later peer input; the executable probe showed a ping and valid successor block remaining unprocessed until unrelated peers released memory. TX denial also fell through iterator handling incorrectly. This is a regression in the proposed mitigation, not an upstream-master vulnerability and not a separate PR. When the response branch is checked out again, adapt this correction together with the `GETCFILTERS`, `HEADERS`, block-`INV`, compact-filter-header, and compact-block-announcement coverage. Keep each independently reviewable rather than replacing the existing stack wholesale.

### Immediately below the cut

* `0ca3674956 index: keep prune locks at committed state` fixes a real persistent restart-denial risk when an unclean shutdown lands after prune metadata publication but before the index locator is durable. The deterministic manual-prune plus `SIGKILL` case requires rebuilding the index and a full pruned-node redownload. Automatic prune shares the ordering, but no standalone remote trigger was demonstrated.
* `9df1d2172c p2p: bound address vectors before allocation` remains the highest prepared bounded-allocation branch. A five-byte `ADDR`/`ADDRV2` prefix causes a repeatable roughly 5 MB allocation, but Cycle 628 found no retained-memory OOM composition.
* The older transaction input/output, block transaction, outer witness, `BLOCKTXN`, and `CMPCTBLOCK` count-only allocations remain local and default-peer reachable, but each demonstrated only one caught roughly 5 MB transient allocation.
* New RPI findings below the remote queue include wallet notification reentrancy (`7895e466d3` through `2090dae4c1`), IPC cleanup lifetime (`47ef7a4bfa`), moved subprocess self-references (`17c810b789`), legacy solving-provider ownership (`c4da280db9`), concurrent SHA256 autodetection (`c7b304f039`), and kernel callback replacement deadlock (`481450626e`). They are real local/API defects but have no demonstrated unauthenticated node attack path. The HTTP `FindAll`, `LineReader`, and `SourceLocation` lifetime branches are API hardening; the only production `FindAll` caller keeps the owning headers alive and consumes the result immediately.

No source branch was checked out, changed, or published during this refresh. The checkout remains detached at `upstream/master` `1bec7fa22c9f`, and all pre-existing untracked files were left untouched.

## 2026-08-11 second fetch: compact reconstruction memory and staging-PR decision

The second fetch adds one source fix after the preceding queue was written:

* `umbrel/cycle666-compact-replacement-memory-cap` at `efee0cf2c2` is based directly on current `upstream/master` `1bec7fa22c9f` and contains `p2p: bound compact reconstruction transaction memory`.
* The same patch is appended to the complete current-master severe stack as `474a5f3e8d`, advancing `umbrel/cycle652-current-master-severe-stack` to 25 source commits.
* `ProcessInvalidTx()` already rejected transactions with `RecursiveDynamicUsage(*ptx) >= 100000` before adding them to `vExtraTxnForCompact`, but `ProcessValidTx()` sent every mempool replacement through `AddToCompactExtraTransactions()` without that bound. An accepted replacement transaction with cheap serialized bytes and large nested witness allocation could therefore occupy one of the configured compact-reconstruction slots without the existing dynamic-usage ceiling.
* The fetched fix moves the same 100,000-byte check into `AddToCompactExtraTransactions()` so both rejected transactions and accepted replacement transactions use one bound. Its production diff is six lines, but it adds no automated regression and the fetched journal does not yet provide the earlier findings' constrained-memory product evidence. Treat it as a newly confirmed accounting gap that still needs characterization, not as a ready-to-publish standalone commit.

### Decision: one local memory-exhaustion staging PR

Prepare one local `l0rinc/` staging branch containing every still-pending memory-exhaustion repair, while preserving independently reviewable commit ownership. This branch is an integration and selection vehicle; it does not imply that the entire series should be submitted upstream as one final PR.

Stack rules:

* Every independent behavior change gets an adjacent passing `test: characterize ...` commit followed by the clearly named fix commit. Put the final safe test structure and old expectations in the characterization commit, mark only expectations that change with trailing TODOs, and let the fix change production plus those exact expectations.
* Keep behavior-neutral movement or refactoring separate from risky limits, accounting, networking, validation, and consensus-adjacent changes. A refactor must have an existing caller and pass independently.
* Preserve already-published prerequisites as recognizable commits when the integrated fixes depend on them; do not describe their published behavior as a new pending finding. In particular, response extensions build on `l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory`, and witness-decoder work builds near the published transaction-byte deserialization helpers.
* Put a finding label in each characterization/fix subject pair so the eventual extraction boundary is obvious from `git log`.
* Validate every exact commit, not only the tip. The final audit must check that later commits do not rewrite freshly introduced code unless the intermediate behavior is deliberate and independently tested.

The frozen source queue after this fetch is: witness decoder transient OOM; compact-reconstruction replacement memory; response-memory `GETCFILTERS`, `GETHEADERS`, block-`INV`, compact-filter-header, compact-block-announcement, and saturation-liveness follow-ups; valid-block spent-script copies; duplicate-prevout prefetch; aggregate receive memory; inbound transaction-relay resources; orphan recursive memory accounting; local address/count-parser bounds for `ADDR`/`ADDRV2`, `CMPCTBLOCK`, `BLOCKTXN`, full-block transactions, transaction input/output vectors, and outer witness stacks. Exclude already-published BIP37, inventory, `GETBLOCKTXN`, and transaction byte-vector fixes as pending findings, while retaining any exact prerequisite code their unpublished siblings require.

No branch was checked out or created at this decision point. Existing untracked files remain untouched, and no remote write was performed.

## 2026-08-12 third fetch: aggregate GETDATA request-queue OOM

The latest all-remote fetch, followed by an explicit successful `umbrel` refresh, adds one new memory-exhaustion source finding. `rpi5-16-3` was unreachable with `No route to host`; no claim is made about refs that exist only on that unavailable remote. `upstream/master` advanced from `1bec7fa22c` to `2f72123f61` through #35867, which does not overlap this finding.

* `umbrel/cycle677-getdata-request-queue-oom` points to standalone current-master fix `a17600020e p2p: bound aggregate getdata request queue`.
* `umbrel/cycle677-current-master-severe-stack` and `umbrel/agent/all-findings` both advance the complete severe stack to `6b367ae259` with the equivalent final fix `p2p: bound aggregate getdata request queue`.
* `umbrel/uber-cycle-588-wallet-weight-overflow-20260805` advanced to audit-only commit `05fad3a18b`, which records the reproducer, constrained-memory trials, and repair evidence. `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/bitcoin-core-critical-assurance` advanced only its campaign journal and adds no production candidate.

Threat vector: an ordinary unauthenticated inbound peer can send one individually legal 1,800,027-byte `GETDATA` containing 50,000 repeated unknown block entries. After deserialization, every entry moves into `Peer::m_getdata_requests`; block items drain at most one per handler turn, and the retained deque is no longer owned by either the per-peer receive bound or the aggregate receive-memory census. Independent live peers therefore multiply payload-derived request queues without an aggregate budget. The fetched journal reports that 80 ordinary peers, with 86,401,296 delivered bytes, OOM-killed the complete prior 25-fix stack at a 180 MiB no-swap boundary after 46 handled messages. This is a default-node availability attack; it requires many inbound identities and bandwidth, but no authentication, bloom support, transaction relay, mining, valid block, disk read, or outbound backpressure.

The fetched repair caps the aggregate queued inventory at the existing legal per-message maximum `MAX_INV_SZ` of 50,000 entries. It accepts one maximum-size request unchanged, ignores a later individually valid request as a whole without punishing or disconnecting its peer, accounts the old-block `GETBLOCKTXN` fallback, releases entries as `ProcessGetData()` erases them, and releases a disconnected peer's residual queue after removing it from the peer map and leaving `cs_main`. The fetched fixed replay remained alive after all 80 messages, peaked at about 116 MiB, and logged 79 denied aggregate reservations. These exploit and fixed-run measurements come from the fetched Cycle 677 journal and have not yet been replayed locally.

This finding is absent from every `origin/l0rinc/*` ref and from the current local `l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory` staging tip. Add it to that staging branch as a new adjacent pair after rebasing onto current `upstream/master`: first a passing `test: characterize aggregate GETDATA queues` commit that drives every maximum-size request through `ProcessMessage()` and records the absence of an aggregate-limit decision, then `p2p: bound aggregate GETDATA queues`, which flips only that TODO-marked expectation and adds the counter, drain, fallback, and teardown accounting. Preserve a success case at exactly `MAX_INV_SZ` and prove that disconnect teardown releases the reservation. Do not cherry-pick the fetched one-commit test/fix shape unchanged.

### Production and build findings

1. **`be4ca63ba0 ellswift: compress aux randomness before declassification` - Low, valid-input constant-time contract defect, highest actionable priority.** `secp256k1_ellswift_create` promises constant-time behavior in `auxrnd32`, but current master declassifies `hash.s` before a non-NULL auxiliary input is compressed. Separate GCC 16.1 and Clang 22.1 `-O2 -flto` Valgrind probes reported 4,738 and 4,531 errors from secret-dependent EllSwift paths before the fix and zero afterward. The old fork PR #38 tip `d975d7ae03` is incomplete because it moves the declassification while leaving `auxrnd32` buffered and secret-marked. The corrected implementation compresses `auxrnd32 || zero32` as a complete block, keeps the raw SHA buffer classified as required by #1863, and then declassifies only the chaining state. No practical key recovery, remote trigger, or invalid cryptographic result was demonstrated.

2. **`3a1651b927 context: define padding before cloning` - Low, caller-visible initialization hardening.** Context creation and preallocated cloning can copy allocator-origin padding into caller-owned context storage. Valgrind and MSan probes demonstrate undefined bytes and the patch zeroes the complete representation before member assignment. A caller already controls and can inspect the process storage, so this is not a remote disclosure or high-severity vulnerability. It is the next security-hardening candidate after PR #38.

3. **`dec24740f0 silentpayments: clear found spend tweaks on mid-scan failure` - Low, secret cleanup on a valid but negligible-probability failure path.** A scan can write a spend tweak for an earlier output, fail at a later `k`, return `0` with `n_found_outputs == 0`, and leave the earlier secret in caller storage. The fetched test constructs the failure by selecting the recipient spend key from the later tweak. A real sender cannot feasibly force this against a fixed recipient key because doing so requires a hash-derived point cancellation. The source fix is directionally correct, but it duplicates the cleanup loop at two exits and bundles its regression with the fix. Before preparing it, extract a passing characterization if possible and centralize only genuinely identical cleanup without broadening failure-output policy.

4. **`94f82602d3 musig: extend prior infinity hardening with pair closure` - informational reduced-order hardening.** The production guard and API documentation correctly reject an aggregate point at infinity. The new pair oracle closes reduced-order coverage missed by the earlier five-identical-key test. Production hash-derived cancellation remains computationally infeasible, and equivalent local guards already exist on older detached refs. Keep this below valid-input runtime and supported-build fixes.

5. **Supported-build availability series - real and unowned, below runtime findings.** `3fe619e910` supplies ctime callbacks for external-default-callback builds. `13dd5e688d` then moves those definitions into one provider shared by ctime, benchmarks, and examples, so the two commits should be reviewed as one history rather than submitted independently. `1303430047` fixes Clang ARM32 assembly by adding the required immediate marker while preserving GNU-as output. `7905c33740`, `6aceb4debc`, and `b9cc31cebd` repair static MinGW benchmark consumption, CMake object embedding under parent-wide shared mode, and static Windows pkg-config flags. These are build failures, not runtime vulnerabilities. The ARM32 Clang fix is the strongest standalone build PR after the security queue.

## 2026-08-12 fifth fetch: storage-failure availability findings

The post-staging ref reconciliation found two new standalone production fixes fetched earlier in the current session. A fresh `git fetch --all --prune` reported `No route to host` for the SSH-hosted audit remotes it could not reach, and an explicit Umbrel retry failed the same way; GitHub remotes completed and did not advance. The findings below are therefore verified against the locally fetched commits and current `upstream/master` `2f72123f61`, while no claim is made about newer commits that may exist only on the unreachable remotes.

### Buffered block-file writes can terminate during error unwinding

`umbrel/critical-assurance-cycle679` advanced from current master to `7ac15459f23a streams: avoid termination on buffered write failure`. On current master, `BufferedWriter::~BufferedWriter()` implicitly runs as `noexcept` and calls `flush()`. A short `AutoFile::write_buffer()` throws `std::ios_base::failure`; a partial pending buffer can therefore throw directly from destruction, while a failed explicit/full-buffer flush leaves `m_buf_pos` set and can throw again when unwinding reaches the destructor. The two production users in `BlockManager::WriteBlock()` and `WriteBlockUndo()` rely on destructor flushing.

The fetched external proof injected a one-byte-short `fwrite()` into `blocks/blk*.dat`. Exact master aborted with exit 134 and `terminate called after throwing ... AutoFile::write_buffer: write failed`. After `7ac15459f23a`, the same fault exited 1 through the existing controlled initialization error. The patch retires `m_buf_pos` before calling the sink and explicitly flushes both production writers while their existing exception handlers are active. Its focused regression reports one sink invocation, and the fetched ledger reports all 21 `streams_tests` passing. These measurements were not replayed in this checkout.

Threat boundary and priority: validated peer blocks reach the writer, but a peer cannot independently cause the required short write or local EIO. This is a medium local-environment availability defect, with no demonstrated memory corruption, consensus divergence, or silent durable corruption. It is absent from `l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory` and every `origin/l0rinc/*` ref, and does not belong in the memory-exhaustion staging PR. Prepare it later as a characterization/fix stack from current master. The fetched commit mixes the regression and fix, so do not cherry-pick it unchanged.

### A retryable block-index write failure can be forgotten

`umbrel/critical-assurance-cycle679-block-index` advanced from current master to `1c0c7e43f335 blockstorage: retain dirty index entries after write failure`; Umbrel's journal ref advanced to `66518dc48240 audit: record block index retry corruption`. Current `BlockManager::WriteBlockIndexDB()` erases `m_dirty_fileinfo` and `m_dirty_blockindex` while constructing the batch, before `WriteBatchSync()` succeeds. A one-shot LevelDB log-append failure is retryable, so a later shutdown flush can see empty dirty sets and commit the newer coins cache without the corresponding block-index entries.

The fetched external proof mined 200 regtest blocks and injected one EIO into `blocks/index/000003.log`. On exact master, the first shutdown flush failed, the built-in second flush committed 200 changed coins with an empty index batch, and restart found a height-200 chainstate with an empty block index, exited 1, and required reindex. With `1c0c7e43f335`, the second flush retried the preserved sets and restart loaded the exact expected tip. The fetched ledger reports all eight `blockmanager_tests` and `validation_flush_tests` passing. The patch clears both sets only after `WriteBatchSync()` returns. These runtime results were not replayed locally.

Threat boundary and priority: a transient local LevelDB append failure is required. Valid peer blocks supply dirty entries but cannot independently trigger the storage fault. The consequence is a durable startup denial and reindex requirement, so prioritize it above the buffered-writer termination fix among local-fault candidates. It is distinct from `origin/l0rinc/flush-state-failure-boundary` (`c42d7fe1cf`), which stops block-index and coins writes after a block or undo file flush failure; it does not retain a failed block-index batch for retry. This new fix is absent from the memory staging branch and all `origin/l0rinc/*` refs. It needs a passing characterization/fault-injection commit before the production fix rather than the fetched one-commit form.

### Other fetched deltas

## 2026-08-12 native-machine OOM reproducer
