### Current top 10 serious unpublished problems

The ordering is severity multiplied by demonstrated reachability, not patch size. There is no unauthenticated default-P2P item in this list. "Threat vector" therefore names the actual prerequisite instead of implying an attacker where none is demonstrated.

1. **Block-index dirty entries can be forgotten after a retryable write failure - `1c0c7e43f335`.** Threat vector: a transient local LevelDB append failure while block-index state is dirty; valid peer blocks can supply the state but cannot cause the storage fault. Current code erases dirty file and block-index sets before `WriteBatchSync()` succeeds, so the built-in retry may commit the coins cache without the matching block index. The fetched one-shot EIO proof restarted with chainstate at height 200 and an empty block index, requiring reindex. This is the strongest remaining node-integrity item because one transient fault becomes durable startup denial. The 12-line production fix applies cleanly to the current tree but needs a separate passing characterization/fault-injection commit.

2. **Transaction-details dialogs can outlive and call a freed `TransactionView` - `42e8852fd6`.** Threat vector: ordinary local GUI use, such as opening transaction details and then unloading or destroying the wallet view before the dialog closes. The contextless destroyed callback captures the view, and merely parenting the dialog is insufficient because derived members die before `QObject` destroys children. The exact Qt wallet test reports heap-use-after-free; the local fix drains dialogs while derived state is alive, adds the parent and receiver context, and passes the full sanitizer Qt suite. No remote trigger or exploit beyond a crash is demonstrated. This is the best small memory-safety PR candidate and applies cleanly to current master.

3. **Index prune locks can advance beyond durable index state - `0ca3674956`.** Threat vector: a pruned node with a block-data index, followed by manual or automatic pruning and an unclean shutdown in the window before the index locator is committed. `SetBestBlockIndex()` currently advances the prune lock from the in-memory tip, permitting deletion of blocks still needed by the on-disk index. The deterministic manual-prune plus `SIGKILL` proof requires an index rebuild and potentially a full pruned-node redownload. There is no standalone peer trigger. The fetched 51-line change applies cleanly but mixes commit-state tracking and RPC flush behavior, so extract characterization and the minimal invariant before proposing it.

4. **A wallet rescan callback can resume into a destroyed Qt model - `b85065a865`.** Threat vector: authenticated/local rescan activity concurrent with closing or unloading the GUI wallet. Ordinary disconnect prevents future callbacks but does not wait for one that already passed its connected check; that callback can later access freed `TransactionTablePriv`. GCC and Clang ASan, Valgrind, both TSan implementations, and an end-to-end rescan/model teardown schedule reproduce the defect. No unauthenticated route is established. The repair is broad at 147 added lines because it adds explicit callback draining to `btcsignals`; it needs a careful characterization/refactor/fix split rather than a one-commit transplant.

5. **Platform quit can destroy owners inside a modal Qt call stack - `7316142e9f`.** Threat vector: local OS/application termination while a wallet dialog's nested event loop is active. A `Quit` event can perform destructive shutdown, after which the modal member function resumes on a freed owner. GCC and Clang real-Qt ASan reproduce the UAF; the local repair defers and coalesces quit until no modal dialog is active. No remote, funds, keys, or consensus path is claimed. The patch applies cleanly and is smaller than the backend-callback repair.

6. **Buffered block-file write failure can terminate during unwinding - `7ac15459f23a`.** Threat vector: a local short write or EIO while writing block or undo data. `BufferedWriter::~BufferedWriter()` is implicitly `noexcept` and calls `flush()`; a failed explicit flush can leave buffered state live, then destruction throws again during unwinding and invokes `std::terminate`. The fetched injected short write changes master exit 134 into the existing controlled exit 1. A peer cannot independently cause the storage fault, and no durable corruption is shown. Split the current mixed test/fix commit into old-behavior characterization and production repair.

7. **LevelDB iterator read errors look like clean exhaustion - local branch `l0rinc/dbwrapper-iterator-read-errors`, tip `16df166000`.** Threat vector: local database checksum or I/O failure. `CDBIterator::Valid()` still returns only LevelDB `Iterator::Valid()` and ignores non-OK `status()`, so UTXO and index scans can return empty or truncated results as successful completion. This is silent integrity loss under corruption, not a remote corruption primitive. The two-commit branch is complete but stale-based and its test patch no longer applies unchanged. Coordinate with open #34931, which covers unreadable coin lookups but not this generic iterator-status contract.

8. **Partial local payment requests can block or spin the GUI - `40764b6093`.** Threat vector: a same-user process that can connect to the PaymentServer runtime socket and send a one-to-three-byte prefix. Holding the prefix blocks the GUI in repeated 30-second waits; disconnecting makes the old false-return loop spin at 100% CPU. The socket is local and permission-restricted, so this is not a network attacker. The event-driven parser repair and split-boundary tests apply cleanly, but the current 98-line test/fix commit needs characterization ownership separated.

9. **Spawned IPC cleanup can call through a destroyed process owner - `47ef7a4bfa`.** Threat vector: multiprocess or embedding teardown where an `Init` proxy is released concurrently with destruction of its `Ipc` owner. Protocol shutdown waits on the proxy after reverse member destruction has freed `m_process`; the cleanup callback captures raw `this` and reads freed state. Native and Memcheck runs reproduce the UAF, while the stock node normally shuts RPC down first. The three-line ownership idea remains applicable, but the old patch no longer applies because IPC interfaces changed and must be reimplemented on current master.

10. **Duplicate `CWallet::RemoveTxs` inputs cause iterator reuse after erase - `4555f86ee9`.** Threat vector: an in-process caller passes the same wallet Txid twice. The method stores the same `mapWallet` iterator twice, commits the database deletion, then erases once and dereferences the freed node on the second entry. Native, Memcheck, and ASan evidence confirms heap UAF, but all reviewed RPC and migration callers currently provide unique Txids and no remote or ordinary shipped path was found. The small deduplication patch applies cleanly and is the simplest latent-API hardening candidate; keep the separate synchronous-notification reentrancy UAF `7895e466d3` as a later adjacent finding rather than bundling it silently.

Immediately below the cut are `481450626e` (experimental kernel callback-destruction reentrancy deadlock), `7895e466d3` and the later wallet notification UAF series (no shipped reentrant subscriber), `17c810b789` (moved `Popen` self-reference UAF, while Core's caller uses guaranteed copy elision), `c7b304f039` (concurrent SHA256 autodetection race, while stock initialization is serialized), and `c4da280db9` (borrowed legacy solving provider, while all production consumers are synchronous). These are confirmed conditional API defects, but they do not outrank the actual node, GUI, and storage-failure paths above.

Recommended next selection: use `1c0c7e43f335` for the highest-impact node crash-consistency work, or `42e8852fd6` for the smallest normally reachable memory-safety PR. Do not start code work until the user chooses. No checkout, source edit, commit, test, or remote write was performed in this reconciliation; only this knowledgebase section was appended, and the pre-existing untracked files remain untouched.

## 2026-08-12 late Core fetch: repeated optimistic compact-block reconstruction [SUPERSEDED by the deep dive below]

This section supersedes only the ordering and next-selection recommendation in the preceding "final Core fetch" section. Its publication exclusions and the underlying finding descriptions remain current. Refs were reconciled after the 17:30 PDT fetch against current `upstream/master` `b2c45888fde0`, every `origin/*` ref, and the detached worktree at `2f72123f613f`. The worktree and its pre-existing untracked files were left untouched.

### New current-master candidate

The newly fetched `i9/codex/btc-fuzz-oracles` branch ends at `fcedb2e2c3ab net: bound optimistic compact block reconstruction`. The branch is based on an older feature stack, but this seven-line production hunk applies to the current tree. Its exact commit and stable patch ID are absent from upstream and every `origin/*` ref, and a live public-PR search found no equivalent owner. Open upstream PR #35321 handles only `READ_STATUS_INVALID` in this path; it does not limit repeated well-formed reconstruction attempts.

Threat vector: a remote peer must be eligible to send high-bandwidth compact blocks for a fresh, valid near-tip header while all three reconstruction download slots for that block are occupied. A deterministic setup uses three stalling peers and a fourth announcer; honest in-flight peers can satisfy some of those slots, but obtaining the fresh header and high-bandwidth position remains a meaningful prerequisite. Once the optimistic branch is reached, the same peer can replay the same compact block without a per-block attempt limit. Each replay builds reconstruction tables and can scan the full mempool in `PartiallyDownloadedBlock::InitData()` while `cs_main` is held and while taking the mempool lock. The input can be far cheaper than the resulting work, so sustained replay can consume CPU and delay validation or relay. The state ends when the full block is accepted or the header ceases to be ahead of the active tip. No persistent corruption, memory exhaustion, or measured process kill has been demonstrated.

The fetched repair remembers recent optimistic block hashes per peer in a rolling Bloom filter and permits one attempt per peer and block. Its production hunk applies cleanly, but its final-state test hunk does not apply unchanged to the current test file and is not a characterization commit. If selected, rebuild it on current upstream as: a passing characterization that proves repeated attempts currently reach reconstruction; then the minimal limit and expectation flip. Add a focused cost or starvation measurement before making a strong DoS claim. The RPI Cycle 20 functional oracle independently proves both success and failure arms of the four-peer optimistic branch, but does not measure resource impact. These results are fetched evidence and were not replayed during this static reconciliation.

### Other new ref deltas and exclusions

* `60d6175ae3 cmpctblock: ignore null extra transactions` is a real historical null-dereference variant on the old branch, but current upstream already removed its production state in merged PR #35670 by appending only populated extra transactions. It is not a current-master candidate.
* `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/bitcoin-core-critical-assurance` advanced from `f4a5f9279a` to `ff256120b5`. Cycles 19, 21, and 22 report clean tx-request/orphanage, I2P SAM, and package-validation censuses. Cycle 20 adds the optimistic-reconstruction behavioral oracle described above. There is no other production repair in the delta.
* `umbrel/uber-cycle-588-wallet-weight-overflow-20260805` advanced to `ddcac2d369` only to archive the already catalogued Cycle 679 block-file and block-index fault injectors. It adds no new finding or fix.
* The new `origin/l0rinc/doc-merkle-root-mutated` and rewritten `origin/l0rinc/psbt-zero-input-output-update` tips are public on the fork and therefore excluded. The new upstream and origin master commits are test, RPC deprecation, build, and secp256k1 updates with no overlap in this queue.

The ordering combines impact with demonstrated reachability. Only changes absent from upstream and every `origin/*` ref are included. 1. **Repeated optimistic compact blocks can rescan the mempool under `cs_main` - `fcedb2e2c3`.** Threat vector: a high-bandwidth compact-block peer replays one fresh, valid near-tip compact block after all three download slots are occupied. ## 2026-08-12 compact-block deep dive: repeated optimistic mempool scans

This section supersedes the preceding section's proof, severity, ranking, and recommendation. Refs were reconciled after the 17:30 PDT fetch against `upstream/master` and `origin/master` at `b2c45888fde0`, all local and remote-tracking branches, the current `l0rinc/bitcoin` pull requests, and the current upstream pull-request set. The affected `net_processing.cpp`, `blockencodings.cpp`, and functional test are byte-identical between the detached worktree and current upstream.

### Verdict

The repeated work is real on current master, but it is not a memory-exhaustion finding. Every out-of-slot announcement constructs a temporary `PartiallyDownloadedBlock`, and `InitData()` can traverse the full mempool while the message handler holds `cs_main` and `pool->cs`. Repeating the message repeats that CPU and lock work, but the small temporary lookup objects are destroyed after each attempt and no cumulative allocation was observed.

This is a preconditioned remote liveness-hardening issue, not the queue's top finding. Its mechanism is high confidence, but an end-to-end block-delay, RPC-delay, or node-starvation impact has not been demonstrated. Keep it below the durable block-index write-failure finding and normally reachable GUI UAFs unless stress measurements establish a stronger impact. A conservative current classification is Low/P3: medium availability impact if sustained, low likelihood because the sender must cross several compact-block gates and the useful attack window is normally short.

### Current-master attack path

1. The sender must have advertised compact-block support. An unsolicited sender must also be one of the victim's selected BIP152 high-bandwidth peers; a merely connected peer is rejected by merged PR #32606. The victim normally selects at most three such peers, retains an outbound peer, and selects a peer only after it supplied a valid best block. This is a meaningful gate, although #32606's discussion explicitly notes that obtaining a high-bandwidth slot can be relatively easy.
2. The compact block must carry a proof-of-work-valid header that connects to a known predecessor, passes the anti-DoS work threshold, has more work than the active tip, has no block data already available, and is at most two heights ahead. A non-mining attacker can race a freshly observed honest header, but normally only until the body arrives. A miner can sustain the window by withholding a valid body at the economic cost of risking the block reward.
3. The normal reconstruction path must be unavailable because all three reconstruction slots for that block are occupied, or because the peer already has 16 blocks in transit. The practical deterministic setup fills the three per-block slots. Because the final slot is reserved for an outbound peer, fully attacker-controlled saturation generally requires influence over an outbound connection or help from naturally occupied honest slots.
4. A minimal accepted `CMPCTBLOCK` payload can be 96 bytes: an 80-byte header, 8-byte nonce, one-byte short-ID count, one 6-byte short ID, and an empty-prefill count. Choosing a random short ID makes a match in the victim's mempool negligibly likely, so `InitData()` scans every mempool entry without the attacker knowing the mempool.
5. The out-of-slot branch records no attempt state. Replaying that payload repeats short-ID hashing across the mempool under `cs_main`, the mempool lock, and the single P2P message-processing thread.

Message handling processes one message per peer in randomized peer order on each sweep. A flooded high-bandwidth peer can therefore keep one message-handler core busy while the window remains open, but it cannot indefinitely prevent an honest peer with queued input from receiving a turn. This fairness and the fresh-header lifetime materially limit the impact of an ordinary relay peer. An attacker that also controls the stalled download slots can extend the window until block-stalling or download timeouts; a malicious miner can extend it until a competing block wins.

### Replayed proof and cost

A current-source functional probe extended the existing parallel compact-block reconstruction test with two more identical announcements after the third download slot was occupied. For each tested block the debug log recorded six `InitData()` calls rather than the four needed to establish the three stored attempts and the first out-of-slot attempt. The full `p2p_compactblocks.py` suite passed.

A second current-source probe proved that repetition can be useful rather than redundant. Its first out-of-slot attempt lacked one transaction and failed to reconstruct; after that transaction entered the mempool, an identical second announcement reconstructed and accepted the block. The full `p2p_compactblocks.py` suite passed with this behavior.

An optimized current-source benchmark used 50,000 synthetic mempool transactions occupying 59,021,520 dynamically accounted bytes and a compact block containing one absent short ID. `InitData()` took 875,994 ns per full scan on this Apple arm64 host. A linear extrapolation to the default 300,000,000-byte mempool is about 4.45 ms per attempt, or roughly 225 attempts per second to occupy one core. At 96 payload bytes per attempt, that is about 21.6 kB/s of application payload. The 300 MB result is an extrapolation, not a measured end-to-end node test, and slower hardware or different transaction shapes will differ.

### Existing local candidate is too blunt as written

`fcedb2e2c3 net: bound optimistic compact block reconstruction` remains the only exact local production fix. It exists only on `i9/codex/btc-fuzz-oracles`; its exact commit and stable patch are absent from upstream and every `origin/*` ref. The branch is 603 upstream commits behind and 44 commits ahead of its merge base, and it predates merged PR #32606. It does not compile verbatim on current master because `block_hash` is now named `blockhash`, so it must be reimplemented rather than cherry-picked.

The candidate gives every peer a 100-element, 10^-6-false-positive rolling Bloom filter and permits only the first out-of-slot attempt for a peer and block. Adapted mechanically to current master, it built and its existing repeat-suppression test behaved as intended. However, the mempool-update probe then failed at the final tip assertion: the filter discarded the second announcement that current master uses to complete the block. The debug log confirmed `Ignoring repeated optimistic compact block` instead of a second reconstruction. This behavior may be an acceptable tradeoff because three ordinary reconstruction attempts are already in flight, but it is a real behavior change and must be made explicit in the test and PR rationale rather than described as cost-free deduplication.

Before preparing a branch, choose and characterize one of these contracts:

* one optimistic attempt per peer and block, deliberately giving up the useful retry for the smallest hard bound;
* a per-peer cooldown or token bucket, retaining later retries while bounding sustained work;
* a more complex state-aware retry after relevant mempool change. Merely keying on the global mempool sequence is not a strong bound because normal churn, or attacker-supplied valid transactions, can advance it continuously.

Whichever contract is selected, put both old behaviors in a characterization commit: repeated identical announcements currently rescan, and a retry after the missing transaction enters the mempool currently succeeds. The fix commit should change only the expectations owned by its chosen policy.

### Related work map

* Merged upstream PR #9352 introduced optimistic reconstruction from compact-block announcements. Its discussion considered repeated `GETBLOCKTXN` requests limited to three, but did not bound the stateless optimistic mempool scan.
* Merged upstream PR #27626 introduced three parallel stored reconstruction attempts and outbound-slot reservation. Review explicitly preserved opportunistic reconstruction and stated that attempts beyond three were filtered, but the limit applies to stored download state; the fallback still creates a fresh temporary reconstruction.
* Merged upstream PR #32606 is the closest prior security work. Its public discussion explicitly describes repeated `InitData()` calls with a single fake short ID. The merged fix rejects unsolicited compact blocks from non-high-bandwidth peers, blocksonly nodes, and peers that never sent `SENDCMPCT`; it deliberately leaves the selected-high-bandwidth residual addressed here.
* Open upstream PR #35321, and closed duplicate #35479, punish `READ_STATUS_INVALID` in optimistic reconstruction. They do not limit repeated well-formed or merely unreconstructable messages. #35321's test is stale across #32606 and needs its fourth peer made high bandwidth.
* Open upstream PRs #35561, #35558, #35724, #34565, and #35502 mechanically overlap peer state, `InitData()`, compact-block logging/prefilling, block-download ownership, or `ProcessMessage()` placement, but none bounds repeated scans. Open #35940 would let explicitly configured `-addnode` peers receive high-bandwidth status outside the automatic set, widening this surface only for opted-in configurations.
* Draft fork PR l0rinc/bitcoin#279 contains compact-block count-allocation bounds (`990bf33634`), retained replacement-transaction memory accounting (`16e93bb651`), `BLOCKTXN` count bounds (`236fb06abf`), and compact-block announcement send-queue accounting (`59dbf2935d`). Those are distinct memory paths and do not limit `InitData()` call frequency.
* Local `60d6175ae3 cmpctblock: ignore null extra transactions` is obsolete on current upstream because merged PR #35670 removed null extra entries. Local `43e9968c50 net: guard repeated compact blocktxn fills` is likewise covered by merged upstream PR #33296. Neither fixes this scan loop.

### Correction to the earlier oracle claim

RPI Cycle 20 commit `615e7eda02ad` is useful historical evidence for the optimistic success and failure arms on its old base, but it is not a current-master oracle. Its parent does not contain merged PR #32606, and its `late_peer` is never selected as high bandwidth, so current master rejects that announcement before optimistic reconstruction. The current-source probes above are the valid evidence. The `fcedb2e2c3` test idea itself does port because it reuses an inbound peer that the test has already made high bandwidth.

No tracked source, branch, commit, or remote was changed during this investigation. Only disposable diagnostic source trees and this knowledgebase were modified; the main worktree's pre-existing untracked files remain untouched.

## 2026-08-12 prepared PR: rate-limit optimistic compact-block scans

This section resolves the contract choice left open by the preceding deep dive. A fresh read-only fetch of `upstream`, `origin`, `i9`, and `umbrel` left the relevant public and local overlap unchanged. The integration base is current `upstream/master` `b2c45888fde06429e86913fab5e7b7a075f091c3`. Local branch `l0rinc/rate-limit-compact-block-scans` tracks the intentionally absent `origin/l0rinc/rate-limit-compact-block-scans` ref and has not been pushed.

### Prepared stack

1. `7fc6b2fd0d80db364b7d1493683442679aaa006a test: characterize optimistic reconstruction` extends the existing four-peer parallel reconstruction fixture. It records that the same out-of-slot compact block immediately reaches `InitData()` twice, then proves that the same peer can retry successfully after the missing transaction enters the mempool and one second elapses.
2. `1f99d4417e9f7d098b6344c8d1094026c61f7320 net: rate-limit optimistic reconstruction` gives each peer an initially full one-token bucket that refills at one token per second. Only the stateless out-of-slot fallback consumes it. The fix changes the characterization commit's single TODO-marked immediate-repeat expectation from another `InitData()` log to the rate-limit log.

Paste-ready PR details are in `scratch_748.txt` under title `net: Rate-limit optimistic compact-block mempool scans`.

The selected policy preserves the useful behavior that the older `fcedb2e2c3` rolling-Bloom candidate removed. The first optimistic reconstruction remains immediate, an identical announcement can use newly arrived mempool transactions after one second, and announcements inside that interval skip `PartiallyDownloadedBlock::InitData()`. The state is per peer rather than per block, so a peer also cannot alternate block hashes to bypass the rate. Current automatic BIP152 selection permits at most three high-bandwidth announcers, which bounds this fallback to three mempool scans per second across those peers while they remain eligible. Connection churn does not provide an immediate cheap reset because a new connection must first become a selected high-bandwidth peer.

This remains Low/P3 remote liveness hardening rather than a memory-exhaustion repair. The 96-byte replay can still trigger header and message-processing work, but it can no longer continuously repeat the full mempool scan under `cs_main` and `pool->cs`. Using the earlier 4.45 ms extrapolation for a default-sized mempool, the automatic three-peer set would spend roughly 13 ms per second in the bounded fallback on this host. This is an estimate, not an end-to-end starvation measurement.

Both exact commit trees rebuilt `bitcoind` and passed `build/test/functional/test_runner.py p2p_compactblocks.py` with the default timeout. Removing only the seven-line gate under the final test made the suite fail at the rate-limit-log expectation while the debug log showed a second `InitData()` call for the same block. Restoring the gate rebuilt cleanly and the same test passed. `git diff --check`, changed-line clang-format, Python compilation, and the final tracked-tree cleanliness check are clean. The pre-existing untracked files remain untouched.

## 2026-08-12 final fetch: local-only top 20 reevaluation

This section supersedes every earlier local-only ranking and the prepared compact-block section's statement that its tracking ref was absent. Current `upstream/master` and `origin/master` are both `b2c45888fde0`. Local branch `l0rinc/rate-limit-compact-block-scans` and `origin/l0rinc/rate-limit-compact-block-scans` both point to `1f99d4417e`, so that problem is now public on the fork and is excluded below. `origin/l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory` points to `0c2bcdcd190d`; every semantically covered memory-exhaustion problem remains excluded even when a later audit branch independently reimplemented it under a different hash.

The reevaluation inspected the exact fetched commits, their containing refs, the live affected code on current master, and all `origin/*` and `upstream/*` containment. Fetched run logs and sanitizer claims are retained as external evidence and were not rerun in this static pass. Bitcoin Core's root `SECURITY.md` is the only applicable repository security guidance and directs vulnerability reports to the security list.

### New ref reconciliation

* `umbrel/critical-assurance-cycle680-witness-oom` at `4a9d7ab45c` is a real roughly four-million-empty-element witness allocation attack, but the root is already public in `origin/l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory`: `e80b28b715` bounds witness stack element counts, while `fa17513583` and the adjacent serialization commits avoid capacity and reallocation peaks. Exclude it rather than count a different implementation as unpublished.
* `umbrel/critical-assurance-cycle681-orphan-memory` at `31b0204e8e` is production-equivalent to public `f2d40b0a29 p2p: account orphan transaction memory`. Exclude it.
* `umbrel/critical-assurance-cycle682-response-memory` at `894b95fe1c` confirms that many ordinary peers can aggregate multi-megabyte block responses into an OOM. The covered response paths already exist on `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` and the public integration branch, including GETCFILTERS accounting. Exclude the root problem. Residual opt-in private-broadcast behavior has no validated default-node escalation.
* `rpi5-16gb-1000gb/audit/bitcoin-core-critical-assurance` advanced through journal and assurance work. Its apparent new production fixes are backports of changes already ancestral to current upstream master. It adds no unpublished current-master repair.
* `i9/codex/btc-fuzz-oracles` added two genuine unpublished current-master findings: failed UTXO batches can lose retry state (`f6f61f91d5`), and cross-network `libbitcoinkernel` block-handle reuse can bypass signet authorization (`e013c1130404`). Its passphrase fix `495de3b655` is semantically owned by public `origin/l0rinc/wallet-encryption-write-failures` and is excluded.
* The RPI matrix added `5764081535`, the authenticated `listtransactions` pagination overflow. It is not contained in upstream or any `origin/*` ref and remains applicable to the current source.

### Superseding top 20 serious unpublished problems

The order is fix priority, combining impact, confidence, reachability, and exposure in normal deployments. A consensus label does not automatically outrank a demonstrated ordinary-daemon durability failure. There is no remaining unauthenticated default-P2P issue in this local-only list. Each threat vector states the real prerequisite.

1. **Failed UTXO batches destructively lose retry state - `f6f61f91d5` - High, high confidence.** Threat vector: a transient, non-sticky local LevelDB log-append failure during `CCoinsViewCache::Sync`; peers can supply accepted state changes but cannot cause the I/O fault. `CCoinsViewDB::BatchWrite()` unlinks and clears dirty entries before `WriteBatch()` succeeds. The fatal-shutdown `Flush()` retry can then publish the target best block while omitting failed coin creations or spends, with no replay marker. The injected failure proved missing coins and a published tip before the fix. This affects the ordinary daemon and is the highest-priority integrity repair. The fetched commit mixes the regression and fix and should be rebuilt as characterization, minimal supporting refactor if required, then behavior change.

2. **A reusable kernel block cache can bypass signet authorization - `e013c1130404` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: a remote block supplier reaches a `libbitcoinkernel` embedding that reuses one `btck_Block` handle across different network parameter contexts. Priming `CBlock::fChecked` with a successful regtest check makes later signet `CheckBlock()` return before `CheckSignetBlockSolution()`. The fetched proof activates an unauthorized proof-of-work-valid signet block and changes that embedding's chain and UTXO set. Normal `bitcoind` uses one parameter set and is unaffected; no deployed multi-network consumer was examined. The consensus impact is the worst in the queue, but the experimental API-composition prerequisite keeps it below the ordinary-daemon UTXO retry defect. Split the current mixed commit into a passing characterization and the 19-line production isolation fix.

3. **Block-index dirty entries can be forgotten after a retryable write failure - `1c0c7e43f335` - High, high confidence.** Threat vector: a transient local LevelDB append failure while block-index entries are dirty. `WriteBlockIndexDB()` erases its dirty sets before `WriteBatchSync()` succeeds, so a built-in retry can commit the coins cache without matching block-index entries. The fetched one-shot EIO proof restarted with chainstate at height 200 and an empty block index, requiring reindex. This is distinct from item 1 and should remain a separate PR with its own fault-injection characterization.

4. **Transaction-details dialogs can call a freed `TransactionView` - `42e8852fd6` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: ordinary local GUI use opens transaction details, then unloads or destroys the wallet view first. A contextless destroyed callback retains the freed view; the exact Qt sanitizer test reports heap use after free. No remote trigger or effect beyond process crash is demonstrated. This is the smallest normally reachable memory-safety PR candidate.

5. **Index prune locks can advance beyond durable index state - `0ca3674956` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: a pruned node with a block-data index prunes and then crashes before the index locator commits. The lock follows the in-memory tip and can permit deletion of blocks still required by the durable index. Recovery can require an index rebuild and a full pruned-node redownload. The current change mixes durable-state tracking and RPC flush behavior, so extract the invariant and characterization before proposing it.

6. **A wallet rescan callback can resume into a destroyed Qt model - `b85065a865` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: authenticated or local rescan activity overlaps GUI wallet teardown. A callback that already passed its connected check can later touch freed `TransactionTablePriv`; sanitizer and scheduled race probes reproduce it. The generic callback-draining fix is broad and needs a careful characterization, refactor, and fix split.

7. **Platform quit can destroy an owner inside a modal Qt call stack - `7316142e9f` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: local OS or application termination while a wallet dialog runs a nested event loop. Destructive shutdown frees the owner, then the suspended modal member resumes on it. Real-Qt ASan reproduces the UAF. No remote, funds, keys, or consensus path is claimed.

8. **Buffered block-file write failure can terminate during unwinding - `7ac15459f23a` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: a local short write or EIO during block or undo output. A failed flush can leave pending state, and the implicitly `noexcept` destructor flushes again during unwinding, invoking `std::terminate`. Fault injection changes vulnerable exit 134 to controlled exit 1 after the fix. Split the mixed test/fix commit.

9. **LevelDB iterator errors can look like clean exhaustion - `16df166000` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: local checksum corruption or I/O failure. `CDBIterator::Valid()` ignores non-OK iterator status, allowing UTXO and index scans to return truncated or empty success. This is silent integrity loss rather than a remote corruption primitive. Rebase the stale two-commit branch and coordinate its scope with open #34931.

10. **`listtransactions` pagination can overflow into invalid iterator arithmetic - `5764081535` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: an authenticated wallet RPC caller supplies legal `INT_MAX` values for `count` or `skip`. Signed `nCount + nFrom` overflows, the loop bound becomes wrong, and reverse-iterator subtraction can go outside the vector. The likely consequence is UB and a process crash, not funds loss. The current commit is small but should gain a passing old-behavior characterization before the type and clamping fix.

11. **Partial local payment requests can block or spin the GUI - `40764b6093` - Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: a same-user process connects to the permission-restricted PaymentServer socket and sends a one-to-three-byte prefix. Holding it causes repeated 30-second waits; disconnecting can spin at 100 percent CPU. This is local availability only. Separate the current mixed parser test/fix commit.

12. **Spawned IPC cleanup can call through a destroyed process owner - `47ef7a4bfa` - Medium, medium-high confidence.** Threat vector: multiprocess or embedding teardown releases an `Init` proxy concurrently with destruction of its `Ipc` owner. A cleanup callback captures raw `this` and reads freed `m_process`. Native and Memcheck evidence reproduce the UAF, but stock shutdown normally releases RPC first and the old patch must be reimplemented after IPC refactors.

13. **`importprunedfunds` accepts an overweight alternate-witness transaction - `2ac352ee1a` - Low-Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: an authenticated wallet RPC caller supplies a transaction whose txid matches the Merkle proof but whose witness makes it exceed `MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT`. Because the proof does not commit the witness, the wallet can persist an impossible confirmed transaction and unnecessary data. This is authenticated wallet corruption/bloat, not node consensus acceptance or remote funds loss.

14. **Receive dialog callbacks can outlive the dialog - `1f014f1ddb` - Low-Medium, high mechanism confidence.** Threat vector: wallet-model `canGetAddressesChanged` is delivered after `ReceiveCoinsDialog` destruction. The contextless lambda captures freed `this`; adding the receiver context makes Qt disconnect it. The direct post-destruction test proves the API hazard, but current stock teardown ordering has not established an ordinary trigger.

15. **Peer-model callbacks can outlive the RPC console - `2a9ade0c1f` - Low-Medium, high mechanism confidence.** Threat vector: peer-model `dataChanged` is delivered after `RPCConsole` destruction. The contextless lambda captures freed `this`. The two-line lifetime binding is correct, but stock teardown currently destroys the model first, so practical reachability remains conditional.

16. **Duplicate `CWallet::RemoveTxs` inputs reuse an erased iterator - `4555f86ee9` - Low-Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: an in-process caller passes the same wallet Txid twice. The second saved iterator is dereferenced after the first erase, producing a confirmed heap UAF. All shipped callers reviewed supply unique Txids, so this is latent API hardening rather than an ordinary RPC path.

17. **Synchronous wallet notifications can invalidate saved transaction state - `7895e466d3` and follow-ups `7711610821`, `7d32ed1bfd`, `2090dae4c1` - Low-Medium, high mechanism confidence.** Threat vector: an in-process notification subscriber reenters wallet mutation while an outer operation still holds iterators or references. The local commits cover removal, AddToWallet, commit, and fee-bump variants. No shipped reentrant subscriber was found. Treat these as one review family but keep independently provable behaviors in separate focused commits.

18. **Replacing kernel callbacks can deadlock in the destroy callback - `481450626e` - Low-Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: an experimental `libbitcoinkernel` embedder replaces a callback whose `user_data_destroy` function reenters the callback setter. The old shared object is destroyed while a non-recursive mutex is held, causing release deadlock or debug abort. This is a small public-API fix with no default-daemon route.

19. **Moving `Popen` can leave internal self-references dangling - `17c810b789` - Low, high confidence.** Threat vector: a C++ caller moves `Popen` and then communicates after the source object's lifetime ends. Forced vector reallocation proves the UAF. Bitcoin Core's only production caller relies on guaranteed copy elision, so no shipped trigger is known and the 94-line patch is too broad for the practical risk without simplification.

20. **Taproot script-path input weight is underestimated - `20fef707e7` - Low-Medium, high confidence.** Threat vector: a wallet user funds a known Taproot script-path spend whose satisfaction is larger than a key-path signature, especially a long `multi_a` leaf. The wallet estimates every input as a key-path spend, can fund below the requested or relay-floor fee rate, and then fails to relay its own transaction. This is wallet reliability without an attacker or funds-loss path. The functional proof fails before and passes after the local descriptor-weight fix.

### Complete local-only inventory below the top 20

The following findings also remain absent from current upstream and every `origin/*` ref. They are ordered roughly by practical priority within this lower tier. Items described as diagnostics or contract hardening have no demonstrated unsafe in-tree caller and must not be presented as runtime vulnerabilities.

21. **Concurrent SHA256 autodetection races on global dispatch - `c7b304f039`.** An embedding that calls `SHA256AutoDetect()` concurrently with hashing can race on global function pointers. Stock initialization is serialized, so this is conditional API hardening.
22. **Legacy solving providers borrow from their destroyed wallet owner - `c4da280db9`.** A caller retaining `LegacySigningProvider` beyond `LegacyDataSPKM` lifetime can access freed key-store state. All production consumers reviewed are synchronous.
23. **Coins reset guards accept temporary views - `f29e6ac245`.** Constructing a reset guard from a temporary cache or overlay leaves it holding a dead receiver. All in-tree callers use lvalues; the patch is compile-time API protection.
24. **Kernel `BlockInfo` can retain a temporary hash - `10b9bba081`.** A caller can construct `BlockInfo` with a temporary block hash and leave its stored reference dangling. In-tree producers keep their hash alive.
25. **Repeated `CMerkleBlock::ExtractMatches()` mixes stale indices with new matches - `d5d8a180e6`.** The method clears matched hashes but not `vnIndex`, breaking their documented pairing when output vectors are reused. The focused reuse oracle fails on current behavior; no security consequence is demonstrated.
26. **Temporary `HTTPHeaders` values can escape through `FindAll()` - `0434b2fac4`.** Calling `FindAll()` on a temporary returns string views into destroyed header storage. The only production caller keeps the owner alive and consumes the result immediately.
27. **`Split()` can return views into a temporary owning range - `e4a249c028`.** Implicit conversion of a temporary string-like range to a span can return dangling elements. No unsafe production call was found; the patch rejects only non-borrowed rvalues when the output is borrowed.
28. **Byte-span helpers accept temporary owning containers - `e1da62b127`.** `MakeByteSpan()` and `MakeUCharSpan()` can return spans into a temporary string, vector, or array. Reviewed production calls are safe; two fuzz-only temporary calls need adjustment with the compile-time guard.
29. **`LineReader` can retain a dead input buffer - `3941e33b77`.** Its iterators refer into the supplied span or string view. The local change adds `LIFETIMEBOUND` diagnostics and does not change runtime behavior.
30. **`SourceLocation` can retain a temporary function name - `ed5c959ff2`.** The class stores the supplied `const char*`; the local annotation makes compiler lifetime analysis diagnose temporary-backed inputs. No unsafe production caller was found.
31. **UniValue reference getters can escape a temporary owner - `08db240356`.** Reference-returning getters and indexing operations can produce dangling references from a temporary `UniValue`. The local commit adds diagnostics only.
32. **BIP324 owner-backed getters can escape a temporary cipher - `6c24112b7e`.** Public-key references and session/terminator spans borrow from `BIP324Cipher`. `LIFETIMEBOUND` documents and diagnoses misuse; no transport path violates the contract.
33. **`TrimStringView()` can return a view into temporary storage - `43cbe83e3a`.** The local change adds a lifetime annotation. No unsafe in-tree caller was found.
34. **`createfromdump` does not consistently handle database transaction failures - `02b38d6d0c`.** Local wallet import can continue through begin, write, or commit failure paths without the intended cleanup/reporting. The one-commit repair needs current-master fault-injection revalidation and a characterization/fix split.
35. **RPC fixed-array schema handling trusts the declared result size - `1841cce080`.** Malformed or inconsistent fixed-array specifications can bypass size validation in RPC/OpenRPC helpers. This is local developer/API correctness and needs current-master scope review before promotion.
36. **`prevector` mutation can invalidate a self-referenced input value - `e8971efebe`.** Insertion or resize using an element already stored in the same prevector can move storage before copying that value. The focused tests prove the generic container hazard, but no vulnerable production caller is established.
37. **Minisketch decode element limits can overflow - `840ded33d2`.** A large decode limit can overflow the vendored minisketch calculation. No ordinary Bitcoin Core call reaches that domain. Any repair must go through the minisketch upstream and then be imported.
38. **Descriptor cache merge can publish a partial update before reporting conflict - `63e33448d6`.** Conflicting cache data can leave earlier entries merged even though the overall merge fails. This is wallet/descriptor consistency and needs exact caller and retry analysis before a PR.
39. **Descriptor keypool state is not restored after commit failure - `8c0de03815`.** A failed wallet database commit can leave in-memory descriptor/keypool progress ahead of durable state. The broad local patch needs decomposition around the exact atomic operation and retry contract.
40. **Partial descriptor-cache upgrades remain incomplete - `180b605b53`.** Upgrade code can stop after a partially populated cache and leave later derivation behavior inconsistent. Treat this together with item 39 for analysis, but keep independent behavior changes separate.
41. **`importprunedfunds` can hide wallet database failure - `8393822fcd`.** The authenticated RPC may report success after `AddToWallet()` persistence fails. This is distinct from item 13's overweight-witness validation and should have its own fault-injection proof.
42. **UTXO snapshot publication can precede durable file commit - `d3129e55b2`.** The RPC can expose a snapshot path before the file contents are durably committed. The six-line local fix needs crash-boundary and filesystem-semantics revalidation on current master.
43. **UniValue can lose floating-point values during type-preserving operations - `e7054c1fe3`.** The value representation can convert or overwrite a real value unexpectedly. This is serialization/API correctness with no demonstrated security impact.
44. **Unusable `-seednode` values can remain in startup retry state - `67bdecf792`.** Invalid or unresolvable seed nodes can interfere with one-shot seednode processing instead of being discarded. This is configuration/network startup reliability.
45. **Compact-block disk fallback mishandles invalid requests and read errors - `51f793297c`, `9ad1c421a9`, `81b39e391e`.** The local series validates `GETBLOCKTXN` before disk access, reports disk failures, and falls back to a header rather than silently losing the announcement. Revalidate as one behavior family on current networking code, with each independent error contract kept in a separate commit.
46. **Corrupt block-file metadata is insufficiently rejected - `72f5cad006`, `a2d12a1230`, `8694ae4c6a`, `b0d5e0bb9b`, `fb85acfc40`, `6819b3dbd3`, `2729dcfce5`, `592aea59ac`.** These local guards cover negative, overflowing, unreadable, missing, empty, and unscannable block-file metadata. They are hostile-local-datadir/startup-hardening findings rather than remote inputs. Revalidate each invariant against current startup continuity checks before selecting any subset.
47. **Several numeric startup options narrow or overflow before validation - `b51f869113`, `fcf3c020ba`, `a6eb752bfe`, `7c2f745c9c`.** The series covers signature-cache, mempool size, `checkmempool`, and cluster-count values. These are operator-controlled startup failures. Equivalent `-limitclustersize`, `-mempoolexpiry`, and `-limitclustercount` repairs already exist on `origin/*` and are excluded from this local-only row.
48. **CI dependencies still include mutable or incompletely authenticated references - `3b7a6821b1`, `81344ed49d`, `aef1c6cc5f`, `76feff7bdf`.** These commits lock test Python dependencies, pin GitHub Actions, pin container images, and pin the lint image by manifest digest. This is build and supply-chain hardening, not node runtime behavior. The separate lint-binary and script-asset download verification fixes already have `origin/*` equivalents and are excluded.

### Complete disposition of fetched findings

The local-only inventory is now the top 20 plus items 21-48 above. The following fetched roots are deliberately not duplicated in it:

* Public memory fixes: witness count/capacity, orphan dynamic memory, aggregate responses, receive buffers, transaction-relay resources, compact reconstruction, compact filters, GETDATA queues, and all transaction/count vector bounds are reachable from `origin/l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory` or `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory`.
* Public adjacent fixes: wallet encryption/passphrase failures, compact-block scan rate limiting, kernel range lifetime, malformed index cursors, settings durability, disconnected-Txid deduplication, unbroadcast and TxGraph memory, headers clock-lag bounds, snapshot cleanup, I2P/Tor key cleanup, empty-header sync, and the merkle-root documentation all have an `origin/*` owner.
* Upstream-owned fixes: descriptor range counter overflow is merged as #35872. Aggregate HTTP chunk framing remains owned by #35735 and should be reconsidered only if that PR closes without equivalent bounded retention.
* Assurance-only commits, backports already ancestral to current master, refactors supporting a public fix, tests, journals, documentation-only contract notes, and refuted candidates are recorded in their dated sections but are not standalone findings.

Historic campaign leads that were never current-master validated remain in the August 2 subsystem inventory with their proof limits. They are not promoted into the current 48-item ledger until their live code path, current public ownership, and practical consequence are rechecked.

### Priority conclusion

Start with `f6f61f91d5` for the strongest normal-node integrity failure. Choose `e013c1130404` instead if consensus-boundary correctness takes priority despite its experimental multi-network embedding prerequisite. Do not combine them: they have unrelated owners, threat boundaries, proofs, and review audiences. The current compact-block rate limiter and all newly fetched OOM roots are already on the fork and must not re-enter the local-only queue.

No source, branch, commit, checkout, build, test, or remote ref was changed during this static reevaluation. Only this knowledgebase section was appended. The pre-existing untracked files remain untouched.

## 2026-08-13 secp refresh: PR #38 publication and current top 20

This section supersedes the 2026-08-12 secp top-20 ordering and publication state. A fresh `git fetch --all --prune` completed for `upstream`, `origin`, `i9`, `rpi5-16-2-secp`, `rpi5-8gb-500gb-secp`, and `rpi5-16gb-1000gb-secp`. `rpi5-16-3-secp` remains unreachable with `No route to host`, so this refresh makes no claim about commits visible only there. Current `upstream/master` and `origin/master` remain `687155df6b76f1da1639a6f0923b69e6beaa3a09`.

### New remote state

* Fork PR [#38](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/38) now points to the rewritten signed tip `3e40186cb1`. The local branch and `origin/l0rinc/ellswift-auxrnd-declassification` match exactly, so the previous note that a force push remained necessary is obsolete. At this snapshot, 109 CI jobs have passed, 14 are running, and 121 are queued; none has failed.
* Fork PR [#39](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/39) remains at `0ee016eef6`. Its new CI run has 220 passing jobs, two running, and 22 queued; none has failed.
* Fork PR [#34](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/34), `l0rinc/silentpayments-validate-opaque-state`, remains at `ee2a84a693`. It is mergeable on the fork and all 244 CI jobs pass. No corresponding upstream PR exists. Open upstream [#1912](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1912) still owns adjacent Silent Payments light-client API work, so rebase and layering review remain prerequisites before upstream submission.
* The only newly advanced audit ref remains `i9/codex/critical-assurance-20260812` at `7b68f1f6b7`. Its five new source commits compare EllSwift decode contexts, inverse-Z conversion, accumulated global-Z ratios, group equality, and scalar bit extraction exhaustively. They report no production discrepancy and remain assurance-only, as recorded in the preceding secp section.
* No other remote-tracking secp branch moved after the preceding secp inventory. The complete upstream PR list was rechecked; no upstream owner appeared for the EllSwift auxiliary-randomness fix or the focused opaque-state fixes below.

### Severity boundary

No item below is a demonstrated high-severity or remotely triggerable vulnerability. Item 1 violates an explicit constant-time guarantee for valid input, but no practical key extraction was demonstrated. Item 2 reaches undefined pointer arithmetic in contrib code. Most remaining runtime findings are latent, astronomically unlikely, supported-build failures, or require callers to forge or overlap opaque objects outside normal API flows.

### Current top 20 findings not submitted upstream

1. **Fork PR [#38](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/38), EllSwift auxiliary randomness - Low, valid-input constant-time contract defect.** `secp256k1_ellswift_create` promises constant time in `auxrnd32`, but master declassifies the SHA256 chaining state before that input is compressed. Dedicated GCC and Clang Valgrind probes fail before and pass after. This remains the highest-priority upstream submission because it affects the main library through valid input, has no upstream owner, and now has a focused characterization/fix history.

2. **Fork PR [#36](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/36), lax DER private-key bounds - Low-Medium, malformed-input pointer UB in contrib code.** A four-byte accurately sized buffer can claim a 65,535-byte inner length and make the old parser form an out-of-range pointer before rejection. Coordinate with upstream #781, which proposes removing these helpers, and #1895, which adds overlapping parser tests.

3. **Fork PR [#11](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/11), ignored opaque-pubkey load failures - Low, misuse-gated silent success.** With a non-aborting illegal callback and an invalid public-key object, ECDH and public-key combination can continue after `pubkey_load` fails and report success. Rebase the stale branch and keep the broader hot-path curve validation separate.

4. **Fork PR [#23](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/23), EllSwift zero inverse input - Low, valid but probability about `2^-255`.** A hash-derived zero field element can abort VERIFY builds and produce an encoding for the wrong point in production. The path is proved by fault injection, but an ordinary occurrence is computationally negligible.

5. **Fork PR [#16](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/16), 10x26 magnitude-32 normalization - Low, latent arithmetic correctness.** First-pass normalize and zero-predicate carries can overflow 32 bits at the documented magnitude bound. No current public or in-tree path reaching magnitude 32 has been demonstrated.

6. **Fork PR [#13](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/13), scalar multiply-shift width - Low, latent internal stack OOB.** `shift = 513` indexes beyond both scalar backends, while the sole in-tree caller passes literal 384. Upstream may prefer an explicit internal precondition over defining the wider domain.

7. **Fork PR [#39](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/39), Clang ARM32 field assembly - Low, supported-build availability.** Generic configure probes accept Clang, but the production assembly rejects symbolic `BIC` immediates without `#`. The one-file source fix is exact and cross-toolchain-tested.

8. **Fork PR [#15](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/15), overlapping tweak input - Low, unresolved alias contract.** Clearing the In/Out object before reading an overlapping `tweak32` can return success with the zero-tweak result. The branch documents overlap support, but released headers did not promise it, so this remains API consistency rather than an established vulnerability.

9. **Fork PR [#26](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/26), zero MuSig nonce scalars - Low, effectively impossible event and blocked implementation.** The fork tip introduces secret-dependent short-circuit control flow. Rebuild from `415cc9cd13`, then rerun real Valgrind ctime and exhaustive order 13.

10. **Fork PR [#34](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/34), malformed Silent Payments opaque state - Low, misuse-gated hardening.** The five-commit characterization/fix split and CI are clean. Before upstream submission, rebase against #1912, decide whether canonical storage validation belongs in core rather than the module's `fe_impl_*` layer, and revalidate whether the serialized `combined` field must be exactly zero.

11. **Fork PR [#18](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/18), off-curve opaque public keys - Low, misuse-gated and performance-sensitive.** It contains PR #11 and adds curve validation to every `pubkey_load`. Hold it until the checked-load subset and hot-path policy are resolved.

12. **Fork PR [#22](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/22), odd-Y opaque x-only keys - Low, misuse-gated opaque-object validation.** Normal APIs create even-Y x-only objects, so this is defense in depth rather than a demonstrated valid-call bug.

13. **Fork PR [#25](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/25), overflowed opaque ECDSA signatures - Low, misuse-gated opaque-object validation.** Parse and sign APIs never produce the crafted overflowing scalar state.

14. **Fork PR [#30](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/30), invalid opaque recoverable signatures - Low, misuse-gated hardening.** No normal parser or signer path emits the rejected state.

15. **Fork PR [#24](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/24), overflowed MuSig partial signatures - Low, misuse-gated hardening.** Only direct opaque-struct modification reaches the state; parse and signing paths already exclude it.

16. **`dec24740f0`, Silent Payments stale spend tweaks after scan failure - Low, valid but negligible-probability cleanup.** A later scan failure can return zero results while an earlier output slot retains a secret tweak. Rebuild it as characterization then fix after rebasing onto #1912.

17. **`f45fabe511`, MuSig randomness overwritten by a pubnonce alias - Low, unresolved overlap contract.** An overlapping `session_secrand32` can be cleared before it is read, but the public contract does not promise this arrangement and the current patch covers only one alias direction.

18. **`3fe619e910` plus `13dd5e688d`, external-default-callback application builds - Low, build-policy conflict.** The local series provides callbacks for in-tree applications, while open upstream #1325 disables affected targets. Resolve that policy before preparing a PR.

19. **`7905c33740`, `6aceb4debc`, and `b9cc31cebd`, Windows static-build metadata - Low, supported-build portability family.** These independently fix static MinGW benchmark consumption, embedded object linkage under a shared parent, and static pkg-config flags. Keep their distinct build contracts separate.

20. **Fork PR [#21](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/21), BER length generator - test correctness.** The helper shifts by byte index instead of eight times the index, making multi-byte BER lengths malformed and leaving the intended lax-parser acceptance path untested. Production behavior is unchanged.

Below the cut remain PR #31's unrealistic Silent Payments output-count width, PR #32's NULL-destroy API consistency, PR #33's field coverage, PRs #35 and #27's unrefreshed optimizations, and PR #37's cleanup. PR #14 remains retired because its `SIZE_MAX` test violates the caller's real object-size contract. PR #19 is superseded by merged upstream #1900. Historical fork PRs #1-#10 remain provenance rather than upstream candidates.

### Current checkout

The worktree remains on `l0rinc/silentpayments-validate-opaque-state` at `ee2a84a693`, exactly matching origin. Only the pre-existing untracked `.idea/` directory is present. No source, branch, commit, or remote ref was changed during this refresh. No Bitcoin Core section was edited because this pass did not fetch or revalidate the Core repository.

## 2026-08-13 external constant-time audit and static-proposal triage

This section evaluates the [otaliptus constant-time briefing](https://gist.github.com/otaliptus/c8671ec27e6da92d6bd6ead43b9bcd74), the supplied canonical PDF pinned to current `upstream/master` `687155df6b76f1da1639a6f0923b69e6beaa3a09`, and the complete five-PR bitcoin-security-council proposal repository. The gist and PDF are two presentations of the same audit, so their repeated compiler, PPC32, MuSig, tweak, `modinv32`, and GLV results are not independent corroboration. The report bundle and physical targets were not available for independent replay in this pass. Source claims, current behavior, local ownership, and upstream discussion were checked directly.

### Priority and severity boundary

The compiler-lowering result is the only newly supplied item that merits urgent maintainer review. It is a **Medium platform-dependent vulnerability candidate with complete-key-recovery impact under a strong local oracle**. The report establishes secret-dependent generated branches and exact complete recovery for one interpreted Clang 17 generic-PPC32 program, but it does not establish a physical, co-resident, total-timing, or remote acquisition channel. The MuSig and chosen-tweak recoveries are exploit scenarios for this one root machine-code defect, not separate source bugs. The finding and candidate remediations can be reviewed publicly as long as the PR preserves these limits and does not present an incomplete portable-C rewrite as a fix.

The modeled `modinv32` and GLV multiplier-latency results remain research leads. They establish deterministic software models on historical early-terminating multipliers, not generated-target execution, physical leakage, or key recovery. The report's earlier ECDSA full-recovery claim is explicitly retracted because it reversed multiplication operand order and must not remain in any finding inventory.

None of the static proposals independently reaches Medium severity. The exact Schnorr overlap behavior reproduces on current master (`same=0 verify_original=0 verify_overwritten=1` when `sig64 == msg32`), but the API exposes separate Out and In pointers and promises no overlap semantics. Local commit `fdcee19fdc` already retracted this finding class as unsupported aliasing. The Silent Payments proposals harden failures of caller-owned callback/cache data or preserve outputs after a documented failure; upstream review explicitly chose to trust API-created label tweaks and only required the group-limit check before writing the first out-of-protocol output. The RFC6979 HMAC change is secret-lifetime hygiene with no read primitive. The 10x26 proposal duplicates the complete five-function fix already owned by fork PR #16.

The compiler-assurance family can be discussed publicly without publishing a claimed portable source fix. Keep it separate from fork PR #38 and other existing constant-time PRs. The focused branch below contains only the supplied cross-target compiler, PPC32 recovery, early-multiplier, and assurance findings, followed by concrete but explicitly incomplete remediation options.

### Complete proposal PR inventory

* [PR #1](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/1), closed at `894cf118a8`, is the first Schnorr message/output-overlap proposal. It is superseded by PR #2 and adds no independent finding.
* [PR #2](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/2), open at `c93fa36a9b`, delays Schnorr signature writes until the message has been consumed and adds an overlap matrix. This is unsupported separate Out/In alias hardening, not an established public-API vulnerability.
* [PR #3](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/3), open at `22577a4272`, contains five independent proposals: the three 10x26 normalization functions, RFC6979 HMAC temporary clearing, Silent Payments label callback binding, Silent Payments recipient-group prevalidation, and the two 10x26 zero predicates. Its description also records the declassified-WNAF observation as assurance-only with no proposed code change.
* [PR #4](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/4), open at `9b5150b4b7`, is documentation-only. It records compiler-generated scalar branches, the exact generic-PPC32 trace model, MuSig and tweak recovery under the short-slice oracle, modeled `modinv32` and GLV multiplier latency, the ECDSA recovery retraction, and proposed build-matrix/final-binary gates.
* [PR #5](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/5), open at `524b1e3e8d`, widens the Silent Payments scan output index and adds an `INT_MAX + 1` regression. Its production change is already owned by [l0rinc PR #31](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/31) and local commit `0bc3ac7dbf`; only the test shape differs.

### Deduplicated finding ledger

1. **Cross-target scalar branches / generic PPC32 - Medium candidate; High impact under the defined local oracle.** Thumb-1, base RV32, generic big-endian PowerPC, selected SystemZ, and selected old x86 tuples lower secret-derived scalar carry comparisons to branches. Local branch `l0rinc/scalar-8x32-ppc-carries` at `b1d90f2db0` fixes the identified carry sites for Clang 17 through 19 on 32-bit PowerPC. The other affected target/compiler combinations and the remaining PPC32 reduction branches are not fixed. Upstream authors already recognize the compiler/hardware assurance class in [#784](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/784) and [#1138](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/1138), but have not opined on this report's PPC32 recovery or its proposed support-matrix response.

2. **MuSig2 key recovery - same Medium candidate root, not a second defect.** Protocol-valid malicious co-signer keys provide public KeyAgg coefficients, and the report recovers three test keys under the short-slice branch-count oracle. New to l0rinc; no project-author opinion on the exact recovery. Physical and remote acquisition remain unproved.

3. **Chosen secret-key tweak recovery - same Medium candidate root, more integration-gated.** The report recovers a test secret when an application repeatedly reloads the same original key and applies attacker-selected valid multiplicative tweaks under the oracle. New to l0rinc; no exact project-author opinion. The API's in-place mutation means ordinary one-way tweak chains do not expose the demonstrated repeated-query surface.

4. **`modinv32` early-multiplier latency - Informational research / Low pending hardware evidence.** Fixed divstep counts still yield secret-dependent modeled multiplier cost on ARM7TDMI and MIPS 4Kc classes. New exact model; no l0rinc fix. Upstream [#1138](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/1138) acknowledges data-operand timing as a general concern, but no author has accepted this model as a physical finding.

5. **GLV split sign classifier - Informational research.** The model reveals approximately one predicate of a transformed scalar on the same historical multiplier classes, with no complete recovery or measured channel. New exact model; no l0rinc fix. Only the general timing concern in #1138 has author acknowledgement.

6. **Machine-code assurance/CI gap - Low process finding.** Host Valgrind/MSan tests cannot prove final code generation or instruction latency across deployment tuples. New audit synthesis, but the concern is already represented by upstream #784 and #1138. It needs a supported-build policy and final-binary gates rather than a narrow correctness patch.

7. **Schnorr message/output overlap - Informational API hardening.** Current code writes `R.x` into `sig64` before hashing `msg`, so overlap can sign the overwritten message while returning success. Exact Schnorr behavior is new, but local commit `fdcee19fdc` already retracted separate Out/In overlap as unsupported by these APIs; no l0rinc PR owns it. Council PR #2 has no project-author review. Do not call it a vulnerability unless upstream first adopts an overlap contract.

8. **10x26 magnitude-32 normalization and zero predicates - Low latent correctness.** Council PR #3 commits `5ee19ad` and `22577a4` duplicate the five-function family already fixed more narrowly by [l0rinc PR #16](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/16) at `b7fc137c35`. The l0rinc patch uses a 64-bit carry while retaining 32-bit limbs and covers normalization, false-zero, and magnitude-32-zero cases. No current public path reaching magnitude 32 is known, and PR #16 has no upstream-author comments.

9. **RFC6979 local HMAC residue - Low secret-lifetime hygiene.** Council commit `440f452` is a narrower duplicate of public l0rinc commit [`8b38596213a0`](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/commit/8b38596213a0b8b2c1a93c47da81b8dadbc44eec) in fork PR #1. The normal RFC6979 owner clears `rng`; the remaining concern is temporary HMAC state left on the stack without an independent disclosure primitive. Project authors have not reviewed this exact HMAC change, but merged [#1863](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1863) and ongoing [#1885](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1885) show support for cheap cleanup of concrete secret-derived residues.

10. **Silent Payments label callback binding - Low callback-contract hardening.** A non-NULL callback can return a valid scalar for a different queried label, causing a successful scan to report the wrong spend tweak. No matching l0rinc PR or local production commit was found. During [#1765 review](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1765#discussion_r3318963207), contributors explicitly kept the simpler contract and assumed label-cache data was produced by the API, so council commit `caed42c` revisits a conscious trust-boundary choice rather than fixing an unambiguously supported-input defect.

11. **Silent Payments group-limit partial outputs - Informational / Low API atomicity hardening.** A late oversized recipient group can return 0 after outputs for earlier valid groups were written. No matching l0rinc fix was found, and the public API does not promise untouched outputs on failure. [#1765 review](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1765#discussion_r2762506274) required checking before writing the first out-of-protocol output, which current master does. The broader all-or-nothing rule remains unaccepted, consistent with the discussion that closed [#1850](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1850).

12. **Silent Payments declassified-WNAF observation - Informational assurance lead.** Council PR #3 deliberately proposes no code because it has no final-binary observation channel or useful recovery evidence. No matching l0rinc item or upstream-author opinion was found. Keep it out of the fix queue unless measurement supplies a concrete secret-dependent observation.

13. **Silent Payments output index width - Low / extreme-resource correctness.** More than `INT_MAX` transaction outputs can truncate the signed match index even though the API count is `size_t`. Proposal PR #5 duplicates the production fix already owned by [l0rinc PR #31](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/31) and local commit `0bc3ac7dbf`. The case requires an infeasible allocation and is not a practical wallet vulnerability; no upstream-author opinion on this exact width mismatch is recorded.

14. **ECDSA complete recovery - Retracted, not a finding.** The report's earlier model reversed the actual `public r * secret key` operand order. Corrected traces remain branch-dependent on affected builds, but no unique complete recovery was validated.

### Published fork assurance PR

Fork PR [#40](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/40) publishes `l0rinc/constant-time-platform-assurance` at `2cec52ac1d`, based directly on `upstream/master` `687155df6b`. It contains five signed commits:

```
e43bd7b2a4 docs: document compiler-created scalar branches
b7500434d7 docs: document PPC32 scalar trace recovery
d08f0d0918 docs: document fixed-step multiplier timing
58ae4d017d docs: define constant-time build assurance
2cec52ac1d docs: outline constant-time remediation paths
```

The first commit records the exact source carry idiom and representative affected/branchless target matrix. The second records the interpreted generic-PPC32 execution, three MuSig and one multiplicative-tweak recovery under the short-slice oracle, integration requirements, absence of a measured channel, and the ECDSA operand-order retraction. The third records the `modinv32` and GLV early-multiplier models and qualifies the source comments. The fourth defines supported-build and final-binary evidence requirements.

The fifth commit gives maintainers concrete starting points without claiming completion. Its Clang 22 statement uses an isolated carry-only helper and is not representative of the real accumulator context. Recompiling the exact sum-and-carry use shows branches with Clang 17 through 19 and carry instructions with Clang 20 through 22. A portable bitwise formula removes the older branches but expands the newer accumulator sequence, so the first concrete fix uses target-specific carry instructions only for the affected older Clang versions. The document's other options remain valid: rejecting unverified secret-operation tuples and requiring fixed-latency multiplication or a data-independent-timing mode.

Default and forced-10x26 full tests pass with 16 iterations in VERIFY and no-VERIFY builds. `git diff --check upstream/master..HEAD` is clean and all five commit signatures verify. Paste-ready PR data is in `scratch_781.txt`.

### Published fork PPC32 carry fix

Fork PR [#41](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/41) publishes `l0rinc/scalar-8x32-ppc-carries` at `b1d90f2db0`, based directly on `upstream/master` `687155df6b`. The local branch now tracks the matching origin ref. Its signed commit makes the 8x32 multiplication and reduction macros obtain each 32-bit sum and carry through one helper. Clang before 20 on 32-bit PowerPC uses `addc` and `addze`; newer Clang versions and other targets retain the existing C comparison. The [Compiler Explorer comparison](https://godbolt.org/z/7bd1nadod) shows conditional branches for Clang 17 and 19 and carry instructions for Clang 20 and 22 in the exact accumulator context.

The helper test compares both outputs against 64-bit addition on boundary and randomized inputs. The final implementation passes focused scalar tests with 16 iterations on the forced 8x32 backend, plus full VERIFY, no-VERIFY, and exhaustive suites on the default and forced 8x32 backends. No physical or emulated PPC32 execution was available. This commit removes the identified older-Clang carry branches but does not claim to remove every conditional branch from the complete PPC32 scalar path.
