### Top 20 findings not yet submitted upstream

1. **Fork PR [#38](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/38), EllSwift auxiliary randomness - Low, valid-input constant-time contract defect.** `secp256k1_ellswift_create` explicitly promises constant time in `auxrnd32`, but master declassifies the chaining state before that input is compressed. Dedicated GCC and Clang Valgrind probes fail before and pass after. This is the highest-priority upstream submission because it affects the main library, needs no API misuse, has a focused characterization/fix stack, and has no upstream owner. No key-recovery exploit has been shown.

2. **Fork PR [#36](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/36), lax DER private-key bounds - Low-Medium, malformed-input pointer UB in contrib code.** A four-byte accurately sized buffer can claim a 65,535-byte inner length and make the old parser form an out-of-range end pointer before rejecting it. The offset rewrite removes the class. Coordinate with upstream #781, which proposes deleting these helpers, and #1895, which adds overlapping parser tests.

3. **Fork PR [#11](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/11), ignored opaque-pubkey load failures - Low, misuse-gated silent success.** With a non-aborting illegal callback and an invalid public-key object, ECDH and public-key combination can continue after `pubkey_load` fails and report success. The checked-load fix is small and covers the last two unchecked production sites. Rebase the stale fork branch and keep the broader off-curve validation out.

4. **Fork PR [#23](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/23), EllSwift zero inverse input - Low, valid but probability about `2^-255`.** A hash-derived zero field element can abort VERIFY builds and produce an encoding for the wrong point in production. The fault-injection test proves the path, but an ordinary occurrence is computationally negligible.

5. **Fork PR [#16](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/16), 10x26 magnitude-32 normalization - Low, latent arithmetic correctness.** The first-pass carries in the normalize and zero-predicate families can overflow 32 bits at the documented magnitude bound. No current public or in-tree path reaching magnitude 32 has been demonstrated, so this is contract-boundary correctness rather than an exposed vulnerability.

6. **Fork PR [#13](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/13), scalar multiply-shift width - Low, latent internal stack OOB.** `shift = 513` indexes beyond both scalar backends. The only in-tree caller passes literal 384, and values above the 512-bit product width have the mathematically forced result zero. Upstream may prefer making the internal precondition explicit instead of defining the wider domain.

7. **Fork PR [#39](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/39), Clang ARM32 field assembly - Low, supported-build availability.** The generic CMake and Autotools probes accept Clang, but the selected production assembly rejects symbolic `BIC` immediates without `#`. The source-only fix is exact and cross-toolchain-tested. It is already public on the fork and should follow the production-security queue.

8. **Fork PR [#15](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/15), overlapping tweak input - Low, unresolved alias contract.** Clearing the In/Out object before reading an overlapping `tweak32` can return success with the zero-tweak result. The branch now documents overlap support and is consistent with nearby tweak functions, but the released headers did not promise this arrangement. Treat it as API consistency unless upstream accepts the new overlap contract.

9. **Fork PR [#26](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/26), zero MuSig nonce scalars - Low, effectively impossible event and currently blocked implementation.** The fork tip introduces secret-dependent short-circuit control flow in the ctime test. Rebuild from `415cc9cd13`, which combines the zero checks without branching and substitutes a dummy scalar before continuing. Re-run Valgrind ctime and exhaustive order 13 before submission.

10. **Fork PR [#34](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/34), malformed Silent Payments opaque state - Low, misuse-gated hardening.** The characterization/fix split is sound, but the module reaches through `fe_impl_*` to validate storage and the exact `combined` invariant still needs review. Rebase and reassess against upstream #1912 before proposing it.

11. **Fork PR [#18](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/18), off-curve opaque public keys - Low, misuse-gated and performance-sensitive.** It contains PR #11 and adds a curve-membership check to every `pubkey_load`. Hold it until the checked-load subset is resolved and the hot-path cost and opaque-object policy are accepted.

12. **Fork PR [#22](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/22), odd-Y opaque x-only keys - Low, misuse-gated opaque-object validation.** The load choke point makes the check complete for in-tree consumers, but normal APIs only create even-Y x-only objects. This is defense in depth, not a demonstrated valid-call bug.

13. **Fork PR [#25](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/25), overflowed opaque ECDSA signatures - Low, misuse-gated opaque-object validation.** It rejects caller-crafted internal scalar bytes that parse/sign APIs never produce. Keep the characterization before the fix and avoid presenting it as malformed serialized-signature handling.

14. **Fork PR [#30](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/30), invalid opaque recoverable signatures - Low, misuse-gated hardening.** The branch validates forged opaque recovery objects before use. No normal parser or signer path emits the invalid state.

15. **Fork PR [#24](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/24), overflowed MuSig partial signatures - Low, misuse-gated hardening.** Parse and signing paths already prevent the state; only direct opaque-struct modification reaches it. The aggregate-side guard is correct but below valid-input and supported-build defects.

16. **`dec24740f0`, Silent Payments stale spend tweaks after scan failure - Low, valid but negligible-probability cleanup.** A later scan failure can return zero results while an earlier output slot still contains a secret tweak. A fixed recipient key makes the required hash-derived cancellation computationally infeasible. Rebuild it as characterization then fix after rebasing onto #1912, and centralize only identical cleanup exits.

17. **`f45fabe511`, MuSig randomness overwritten by a pubnonce alias - Low, unresolved overlap contract.** If `session_secrand32` overlaps `pubnonce`, the output clear erases the randomness before it is read. The current patch supports only one overlap arrangement and the public contract does not promise it. Decide the alias policy and add a focused characterization before treating this as a production defect.

18. **`3fe619e910` plus `13dd5e688d`, external-default-callback application builds - Low, build-policy conflict.** ctime tests, benchmarks, and examples fail to link when default callbacks are supplied externally. The local series provides one in-tree callback provider; open upstream #1325 instead disables affected targets. Resolve that policy question before preparing a PR.

19. **`7905c33740`, `6aceb4debc`, and `b9cc31cebd`, Windows static-build metadata - Low, supported-build portability family.** These independently fix static MinGW benchmark consumption, embedded object linkage under a shared parent, and static pkg-config flags. Keep them as separate commits or PRs according to their distinct build contracts; none is a runtime vulnerability.

20. **Fork PR [#21](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/21), BER length generator - test correctness.** The test helper shifts by byte index instead of eight times the index, so multi-byte BER lengths are malformed and the intended lax-parser acceptance path is not exercised. This is a real false-sense-of-coverage defect but changes no production behavior.

Below the cut: fork PR #31 needs unrealistic Silent Payments output counts, PR #32 is NULL-destroy API consistency, PR #33 is field coverage only, PRs #35 and #27 are optimizations requiring fresh measurements, and PR #37 is cleanup. Fork PR #14 should remain retired because its `SIZE_MAX` regression supplies a buffer smaller than the claimed object, violating the caller contract. PR #19 is superseded by merged upstream #1900. Historical fork PRs #1-#10 remain provenance, not upstream candidates.

## 2026-08-12 post-snapshot Core fetch: undo cursor overflow and assurance delta

This section updates the `2026-08-12 final fetch` Bitcoin Core inventory. Current `upstream/master` and `origin/master` remain `b2c45888fde0`. Nine ref events after the 23:12 snapshot exposed 18 commits: two source commits on i9, one compact-cache repair, one spent-script repair, one consensus differential test, one audit snapshot, ten clean-sweep journal commits, and two assurance journal commits. The stored Elements cross-check ref added no new object. This was a static reconciliation: fetched runtime claims were inspected but not rerun, and no source, checkout, branch, commit, test, or remote ref was changed.

### New local-only finding

**A 32-bit undo-file cursor can wrap and overwrite earlier undo records - `ebeac6bb52f9` - Medium-High impact, high static confidence, extremely expensive miner trigger.**

Threat vector: a miner builds an active chain whose blocks in one 128 MiB block file spend enough unusually large prior output scripts for the paired `rev` file to exceed 4 GiB. Current master stores both `CBlockFileInfo::nUndoSize` and `FlatFilePos::nPos` as `uint32_t`, and `FindUndoPos()` increments the former without checking overflow. Once it wraps, later undo writes reuse low offsets and can overwrite earlier records. A subsequent disconnect or reorganization that needs an overwritten record fails fatally. The input is consensus-valid, so typical 64-bit POSIX nodes following the same chain can persist the same bad layout. Platforms whose legacy `fseek` cannot represent the high offset may fail earlier instead of reaching the alias. The impact is broad availability and local block-storage corruption rather than a peer-local transient allocation.

The prerequisite is exceptionally costly. The attacker must first put several gigabytes of spendable, poorly compressed script data on chain, then mine the compact-input spending blocks into one block-file interval and later supply enough valid proof of work to cause a disconnect. There is no malformed-message, ordinary-peer, RPC, or zero-work trigger. This cost keeps the finding below the three ordinary integrity defects in the current ranking despite the wider blast radius.

The fetched commit widens undo positions and file-info sizes to 64 bits, adds checked arithmetic and platform 64-bit seek/truncate helpers, deliberately starts the first boundary-crossing record at `2^32` so old readers reject the index, and adds serialization, sparse-file seek, real undo read, reorganization, and reload coverage. The relevant current-master fields and unchecked addition still match the vulnerable shape. However, the commit sits on the old multi-feature i9 stack, changes 12 files in one 404-line patch, and introduces the regression tests together with the behavior change. It is evidence and a design candidate, not a review-ready cherry-pick. Restack it on current master as a passing boundary characterization, any independently justified 64-bit file-helper refactor, then the cursor/storage-format change. Preserve exact old-format compatibility assertions and test both the last accepted 32-bit position and the first position above it.

No exact or semantically equivalent fix is reachable from current upstream or any `origin/*` ref, and the fetched ref is its only remote owner in this checkout. The public search performed for `nUndoPos`, `nUndoSize`, and 4-GiB undo-file handling found no active Bitcoin Core issue or PR owning this repair. Because it is a valid-work, multi-node availability finding, follow `SECURITY.md` rather than opening a public issue before maintainers have assessed it.

**Priority update:** insert `ebeac6bb52f9` at number 4 in the prior local-only ranking. The previous items 4 through 19 become 5 through 20. The Taproot fee-estimation item becomes 21, and the prior lower-tier items 21 through 48 become 22 through 49. The first three priorities remain unchanged.

It moves the existing strict 100,000-byte recursive-usage gate into the sole `AddToCompactExtraTransactions()` mutator so accepted RBF replacements cannot bypass the limit already applied to rejected transactions. Its production patch ID is `5addd401c60a843e0c13cf32d2a3e5d3be74db5d`, identical to the previously fetched standalone repair, and the same production behavior is already present in public `origin/l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory` through `16e93bb651e5`. Keep it excluded from the unpublished queue.

It reports a standard 391,339-WU transaction with 175 inputs and 999 empty witness elements per input retaining about 4,424,144 recursive dynamic bytes. Under an externally imposed 220 MiB cgroup limit, exact master was killed after 29 valid replacements while the `-blockreconstructionextratxn=0` control and the patched 50-replacement run remained below the fatal boundary. These are fetched external results, not rerun proof. The production conclusions below therefore apply equally to both masters. Fetched runtime, sanitizer, and OOM claims are retained as external evidence and were not rerun. ### New current-master findings

**An unvalidated AssumeUTXO snapshot can select a fork it cannot disconnect to - `8edb06bd7013` - Medium, high confidence.**

Threat vector: before the user loads a recognized snapshot, an unauthenticated peer gets a valid competing prefix stored below the future snapshot base. While the snapshot chainstate is active but background validation is incomplete, the peer extends that prefix until it has more work. Current master admits the fork to `setBlockIndexCandidates`; activation then tries to disconnect below the snapshot base even though that chainstate has neither block nor undo history there. `DisconnectTip` fails and the node shuts down fatally. The fetched functional proof used a pre-stored height-200-298 prefix, loaded a height-299 snapshot, then supplied blocks 299 and 300. A fork introduced wholly after snapshot loading is normally not downloaded, so pre-positioning plus local snapshot opt-in are real prerequisites.

The fix routes direct candidate insertions through `TryAddBlockIndexCandidate`, rejects candidates not descending from an unvalidated snapshot base, independently filters them in `FindMostWorkChain`, and repopulates candidates only after background validation. Current upstream still has the unguarded direct insertions and no unvalidated-base eligibility check. The fetched commit combines 43 production lines with 58 functional-test lines and is not review-ready under our characterization-first rule. Restack it on current master with a passing pre-fix candidate-eligibility characterization, then make the smallest assertion transition in the owner commit.

**Mining C++ callers can carry trusted `CBlock` caches across mutation - `13d6731654a1` - catastrophic API-integrity effect, local/in-process prerequisite.**

Threat vector: an in-process integrator validates a `CBlock`, mutates its transactions or witness while its mutable `fChecked`, merkle-root, or witness-commitment flags remain true, and passes the same object to `Mining::checkBlock()` or `Mining::submitBlock()`. Current master forwards or copies the object with those caches intact. The fetched tests demonstrate witness-invalid and merkle-invalid blocks reaching the active chain. Network, disk, RPC, compact-block, and Mining IPC paths deserialize or construct fresh objects, and the stock tree has no non-test direct C++ consumer, so no default remote `bitcoind` route is claimed.

The fix reconstructs a header-plus-transaction `CBlock` before both public Mining calls, clearing the mutable validation caches while preserving bytes and shared transaction lifetimes. This is distinct from the kernel C API finding below because it owns a different public boundary. It belongs beside that finding in the queue, but behind ordinary-daemon durability failures until a shipped or deployed direct-C++ consumer is established. Rebuild the mixed 132-test-line commit as characterization then minimal fix before review.

### Existing kernel cache finding gets a stronger current-master owner

`umbrel/critical-assurance-cycle698-kernel-cache` adds `abddee3f5d75 kernel: isolate block validation caches across contexts`. It is not a second root cause: previously recorded `e013c1130404 kernel: isolate block validation cache state` already cache-cleans both `btck_block_check()` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block()`. The new branch is a cleaner standalone current-master implementation with a stronger direct proof: a block accepted by an `OP_TRUE` custom Signet manager is rejected by an incompatible `OP_FALSE` manager after the fix, whereas the vulnerable code activates it at height one. Use `abddee3f5d75` as the preferred evidence/fix owner and retain `e013c1130404` as provenance. Neither is on `origin/*` or upstream.

### Prune-assumevalid finding belongs to fork PR #190, not upstream master

`07919ca09ddf validation: preserve prune-assumevalid provenance` fixes a real Low, high-confidence failure in the experimental `-pruneassumevalid` stack. A peer with a genuinely higher-work fork below intentionally omitted blocks can replace `m_best_header`; the old code then loses the mutable classification that those blocks were intentionally stripped. Reorganization attempts to read an absent block, fatally shuts down, flushes the competing header, and restarts into a persistent `-reindex` requirement. The fix persists an omission bit, migrates old records, and preflights the full disconnect path.

This does not enter the current-master queue. Its parent contains the eleven-commit prune-assumevalid feature stack beginning at `1d90c0ddcb`, while upstream has no `feature_pruneassumevalid.py`, option, or production code. The underlying feature is already public as fork PR #190. Add this repair to that feature branch before further publication; do not describe it as an upstream-master vulnerability.

The surviving RPI candidates are deliberately below the main queue:

* Cycle 390 confirms depends pins `freetype 2.11.1` and `expat 2.7.3`. In the deterministic Linux GUI build, Qt uses system FreeType and fontconfig depends on FreeType plus Expat; macOS and MinGW explicitly disable Qt FreeType. The journal names later security fixes, but it did not build the bumped packages or prove that a hostile font/XML input reaches a vulnerable function. Treat this as supply-chain update work requiring advisory-by-advisory reachability and deterministic-build proof, not as a confirmed Core vulnerability.
* Cycle 404 reports `RPCConsole` scroll preservation forming NaN from a zero range and casting it to an integer. That is local GUI undefined behavior with a cosmetic or crash effect, not a remote or consensus path. The patch artifact is not fetched as source.
* Cycle 435 confirms `FlatFileSeq::Flush()` ignores directory `fsync` failure because `DirectoryCommit()` returns `void`, then reports success. The fault requires local storage failure and affects rename/directory durability rather than already committed file contents. Equivalent fixes already exist on old public `origin/umbrel/*` refs through `7f6566ee5c`, so this is not a new unpublished owner; reassess and restack only if it outranks the ordinary LevelDB durability work.
* Cycle 444 shows generic map/set deserialization can allocate far more than its encoded bytes because each tree node is individually allocated. The journal's 256 MiB/32-million-entry probe reaches `std::bad_alloc` under a 1 GiB cap, but the identified production readers are disk or authenticated surfaces such as mempool persistence, not default P2P. Keep it as a Low parser-hardening candidate until a remotely scalable caller is found.
* Cycle 445 records a `TX_WITH_WITNESS` round-trip asymmetry for a transaction with an empty input vector: the legacy/witness marker ambiguity causes the serialized value to decode differently. No in-tree producer emits that state, and consensus/network transaction handling rejects it. Keep it as Low serialization API contract work.

Cycle 437's assertion that PR #35493 is absent is wrong for the fetched tree. GitHub reports [#35493](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35493) merged as `2c01832f7b`, and that merge is ancestral to both `origin/master` and `upstream/master`. The separate crafted MuSig2 PSBT abort remains owned by open [#35933](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35933), as already recorded. Neither is a new local finding.

It marks an already-public point before variable-time validation and does not demonstrate a timing leak. Keep it as Low constant-time assurance after PR #38, not as a key-recovery finding.

Callers must ignore those outputs, and upstream previously declined the broader clear-on-failure policy in #1850. Keep this family deferred unless a real wrapper ignores the return or maintainers revisit the API policy.
* **Generated vector comment injection:** `1ec5c95460` blocks external JSON `*/` text from escaping into generated C. The source escape is reproduced across Wycheproof and Silent Payments generators, but execution requires a maintainer or CI job to regenerate from attacker-influenced vector JSON. Keep as Low developer-supply-chain hardening, above generic CI pinning but below supported runtime/build fixes.
* **Mutable GitHub Actions and `debian:stable-slim`:** `22ca59b17d` and `5192666afb` remain Low CI hardening and should be handled with the three sealed supply-chain findings as one dependency-provenance program.
* **Silent Payments bounded rescan:** the 23,250-output fixture measured 38.417 seconds at `K=1000`. The `K=2323` case timed out before a result. This remains a documented bounded availability lead pending caller and policy evidence.

The Core dossier also preserves two secp findings outside the extended A6XIUV report:

* `3a1651b9270e` defines context padding before preallocated clone copies. GCC/Valgrind and Clang/MSan reproduce caller-visible undefined bytes on the tested ABI, but the caller already owns same-process allocation storage. Rank this as Low API initialization hardening after the currently ready PRs.
* `f45fabe511d1` snapshots `session_secrand32` before an overlapping `pubnonce` output can clear it. The current header does not promise this overlap, absent `restrict` is not contract evidence, the patch supports only the `pubnonce` direction, and `secnonce` overlap remains different. Keep it Low and blocked on an explicit alias-policy decision. Do not inherit the dossier's High label without resolving that contract.

Two orderings are useful and should not be conflated:

## 2026-08-13 final secp audit reconciliation and current top 20

This section supersedes the earlier 2026-08-13 secp rankings. A fresh fetch left local `master`, `origin/master`, and `upstream/master` at `687155df6b76f1da1639a6f0923b69e6beaa3a09`. The worktree contained only the pre-existing untracked `.idea/` directory. Current fork and upstream PR inventories were read directly before assigning ownership.

### Source completeness

Every finding in the otaliptus constant-time gist and the supplied `secp256k1_constant_time_audit_canonical.pdf` is represented here. The two documents describe the same audit rather than independent corroboration:

* Cross-target scalar branches, the exact Clang 17 generic-PPC32 branch trace, MuSig2 recovery, and chosen multiplicative-tweak recovery share one machine-code root. Fork PR [#40](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/40) documents the evidence and limits. Fork PR [#41](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/41) fixes the identified carry sites for Clang 17 through 19 on PPC32, but does not claim to remove every branch in the complete scalar path or cover the other affected target/compiler tuples.
* The ARM7TDMI/MIPS `modinv32` latency and GLV sign-classification results remain modeled research leads. Neither has target execution, a physical observation channel, or complete recovery. They are recorded with the general data-dependent-instruction concern already discussed in upstream [#1138](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/1138).
* The machine-code assurance gap is owned by fork PR #40. Upstream [#784](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/784) and #1138 establish that maintainers already recognize the compiler and instruction-timing class, but they have not opined on the audit's PPC32 recovery experiment.
* The earlier ECDSA full-recovery claim is retracted because its model reversed scalar multiplication operands. It is not a finding.

The canonical 20-item summary gist is also complete. Items 1-8 are the constant-time family above; item 9 is unsupported Schnorr output/message alias hardening; items 10-11 are fork PR #16; item 12 is the public RFC6979 HMAC-clearing commit in fork PR #1; items 13-15 are Silent Payments trust, output-atomicity, and assurance leads; and items 16-20 are fork PR #34.

The newer `security-review/` scan at `cbd48358db` was reconciled finding by finding:

* Already owned: MuSig zero nonces (#26), ignored public-key loads (#11), 10x26 magnitude 32 (#16), scalar shift width (#13), ordinary `ecmult_const` residue (upstream #1885), tweak overlap (#15), MuSig partial-signature overflow (#24), invalid recoverable signatures (#30), EllSwift zero `u` (#23), MuSig clear-on-failure (#1/#2), odd-Y x-only keys (#22), off-curve opaque keys (#18), EllSwift auxiliary randomness (#38), ECDSA opaque-signature overflow (#25), lax DER bounds (#36), Silent Payments ctime coverage (upstream #1898), opaque Silent Payments state (#34), and label-index width (#31).
* Newly catalogued and unowned: `secp256k1_ecmult_const_xonly` returns without clearing its secret-derived Jacobian result `rj` or inverse `i`. Upstream #1885 clears the sibling scalar temporaries in `secp256k1_ecmult_const` but does not touch this frame. This is Low secret-lifetime hardening requiring a separate memory-disclosure primitive, not a standalone key leak.
* Policy-deferred: ECDH and EllSwift XDH leave deterministic output on invalid-secret failure, while MuSig failure paths leave stale public outputs. Callers must ignore outputs after return 0, and upstream declined broad clear-on-failure changes in #1850. Keep these out of the ready queue without a real caller that consumes failed output.
* Build/test/documentation: the CMake ecmult-window dead zone is blocked on #1791's regeneration design; the stale generator-table comment has a local fix; unpinned `lief` is CI supply-chain hygiene; and the Silent Payments label serialization mismatch is documentation-only.

The later source-only dossier entries remain recorded with their evidence boundaries: upstream #1913 owns context padding; `1ec5c95460` covers generated-vector comment termination; `5e352b4b15` is MuSig public-point checkmem annotation; `594c34f46a`/`3cde91b7e5`/`dccbb3df6f` are policy-deferred failure outputs; `22ca59b17d`/`5192666afb` and the mutable PyPI/Sage/Homebrew inputs are CI provenance; the 23,250-output Silent Payments timing result is a bounded availability lead; and `f45fabe511d1` remains blocked on whether pubnonce/output overlap is supported. Those commit IDs are archival evidence when their objects are absent from the current advertised refs, not confirmed current branch ownership.

### Current top 20 secp findings

This order uses demonstrated impact, reachability, and evidence strength. It is not an upstream-submission order. No item is a demonstrated remote or physical key-recovery vulnerability.

1. **Cross-target scalar machine-code branches - Medium candidate, High impact under the defined local oracle.** Generic PPC32, Thumb-1, base RV32, selected SystemZ, and selected old x86 builds can branch on secret-derived scalar carries. The audit recovers MuSig2 and chosen-tweak test keys from one interpreted Clang 17 PPC32 branch-count oracle. Fork PRs #40 and #41 partially own this; a measured channel and the remaining target/compiler fixes are open.
2. **EllSwift auxiliary-randomness declassification - Low constant-time contract defect.** Fork PR [#38](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/38) covers valid input, has direct Valgrind characterization, and has two complete green CI runs.
3. **Lax DER private-key pointer formation - Low-Medium contrib parser UB.** Fork PR [#36](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/36) removes out-of-range pointer formation for accurately sized malformed input. Coordinate with upstream #781 and #1895.
4. **Ignored opaque public-key load failures - Low misuse-gated silent success.** Fork PR [#11](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/11) makes ECDH and public-key combination honor the failed load.
5. **Uncleared `ecmult_const_xonly` intermediates - Low secret-lifetime hardening.** The EllSwift XDH path leaves `rj` and `i` in its stack frame. It is unowned and adjacent to, but not fixed by, upstream #1885.
6. **EllSwift zero inverse input - Low valid-input correctness with probability about `2^-255`.** Fork PR [#23](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/23) owns the fault-injected path.
7. **10x26 magnitude-32 carry loss - Low latent arithmetic correctness.** Fork PR [#16](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/16) fixes all three normalization functions and both zero predicates. No current public path reaches magnitude 32.
8. **Scalar multiply-shift index past 512 bits - Low latent stack OOB.** Fork PR [#13](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/13) owns it; the only in-tree caller passes 384.
9. **Malformed Silent Payments opaque state - Low misuse-gated hardening.** Fork PR [#34](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/34) validates labels and prevout summaries. Reconcile its layering with upstream #1912 before submission.
10. **Zero MuSig nonce scalars in no-VERIFY builds - Low negligible-probability correctness.** Fork PR [#26](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/26) owns it but needs its constant-time-safe history rebuilt before upstream use.
11. **Overlapping tweak input is cleared before use - Low unresolved alias contract.** Fork PR [#15](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/15) owns two sites. The public headers do not promise arbitrary separate-argument overlap.
12. **Silent Payments failed scan retains earlier spend tweaks - Low failure cleanup.** Local `dec24740f0` records the behavior. Output on failure is not promised and the trigger is negligible; rebase onto #1912 before reconsidering.
13. **Context clone copies allocator padding - Low initialization hardening.** Upstream [#1913](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1913) owns the fix. No remote disclosure path is demonstrated.
14. **Generated-vector comments can escape into C source - Low developer supply-chain integrity.** Archival `1ec5c95460` escapes `*/` in generator input. Current tracked corpora contain no hostile comment.
15. **MuSig pubnonce output can overwrite session randomness - Low pending alias policy, potentially severe only if supported.** Archival `f45fabe511d1` covers one overlap direction. The headers do not promise it, and the opposite direction remains unresolved.
16. **ECDH invalid scalar leaves deterministic output - Low failure-contract hardening.** Return 0 is correct; impact requires a caller to consume output after failure. No such caller is known.
17. **EllSwift XDH invalid seckey leaves fallback-derived output - Low failure-contract hardening.** Same policy boundary as item 16, with no demonstrated consumer of failed output.
18. **RFC6979 local HMAC residue - Low secret-lifetime hygiene.** Public l0rinc commit `8b38596213a0` clears local HMAC objects. No independent stack-disclosure primitive is known.
19. **CMake ecmult window 16-24 configures but cannot build - Low fail-closed build defect.** The old clamp conflicts with upstream #1791, which can generate the larger tables. Any fix must make the valid range conditional on table generation.
20. **CI dependency provenance - Low build-integrity program.** Unpinned PyPI `lief`, mutable Sage/Homebrew inputs, mutable actions, and `debian:stable-slim` should be handled together with digest and update policy rather than as runtime vulnerabilities.

## 2026-08-13 x-only constant-multiplication cleanup

Prepared unpushed branch `l0rinc/ecmult-xonly-clear-temporaries` at signed commit `aeff86555f ecmult: clear x-only multiplication temporaries`, based directly on `upstream/master` `687155df6b76`.
The branch adds only `secp256k1_fe_clear(&i)` and `secp256k1_gej_clear(&rj)` after `secp256k1_ecmult_const_xonly` computes its affine X output.

Severity remains **Low secret-lifetime hardening**.
The Jacobian result `rj` depends on the secret scalar, and the inverse `i` depends on its Z coordinate, but exploiting their residual stack values requires a separate memory-disclosure primitive.
The public EllSwift XDH path reaches this helper with its private scalar, then clears the returned affine X coordinate and scalar while these two helper-local values were previously left uncleared.

This is a focused companion to upstream [#1885](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1885), not a replacement or duplicate.
That PR clears secret-derived locals inside `secp256k1_ecmult_const`; real-or-random explicitly asked its author to clear every value derived from the secret scalar, but the PR does not touch the x-only wrapper's own `rj` and `i`.
All earlier returns in the wrapper occur before the scalar is used, while `g` and `p` depend only on the public x-only input, so no broader cleanup belongs in this commit.

Focused `ecmult`, `ecdh`, and `ellswift` tests pass in VERIFY and no-VERIFY builds on the default and forced-int64/10x26 backends.
Full `tests`, `noverify_tests`, and `exhaustive_tests` also pass on both backends.
AppleClang 21 at `-O2` retains explicit zero stores for both locals immediately before return, and the existing x-only multiplication microbenchmark shows no measurable minimum-time change at its short-run resolution.
`git diff --check` is clean and the commit signature verifies.
The branch locally tracks the matching, currently absent `origin/l0rinc/ecmult-xonly-clear-temporaries`; only the user may publish it.

### Partial overlaps and related non-duplicates

* **Council #17 partially supersedes a narrower public fix.** Public l0rinc commit [`522c9168fbf9`](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/commit/522c9168fbf9379a0f16c4101524b8429146fcf4) explicitly cleanses the wallet passphrase KDF's local `CSHA512` context. Council #17 puts cleanup in the generic destructor and therefore covers every caller. Count the wallet KDF residue as already pushed, while retaining the broader generic-lifetime change as new scope.
* **Council #33 closes more than the prior public ancestry-error patch and now has a prepared public owner.** Public l0rinc commit [`bbbf3613b62f`](https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/commit/bbbf3613b62fbdfb9e822b0fc6d9c59ee8f43fcc) distinguishes Git exit status 1 from operational errors, fixing the already-recorded nonexistent-object success case. It still returns success without signature verification for any ordinary non-ancestor, including divergent commits. Local branch `l0rinc/verify-commits-divergent-history`, based on `upstream/master` `683e05a265c8` and tracking `origin/l0rinc/verify-commits-divergent-history`, now has two signed commits: `b3d1dca33882` fails on Git ancestry errors and validates the exact-root success path, then tip `465bca734ebf` requires reverse ancestry proof for the trusted commit and Tree-SHA512 roots while naming the relevant root in ancestry failures. Separate manual checks prove both boundaries: a missing revision returns 0 on master and 1 from the first commit onward, while divergent history returns 0 at the first commit and 1 at the tip. Rob Hamilton is credited with a verified GitHub noreply coauthor trailer on both commits. Public Bitcoin Core issue and PR searches found no full duplicate. The public draft credits responsible `Red Team🟥` disclosure without exposing restricted source links.
* **Council #6 and public `3c029f458fdc` touch the same `MarkUnusedAddresses()` persistence boundary but select different failure behavior.** The public patch force-writes within `TopUpInternal()` and restores the live descriptor when the transaction fails. Council #6 persists an observed used index before a later locked hardened topup can return false. Keep Council #6 as a distinct follow-up until the two behaviors are reconciled.
* **Council #31 is distinct from fork PR #281 and Council #10.** PR #281 rate-limits the already-untracked optimistic branch after all retained reconstruction slots are unavailable. Council #31 targets a reconstruction that first acquired tracked state and was then removed solely to reserve the final slot for outbound. The existing token bucket is not reached on that earlier branch.

No pushed semantic owner was found for Council #4, #5, #7-#9, #11, #13, #15, #16, #20-#25, #28, or #29. Council #24 and #25 now provide external proposal owners for the two established retry-state findings, but they remain absent from `bitcoin/bitcoin` and `l0rinc/bitcoin`. Council #32 and #33 remain contrib-tooling scope even though their underlying verifier failures are security relevant.

## 2026-08-13 bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin refresh: PRs #34-#44 and corruption-excluding top 20

Read-only refresh frozen at `2026-08-14T02:35:40Z`. Council `master` remains `b2c45888fde0`, current `upstream/master` is `11090c8bb359`, and current `origin/master` is `b2c45888fde0`. The Council pull-request refs were refreshed into `security-council/pr/<number>`. GitHub now lists 44 draft PRs: 39 open and five closed. PRs #18 and #19 changed from open to closed without changing their heads. Eleven new open proposals, #34 through #44, are each one commit on Council master and remain absent as exact patches from current upstream.

The triage below is static. Council test and PoC claims are retained as external evidence and were not rerun. `confirmed` means the source path and consequence are established under the stated preconditions. `needs_review` means the repeated-work path exists but practical exploitability is still unmeasured. `not_actionable` means the item does not enter the security queue under the current policy, including findings whose only meaningful prerequisite or consequence is local data corruption.

### New proposal triage

* [#34](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/34) `b6cb8c7bb3bd`, **needs_review, medium confidence**: an exact-cardinality wrong `BLOCKTXN` from a selected parallel compact-block peer removes its failed reconstruction state, allowing the same peer to repeat mempool matching. The patch retains bounded full-block fallback. A valid near-tip header, a surviving first owner, selected high-bandwidth status, and precise wrong content are required. No replay-rate, CPU, lock-delay, or propagation impact was measured.
* [#35](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/35) `ec48fb1a6e19`, current rebased head `0bdf24db22c7`, **confirmed source defect, Low severity / normal urgency**: `util::ReplaceAll()` interprets replacement metacharacters through `std::regex_replace`. On POSIX, a wallet name containing `$'` can make the replacement engine reinterpret the already shell-escaped `%w` value and alter an operator-configured `-walletnotify` command. Preconditions are a non-default wallet notification command, `HAVE_SYSTEM`, and authenticated wallet RPC access that can create or load a chosen-name wallet. Live arbitrary payload execution was not tested. The safe model PoC created a marker, while the committed regression checks literal notification filename substitution. The Council discussion explicitly classified the finding as Low. Local branch `l0rinc/walletnotify-literal-replacement` carries signed commits `2925655c5f30` and `481cf23c8c28` on `upstream/master` `a8b582ec1d25`. The focused `util_ReplaceAll` unit test and `feature_notifications.py` pass at the tip.
* [#36](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/36) `f7b17d86fcbb`, **confirmed, high confidence, duplicate root**: a hardened PSBT MuSig2 derivation reaches the always-on `CPubKey::Derive` assertion and aborts the process. Open upstream [#35933](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35933) owns the same finding at `73a94b45459a` by rejecting hardened path elements in `SignMuSig2()` and also handles the mismatched-derived-key assertion. Council #36 moves the hardened-child rejection to the generic public-derivation sink, so its patch is broader but does not add an independent vulnerability.
* [#37](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/37) `e5230834bc0d`, **not_actionable for the security queue, high confidence**: recognized JSON-RPC 2.0 requests that fail late parsing falsify an `Assume()` and abort only builds configured with `ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME`. Normal release builds return the wrong HTTP status but preserve a structured error. This is protocol and assertion-build robustness, not a demonstrated production security boundary violation.
* [#38](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/38) `074b704c2823`, **not_actionable under the current local-corruption policy, high confidence**: a peer can activate an assertion in `GETBLOCKTXN` only after an independent local recent-block read failure. The same source family was already recorded in local commit `9ad1c421a9`. A healthy node is unaffected and the peer cannot create the storage fault.
* [#39](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/39) `b9cfc146fbfc`, **needs_review, medium confidence**: after successful compact reconstruction followed by context-free block rejection, the request state is removed without retaining same-peer duplicate suppression. The same peer can repeat reconstruction after scheduling recreates state. Exploitation normally requires mining and sacrificing a valid-proof-of-work block whose reconstructed body is context-free invalid. No practical availability effect was measured.
* [#40](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/40) `2227c8a4374c`, **not_actionable, high confidence, already pushed**: V2 long-form unknown commands accept `0x7f` while V1 stops at `0x7e`. The command is ignored and no resource or dispatch consequence is demonstrated. Public l0rinc commit `cfcff2e6a0` already fixes the same parser boundary.
* [#41](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/41) `427d2739557b`, **confirmed, high confidence**: independently valid `listtransactions` `count` and `skip` values can overflow signed addition and form an invalid reverse-iterator range. An authenticated wallet RPC caller can cause undefined behavior and likely process termination. This is the same root as existing local finding `5764081535`, now with a current-master Council owner and broader RPC coverage. No upstream or pushed l0rinc owner was found.
* [#42](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/42) `afd980fbc38f`, **confirmed, medium-high confidence, partially pushed and partially upstream-owned**: `ExternalSigner::SignTransaction()` accepts a decoded signer response by replacing the host PSBT wholesale. A compromised or desynchronized optional signer can substitute transaction fields and discard host metadata before Core finalizes, records, and relays the result. Public l0rinc commit `14e8454c28` already binds the complete unsigned transaction hash but still replaces the PSBT. Open upstream [#35358](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35358) at `e5ca77ed5049` checks outputs and sighash policy but also still replaces it. Council #42 checks every unsigned-transaction field and PSBT version, then merges into a copy, so its metadata and atomic-publication scope is not fully duplicated.
* [#43](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/43) `ae2b675f1af9`, **not_actionable for the security queue, high confidence**: manual-input `sendall` substitutes zero when combined bump-fee calculation is unavailable for an enormous unconfirmed cluster. The result can be committed locally and rejected from the mempool, causing payment-delivery and wallet-state confusion. Recovery is available through abandonment, and no attacker-driven fund loss or privilege boundary is established.
* [#44](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/44) `5864abe6159f`, **confirmed, high confidence**: the Signet commitment parser treats malformed `GetOp()` failure as clean exhaustion after finding a valid solution. An observer can append a malformed suffix to a signed block, recompute the ordinary Merkle root, redo proof of work, and reuse the original Signet authorization for a different block hash. This is a Signet-only authorization and consensus-boundary bypass. Mainnet, testnets, and regtest are unaffected. No pushed or upstream owner was found.

### Ownership and overlap delta

* Council #36 is the same MuSig2 crafted-PSBT abort owned by open upstream #35933. Prefer advancing the complete upstream fix rather than proposing the generic sink change as a second vulnerability.
* Council #40 is a full semantic duplicate of public l0rinc commit `cfcff2e6a0`.
* Council #41 is a current-master rewrite of existing unpushed finding `5764081535`.
* Council #38 is a current-master rewrite of existing unpushed `GETBLOCKTXN` disk-read finding `9ad1c421a9`.
* Council #42 strengthens public l0rinc commit `14e8454c28` and open upstream #35358. The transaction-substitution root is already pushed, while PSBT-version binding, merge-on-copy, and host-metadata preservation remain additional Council scope.
* Council #34 and #39 are distinct from Council #10, Council #31, and fork PR #281. They cover failed parallel response cleanup and post-reconstruction invalid-block replay respectively.

### Current global top 20, excluding local-data-corruption-only findings

This ranking covers Bitcoin Core and secp256k1 findings in the shared knowledgebase. It includes findings already pushed to `l0rinc/*` or proposed upstream because urgency describes the unresolved upstream security exposure, not novelty. Findings whose only consequence is damage to the same node's local database or files are deliberately excluded, including failed UTXO/block-index batches, prune-lock durability, iterator corruption handling, undo-cursor overwrite, malformed persisted wallet/index data, and storage-only retry state.

1. **[Corrected 2026-08-14: below the top 20.] Wallet notification replacement metacharacters - Council #35 - Low.** The source behavior is confirmed, but live payload execution was not tested. Exploitation requires non-default `-walletnotify`, POSIX `system()`, and authenticated wallet RPC access. Local branch `l0rinc/walletnotify-literal-replacement` prepares the public fix.
2. **Transaction witness decoder transient OOM - public `origin/l0rinc/bound-untrusted-memory` - confirmed.** One ordinary unauthenticated peer can send about 4 MB of canonical witness bytes that transiently expand to roughly 96 MB and kill a 180 MiB node. This remains the clearest default-node availability attack.
3. **Orphan witness memory undercount - public `f2d40b0a29` family - confirmed.** Empty witness elements make a roughly 400 kB standard orphan own about 9.6 MB while the orphanage charges weight. Eight ordinary peers OOM-killed a 140 MiB node. This is the previously questioned orphanage witness-memory undercount bug.
4. **Aggregate large-response memory - public `origin/l0rinc/bound-large-response-memory` - confirmed.** Twenty stalled peers used tiny `GETDATA` or `GETBLOCKTXN` requests to retain multi-megabyte responses and kill a 180 MiB node.
5. **Aggregate receive memory is only per-peer bounded - public untrusted-memory stack - confirmed.** Legal partial frames or queued complete messages across 39-54 peers killed constrained nodes. The attack is unauthenticated but bandwidth-backed.
6. **`relay=0` transaction-request/orphan cross-product - public untrusted-memory stack - confirmed.** Ordinary inbound peers excluded from relay-slot accounting can multiply retained parent-request state. The demonstrated kill required nearly all default inbound slots.
7. **Aggregate `GETDATA` request queues - public untrusted-memory stack - confirmed.** Eighty ordinary peers retained individually legal 50,000-entry request queues and killed a 180 MiB node. No mining, authentication, or malformed payload is required.
8. **External-signer transaction substitution - Council #42, public `14e8454c28`, and partial upstream #35358 - confirmed.** A compromised optional signer can return transaction B after the host approved transaction A and use Core's wallet, commit, and relay path. Council #42 is the most complete invariant and atomic-merge proposal.
9. **Malformed Signet commitment tail reuses authorization - Council #44 - confirmed.** An observer can modify a signed Signet block and reuse its authorization after recomputing the Merkle root and proof of work. Scope is Signet only, but the violated property is consensus authorization.
10. **Cross-target secp256k1 scalar branches - fork secp PRs #40/#41 family - needs_review.** Several 32-bit compiler/target tuples emit secret-dependent scalar carry branches, and the interpreted PPC32 branch-count oracle recovered complete MuSig2 and chosen-tweak test keys. A physical or deployable observation channel remains unproven.
11. **Reusable libbitcoinkernel block cache bypasses Signet authorization - `abddee3f5d75` / `e013c1130404` - confirmed under an embedding prerequisite.** Reusing one block handle across incompatible network contexts can carry `fChecked` past Signet validation and activate an unauthorized block. Normal single-network `bitcoind` is unaffected.
12. **Unvalidated AssumeUTXO snapshot can select an undisconnectable fork - `8edb06bd7013` - confirmed.** A peer can pre-position a valid competing prefix before snapshot loading, then extend it after activation until the snapshot chainstate fatally attempts to disconnect below its base. User snapshot opt-in and pre-positioning are material prerequisites.
13. **MuSig2 crafted-PSBT assertion abort - upstream #35933 / Council #36 - confirmed.** A counterparty-supplied or authenticated RPC PSBT with hardened or mismatching aggregate derivation can terminate the node through always-on assertions. The fix is already open upstream and should be advanced rather than duplicated.
14. **Trusted-signature quorum bypass in `verify-binaries` - Council #32 / public `0ba63f01390d` - confirmed.** Valid signatures from untrusted keys count toward `--min-good-sigs`, weakening the user-selected trusted quorum for downloaded binaries. The root is pushed to l0rinc but has no upstream owner recorded.
15. **`listtransactions` pagination overflow and invalid iterator range - Council #41 / `5764081535` - confirmed.** An authenticated wallet RPC caller can supply valid `INT_MAX` pagination values and reach signed overflow plus out-of-range iterator arithmetic, with likely process-wide availability impact.
16. **Repeated optimistic compact-block reconstruction under `cs_main` - fork PR #281 / Council #10 - needs_review.** A selected high-bandwidth peer can repeat mempool matching when all reconstruction slots are occupied. The source path is proven and a rate limiter is public on the fork, but starvation or exhaustion has not been measured.
17. **Failed parallel compact reconstruction can immediately retry - Council #34 - needs_review.** A selected second owner can erase its suppression state with exact-cardinality wrong `BLOCKTXN` content and repeat reconstruction while the first owner remains. Practical cost and propagation impact remain unmeasured.
18. **Rejected reconstructed compact blocks can replay - Council #39 - needs_review.** A peer can repeat a successfully reconstructed but context-free-invalid compact block after request state is recreated. The need for valid proof of work and the lack of measured impact keep it below the cheaper compact-block path.
19. **`verify-commits` accepts side-branch or unrelated ancestry - Council #33, partial public `bbbf3613b62f` - confirmed tooling boundary.** The existing public fix handles Git operational errors, while Council #33 adds reverse ancestry and equality checks needed to distinguish a proven historical ancestor from an unrelated valid commit.
20. **Mining C++ callers can carry trusted block caches across mutation - `13d6731654a1` - confirmed under an in-process prerequisite.** A direct C++ integrator can validate a block, mutate transactions or witness, and pass cached validation state into `Mining::checkBlock()` or `submitBlock()`. Tests demonstrate active-chain acceptance, but stock network, RPC, IPC, and disk paths construct fresh objects.

Immediately below the cut are the contract-dependent Schnorr message/output overlap key-recovery scenario, ordinary local Qt lifetime crashes, the experimental IPC destroy race, Council #31's unmeasured final-slot compact path, Council #37's assertion-build JSON-RPC abort, Council #43's `sendall` delivery confusion, and informational V2 DEL parity. None outranks the listed remote OOMs, authorization failures, potential command execution, supply-chain checks, or demonstrated consensus/API boundary violations under the current policy.

## 2026-08-14 Council refresh: secp256k1 PRs #4 and #6-#8, Bitcoin PRs #45-#78

Read-only snapshot at `2026-08-14T19:54:22Z`. In the secp256k1 repository, `upstream/master`, `origin/master`, and Council `master` all resolve to `687155df6b76f1da1639a6f0923b69e6beaa3a09`. Current Council proposal heads are #4 `b8c34a3a12ad`, #6 `6d6881ebe803`, #7 `02724102317c`, and #8 `f0d377f58c75`. In Bitcoin Core, current `upstream/master` is `230185a5ee74`, while `origin/master` and Council `master` resolve to `b2c45888fde0`. All Council refs were inspected read-only. The external test and PoC claims below were not rerun in this pass unless an entry says otherwise.

### secp256k1 delta, ordered by priority

1. **Cross-target scalar machine-code branches, [Council secp256k1 #4](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/4), Medium candidate and urgent maintainer-assurance work.** This is not a new root finding, but head `b8c34a3a12ad` materially strengthens the evidence recorded for fork PRs #40/#41. Clang/LLD 21.1.8 produces a final static generic-PPC32 consumer from the real pinned source and precomputed translation units, the consumer runs under `qemu-ppc`, and the scalar reduction/overflow path retains 28 semantically secret-dependent branches. Four secrets by four tweaks yielded nine traces and 542-545 scalar-reduction instruction counts. The final Clang 21 multiplication kernel is branchless, so this evidence localizes the remaining variation to reduction rather than the older Clang 17 multiplication surface. Pwr8, Thumb2, RV32 Zicond, SystemZ, i686, AArch64, and optimized x86-64 were clean controls in the classified path. No supported deployed PPC32 application, physical target, timing/PMU/cache/power/EM channel, remote channel, or held-out key recovery was demonstrated. Keep the existing classification: platform-dependent Medium candidate, High cryptographic impact under the older defined local oracle, no demonstrated practical extraction channel. Upstream issues [#784](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/784) and [#1138](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/issues/1138) establish maintainer awareness of the compiler/hardware assurance class, but not an opinion on this exact final-binary result.
2. **EllSwift auxiliary-randomness declassification, [Council secp256k1 #7](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/7), Low severity and ready for upstream review.** This is an exact duplicate of open fork PR [l0rinc/secp256k1#38](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/38): the Council tree at `02724102317c` equals `origin/l0rinc/ellswift-auxrnd-declassification` at `3e40186cb1`, including the dedicated auxiliary-buffer characterization and the hash-before-declassification fix. The independent proposal adds no new defect, but its reported GCC/Valgrind and Clang/MSan failures strengthen the evidence for the already-pushed valid-input constant-time contract violation. No key or auxiliary-randomness recovery is demonstrated.
3. **Generated-vector comment termination, [Council Bitcoin #76](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/76), Low build-time supply-chain severity and normal urgency.** Although staged in the Bitcoin repository, every production file is owned by secp256k1. Silent Payments and Wycheproof generators interpolate untrusted JSON comments into C block comments; `*/` can terminate the comment and activate C or preprocessor tokens during regeneration. The finding already exists locally as archival commit `1ec5c95460`; Council #76 adds a current external proposal, a shared renderer, broader generator tests, and a Wycheproof `tcId` type check. Ordinary builds consume checked-in headers, so exploitation additionally requires influence over vector metadata, regeneration, compilation or test execution, and missed review. Any fix must be proposed in secp256k1 first and imported normally.
4. **Overlapping public-key tweak input, [Council secp256k1 #8](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/8), Low correctness/API-contract severity and normal urgency.** Stable patch ID `7dca0f9568fa` and the full tree match fork PR [l0rinc/secp256k1#15](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/15) commit `d8e99900ce`. Council #8 therefore adds no new finding and covers only the `ec_pubkey_tweak_add` half; fork PR #15 additionally handles `keypair_xonly_tweak_add` at `8c61878e8d`. All 33 contained overlap layouts reportedly return success with the wrong untweaked key before the fix. No production caller or security consequence is known, and the API-wide overlap policy remains a review question despite the local branch explicitly documenting support for these two functions.
5. **Development package-version drift, [Council secp256k1 #6](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/6), Informational and no security urgency.** This is the only genuinely new secp256k1 root in the refresh. At the same development revision, CMake publishes exact version `0.8.1`, while Autotools appends `-dev` and publishes `0.8.1-dev`; exact-version consumers can therefore accept or reject the same source solely according to build generator. The proposal reports four fresh shared/static installations, identical protocol behavior, and no security-sensitive consumer. Maintainers should decide the intended development-version semantics before a code change. Keep this out of the security top 20.

### secp256k1 novelty and ownership conclusion

Only package-version drift is a new root. Council #4 is stronger final-binary evidence for the existing cross-target constant-time family. Council #7 exactly duplicates fork PR #38. Council #8 exactly duplicates the first half of fork PR #15. Council Bitcoin #76 supplies a current proposal for the already-recorded generated-comment finding. No new secp256k1 vulnerability outranks the existing cross-target machine-code concern, and no newly fetched proposal displaces fork PR #38 as the highest-priority ready runtime fix.

Do not count it as a new vulnerability.

An attacker needs enough inactive private keys plus control of manifest, signatures, and binaries. This is distinct from Council #32/public `0ba63f01390d`, which prevents untrusted but active keys from satisfying the trusted quorum.
* [#73](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/73) `2216a4fa594c`, **Informational / no security urgency**: correct documentation of `TxGraph::Trim()` dependency direction; no runtime defect or behavior change.
* [#74](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/74) `3d82fc51e594`, **Low opt-in privacy/liveness / low urgency**: track wallet transactions pending private broadcast so sign-then-raw-broadcast workflows do not let another wallet spend race the accounting state.
* [#75](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/75) `23e5115eda0b`, **Low local/opt-in liveness / low urgency**: preserve transaction ownership of private-broadcast connection demand when aborting one transaction. The original reproduction is a synthetic state-machine model, not a live schedule.
* [#76](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/76) `7bb13ac966f7`, **Low secp256k1 build-time supply chain / normal urgency, existing root**: reject unsafe generated C comments. See the prioritized secp256k1 entry above; this belongs upstream in secp256k1, not directly in Bitcoin Core.
* [#77](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/77) `b216876b0637`, **Low operator-mediated malformed-LevelDB memory safety / low urgency**: stage upstream-first length-addition and file-range checks. Authoritative fixes belong in LevelDB PRs #1323/#1326 and normal subtree import; native Windows failure was not reproduced.
* [#78](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/78) `9eceb27f6615`, **Medium authenticated-PSBT availability / already owned**: replace the mismatched MuSig2 derived-key assertion with candidate rejection. This is not independent of open upstream [bitcoin/bitcoin#35933](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35933): current upstream head `73a94b45459a` contains the same mismatch guard and also rejects hardened derivation elements. Council #78 is a strict subset of that live upstream fix despite its description treating #36 as separate. Advance #35933; do not prepare another PR.

### Priority change after the Core intake

Council #50 is a real PSBT signing gap with narrow prerequisites. Public issue #35977 now owns it, and its public handling supports Low-Medium severity and normal urgency rather than the earlier High/immediate classification. Council #71 remains high priority but is a duplicate of the existing public orphan-memory family. Council #72 is the highest-priority genuinely new Medium item because it weakens current release authorization using cryptographically valid but inactive credentials. Council #78 is fully owned by upstream #35933. The remaining new Core proposals are predominantly exposed-service availability, user-assisted malformed-file handling, optional-feature privacy/liveness, or local shared-directory hardening and do not displace the current global top tier.

## 2026-08-14 Council follow-up: Bitcoin PR #80

Read-only snapshot at `2026-08-14T20:33:05Z`. Fetching all Council Bitcoin pull-request heads added only [PR #80](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/bitcoin/pull/80) at `50007cf9beb3`; no PR #79 ref or list entry exists. The branch changes only `src/test/data/script_tests.json`, `tx_valid.json`, and `tx_invalid.json`. Its six vectors represent five root divergences reported in the external Scala bitcoin-s implementation. Bitcoin Core already exhibits the expected behavior, so this is assurance coverage rather than a Core production fix. Relative to Core the intake verdict is `not_actionable` with high static confidence. Relative to bitcoin-s the findings remain `needs_review` with medium confidence because the PR does not identify the affected bitcoin-s revision or source locations.

### PR #80 downstream findings, ordered by urgency

1. **Invalid-x Taproot program treated as unassigned witness, High consensus/funds candidate, immediate downstream validation.** A 32-byte version-1 witness program remains Taproot even when the x coordinate is invalid; treating it as an unknown anyone-can-spend program could accept an invalid spend. This is the most serious reported bitcoin-s divergence. Core dispatches every such program to Taproot before key validation. This is crypto-adjacent but not a secp256k1 defect.
2. **Negative `CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY` operand other than `-1`, High consensus candidate, immediate downstream validation.** The report says the affected implementation special-cased `-1`; accepting `-2` would admit an invalid spend and create block-validation divergence. Exact downstream source reach is the main proof gap.
3. **`IFDUP` on noncanonical zero byte, Medium-High consensus candidate, high downstream urgency.** `0x00` casts to false and must not be duplicated. Opposite stack semantics can change script validity. The vector establishes the Core oracle, while the affected downstream path is not cited.
4. **`OP_16` rejected as non-push-only, Medium consensus-availability candidate, high downstream urgency.** `OP_1` through `OP_16` count as push-only for P2SH scriptSig evaluation. Rejecting `OP_16` can reject a valid transaction or block. The transaction and script vectors cover one root finding.
5. **`LOW_S` without explicit `DERSIG` accepts padded DER, Low-Medium flag/API compatibility, normal downstream urgency.** Core's `LOW_S` check first enforces strict DER. The standalone flag combination is primarily a library/policy contract issue because normal post-BIP66 network validation already requires strict DER. This is ECDSA-adjacent but not a secp256k1 arithmetic, parser, or verification bug.

### Priority effect

PR #80 does not change the Bitcoin Core or secp256k1 security queues. For the external bitcoin-s review, validate the invalid-x Taproot and negative-CSV paths first, then `IFDUP`, `OP_16`, and the standalone `LOW_S` implication. For Core, keep PR #80 as useful cross-implementation consensus test coverage below production security fixes. The secp queue remains: cross-target scalar machine-code assurance first, EllSwift auxiliary-randomness declassification as the highest-priority ready runtime fix, generated-comment termination as Low build-time supply-chain work, overlap fixes as contract-dependent, and package-version drift as Informational.

### New focused Council proposal heads

1. **[Council secp256k1 #9](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/9), 10x26 normalization carry loss, Low latent correctness, normal review urgency.** Commits `12cc34ee33` and `a9a944bc65` characterize a legal magnitude-32 state and widen the three normalization routines. This is not a new root finding. Fork [l0rinc/secp256k1#16](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/pull/16) at `b7fc137c35` already fixes the same three routines plus the two false-zero predicates and tests the complete five-function family. PR #9 omits the zero-predicate carry loss that was present in closed Council PR #3, so it must not replace or supersede fork PR #16. No public or in-tree path reaching magnitude 32 has been demonstrated.
2. **[Council secp256k1 #10](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/10), finalized HMAC state residue, Low secret-lifetime hygiene, normal review urgency.** Commits `588cf6565c` and `8d253a2746` characterize retained HMAC state and clear the local object in `secp256k1_hmac_sha256_finalize`. This is a narrower focused version of public l0rinc commit [`8b38596213a0`](https://github.com/l0rinc/secp256k1/commit/8b38596213a0b8b2c1a93c47da81b8dadbc44eec), which also clears related SHA256, RFC6979, and EllSwift hash state. Exploitation still requires a separate stack or memory disclosure, and source clearing alone does not prove compiler-spill erasure. Upstream #1863 and #1885 support the general cleanup policy but do not review this exact site.
3. **[Council secp256k1 #11](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/11), Silent Payments label callback binding, Low integration hardening, normal-to-low urgency.** Commits `f37737f1a3` and `be9d4e3b93` make a non-NULL callback result prove that its scalar derives the queried label point. A faulty or compromised application callback can otherwise return a scalar for another candidate and create inconsistent spend metadata. A transaction-only attacker cannot choose the callback result. No matching l0rinc implementation branch exists. Upstream #1765 review consciously trusted label-cache values created by the API, so this revisits an accepted trust boundary and adds one constant-time generator multiplication per actual label hit.
4. **[Council secp256k1 #12](https://github.com/bitcoin-security-council/secp256k1/pull/12), Silent Payments group-limit partial outputs, Informational to Low failure-atomicity hardening, low urgency.** Commits `24115c5504` and `ce75f7042c` show that an oversized later recipient group can return 0 after 2,323 earlier output objects were written, then prevalidate sorted group sizes before derivation. No matching l0rinc implementation branch exists. The API does not promise untouched output storage on failure, callers must already honor the return value, and recipient pointers remain reordered as documented. Upstream #1765 required rejection before the first out-of-protocol output, which master already does; the broader all-or-nothing contract remains unaccepted and resembles the declined output-clearing policy in #1850.

Closed Council PR #3 is therefore fully accounted for: PR #9 owns only its three normalization routines, PR #10 owns HMAC cleanup, PR #11 owns callback binding, and PR #12 owns group prevalidation. Its separate zero-predicate commit has no new Council split, but fork PR #16 already owns and tests it. None of PRs #9 through #12 changes the secp top-five priority order.
